review_text: Post cruise, four of us wanted a private tour of Valparaiso, Vina del Mar and Santiago. Hector arranged the whole thing. As much as time allowed, I think we hit all the high points. The first concern in a foreign country is trusting the tour company you are working with. Hector has received the accolades and they are well deserved. The financial part of the transaction was clear and secure. He gave us many options and told us what it would cost immediately which we appreciated. The second best part about Hector is his willingness to tailor the tours to the needs of his clients. We were an active two couples so we very much wanted to walk the streets of Valparaiso to see the city first hand. Our tour guide in Valparaiso was wonderful. He even went off script as we were heading to Santiago for the night. He knew we had time to spare so we stopped in a Chilean winery for a sip of vino and a snack before driving the final half an hour to our hotel. The second day of our two-day tour we had Hector himself. His knowledge of the city was phenomenal. In addition to seeing the usual sights we also went into Argentina's version of the stock market. Again, his willingness to go off script and allow us to spend extra time at the Museo De La Memoria Y Las Perechos Humanos documenting the people who disappeared following Allende's overthrow my General Pinochet. Hector went above and beyond. Our tour was supposed to be over at 4:00 pm but there was Hector showing us a few last sights before 6:00 pm. Bravo Hector.

review_text: My friend and I enjoyed seeing the penguins, but the timing was very off. Since we weren't coming from a cruise or staying at a hotel, we were told to arrive at the Terminal by 9:20 am. We waited in the waiting room for quite a bit, where they had free wifi and souvenirs if you're interested. We didn't get on the catamaran until about 10 am. The tour description said that the boat ride to Magdalena would take about 90 minutes, but it was closer to 2 hours. One of the two bathrooms on the boat was not working, which was an inconvenience when we were told about 20 minutes before landing that there was no bathroom on the island, and about half the 52 passengers lined up to use the loo. The catamaran was really just for taking us from the mainland to the island, so if you want snacks or coffee, you're out of luck. When we arrived at the island, we were docked next to another ship, and the captain determined that we couldn't get on the dock safely. They had a group of 10 get on a Zodiac lifeboat from the back of the boat to go around the other ship. There seemed to be communications issues because those 10 people sat in the boat for a while, and by the time they got around the other boat to the dock, the other boat left and our captain decided it was okay to disembark from the front of the boat. On the plus side, Catalina was a great guide. She was very knowledgeable and spoke English well. There were two other guides, but they didn't really do much. We were told to stay 2 meters from the penguins. The island was full of penguins and seagulls. There is a circular walkway marked by a rope from the dock, up to the lighthouse, around the other side of the beach. We saw so many penguins, including down-covered babies, that it was a real treat to see them. We were on the island about an hour, which was plenty of time to walk all the way around and take pictures. I would give 5 stars for delivering on the penguins, but 3 for the disorganization of the company. We thought we would be done by 1 or 2 pm, and we didn't return to the mainland until 4:30 pm. Review of: Shore Excursion: Magellan Penguins Natural Reserve in Magdalena Island from Punta Arenas

review_text: Having seen many home museums in our time this one is especially different. It's like the occupants are out and you just wandered around when they weren't home . Neruda was obviously a colourful character who had an interesting life, and travelled to many places, held strong political views, all of which are reflected in the love nest he built for he and his lover and later wife Matilde. This place is a must see, if time permits we will try and see his other homes as well.

review_text: We had a great time with Diego touring Pomaire by bike and getting to learn the history of the greda (or clay) work. We were able to learn about the whole process from collection, refining, and then meet and watch a long time greda maker do his craft of making beautiful clay pieces. We also rode the bikes out to Diego's home to spend time with his family and learn how to make Empadas, which was a real treat. It was a great day and really neat to see how Diego is honoring the greda history and on restored bicycles. I would highly recommend this trip for anyone who wants a more authentic experience of Pomaire and would enjoy cruising around on a bike. We were a family of 5 (ranging in ages from 14 to 75) and the cycling was enjoyable.

Despite the fact that the Geysers del Tatio is amongst the largest fields worlwide (by number of geysers) but the eruption hight is, my guess, a few cm to probably 1 m and thus no comparison to the geysers e.g. in Yellowstone NP. However the drive to the Geysers del Tatio (ca. 80 km oneway) is spectacular and offers breathtaking views (see enclosed pictures) together with a superb driving experience. There are two alternate routes to the Geysers del Tatio allowing for a nice 'round-trip'. We rented our car at Calama airport and we also stayed at the Calama Hilton (Calama has a superb infrastructure when compared with other destinations in the area with a easy handycap of an additional 1 hour drive e.g. to San Pedro de Atacama).

review_text: My wife and I visit Neyen during a two week wine and food adventure through south america. We visited first thing in the morning and got a nice tour through the facility and the vines. There very old vines in conjunction with a few techniques they are using made for very good wine (grafting, no irrigation, non traditional trellising, etc.). We tasted through a a few years of Neyen's signature wine (a blend of Carmenere and Cabernet) and we were very impressed. This is a complex signature wine that can be very unique year to year. I know may manufacturers strive to make a wine that is consistent, sometime to a fault. At Neyen it seems like they strive to make a great wine that expresses the terroir of the place the climate that year.

review_text: This winery is absolutely beautiful, especially in the fall, when you can see all the amazing colors of the vineyard. The winery is over 100 years old and it shows - all of the buildings are amazingly well preserved and everything can be summed up as picturesque. We had a delicious lunch at the cafe (cheaper and simpler compared to the restaurant) and enjoyed the view and the afternoon sun until our carriage tour started. I was originally skeptical of the carriage ride, but it was a great way to take it all in. Our guides were very engaging and entertaining. Before finishing the tour with the tasting, we were shown the vats full of wine and were given small samples of wine that still has a few months left to go before it's ready to be bottled. I thought that was especially interesting, as I know very little about wine and it was the easiest way to demonstrate when wine is 'ready'. The tasting was in a large hall and we were given as much time as we wanted to be able to enjoy the four (large) samples we were given. Delicious!

review_text: Our cruise line only offered a transfer from the San Antonia cruise port to the Santiago airport. As we wanted to stay 2 nights in Santiago and see the sites before we returned home, we booked a private transfer with Chilitours to see the surrounding area. The transfer to our hotel in Santiago would be at the end of a wonderful full day tour. The owner, Carola, met us at the San Antonio cruise terminal with a large SUV. Normally, the Chilitours guide is also the driver. However, on this occasion, Carola was accompanied by Camilo, our driver for the day. Carola offers much insight into Chile, with a great knowledge of Chilean history and culture. We toured the port city of Valparaiso, which included a funicular ride to the top of one of the many hills, giving us a spectacular view of the city.She even provided us with the small change necessary for the restrooms in the city. We stopped for lunch at a small winery restaurant which appeared to be a favorite with the local residents. We asked if we could visit some beach resorts, so Carola brought us to some outstanding beach communities, which were really beautiful. We were dropped off at our Santiago hotel late afternoon after a wonderful day. The next morning, Carola picked us up, again with our driver, Camilo, for a ½ day tour of Santiago. Santiago is a very big city, but it was easy to see so many of the city highlights with our private car and tour guide. We highly recommend Chilitours for a wonderful personalized tour. I can whole heartedly recommend doing at least 1 if not 2 tours with these great guides ! This is a great deal !

review_text: Knowing that a friend and I would be spending 2 weeks in Santiago in early May, and not wanting to rent/drive a car, I arranged for three different day-tours to visit the Andes, and the countryside surrounding Santiago (mostly the wine areas). My daughter, who was working in Santiago at the time, also joined us on two of the tours. The Ecochile tours were the lest expensive I could find on line--and in retrospect I can't imagine more fun and value for the money. Our guides were terrific: youthful, personable, knowledgeable, with a sense of humor and great English skills--and very good drivers (my only complaint is that the windows in all the cars/vans we traveled in were horribly dirty--which made it difficult to appreciate the views afforded by the road-trips). They were also experts in Chile in general, and in the areas we covered in particular. We all really appreciated the informality of the tours, and the way our guides customize each on a moments notice. One day we went to the Casablanca Valley--where we visited a great winery (Emiliana) and also Valparaiso--where we had a blast photographing all the graffiti murals and riding the funicular rails. Another day we visited the Aconcagua Valley and two very special wineries (San Esteban and Vina Sanchez de Loria)--the latter one of which our guide arranged a VIP visit with the owner. In between the vineyard visits we visited the Paidahuen Archaelogical park to see some petroglyphs, after which we had lunch at an obscure, but lovely, family restaurant (Casa- E-Campo). The piece de resistance was our final tour, a visit to a glacier and a hot-springs in the Andes---simply outstanding in every respect, and very memorable. Check it out here: https://picasaweb.google.com/113422600749141609489/VisitToElMoradoGlacierOutsideOfSantiagoChile# If you are visiting Santiago, and you want to see some of the surrounding areas, but you don't want to drive, you can't go wrong with Ecochile tours (as guides, ask for Guillermo, Heni and/or Joaquin). Also, since we booked late in the year (May)--we were, for the most part, the only ones on the tours (the exception was our visit to the Aconcagua valley during which we were paired with a lovely couple from Mexico who were also interested in wineries).

In between the vineyard visits we visited the Paidahuen Archaelogical park to see some petroglyphs, after which we had lunch at an obscure, but lovely, family restaurant (Casa- E-Campo). The piece de resistance was our final tour, a visit to a glacier and a hot-springs in the Andes---simply outstanding in every respect, and very memorable. Check it out here: https://picasaweb.google.com/113422600749141609489/VisitToElMoradoGlacierOutsideOfSantiagoChile# If you are visiting Santiago, and you want to see some of the surrounding areas, but you don't want to drive, you can't go wrong with Ecochile tours (as guides, ask for Guillermo, Heni and/or Joaquin). Also, since we booked late in the year (May)--we were, for the most part, the only ones on the tours (the exception was our visit to the Aconcagua valley during which we were paired with a lovely couple from Mexico who were also interested in wineries).

review_text: This was the most fantastical, romantic, spectacular, well-informed, charming, entertaining, educational and lovely evening imaginable. To say Jorge is an enthusiastic astronomer would be a gross understatement. He is knowledgeable and excited about astronomy - like a little kid, but with more than a dozen amazing telescopes and a beautiful space from which to observe the skies. It's chilly in the evening. Jorge provides super comfy chairs what allow you to lie back and watch the sky...and shooting stars! He provides a wall of heaters, cozy blankets and hot coffee, tea and hot chocolate. During a break in the middle of program, his assistant puts out a lovely spread of sandwiches, sweets and other snacks. Jorge delights in the history of astronomy, and is so well informed. He is able to identify and point out the constellations with the use of a pretty amazing laser. Within only the first few minutes, Jorge knows your name...and remembers it! (I marveled at this, and it made us all feel more like friends than strangers.) Jorge picks you at your lodge or hotel, and brings you back. For us, the really cool thing was that there was a full moon that night, and we were able to stay with Jorge for hours beyond the standard star gazing program so that we could witness the moonrise. It was spectacular. It's only because Jorge is such an enthusiastic astronomer that all regard for time was ignored, and we were treated to something absolutely majestic. I can't imagine any other star gazing tour being as good as this. I couldn't recommend it more.

review_text: I bought the night tour via the CKOI hotel at this agency. The agency informed the hotel that it could do two tours on the same day, one at 4pm and the other at 8pm. I bought both tours and the first one was delayed. It was supposed to arrive at 6pm and it arrived almost 7pm. I had about an hour to walk 1.5 km, shower, eat and walk another about 1 km to catch the second ride. Obviously I couldn't. I tried to warn without success, as it was already night. When buying the tour I didn't know it was the Feel agency and unfortunately fate made me go to that place - which I don't recommend - and I bought the tour I missed together with a friend, Rodrigo. Photos of the tour are included in the price. It took a maximum of 3 days for the photos to arrive. Going for 6 days and no photos. The person responsible for the agency does not respond to me. My friend, who is still in São Pedro today, went to the agency and the attendant mentioned a possible delay. Questions: Why wasn't I notified of the delay? I sent a WhatsApp message almost 48 years ago and they haven't responded. They took me out of the group. In other words, two customers without photos of the tour. It doesn't stop there: the night tour guide was rude, rude, arrogant, impatient. The driver was also rude and mistreated Rodrigo. I do not recommend this agency. And I'm still waiting for my photos and Rodrigo's. In short, I don't recommend it: there are infinitely better agencies!

review_text: We had an excellent afternoon rafting with the folks from Chilean Adventures at the end of December. Thankfully they were able to accommodate our reservation request, which was made rather last minute, through the host at our lodge (Mapuyampay). The outfitter is located at the beautifully located Los Quenes River Lodge & Cabanas. The owner's dad was there to greet us when we were arrived, and he was super friendly and explained everything we needed to know. All of the gear was provided, which was of high quality and we appreciated that the wet suits were dry. Our guide on the river was excellent and provided all the directions we needed for paddling and safety. We had two Chilean's in the boat, and the two of us, along with our guide. Our guide was able to switch between English and Spanish and made sure everyone was having a good time. I appreciated that he pointed out specific sights along the way, as well as birds and other wildlife. We were the only raft on the river and pretty much surrounded only by nature for over a hour. The views are breathtaking and the rapids are excellent. Don't hesitate to book a trip with this outfitter, you won't regret it. We are so glad you had a good trip. We value our Mapuyampay customers just as much as our own. Best regards!

review_text: The W Trek through Torres del Paine is probably one of the most well-known trails in Chile. And for good reason - on a good day you can get fantastic views of the towers from multiple miradors (lookout points) along the trail. But when the weather gets bleak, it’s a different picture: wind gusts up to 70km/h on the W, even stronger on the O; incessant rains that go on for hours; trails that exist one day but are flooded the next day; and generally no view to speak of other than lots of water, rocks and mud. We did get good days at the base of the towers and at Mirador Britanico, where one typically finds the best views in the park. But the route was tough, especially when we planned a route that allowed us to stay in refugios every night - 1 night in Chileno, 2 in Cuernos, 1 in Grey and 1 in Paine Grande. Because it’s a W, there are also sections that require backtracking on the same day/previous day’s walking. Fortunately the campsites are often ok with hikers leaving their packs, turning steep climbs like those from Chileno and Campamento Italiano (in the middle section of the W) into day pack hikes. Even then, the terrain while not technically difficult remains rocky and hazardous to any careless steps. Glacier Grey is another wildcard - we were lucky in a sense that the kayak trip to the glacier was cancelled due to winds and replaced with a motorboat trip that took us further out with much less effort. Global warming is causing the glacier to recede so if another calving of the glacier happens things may be very different in a couple of years. That said, we got lucky with 2.5 good days of weather out of 5. The views justified the effort but as with all activities involving the weather in Patagonia, it’s all up to luck. Those that completed the O circuit bumped into more wildlife (pumas especially) - the W seemed pretty tame. Do note that the rangers are now extremely strict about visitor policies and that winging it with no bookings even for campsites is no longer allowed, and entry for more than 1 day will be denied if you don’t have reservations for accommodation. Makes things a little tougher given the weather does change plans but that’s the price to pay.

review_text: When planning our vacation to Chile, I wanted to see as much as possible in the five days we had. I found Thomas on Trip Advisor and booked him for our five day visit, six months before we came to Chile. We had three days of wine tours with Thomas. We spent one day in the Casablanca Valley doing wine tastings at Kingston Vineyards and Bodegas Vineyards. We then spent two days in the Colchagua Valley doing wine tasting at Vina Viu Manent, Vina Lapsotolle, and Vina Montgras where we also did a blind taste test. My husband and I really enjoyed the wine tours. I wasn’t sure which wineries to visit and Thomas came up with some wonderful suggestions. We dined at some of the vineyards and some of Thomas' favorite restaurants which were all gastronomically delicious! Our additional two days were tours of Valparaiso, Vina Del Mar, and Santiago. WOW! What a beautiful country! We gained a broad perspective of the key geographical areas together with the history, politics, personalities & passions that color all the areas that we visited. Thomas is a wonderful guide, and tailored our five day itinerary perfectly. I recommend Thomas 100%. As others have mentioned already, Thomas is well worth the price! You will not regret it! Thank you Thomas for the wonderful fun times we had with you, and our pictures of Chile will always bring back wonderful memories!

review_text: The hotel itself is OK. The casino is small by Las Vegas or Macau standards but the view of the rooms to the ocean is outstanding. The prices for the room as way higher than what you would pay in Las Vegas and hard to justify. The casino has many of the same games you find in North American casinos, except the betting is in pesos. However, the conversion is pretty easy (about 520 pesos to a US dollar) and so the penny, nickel and quarter slots and videos are easy to figure out. 10,000 pesos is the equivalent to about $20 US. The restaurants on the second floor are really good for Chilean standards. The pisco sours are great, the pizza is some of the best I have had in Chile and the sushi is good and safe to eat (I am careful eating sushi in Chile as I am not sure how they store the raw fish. As well, the penalty re heath violations are not as severe as they are in North America).

review_text: We had a fantastic experience with Chef Carolina. We visited in the low season so we were lucky to have a completely private class, just the two of us. We were able to choose the recipes we wanted to make, then went to the market with Carolina to buy all the ingredients fresh, which was an experience in itself. She was able to judge our competency in the kitchen and help out where needed or leave us to get on with parts we felt confident about. We made pebre (still the best we have tasted in Chile), starter, main and dessert as well as empanadas and ate it all with pisco sours and wine to wash it down! Whatever level of cook you are, I highly recommend it.

review_text: myself and several friends all turned 50 this year, and one of them came up with the brilliant idea of hiking the w trek as a celebration. we booked a full room and board trip thru Patagonia Trails. Maria was great and took care of everything. we were here early oct. 2014. so the park had only been open 2 weeks. the refugios were still getting opened up, and having work done on them. but it was not crowded at all, which was great. our bus driver told us that when the season gets rolling (nov-feb) that there can be lines of trekkers going up each valley. the first thing we noticed was the fresh air. it smelled like sage and rosemary from everything greening up and starting to bloom. I see a debate online about which way is better to go, start from the east or west. my two cents would be start from the east (refugio torre central). my reasoning is that the hike to the Torres del Paine was the longest and most strenuous of the 4 hikes. so if you do that first on fresh legs, the next day across to los cuernos refugio is a good recovery day. I haven't ever been a big hiking person, but am in reasonable shape. I did not find any of the hikes too difficult. and the scenery you get to see is awe inspiring. we got to see several avalanches in the French valley, and a chunk of ice break off from the ice at glacier grey. bonuses to the natural scenery that abounds. trekking poles are really helpful (we debated this before going). go here and enjoy !!

review_text: Turistik hop on hop off bus stop right at the base of Cerro San Cristóbal Hill. The main attraction is to take the funicular to the top. On its summit there is a sanctuary dedicated to the Immaculate Conception, with a ~ 70 feet statue of the Blessed Virgin Mary, an amphitheater and a chapel. Within the pedestal there is a small chapel in which Pope John Paul II prayed and blessed the city of Santiago on April 1, 1987. We purchased the round trip funicular option, so we could save time to move on to other sightseeing. If you have time, we would certainly recommend you walk down. The view to the city on a sunny day is very rewarding! The day we arrived, the funicular operation started at 1 pm. We walked over to Patio Bellavista area for lunch. Not sure where the operating hours information would be available. Definitely plan your day accordingly.

review_text: Hi, I want to write commenting that there are some moments in life that are super important. Last Saturday was my bachelorette party, and my best friends, sisters-in-law decided to take me to candelaria. We arrived 30 minutes early and followed the prompts of Guard Cristian, who instructed us to line up and that no matter if we arrived ahead at 12:01, we would be honored for the list of my hen party, given that he was going to make a cut in line when it was 12. We followed his instructions, and we went to warn him when we saw that a lot of people were sneaking in, among this group 2 more hen parties... the result. Don’t give us the list, I go and ask Cristian to help me comment on the door where he made the cut and that he witnesses that we had been following the rules for a long time. Christian makes me the stranger, at the door they tell me that he is no one and that he is not worth anything he has told me. I come back and the guy at the door says it’s going to be “good” and I won’t pay, but all my friends will. My friends (who had already paid for all of the above from my hen party, and who had kept to invite me inside) could not all stay, and they give me the hard time of life on one of the most important days of my life. I don't want compensation. I'm not really interested in going again. But as a professional I find it unusual that you do not have proper control of the entrance, that you do not follow your own rules, that your own staff does not know each other. And they are terrible mistakes if they want to position themselves as a discotheque for a public that is not just out of school, that looks for an orderly place to go and consume once in the thousands, for all the responsibilities that they have, and that moreover chooses them to spend such an important moment. And to top it off, they have no channel to leave a claim.

review_text: We couldn't stay away from this charming shop! We returned three times to continue buying more. The owner (Patricia) and her friend hand make almost all of the items offered at the shop with local wool - sheep and alpaca. There are hand-knitted wearable items - beanies, sweaters, muffs, etc., as well as for the home, such as wall hangings, mobiles, ornaments. Everything is tasteful and of high quality. Patricia knits as she tells you about her passion for handiwork - she has an incredible eye for color and design. And if you don't buy an item the first time you see it, you may be disappointed to find it already sold when you return (as we did). This exquisite shop is a must-visit location when in Puerto Natalas. Prepare to shop with a smile on your face!

review_text: I met Jorge on June 7th 2015, with a lovely couple from Holland. I knew I wanted to see the stars in the desert, a dream I have had for a long time! After reading the reviews about Jorge, I decided to spend the extra money and book with him, and oh my was it worth it!!! Jorge is incredibly knowledgable and passionate, invigorating us all with the same excitement he shares for the cosmos and beyond. I loved learning about the Andean cosmology, learning how to navigate the skies above and a bit of history about the subject. Then we were greeted by his lovely wife Norma, who served us the most delicious hot chocolate and snacks. There is something so special about sharing this moment in pitch black, with strangers who feel like friends in an instant. As we sipped our hot chocolates, we began looking through telescopes at various stars, clusters, a lazies, nebula, planets and more! I could sit here and describe everything, but the moment was such special one, that without experiencing it, my explanations means nothing! With every new image to discover, Jorge was more passionate and knowledgable, seeming to be the encyclopaedia of the southern sky. We finished with the rising moon, which was nearly full still, lighting up the desert as if it were daylight. I cannot sing Jorge's praises enough!!! If this is something you want to do, it is worth spending the extra money to have it done right, by someone who will treat you as family. I heard about other tours, offering 2x telescope for 30 people... our group of 3 had access to 10 telescopes AND we were taught how to use them. Top quality. I would do this over and over again... it is a MUST!!! P.S. viewing the Milky Way is a moment that you will never forget... pure bliss and breath taking! Thanks Jorge! review_text: We visited this museum on a weekday, and admission was free. It's a rather samll museum, with exhibits on two floors, most from the colonial period until Pinochet. I had expected a rather large exhibit of the War of the Pacific, but surprisingly, there was very little, and just as well. The museum mostly contains artefacts from the periods mentioned plus a few models, such as of a typical hacienda, and a lot of paintings, some of which would not be interesting to the foreign visitor. Thye section on Allende and Pinochet was perhaps the most political, but even so there was very little commentary, just photos, newspaper facsimiles, and other historical items which allowed the visitor to make up his own mind. Centrally located on the north part of the Plaza de Armas. No English explanations.

review_text: Rodrigo and his team at Escuela Soul Surf are first rate! They took such good care of our family with young children that we decided to host our daughter’s birthday there, and the kids had an unforgettable experience. The parents were also impressed. The instructors are very hands-on, and not a single kid that got in the water to surf came away upset or fearful. And only 1 of them had ever surfed before! The atmosphere is laid back and you could easily spend hours of leisure here. The restaurant serves up artisanal pizzas and empanadas, and the second floor terrace has tables with spectacular panoramic views of the main road into Concón and the beach, a ping pong table, a rock-climbing wall, music, and a jacuzzi. There’s also a well-equipped store with surfing gear on the first floor. As if this weren’t enough, the owner Rodrigo has a tremendous heart for people and social justice. He may not advertise it, but he often gives away surf classes to groups of disabled kids and adults, some coming regularly from Santiago. If you’re looking to learn to surf, have a relaxing time with good food and atmosphere, or support a place that’s giving back to its community, this is it! review_text: I (30) can't begin to describe the amazing experience that I shared with my father (72). This was the highlight of an incredible 3 week trip to south america, which included many once in a lifetime experiences, including rappelling into an ice cave, puma tracking and seeing puma cubs in torres del paine, and doing some incredible hike and flies with my paraglider. The knowledge, enthusiasm , and fun spirit of the crew is incredible. And they work very hard to ensure you are comfortable and having a great time. The food was great and always more than enough, with plenty of drinks like coffee and pisco sours. The amount of wildlife we saw was unending. Humpback, sei whales, dolphins, seals , sea lions, fox, penguins, cormorant, and many other birds. Taking the boat each day had new adventures with magnificent glaciers and other-worldy terrain surrounding, abundant life. Pictures and videos really can't begin to do justice, but there were plenty opportunity for great photos for those interested. While it may seem expensive at first glance, my dad and I both considered it a bargain for the experience and service we received. Our dome was perfect and cozy and fed by a cute fireplace. It had a great view and is one of the most memorable places we have ever stayed. PS I recommend starting your morning with a cold plunge with the crew. Thanks again to Paula, Andres, Simon, and Miguel for this amazing experience that I feel lucky to have shared with my dad Sam and John (Also thanks to rest of the crew who i forgot learn their names but worked behind the scenes to help make it happen)

review_text: Two weeks hiking in northern Patagonia with a National Geographic group tour, we were told this was going to be our most strenuous hike and they did not lie. The path is very well maintained but the slope is so steep that we all struggled. I think I may have been able to make it to the top if I could have gone slower but since we were with a group I had to turn back when the back half of the group decided they couldn't make it anymore and I couldn't keep up with the front half of the group. The front half of our group made it up but all agreed that it was very hard and they were regular hikers. I struggled with catching my breath on the way up but had no problems coming back down. Older people with knee problems struggled coming back down but had no problem going up. The view was okay but not nearly as spectacular as I had seen on other hikes in Bariloche, Puerto Varas, or Futaleufu. On the way back down, I took my time and focused on the nature around me and appreciated and photographed the vast variety of flora. There are very clean bathrooms at the base but bring your own toilet paper. Our group had a picnic spread set up for us when we came back down, which was nice. This trail was the only trail where we encountered other hikers, and many other hikers going in both directions. There is plenty of room on the path to allow others to pass and we saw lots of young kids. It was neat to be able to see the steam rising up from the volcano.

review_text: A couple of weeks ago I booked a tour to Laguna del Inca alone and everything during the tour went ok until I arrived back to my hotel and I had a message in my phone number from someone related to the company asking for my telegram and saying that he was "an admirer". If you are travelling alone and, specially if you are women, think twice before booking with them!! :) Review of: Portillo and Laguna del Inca Tour The company will never have this type of attitude, in fact, passenger data is only recorded by the administration and the guide so that they can communicate with the passenger at the time of the pick-up. We identified that the number spoken to the passenger did not have access to your number, as it is not part of our system that gives access to numbers and, speaking to the guide, we verified via the company's phone that the number was not forwarded to anyone. We have no way of knowing the communications between passengers and employees throughout the day, your number was passed between people in another way. In fact, your tour was on the 16th and you sent us a message complaining almost 10 days later. Why didn't you send it at the time? Likewise, I understand your frustration, but coming here to accuse us of insecurity because of a message that was not sent by us is a bit exaggerated.

The poor guide had to work an hour underneath the car to fix the problem temporarily so we could reach the nearby hotel. We waited two hours total in the cold in the car as well 👍 Second day : our first guide had to drive the car back to Uyuni to fix it so they sent another guide with another car. The day went superb, the salt hotel at the end was great but the next morning at 4am everybody was feeling sick, diarrhea, nausea, etc. We all got very bad FOOD POISONING from either the food from lunch or dinner. Even the guide was sick ! And that's super rare because they cope woth the germs in the food. This one must have been super toxic. We couldn't do the Salar that day so we spent it at the hotel. 39° of worst fever ever, shivering, feeling super weak. We had to go to the nearby clinic to get antibiotics. No apologies from the company whatsoever. This is us who had to tell them that we couldn't do the salar, we had to arrange everything. That night we asked for another bottle of water at the hotel (which is run by Cruz Andina) and we had to pay for it even though we barely ate anything. No favours were given to us. 4th day : another guide came because the 2nd one was still sick (Joke right ?) The third guide was useless, no info, not talking if we asked him for something. Not helping us at the Salar for the perspective photos. We were given basically the worst of the worst. So let me tell you that this "premium" tour was our worst experience in Bolivia. Most of all the reaction of the company and the lack of communication as usual in Bolivia 👎 We had to fight to get a private room the last day for instance. So many bad little things on this tour. Lucky we had a great group so we could support each other !

review_text: The start was as bad as it could get: the taxi driver who brought us to Aruco Park (starting point of the tour to Undurraga Vinery) said to us: Ahh Undurraga, that is vinery fast food for tourists in a hustle... The drive with the (sold out!) bus of Turistik was OK, the guy giving good background explanations about Chilean wine industry. On the estate we joined a small group guided by young guide Javier. The group resulted to be composed by wine amateurs, including ourselves (my partner's parents were wine producers, I have participated myself to several harvests and hand-bottling of family wine in the Mosel region in Germany). Hence the questions were "good, substantial ones". And Javier mastered with sound answers based on solid knowledge and spiced with wit, fully satisfying our curiosity. The Undurraga estate is beautiful -- a massive stately mansion, large fields, beautiful garden. In my memories to date, palms, bouganviles and other tropical/subtropical plants did not go with vitis vinifera. At Undurraga they beautifuly harmonise together. The cellar and industrial processing and bottling areas are impressing. There is "museum" showing a collection mapuche items, masks, jewels, totems, telling a bit of the history of this Chilean native people. The exposition was better and more interesting than expected. The wine tasting was OK, no wine I would die for. The history however of prize winning wines from Undurriaga is impressive. The history is well presented in the shop room. Sure, to get back to my taxi driver, I would also prefer to drive myself to a small vinery down in the valley and stay two days there. But reality was that I had no time for doing that (I gave priority to Torres del Paine and Chiloé). Hence: Undurriaga was a great compromise!

review_text: We had an unforgettable experience with Sorbac. We stayed in their hostel and did tours with them for a little over a week and it was a really sweet time. We made our choice to stay with them solely based on the great reviews they had (kinda skeptical bc they sounded too good to be true) but they still surpassed our expectations. The places we visited were beauuuuuuuuuutiful and it was such a fun time. They also rent out bikes, and so we did that one day and it was so so fun. Also, the hostel is super close to the Pukará de Quitor which has a surprisingly beautiful view if you hike up it. Overall, our time there was so special and Sorbac ended up finding its way into our hearts, which neither of us were expecting. I think the distinguishing aspect of Sorbac is that they put people first and good business seems to be a happy side effect. Can't recommend them enough!

review_text: General comments about logistics and refugios we stayed or saw along the way. >WATER: Delicious, safe, plentiful. Drank from springs everywhere over 5 days, non filtered. >PASSPORT: Must have with you! And PDI!! (If you lost your pdi, get a dupe at police station in Puerto Natales police station by the plaza) >SLEEPING: Reservations are a must but the weather does force the refugios and campgrounds to be accommodative. We did hear of people getting beds without reservations due to closures and we did upgrade to beds at different places. If you have beds and bedding reserved, you do not need pads or sleeping bags. All bedding/camping bags were very clean. >TREK INFO: Surprisingly, misinformation from hostels is common (wrong bus times, wrong fees, etc). The Erratic Rock Hostel folks give an excellent 1.5 hour talk at the Zero Day store at 3 pm daily. Gets crowded. Arrive early for a seat or stand. >PARK ENTRANCE FEE: 21000 CLP. Fees keep going up so check for latest info on arrival. Can be paid by credit card (vs cash only at the Laguna Amarga entrance) at bus station but does NOT save you time as you still have to wait for everyone on your bus to fill out form, watch a 2 minute video before leaving for Catamaran. Also, they did not check papers for our refugio reservations. They just asked verbally. >BUS FROM PUERTO NATALES: 15000 CLP round trip. Buy at the bus station the day before. Multiple companies but same price and they all have a 7 am option. Some take CC. All are non assigned seats. Don’t panic if the bus looks full, they will just put you in another one. >CATAMARAN: 23000 CLP (cash only!!!). After Laguna Amarga check in, load back up on the same bus for 30 minute drive to catamaran which leaves at 11 am. Pay the guy on the boat. Backpacks go on a big pile in center. Upstairs open air and inside will be full but generally everyone arriving for the 11 am does get onboard (in unusual event it is full, supposedly they will make a second run). There is a small cafe there or better yet, do the short hike to the waterfall before the boat leaves. >SHUTTLE AND BUS BACK TO PUERTO NATALES: 3000 CLP for shuttle. Buses leave from Laguna Amarga at 2:30 and 7:30 pm, option you preselect assuming you bought a return ticket. To get to the bus, you can catch a 30 minute shuttle from the Welcome Center which is a 15 minute walk from Hotel Las Torres at the end of your hike. Has food, supplies and pay to use WIFI. There is also an earlier shuttle at 1 pm at this writing. REFUGIOS were pretty great in general considering the remote location. Some had better amenities than others but all offered unlimited hot water, access to bathrooms and accepted credit cards. Prices were high for beer (5000 CLP ~$6) and wine (19000 CLP ~$25 per bottle) but plentiful. Some like Cuernos had full bars.

review_text: Francisco and his spouse Connie provide outstanding service and a comfortable schedule of tastings at a variety of vineyards. Connie is fast to respond to my many questions with detailed follow up and email reminders. Francisco picked us up at our hotel and provided a good overview of the Colchuagua wine region. Wineries were still harvesting so our first stop at Mont Gras allowed us to see the grapes in bins being processed in their facility. Nice wine tasting outside and a good discount if you are interested in stocking up for your trip. We also visited Neyen, had lunch at the Viu Manent restaurant, Ventisquero (beautiful small tasting room high in the valley) and one added winery, Apaltagua. Francisco was very interested in what we wanted to see/do and stopped at a local shop so my wife could look forward Chilean gifts. He also dropped us at a nice Peruvian restaurant and even picked us up afterwards to return us to our remote hotel. The excellent service did not end there. The next morning they provided driving directions to Valparisio and suggested a stop for lunch at Matetic winery. Connie even called the winery and a table was awaiting us when we arrived. This is another beautiful winery in the Casablanca valley with a small lodge, gift shop, lovely grounds and fine restaurant. We could not have had a better experience and thoroughly enjoyed the service provided by Colchuagua Wine Tours

review_text: I have been trying to be more active and figured a hike in the Andes would be a great day trip from Santiago. I was worried that it would be too easy as it was less than 2 miles and I regularly walk about 4 miles/day, but with the altitude and terrain it was a perfect level of not too easy and not too hard. Sebastian was our guide and Ernesto was our driver and both were excellent. It was a changeable weather day - cloudy then sunny, then rain and a bit of snow! Sebastian made sure we were warm enough and felt secure on the hike, offering hats, gloves, pants and walking sticks. I especially loved the fact that he had a bird book! I love birds and am always frustrated not to know what they are when I am travelling. His book was in Spanish, but had the names in English. Ernesto was also very good at picking out the condors on the far horizon, as well as bringing up the rear on the hike to make sure we got down in one piece. I had a great time and also appreciated that it was a small group, 5 total including me. I had also emailed with Carol to help me decide which tour to book and she was very helpful and quick to respond. Everyone was great to work with and made the experience easy and enjoyable! Dear Sandra! Thanks a lot for your review. We are really happy to hear about Sebastian, but its not a surprise for us, he is a very good guide! Also thanks for mentioning our "backstage crew" WICH ARE AS IMPORTANT FOR US AS OUR GUIDES!!! Hope you had a great experience in Santiago!

review_text: We booked the trip up the volcona at Paredon, which was a great company to do this with. We arrived late at night the day before we went up, but in the next days the weather was about to turn bad so we really wanted to do this the next day. They got to our hostel late at night, giving us all information we needed. The next day we gathered at 6.30 in the morning and were provided with all necessary equipment (hiking boots, wind jacket, backpack, waterproof pants, helmet, icepick, crampons, slide, and handgloves). We only had to bring warm underclothes,food, sunglasses and sunscreen (very important!!) and money for the chairlift that takes you up the first 400 meters. Unfortunately the chairlift wasn't operating due to hard winds, so we had to walk all the way up which for us, as rather fit and experienced hikes, was pretty tough. The views were stunning however, and it felt very good to be in just a small group (6 people, and 2 guides), cause we saw others in very large groups. We felt very safe and our guides took everything very seriously. Downhill we slided mostly through the snow, which I found pretty scary cause it went very very fast, the weather already started to get worse so there were no views anymore and sometimes I had a hard time stopping myself. After the climb, we got to the Paredon office where we were treated with beers and popcorn, which was great. It was a fantastic and rewarding trip, but do not take it lightly!

review_text: We were very happy to find Turismo Laguna Azul was still running the full day tour to the King Penguin Reserve on Tierra del Fuego after our first tour operator had cancelled out. We were there in late October when protests and demonstrations were causing issues with road blocks and damage to the buildings around the square. Our hotel pick up was right on time, our guides/driver were friendly and informative, the scenery was stunning and the weather was gorgeous. We had a smooth sailing on the trip across the Straits to Porvenir where we stopped at the small museum and at a restaurant for a delicous bowl of King Crab stew. Arriving at Parque Pinguino Rey we heard a small talk from the staff and then walked on the boardwalks to the blind. There were about 25 penguins in various stages of molt and it was quite amazing to see their large size as compared to other penguins. This is not a close up view, so good camera with a zoom is recommended. Seeing the penguins was a once in a lifetime experience since they are not found in many locations! After the reserve, we saw a few other sites on Tierra del Fuego before going to another ferry landing and heading back to Punta Arenas. Five stars to Turismo Laguna Azul for this unforgettable day!

review_text: Concha y Toro is Chile's largest winemaker, responsible for brands that are well known in both Europe and North America. It offers regular tours in Spanish and English, although there are very tourist-oriented - don't expect to see any actual wine being produced. Start by checking out the website for an English language your - it's possible to make reservations, though not essential. Tours are not cheap (a lot more than in Mendoza, in Argentina, for example) but are well organised, showing some of the landscaped grounds, demonstration plots of the main grape varieties grown by the company, and then - what everyone is waiting for - decent samples of three of their wines. Before the third tasting you are led into the Casillero del Diablo (after which their largest selling wine in named) and given a rather corny sound and light show. Still, it's all good fun, and at the end you are allowed to keep the tasting glass (in reality a large and quite robust wine glass). Not recommended for families, but fun for anyone who's not a teetotaller! Advice - it's easy to take a bus from the end of the metro to the winery - most Southbound buses towards El Pirque go there (some include the destination in the window) and they take cash, not the bip! card. Get off at the Shell petrol station and walk around the corner to the right where the main entrance is.

The walks we did, particularly to Grey Lake and the glaciers (where the rain & sleet came horizontally at us), through the forests and going to see the condors, showed the majesty of the National Park, but the Torres never revealed themselves. Can only award three stars because of the weather, and for what we could see, just bitterly disappointed. ...but thank heavens we spent a lot on getting quality gear and taking an extra suitcase......

review_text: What they asked: Have you ever ridden a horse? What they should have asked: Would you perhaps feel a bit queasy if we put you on a horse that is navigating a 10" gravel path in the mountains with nothing between you and the river 3000 feet below? It was a great experience but not for the faint of heart. Certainly not something I would take my family on. If you are afraid of heights, I do not recommend this outing. If you are a thrill seeker, this is a trip of a lifetime. I will say, that the owners were very responsive to my last minute request and everything was organized flawlessly. I am sorry that you were made nervous by this ride. The problem is that riding in the mountains involves some steep inclines. Some other people have been a little surprised by the terrain as although the path is good it goes along the top edge of a valley with a steep slope, covered with bushes, between you and the river about 400 metres below (not 3000 feet although it might feel like that!). Most people enjoy it but it is not suitable for people who suffer from vertigo. I will change the text which we send out describing the ride to make it clear that we go up into the mountains along narrow paths. If the path had been a track wide enough for cars I do not think you would have felt at all nervous. But there are bushes all alongside so it would be impossible to fall down the slope even if our sure-footed horses, born and bred in the higher mountains, were to make a mistake and stumble. I am sorry that the ride was not what you expected and will try to be clearer in future. I must just add that we often take families with small children (including my 5 year-old granddaughter) as it is one of our safest rides.

review_text: This valley sits east of the narrow waist of Chile and is home to a number of astronomical observatories - our main reason for visiting this part of the country. We came by cruise ship to Coquimbo and we were very lucky to have rare seats off the ship to visit this area in the mountainous region - book on the ship asap as guests numbers are limited inside these observatories. The other main drawcard is wine located around the Elqui River which supplies the lifeblood of irrigation for vines and fruit growing areas - also at the southern end of the Atacama Desert. Once leaving this fertile strip of valley, the starkness of the mountains is very evident - their famous Pisco is made from fruits grown in the valley but each South American country lays claim for the best Pisco! Vicuna is the main town of the region with a few historical buildings, a couple of good restaurants and some decent souvenir shops. It's a small town centre and easy to walk around but it can be hot during the summer months without sea breezes. We loved the observatories and the views that go on forever up there. Enjoy your experience!

When we arrived at the memorial of the former president Allende we sat down and she gave us her personal view of the historical events of Pinochet's dictatorship and we had the possibility of asking questions. A really nice way to tackle a sensitive subject in the Chilean society. We ended the tour at a local bar where we tasted the local Chilean drink called Terremoto. Since the tipping is voluntary the amounts differs but we gave 10.000 pesos and had our budget allowed it we would gladly have given more. review_text: Great experience. We hiked east to west and stayed at a mix of camping and Refugio’s at Grey, then Paine Grande, Cuernos and Chileano. I booked on 8 June for a December trip and got spots at the best Refugio’s and campsites. - I paid for the Catamaran when boarding using cash. You can pre book prior. My partner and I are fit and in our late 20s. We did not find the trek challenging and considered this a very luxurious experience with hot coffee, hot meals and beers at the end of each day. review_text: My partner and I recently travelled with Turismo Selknam on a day trip from Punta Arenas to Tierra Del Fuego. The main attraction of any visit is to see the King Penguins in the Pinguino Rey colony, although this involves around 9 hours of travel so to break this up various other interesting (and less interesting) stops are added along the way. Note that these are KING penguins, not the Magdalen penguins which are on offer at the nearby colonies of Isla Magdalena and Seno Ottway. Having seen my fill of this subtype at Punto Tombo we wished for something different so signed up for this long but rewarding journey. This tour cost 48000CP + 12000CP (ticket to pinguino rey). This same tour is also provided by Turismo Laguna Azul, so if you can't get in with Turismo Selknam that's another equally well rated option. They follow the exact same itinerary and we literally crossed paths all day. Our guides name was Mario and he spoke fantastic English. He was able to give a terrific insight into the often dogged history of Tierra Del Fugo and this became obvious with his insightful guiding at the history museum in Porvenir. A typical tour begins with a 0730 pick up from the hotel. After a short drive you board the 0800 ferry and cross the Magdalena strait arriving at 1000 to Porvenir, the main town of Tierra Del Fuego (which has all of 700 inhabitants). You visit a very small park for around 15 minutes (not particularly interesting) before visiting the local museum which outlines the tragic history of the natives of Tierra Del Fuego and their eradication in the 1800's to make way for sheep production. 1130 is lunch (can buy at local bakery) before another 2.5 hours of driving to pinguino rey. The pinguino rey colony is quite small - consisting of around 200 birds, of which 100 are usually out at sea. You pay 12000CP for entry into a very makeshift area which allows you to view these creatures from behind rope at a distance of around 100m. This is undoubtingly the highlight of the trip. At 1600 you continue on but instead of tracing back the way you came (that ferry doesn't cross in the afternoon) you go North to another ferry which takes only 20 minutes to cross the strait. From here you visit a sheep ranch and desert ghost town on the way pack to Punta Arenas. You should arrive back at around 2100. Without stating the obvious this was a very long day. However, it was very satisfying too. I loved the penguins and the photos I have are awesome. In addition we got to cover all of the attractions of the Tierra Del Fuego in one day which was a great investment of time. review_text_preprocessed: My partner and I recently travelled with Turismo Selknam on a day trip from Punta Arenas to Tierra Del Fuego. The main attraction of any visit is to see the King Penguins in the Pinguino Rey colony, although this involves around 9 hours of travel so to break this up various other interesting (and less interesting) stops are added along the way. Note that these are KING penguins, not the Magdalen penguins which are on offer at the nearby colonies of Isla Magdalena and Seno Ottway. Having seen my fill of this subtype at Punto Tombo we wished for something different so signed up for this long but rewarding journey. This tour cost 48000CP + 12000CP (ticket to pinguino rey). This same tour is also provided by Turismo Laguna Azul, so if you can't get in with Turismo Selknam that's another equally well rated option. They follow the exact same itinerary and we literally crossed paths all day. Our guides name was Mario and he spoke fantastic English. He was able to give a terrific insight into the often dogged history of Tierra Del Fugo and this became obvious with his insightful guiding at the history museum in Porvenir. A typical tour begins with a 0730 pick up from the hotel. After a short drive you board the 0800 ferry and cross the Magdalena strait arriving at 1000 to Porvenir, the main town of Tierra Del Fuego (which has all of 700 inhabitants). You visit a very small park for around 15 minutes (not particularly interesting) before visiting the local museum which outlines the tragic history of the natives of Tierra Del Fuego and their eradication in the 1800's to make way for sheep production. 1130 is lunch (can buy at local bakery) before another 2.5 hours of driving to pinguino rey. The pinguino rey colony is quite small - consisting of around 200 birds, of which 100 are usually out at sea. You pay 12000CP for entry into a very makeshift area which allows you to view these creatures from behind rope at a distance of around 100m. This is undoubtingly the highlight of the trip. At 1600 you continue on but instead of tracing back the way you came (that ferry doesn't cross in the afternoon) you go North to another ferry which takes only 20 minutes to cross the strait. From here you visit a sheep ranch and desert ghost town on the way pack to Punta Arenas. You should arrive back at around 2100. Without stating the obvious this was a very long day. However, it was very satisfying too. I loved the penguins and the photos I have are awesome. In addition we got to cover all of the attractions of the Tierra Del Fuego in one day which was a great investment of time. The cost was cheaper than hiring a car and attempting to do this ourselves plus our experience was improved by the historical context added by our guide. The driving was certainly not a highlight but as long as you are prepared for this you'll be alright. It is very cold down here so dress in layers (layer up outside but strip down in the bus). Overall I would recommend this to others keen on seeing wild King Penguins.

review_text: The 4th largest urban parkland in the world certainly offers plenty to see and do. I spent 4-5 fantastic hours exploring the park and still didn't get to see everything. I decided to use the cable car, which has a couple of stops, as well, so I got a return ticket for both. Total cost was 4700 pesos (about $10AUD) which is excellent value. You can also start from the other end at Oasis cable car Station. Apart from the church and huge virgin Mary statue at the top of the Funicular at San Cristobal hill, there is a Japanese Garden, Zoological Garden, huge swimming pool with a cool story behind it, and just so much more. The views from San Cristobal and from the Cable car are breathtaking. A fantastic day out!

review_text: We walked in San Pedro and talked with many tour companies and it was Alabalti Atacama that we picked. It was Gloria that welcomed us and her empathy and good communication gave us the confidence to choose Alabalti. Not the cheapest price we got but just a few dollars more expensive. In the end we realize we were very lucky to book through this company because the service was excellent: safe drivers Winder and Franco, excellent guides Jimena, Joaquín and Hugo and very tasty snacks (including dried fruits, cheese, ham, chips, biscuits, juices, wine and their one pisco sour with rica rica). We did 3 short tours: swimming and floating in the lovely Laguna Cejar (this company makes sure to choose the slots when the lagoon is less crowded), the astronomic tour with sky observation (they have a partnership with a company that only do Astronomic Tours) and the cherry on the top of the cake was the Archeological Tour with Hugo. This last tour is a very complete tour and a must if you want to contextualize the history of the pré-colombian civilizations that were able to adapt to the harsh living conditions in the Atacama desert more than 9000 years ago. In the end, it is not about the landscapes that you see (or paying a few less dollars) but the service that you get. Our guides were very good! Ask Hugo for the Archelogical Tour and you will have a lovely day of history with the similar landscapes from the Valle of La Luna and Vallecito. Review of: Puritama Hot Springs, San Pedro de Atacama

If you want a meal there are small restaurants at the end of the market as well. Parking is difficult, but there are cabs available.

review_text: We travelled on the December 6-13, 2021 Classic Antarctica trip on Magellan Explorer, during the pandemic. We flew to Antarctica on Day 1 of the itinerary because it was not clear if we could fly as scheduled on Day 2. That created a bit of a commotion, also because a group of passengers in the end couldn't go due to one of their members testing positive for Covid during the pre-trip screening done by Antarctica21. After we left Punta Arenas for Antarctica, everything went very well. Being in Antarctica is wonderful, like a paradise. Magellan Explorer is in excellent condition and service is excellent. The food is very good, with a lot of variety. Excellent service in the dining room. The wines are very good and abundant. The gym is very good, as is the sauna. We had a barbecue dinner on the top deck and that was a hit, a very happy occasion for everyone. The landings and excursions were very good. The Expedition Team is excellent, very professional and well prepared. The zodiacs are impeccable. On the ship we enjoyed great presentations but we noticed that sometimes other guests seemed tired, which must have been a bit demotivating for the presenters. We didn’t see the officers much. As part of the Covid protocols, there was practically no contact with them. Our last day in Antarctica was a bit of challenge. There was some uncertainty on what to do with our luggage, when we would disembark, etc. Once we did disembark, we had to wait a long time in the open air before boarding the aircraft. It was windy and cold, with no shelter or bathroom. It was nothing compared with what early explorers experienced but any Antarctic traveler should be prepared for some discomfort. In the end, it was quickly forgotten and the good memories of a special trip is what remains.

review_text: As it looked as if it might rain we took the funicular up to the top (cost for a return on the weekend was CLP2,600). We had read that the funicular can get very crowded so we arrived at 9.45am, 15 minutes before it opened at 10.00am, and were on the first trip to the summit, stopping once to let some people out who were visiting the zoo. At the summit there are some very large terraces (and some tacky shops) where you can get great views of the city and the Andes, though unfortunately we could not see the latter due to the smog and low hanging clouds. A further 183 stairs took you from these terraces up to the base of the pedestal of the statue of the Sanctuary of the Immaculate Conception where the views of the city were even better, albeit we could still not see the Andes. There is a small chapel in the bottom of the pedestal that was closed off by glass. Overall the statue and the surrounding area was in need of a bit of a refurbishment and some paint which it might receive before the Pope’s visit in 2018. There were some good walking paths around the hill but we did not venture too far given that it was very cold and it looked as if it would rain. Recommended.

review_text: We found the Turistik hop on hop off bus to be an excellent way to gain an overview of Santiago. It takes about 2 hours to make the full circuit during which you can get an idea of where you might want to hop off. A few differences from other HoHo services: the ticket is for one day not 24 hours, so you need to get going by 9am; get organised by buying your tickets online and have the voucher on your phone rather than trying to find a bus and get a ticket. Until we did the circuit we found it difficult to identify where the stops were but once you have the map it’s easy, and a useful map. The staff (host and driver) were great - welcoming, friendly, cheerful and very knowledgeable and helpful. The bus was clean and comfortable and our driver was careful and considerate of folks getting on and off and negotiating steps. The audio system is the best we’ve experienced: you get a cellphone (hand back when you hop off then another when you hop back on) and earphones that replace the more usual ’plug into the back of the seat in front’. It works really well. review_text: I took the Hop On Hop Off bus tour today, Nov 2, in Santiago. I was looking forward to getting to know the city the through the usual excellent commentary I have experienced in other cities. Because of the recent riots, the routing has been modified, which is understandable. Sadly the whole historic area was skipped. What is even sadder is that the ear phones with multi lingual translations have been taken away , as the new routing does not match the old commentary. Instead, on the bus is a "guide" whose only job seemed to be to facilitate the tourists getting on and off the bus. There was one young man who, when asked, gave quite a good commentary in 2 languages to the 4 tourists on his bus. However on the other 2 buses I took, there was no commentary offered. The new routing goes to east part of the city and at its new stops there is not much to see or do. I paid extra to take the gondola up to a look out point and then a funicular down. Hop on Hop Off are still offering their shuttle to the start of the gondola but have eliminated a bus at the funicular station. So one has to walk quie a distance to get back on a bus after doing this gondola-funicular stop. I requested half my money back in recognition of an unsatisfactory day on the bus and was just given a run around. At the end of the day, I rode around on a bus on some nice streets but I got no sense of the city of Santiago. I have done these tours elsewhere with great satisfaction. I totally understand the changes that had to be made to the routing, but they have not adapted a new commentary of any sort. Until they go back to their old routes and commentary, or provide a new commentary to match the new routing, I suggest giving this tour a miss.. avoid disappointment. We stayed long after the buss loads of tourist left and that is when many of the local residents appeared. We saw foxes, vicuñas, different birds etc. none of them particularly shy. review_text: I had one full day in Puerto Varas and wasnt quite sure what to do. Once you re there you will quickly realise that there is quite a few things to do ... from biking to hiking to boat rides, full day trips to chiloe or the volcanoes or Puerto Peulla etc. I booked this particular trip because it sounded promising, offering a boat ride next to the volcanoes and hiking possibilities when you have your large break in the afternoon plus a bilingual guide for the whole day. I paid about 60 US Dollar for this. Here is what actually happened: The boat ride was very nice ... and thats it! The bilingual guide is a joke, cause when you re on the bus most of the time a recorded audio file does most of the talking, in different languages. And when the guide actually takes the microphone and speaks himself he is either doing some simple jokes or is trying to sell you tours. Cause that s really what it is ... a sales tour. If you start in Puerto Varas, you start at 8:30 with a bus ride of about 1 hour, on the way you make a bathroom break of 30 minutes at little waterfalls, that were not too impressive and for which you have to pay a little extra to actually see them. Then you continue to meet the boat. The boat ride is about 1:45 and goes through beautiful scenery. During the ride the guides will again try to sell you tours, anouncing it through the general speaker system several times. There is a whole cash counter inside the boat for the extra packages. The guides also prepare you for the fact that we are going to make a large break of roughly 4 hours in the small town of Peulla where there is no shopping and generally not much to do, EXCEPT for the extra tours that are being sold on the boat. These tours are for example horseback riding, a helicopter ride, or another little trip by bus and boat. We've been to Yellowstone and while these aren't as extensive or impressive they were certainly engaging and you can't beat the early dawn light at over 4,000 m above the sea! Our guides put a bag of fresh eggs into one of the boiling pools and we had fresh hard boiled eggs for breakfast. Delicious! Plus a couple of eggs in a pocket made for very good handyman handwarmers! Lots of people but still room to marvel and watch the vicunas and flamingos too. Highly recommended.

Pity, because the surrounds are stunningly beautiful.

review_text: Traveling with our family of 5 (kids aged 20, 17 and 9) we were limited to just 3 days in Patagonia. We had researched the area and what to do, and generally do everything ourselves. But this area seemed more complex to figure out : the weather is changeable, the condition of the roads is variable, it's not clear what the driving times are on unsealed roads. We also know our family dynamic, and with my wife and I as party leaders we can get around 3 hours attention from our kids before mutiny. We got in touch with Far South Expeditions and they customized a 3 day schedule. Claudio, our guide, and Jose, our driver, spotter and bouncer have spent decades living in this part of the world. They have a genuine infectious passion for the great outdoors and they can spot interesting wildlife you'll likely drive right by. On Day One, Claudio proved his worth by approaching a tree outside the Milodon caves and starting to chirp and call. Moments later we were surrounded by birds chattering back at him and swooping over our heads. He kept this up for 10 minutes as we laughed in disbelief. Claudio is Dr Doolittle. Torres del Paine was stunning, and if it had not been (due to the weather) I'm confident that Claudio and Jose would have worked out the best thing we could do under the circumstances. Under our own steam we would have kept our kids interested for 3 hours a day. Our Far South Expedition encompassed 12+ hour days on the go...but not at breakneck pace, and always with consideration for what we were up for. And we had chances to nap on the longer drives. We feel very fortunate to have met Claudio and Jose. Dear Paul, Thanks very much for your kind response and comments. We feel quite honored that you and your family decided to come to explore Patagonia using our company. We are passionate to show our guests, and especially young people, the natural wonders of this dramatic and scenic part of the world. It was wonderful to see the true interest that all your family members showed to the peculiar wildlife and rugged scenery of the 'ends of the world'; it was very inspiring and encouraging to share the road with you all. Until we meet again! The Far South Expeditions team.

review_text: The Valley of the Moon is only a short drive outside San Pedro de Atacama. The road to the park is sealed and roads inside the park a mix of sealed and unsealed. There is parking near the major viewpoints and walks, and bathrooms available. Access inside the park is restricted and you can only walk on the marked paths. We went on a summer afternoon and it was very hot and crowded. Hats, sunscreen and plenty of water required. We didn’t enjoy the hike through the salt cave as it was dark, narrow and cramped in places so you had to walk almost bent double and use a cell phone or torch for light to see where you were going. It was also very rocky and tough going, unsuitable for anyone with fitness or mobility issues. There was a lovely view from the top though. We also climbed a large dune for the view from the top, saw the Three Maries which was interesting. We then drove to nearby Death Valley for sunset. Again big crowds but the colour of the rocks at the sunset was quite lovely.

review_text: The rafting experience is wonderful, worth it for the views, for the contact with nature and for the very experience of coming down a river with good rapids.; but the tourist agency has many aspects to improve. They issued a fine and we lost about 25min. Lockers are not secure, belongings are left unsafe. The life jackets, the older ones are pretty sloppy, smelly. Halfway through the rafting experience you have to get off the raft to go down a somewhat complicated stony side road in a wetsuit. The guides tell you nothing, they leave you alone and without assistance to climb the rocks or go down sandy terrain. If you're one of those who doesn't throw off the rock, no one tells you where to go and you're just the way I go. The guide came to find me visibly upset so that I would get back on the raft. A mess! After the activity, the guides gathered for lunch, leaving the whole group waiting for more than half an hour for the return bus without any of them notifying the waiting times.

review_text: If you love hiking, lakes and waterfalls then this is the place for you. We spent several hours hiking up to Lago Verde, diverting for the wonderful waterfalls and stopping for photos at the scenic outlooks (6 hours total round trip). We couldn't go much further as the snow was still too deep and, be warned, it is VERY muddy as the melt kicks in! You absolutely need walking poles - you can usually pick up some good bamboo sticks at the start of the hike that previous walkers have discarded. The route is clearly marked and, whilst there are many steep and stepped areas, it is not a difficult hike - but do wear proper walking shoes/boots! There are no facilities once you are on your way, so make sure you have plenty of water and snacks with you.

review_text: I recently took the Red Lagoon tour with *Chilean Way* from Iquique. While the destination itself is breathtaking, the experience was disappointing due to poor organization and lack of basic safety and comfort. Pickup was scheduled between 4:30 and 5:00 AM, but we didn’t leave until nearly 7:00 AM because other passengers were late. The agency should enforce stricter departure times to respect everyone’s schedule. We were told a guide and oxygen would be provided due to the high altitude — neither were. No safety instructions were given, which felt especially irresponsible in a region known for seismic activity. As a traveler from Canada, where earthquakes are uncommon, I expected at least a basic safety briefing. Water was only offered at meal stops, not on the shuttles — which is inadequate considering the dry climate, high altitude, and long drive. Food options at the breakfast and supper stops were limited, with no clear explanations, and no access to feminine hygiene products. We switched vehicles in Camiña. The second shuttle had no air conditioning and was filled with dust, making the ride very uncomfortable. When we arrived at the Red Lagoon, the driver did not accompany us. This may have been due to religious or cultural beliefs tied to local myths, which I respect — but this left the group completely unsupervised in a remote and potentially hazardous location. There was no guide or support in case of altitude sickness, falls, or other emergencies. Later, a fellow traveler felt unwell, and only paracetamol was offered — no proper first aid or medical support. There was also no emergency communication (such as a satellite phone), which is very concerning for such an isolated area. In summary, while the Red Lagoon is a must-see, this tour lacked preparation, comfort, and basic safety measures. I would not recommend booking with *Chilean Way* unless they make significant improvements.

review_text: This was a day trip from Santiago Chile to the El Morado glacier. Separate from most trips offered within the national park. It was a fun, uphill climb gaining several thousand feet in elevation. My guide, Reto, was incredibly professional from the time he picked me up in Santiago to when we returned downtown at the end of the day. We totally hit it off. Everything was at my pace, with Reto making suggestions and giving options of things to explore. His knowledge of the glacier hiking route along with the sights we saw on the way to and from the glacier was excellent. You could tell he knew the area well. I just wore sturdy, low cut hiking shoes and packed multiuple layers of clothes. Hiking poles might have been nice, but not necessary. There was more snow than expected on the trail for this time of year, but it made the trip down a blast as we essentially were able to "ski" down in warm snow vs. taking the rocky trail. It was about 2 hours up to the glacier and less back. Plan for a day from Santiago. I was picked up at 7:30am, but even 6:30 or 7:00 would have been good as the weather shifted from pure sun in the beginning to lots of clouds by the end of the time up next to the glacier. I was able to get some great photos and video. We only met three other people the entire day. The geology is interesting -- you can clearly see copper, iron, and gypsum deposits and there is a gypsum mine on the way to the site. An added bonus was seeng a live volcano as you enter the valley -- steam coming out on top. If you're looking to get out in "the middle of nowhere" with a professional guide to see a natural wonder, this is the trip for you!

review_text: This museum is free for all. There is a place to check your bag (store it) for free at the entrance. You can receive a free passport which allows you to interact with the museum exhibits and stamp your passport as your progress the museum (12 stamps). There's also an audio guide available for non-Spanish speakers. Finally, there is a cafe and a gift shop outside the lobby. You see exhibits/photos showing other locations where human rights abuses have occurred or are currently occurring in the world before you begin on the second floor. First you see what led to the abuses in Chile, the coup d'état by the military of the government of Salvador Allende on September 11, 1973. You'll also learn about the American CIA's involvement in supporting that coup. The ensuing exhibits will show the flight and plight of those exiled from Chile (either self-exiled or ejected by the government) and what events occurred in Chile from 1973 to the end of the Pinochet dictatorship in 1988. Lots of pictures, videos, artifacts, and interviews. Don't miss this important museum on your visit to Santiago.
