review_text: As part of the tour options for the Todos Los Santos lake crossing, a helicopter ride was offered for about US $250 per person. I'm not sure that this runs all the time but we had sensational weather, no wind and clear skies so it was too good an opportunity to miss. Of two weeks in Chile and Argentina, this would have to be the best thing we did. We climbed from lake level to around 8000ft and were right next to cliffs, glaciers and had amazing views all round. The pilot was excellent and explained things well in English. We had close up views of waterfalls and at times seemed only metres away from snow and ice. Extraordinary!

I recommend you to visit this amazing park, because it has everyting if you want to spend a good time and relax.

review_text: This was the absolute highlight of my trip so far. The 3 day tour is packef full of Wow moments - just when you think you've see the best, it blows you away again. I am now certain Bolivia is the most beautiful country in the world, but what also made the trip so special was our driver/guide Efrain Flores (better known as Chacho). I won't tell you everything he brought to the tour because I want you to be as surprised and delighted as we were, but he was kind, funny and knowledgeable, has a very eclectic taste in music and the patience of a saint for answering all our ridiculous questions. I was worried my poor Spanish would be a problem, but not at all - don't let lack of a 100% English speaking guide put you off. Also the driving was excellent - very careful and comfortable; we had 100% trust in Chacho who always seemed to get us places ahead of the crowd and keeps his landcruiser in an excellent (and clean) condition. I'm traveling alone and made lovely friends on this tour. We all agreed it is excellent value for money. The vegetarians amongst us were well catered for and often felt our food was (secretly) better than the carnivores. One night of accommodation was a little basic, but the second night was amazing - there was even wifi!! And the beds were super comfy. You can end the tour in Uyuni or return to San Pedro, but either way this is not to be missed.

review_text: These high altitude (4000+ meters) geysers are geysers of steam rather than water. We arrived before sunrise, following a queue of others doing the same. The toilets at the site are limited and it took a good 15 minutes for the women in our small tour group to negotiate the long line. People arriving in tour buses with internal toilets had a definite advantage. A few visitors were ill with the high altitude and it is suggested to spend a few days in San Pedro (2000 m) before attempting this trip. The steam geysers are best seen when the air is cold, at sunrise. We wore snow gear and were warm. The geysers are reasonably good to view. The water boils at 85 degree C due to the high altitude. Make sure you take you swimming costume. There are changing sheds at the thermal pool which is about 28 degree C and makes for a wonderful sunrise swim when followed by breakfast.

review_text: Would recommend this company to do white water rafting. You can order, and pay online and it's an all-inclusive price. They have free pickup and drop off in Puerto Varas (or anywhere nearby including Ensenada). They talk you through their safety measures (in Spanish and English), and then you pick up your gear and get going to the start in their shuttles. You can have smaller groups, but the rafts can hold max 5-6 people with guide. You go through class 2 and 3 rapids, but on my day the river wasn't flowing as strong, so they were softer than I though, but had an excellent experience. There will be times to stop, take a photo, swim a bit before you end you journey about 45-1 hour after the start of the rapids. There will be changing areas at the end, and then you get transported back to base and are given a pizza slice and drink. There is an official photographer with whom you can purchase photos for 30,000 CLP. Overall, it was a great, efficient, organized kayaking company with great guides, and easy process. review_text: We did the Sairecabur day trip with this company. Our guide drove us up there and then was unable to go with us due to illness, which we discovered had been known about before we left. It was poor that this guide was sent with us at all, and poor that he was not honest with us - he said we could start and he would catch us up. He never left the vehicle and we had to find our own route up and down. This is not easy, it was challenging. After our descent we had to leave immediately ( no time for refreshments) as it was deemed that the guide was so I’ll he had to return to lower altitude. Although the trip was successful, I don’t believe the tour company or their guide made good decisions and it could have ended very badly, had we, and the other client, not been fit, prepared and capable ( unlike the guide).

review_text: Julio is the real thing. So many tours are high in promises and superlatives and ultimately underwhelm. Not Julio! He asks us questions about our tour objectives, did some homework and came up with a comprehensive, intellectual yet low key day. review_text: Fuerte Bulnes marks the spot where the Spanish tried to establish a colony to secure the Magellan Straits. After less than ten years the colonists (those left) moved to the spot that became the town of Puente Arenas. The original fort has vanished (was built of wood or peat) but the Chileans have built a replica of the original that resides on the spot and this is what you visit when you go to Fort Bulnes. Most tours require you to pay the entrance fee (23$ US) and then you can visit the spot and the interpretation center. I found the visit informative, but because all the buildings are replicas and not furnished, you can not glean that much from the visit. The fort is really the collection of wood buildings sitting on a hill so not really very fort-looking. It does occupy a prime spot on the coast, however, that gives great views of the straits. And the fort is clearly important to those interested in the history of this city. What I liked better than the fort was the 60 Kilometer drive along the coast that you take from Puente Arenas to get here.

The original fort has vanished (was built of wood or peat) but the Chileans have built a replica of the original that resides on the spot and this is what you visit when you go to Fort Bulnes. Most tours require you to pay the entrance fee (23$ US) and then you can visit the spot and the interpretation center. I found the visit informative, but because all the buildings are replicas and not furnished, you can not glean that much from the visit. The fort is really the collection of wood buildings sitting on a hill so not really very fort-looking. It does occupy a prime spot on the coast, however, that gives great views of the straits. And the fort is clearly important to those interested in the history of this city. What I liked better than the fort was the 60 Kilometer drive along the coast that you take from Puente Arenas to get here.

Cost of one ride is 800 peso for adult.

In hindsight using Pocket Earth Pro (iOS/Android) which uses Open Street Map did show the path to the lake, zoom in on the lake and follow the brown dashed line backwards to highway 27. If you decided to do it alone you'd definitely need a 4x4, however I would still opt to go with a guide as the insights shared made it worth while. Salar de Tara is around ~4300m ASL (~13000ft), and the drive there got us up ~4900m ASL (~15000ft) and I did experience a bit of altitude sickness after getting back to S.P. de Atacama so keep this in mind when booking the trip. Some people on the trip suffered once they got home, others were just fine. I'd make a point of going if I was in S.P. de Atacama

review_text: Was there during the start of the summer season for a short biz meeting. Had a few days to spare and was looking for something not too far from Santiago. Found this website offering hike at La Parva ski resort for a day trip. The company, Andes explorer, fetch us from downtown and headed down south. The drive up to La Parva was winding - with apprx. 40 sharp curves. and we saw foxes in the bush!! We took a chair lift up to 3000m and started our hike. Coming from Asia, we did not expect their summer could be so chilling and the wind velocity was high. Our guide had to lend us face mask to shield from strong UV and wind chill. We took AMS pill the night before and I did not think it did not worked very well. Our heads were pounding .. We hiked very slowly.. Overall, we truly enjoyed the experience - the stunning view of snow capped Andes ranges.. the lake, the hike, the landscape, the weather ... Worth every single bit of the time we spend there..

review_text: During June 2014, I had the pleasure of the opportunity to participate in this amazing 3 day learning by doing course. It was during the rainy season, with low temperatures (3 to 7 degrees celsius) but always feeling safe under the supervision of our instructor Juan Federico Zuazo. On the first day we covered assisted and self rescuing techniques, as well as theoretical components, such as tides, currents, use of a compass and other important information to successfully prepare your rowing journey. The second and third day of the course consisted of doing a rowing trip though the fjord of Reloncaví, camping overnight, experiencing the local ways of life, observing wildlife such as dolphins, sea dogs and birds. We also revised the techniques learnt on the first day. In conclusion, it was an awesome learning experience for someone wanting to start experiencing the world of sea kayaking. I highly recommend Juan Federico Zuazo and Yak Expeditions as a guide to safely enter into this kayaking world.

review_text: Cerro Santa Lucía is a great spot to begin a walk around downtown Santiago de Chile, and is well-maintained - a credit to the city authorities. The centerpiece is an old Spanish fort atop a volcanic hill rising steeply about 70 meters over the surrounding area. Remodelling from the 1870s turned the fort into a picturesque city-center park of rococo architectural follies, fountains, gardens and lookouts which soften the original military use of the site, which dates back to the 1540s. We visited on a Sunday, finding ourselves among mostly Chilean families visiting to enjoy the ambience and the views. City officials and police were on hand for safety, security and information. Entry was free, with visitor book registration. Visitors with mobility problems would have difficulty visiting the higher, steeper levels accessible only by steep stairs with handrails. Overall, highly recommended as a must-see sight of Santiago.

review_text: When we booked this tour in August, Victoria quickly responded to our e-mails, although we thought it strange that this was the only South American independent tour group that required full payment up front and our cost was a few dollars higher than another Cruise Critic member paid. We shook off the feeling, thought maybe it had to do with paying with PayPal and settled back to wait for our cruise. As the cruise got nearer, we reached out several times to confirm our reservation, meeting times, location, etc. and received no feedback. Eventually the initial CC member who mentioned this tour, got an e-mail stating 30 days prior to the cruise information would be sent, Unbeknownst to us, others were experiencing this lack of communication and withdrew from the tour. We decided to stick with the tour because the sites offered seemed interesting. A few days into the 30 day promise, info was sent and it was mentioned that if some people joined now they could pay half at departure if they decided to join the group. What wasn’t said was what happened the actual day of the trip. The day of the trip, no representative could be found at the San Antonio port. Other tour companies assured us they would turn up. Eventually they did, but with a list that did not include everyone who thought they had a seat on the bus. Our name was on the list as paid, but others were not who had also paid. Some people were add-ons and they were listed. It took over a half hour of tour time to sort this out and then people were added to the vans which meant every seat, even uncomfortable ones, had to be used, which caused grumbling throughout the day. We began questioning arrival back to the port, promised at 4 and were told there was no problem. It seemed as if stops were added as we went along, as no itinerary had been planned. We stopped at Pablo Neruda’s house but did not tour it. I guess the view was the reason. Other stops were like this. Bathroom stops were not planned and required money. No one wanted to walk the hilly streets of Valparaiso, especially as several people had walking difficulties, but the guide had us do this, though all it led to was the port. The added walk and stop at a second funicular, after the first one was closed, pushed us later. We told the guide we did not need to experience the funicular, but she thought it a must experience. Seeing one of the cables fixed with duct tape was not very soothing. Again, more time. Vina Del Mar was solely for lunch at a seaside restaurant. Lovely setting, but packed with other tour groups, so we sat by the pool, not the sea, facing the back wall of the restaurant. The food was very high priced. Lunch for two was $36 and that did not include any beverages, not even water. A small cereal size bowl was a “Chicken Caesar salad” containing one cherry tomato, one olive, several grated pieces of lettuce, some sprinkled cheese and about 4 bites of chicken. This was not even a true Caesar salad, It cost over $11. Our group was split. One table placed their order and then the remaining 8 of us placed our order but ours never came. The other table got their food and ate. Departure time was coming and someone went to look for the guide. The guide was upstairs on another floor in a small dining room and came to see what was happening. The food magically appeared except for my husband’s meal. His beef and fries couldn’t be found. Another meal appeared and was offered to him, but it wasn’t what he ordered. Finally they found his meal. For this he paid almost $20. The final insult was the bill with gratuity added on the check. No one was happy as the hot food was lukewarm at best and much was left uneaten on the table. We couldn’t help but wonder how GV Tours benefitted from this stop. Again, we asked about arrival back to the ship, since again we were running late and were assured everything was on schedule. Arriving at the winery 20 minutes before we were due back at the port, we knew our timing back to port would be late. The visit was short, but it was already past the time we had been promised. Our guide told us our ship was not leaving until 5:15 and we would be back in plenty time. Partway back a fellow traveler panicked as she realized we had turned off the road previously traveled in the morning. We were told it was to avoid traffic, but when the passenger gave a phone number to the guide to call the port to report our late arrival, we were told the guide could reach no one. The final problem was when the guide tried to collect money from someone in the van who took the trip, but bragged to everyone how she would not prepay for her trip and was told she could pay the full amount on the day of her and her husband’s tour. Her price? Eight dollars per ticket cheaper than our quoted price and our money had been in GV Tours hands from August which was 7 months ago! We arrived at the port at 5:00. By the time we walked through the drop off point, we barely made the onboard time. The guide was kind and friendly and began the day with a scheduling mess, but the tour, the lunch, and the tour company is not one we can recommend. Review of: Small Group tour to Viña Del Mar, Valparaiso from San Antonio port Hi Deborah, Here at GV Tours we take customer care very seriously as it is one of our top priorities. This is why we’ve never missed a cruise for 20 years. We are happy to hear you enjoyed our guide Carolina! She took so many pictures of your group smiling in all of the stops, so you seemed to be having a great time. As mentioned to you on the day of the tour, there were 4 passengers who showed up on the day of the tour from your cruise who had not prepaid and were not confirmed on this tour for that same reason, but they asked if we could accomodate them. We accommodated since we had two vehicles and 8 empty seats. Your group booked a shared tour not a private tour. The price paid by you and your group of 6 was $80 dollars per person for our “All day small group tour with pick-up and drop-off in San Antonio port with stops in Valparaiso, Viña Del Mar and complimentary wine tasting at Indomita Winery.” Per our policy on our website, we do not require anyone to prepay until 30 days before the tour. I am sorry if there was misunderstanding concerning that situation. Please resend any email where we state that your reservation will not be held unless you pay 7 months before, so that we may understand where the misunderstanding occurred. For lunch, our customers can order absolutely whatever they want. There are a variety of pricings and each person can choose whatever they’d like. Your friend on your group who also emailed us said your arrival time was 4:40 pm, but now you stated it’s 5;00 pm. We did everything on our itinerary (which is clearly stated on our website) and our guide added a stop at Pablo Neruda’s house, however, it was closed with no notice. Vina Del Mar has two short stops as listed on the itinerary; one at the Moai and one at the beach, your group did not want to go to the beach, so that just left lunch. I appreciate that you did not like what you paid for lunch and I am sorry if there was a misunderstanding about the prepayment, but some of your friends even paid later on. We will make sure we are very clear about prepayments in the future. We do hope you have a great rest of your trip and thank you again for taking time to write. Kind regards, Victoria Stein

review_text: I didn't have a lot of time in Chile to visit wineries and so when I saw the opportunities that Maipo Valley Wine Tours provided, I was very interested. I booked the Top 3 Wineries full-day tour and I was not disappointed. Felipe picked me up at my hotel in Santiago right on time and was my driver for the entire day. His colleague, Christian, joined as my personal guide at the conclusion of the first winery tour at Undurraga. From there we traveled to Santa Rita winery where I was able to enjoy a delicious meal at Doña Paula restaurant. The restaurant was closed for two large groups, but Felipe was able to work his connections and get me a table. It was fantastic! From there we went to Concha y Toro where I was delighted by another tour and wine tasting. The best part of all was the friendly and gracious hospitality of Felipe and Christian who, I felt, were like long lost friends. I would highly recommend Maipo Valley Wine Tours to anyone... it's organized, friendly, punctual, and well-connected with all the wineries you'd like to visit. It made the tour an adventure with great memories.

review_text: This ride was great. We were out for a few hours in the mountains surrounding Santiago with amazing views. The horses were lovely and our guide Jean Paul was super experienced and knowledgeable. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience and would certainly recommend it for either beginners or experienced riders. The horses were very well trained and well behaved and looked after us beginners! The only downside is that the place is rather difficult to find as it's right on the edge of the city in an area with many stables. Whilst we eventually managed to find it due to our patient taxi driver we did have difficulty getting a cab back so I'd recommend asking your cab driver to pick you up again at the end of the ride. Jean Paul kindly took us back to the main road with the horses so we could find a cab! It's a fantastic experience, we'd certainly recommend it.

review_text: This was truly one of the most special experiences of my life. We saw multiple humpback whales, dolphins, sea lions, penguins and various birds and the landscape of where we sailed around was breathtaking. The captain and crew were tireless in helping us spot as many of these marine life as possible and provided us so much information on what we were seeing along the way/ Service: Our guide Paula, together with the wonderful crew Captain Simon, Miguel, Franco was the best crew that we have encountered - in addition to keeping us safe on the very choppy waters, they had a wealth of information and were great hosts. Also Captain Simon is an amazing chef and the crew prepared lunch every day on board that was out of this world amazing. They also went out of their way to ensure we were happy and we even had lunch in front of a massive glacier and the crew fished out small icebergs that were floating near the glacier so that we could see it up close. 5 star service! Food: The food on the boat that was cooked by the crew, helmed by Captain/Chef Simon was soooo good and comforting. It was amazing seeing them prepare food in a small galley of such high standard. The dinner cooked by the resident chef on the island was even better - rivalling those of big chain hotels. To be honest, across our entire trip with Whalesound, we ate extremely well and was so so full after each meal. We definitely did not expect to be dining so well on this trip. Accommodation: We were initially bit worried about sleeping in the eco tents on the island having been used to big chain hotels and it's creature comforts. We were wrong to be worried because these eco tents were amazing which battles our minds as the island was right in the middle of the marine reserve. It was huge, clean and we had a great fireplace, a nice little sitting area with a view and most of all, the beds were out of this world comfortable - a true glamping experience. Great mattresses, amazingly thick and luscious duvets and good pillows. The showers are shared but was just a 1 min walk away with good water pressure and hot water. Tip: They do not provide toiletries so remember to bring your own - although towels were provided. Boat: When we first saw a photo of the boat, we were bit anxious that it was quite small. My friend in particular has pretty bad sea sickness. Not going to lie, the 7-8 hour crossing each way was definitely very bumpy at times so highly recommend that guests bring along their own sea sickness medication as it was quite choppy at times. However, it was just bumpy for the trip to the eco lodge island and back - the cruising around each day was calm and glorious. The boat, although small was surprisingly very comfortable with different areas you could chill in, take a nap etc. You never felt crowded on the boat at all and it really seemed homely. There is a small library on board as well with books about the marine life in the area, indigenous history etc to keep you occupied. They have also made an order on a larger boat that will hopefully start in 2025 which would allow them to sail further and hopefully be better equipped against choppy waters. Overall, our experience from start to finish was absolutely out of this would and we had smiles plastered on our faces all the time. We were also lucky that the rest of the guests on the boat were so friendly and diverse which really enhanced the experience. The best way to describe our experience was that we felt like we were hosted by an amazingly welcoming and warm family at a bed & breakfast (on the seas and on the eco tent island) and we are already looking forward to coming back in the near future If you have any doubts - cast them away as you are definitely in for a truly special experience that will live on in your memories forever.

Review of: Chilean Cuisine Cooking Class with Traditional Market Tour Hello Katie, Thank you for your review. We have read it carefully, and are really taking some of your constructive criticism into consideration. Some other parts we felt you may have taken our cuisine for granted, and maybe you expected us to be something we are not, and I honestly doubt we will ever be. Our group classes focus on traditional meals; on century old recipes, and we try our hardest to bring these recipes to our visitors. We are always disappointed when they are not good enough for certain people; however, we understand not everyone has the same tastes. Now, to provide a brief background on this, so readers can understand... you had wanted a private Wine Pairing Class, and decided on the group option after we sent over all of our options and prices. The group option DOES NOT include a lot of things that the private classes include, such as Coffee, Wine, Tea, Private Transportation, etc. So, for that part, we can't really take blame for something that we explained beforehand. It does include 4 Courses of Chilean Food + Coktail or Soft Drinks: 1. Empanadas and Pebre (Salsa) 2. Ceviche or Avocado with Hearts of Palm 3. One of 4 Meals (Countryside Recipes) 4. Dessert (Fruit or Cookies) + Pisco Sour + Soft Drinks such as still water and fruit juice or lemonade if you do not want pisco sour. We invite anyone reading this to see the prices on our site and be the judge whether this is expensive or not for a 4 course cooking class. Now, Chilean Cuisine isn't French Cuisine, or Italian Cuisine -- It's Chilean Cuisine. We make hearty home made stews, and soups. We are sorry if this may seem "basic" to you, but we stand behind our national meals, and respectfully disagree with you on that part of the review. We use the amazing produce from Chile, such as pumpkins, avocados, potatoes, chard, coriander, tomatoes, etc, and we cook them with our amazing fish and beef products. To get this produce, we go to one of the busiest places in the city, Mercado Cardonal. Here we have to understand that people here are working; they're running down its corridors with boxes on their shoulders and we have to be mindful and respectful of their craft. If this means having to move out of the way, and not being able to stop at every fruit, or every vegetable to talk about them, it's the price we pay in order to see the realest place in the city. In regards to the hard cookie... what can I say? If you try any traditional pastries, they tend to be very diffrent from the ones in other countries. Google "Dulces de La ligua" (which is what you chose to make) and see them for yourself. Once again, we respectfully disagree with your words there, as we have followed old recipes to make these products. In regards to Veronica, she was kind enough to fill in on a day when our main chef was sick; she is an excellent cook, and we know that day she did her best. From what I hear, the other couple had a great time -- I'm sorry she wasn't a fit for your party. Finally, recipes are sent out the last day of each month to all of our participants that month, though sometimes people request them sooner, so we provide them earlier when they do.

review_text: Paidahuen Archaeological Park is a National Monument located in Chile's 5th Region along the northern bank of the Aconcagua River, in the rural town of San Esteban. The top of this isolated hill holds slabs of large rocks adorned with petroglyphs, work of native populations dating from 450 to 1000 years ago. The park land is "owned" by the Vina San Esteban (Vineyard), makers of In SItu wines, which in itself is well worth a visit. We picked up a brochure about Paidahuen at the vineyard. After parking one walks along a well marked pathway that slowly winds uphill towards the mountain top. Most of the petroglyphs are found along the path and near the top of the mountain. There is a nice "Los Andes View" rest area at the top. This is not a heavily traveled site, and the walk uphill requires some stamina---but is very doable if one is in halfway decent shape. One can do the walk in about one hour--but that's if you don't stop and rest at the top which we did (the view is spectacular).

review_text: You shouldn't leave Santiago without seeing the spectacular views from Cerro San Christobal, but it's probably not worth queuing up for hours. If you can, why not walk up? The walk was half the fun. I'd previously read that it wasn't safe to walk due to muggings. I think these reports were from a few years ago as It seemed very safe with plenty of people strolling up and down, enjoying picnics etc while I did see mounted police in the park too. Having said that I wouldn't venture up at night as there's no lighting. Once at the summit there are spectacular 'almost' 360 views over Santiago. There is a giant statue of the Virgin Mary which is often compared to Christ the Redeemer in Rio (not a comparison I'd agree with, but the Virgin Statue is still quite impressive). Like Christo in Rio, Santiago's Virgin Statue is a relic of the past when South America was deeply Catholic. Today Chile is much more secular and most people seem to visit the statue as a charming curiosity but mostly for the views. The experience of walking through this little pocket of woodlands surrounded by urban sprawl and viewing the spectacular views at the top is a must do in Santiago. And it doesn't cost a cent.

review_text: We arrive at this ecocenter for a "family experience" off of our Silversea. Although the center provides horseback riding, kayaking, and camping experiences our event was a lunch prepared by the extended La Pancha family (grandparents, family, children and grandchildren) in their family for our group of 15 senior citizens who were bussed in for the three hour experience. A lamb was bar-b-cued on a metal spit on an outdoor fire pit and served with a variety of vegetables and the Chile's famous pisca sour and wine beverages. The lamb was delicious. After lunch we had an opportunity to walk around the center's lovely grounds at the foot of the Patagonia hillside. The family greeted us upon arrival and hugged each of us with their warm embrace. Midway through the lunch the family provided entertainment in the form of the children dancing the Marinera in traditional costumes. The adults later provided their own dance routines and invited our group to join them (we were terrible). There is not much to see in the nearby town of Puerto Aysen which claims to have the longest suspension bridge in Chile. thank you for your opinion,. is very important for us recieve english language opinion. really thank very much, bye bye. We told the guide we wanted to do the lunch but we were told that it wasn't part of the tour and if we stopped for lunch we would have to make our own way back to the hotel. We decided to stay with the bus and were dropped off at the hotel at 12:30 PM so the tour took 3 1/2 hours rather than the advertised 5.

review_text: Cyril of Chiloe Natural made our three days on the island into an exceptional experience. Not only did we see many of the historical UNESCO churches, but he also taught us much about local bird life. The black necked swans were especially beautiful. As for the churches—Cyril went above and beyond in so many ways. Not only did we visit about half of the 16 UNESCO churches, but we also had access behind the roof in one church so that we could see how the native people constructed the ceiling like an upside down boat. And he knew several of the church caretakers and was able to obtain the keys so we could enter when the church would otherwise have been locked. He had great restaurant recommendations and knew wonderful coffee places in several of the smaller towns. We are avid coffee drinkers, so this was another plus. He placed us in a wonderful accommodation in Castro. Sizigia is a palafito (structure built on stilts over the water) and very recently remodeled. We looked out over the water and the fishing boats from a luxurious room. The breakfasts also were delicious and generous. My husband and I both highly recommend Chiloe Natural.

The whole place is generally nice, service level average (but that's normal in Chile), and the only thing that is quite bothering is attracting people by calling the place ecological when it is not. I'm sure you can do better.

review_text: We came across this agency when looking for a star gazing tour. They seemed to have the biggest telescopes compared to the other agencies we checked out. I don’t have much knowledge about telescopes but I assumed, as with a lot of things, the bigger the better. So it was the deciding factor plus the price was roughly the same level others are asking, we paid 18k pesos pp, as a reference. We had an absolutely brilliant experience during that star gazing tour! Elisa, the guide gave a brief introduction to theory, which was great, short but detailed, easy to follow even for a non native speaker. After that we went to the field with two telescopes of size of a person. This is where you are going to go “ah I don’t regret paying for this tour”. Although the group might seem a bit big, we had 15 people or so, don’t worry that you miss your chance to see the stars. Elisa is not only super passionate about the stars but also runs in between the telescopes to make necessary adjustments so everyone can see the objects the best. So don’t worry if you’re in the end of the line to the telescope, you’ll see the same as everyone else! Group photo is take afterwards and included in the price of the tour. Personal photo costs 3k pesos per photo. Snacks and drinks are also provided after the tour in the room where the presentation took place. Honestly I wasn’t really exploring what snacks were there, but it’s nice to have a cup of tea after being out, it’s a bit cold outside during the night. So thanks to everyone involved for organizing such a great trip, and special thanks to Elisa for making sure everyone has such a great experience.

review_text: Myself and a friend booked through Ruth the 5 day, 4 night W trek in Torres Del Paine with accomodation and meals. Though we were only about 1 month away, and it was high season, Ruth somehow managed to secure us the trek with accomodation which was appreciated. She was also helpful and informative when we met her to pick up the vouchers in Puerto Natales. We found the dorm accomodations to be great, no problems - especially at Domo Francis - and found the food to be good and sufficient, and no problems whatsoever using the vouchers for the meals, accomodation and transfers. We were actually quite surprised at how many facilities there were at each Refugio given how inaccessible some were, and found the stays (in dorms) to be comfortable. The hiking itself was amazing, and we got a bit lucky with the weather with it being sunny and clear during the day, and only windy/raining in the later afternoons and evenings, so if you left early, no problems. This isn’t always the case though Ive heard with the weather being pretty changeable. I would definitely recommend the W package, with the price seeming very reasonable given the quality of the accomodation and meals, and in such a naturally beautiful area for hiking. Only thing I’d add is that you need to be reasonably fit and OK with getting wet given the changing conditions. Well worth it though. Hello Damian! review_text: We were with Miguel, the "Puma tracker" for a whole day trying to get a sighting of a Puma. Miguel doesn't have an assigned "plot" to look for, so he moves freely around Torres del Paine National Park and its surroundings. He is not sure you can see him, so while Miguel was looking for him he was explaining what he was looking for to decide which route to follow, which area to look for. He drives, gives you explanations and, at the same time, fixates on everything. After about six hours of searching, Miguel saw that "a stone had moved" and indeed, there was a pregnant female cougar. Miguel advised us where to place ourselves and what to do so we could see the cougar as well as possible. It was a fantastic experience! Miguel is also a great nature photographer and carries spectacular photography equipment and telescope. He took the opportunity to give us some photography tips. He was kind enough to pass us the pictures he had taken, which were much better than ours. After the sighting, Miguel asked us if we had the desire to follow and we said yes. So we went on for a couple more hours walking around the park, while it was dark. The landscapes were very beautiful. It was an experience we will never forget and Miguel, a great explorer, a great photographer and a better person.

review_text: This was very close to the Fonck Museum which is definitely worth your time. When we visited, the Palacio Rioja was closed for reconstruction which, according to our guide, happens quite a lot. The building was constructed for Fernando Rioja who acquired the property in 1906 after the initial home was destroyed by the destructive earthquake of 1906. The building started in 1909. It was later acquired by the city of Vina del Mar in 1956 and was turned into government offices and now a museum - primarily of French furniture which was inside the home. We were not allowed to go inside but we would like to come back since we researched the place. At least we got some great photographs of a French palace in the middle of Vina del Mar.

review_text: Given that weather is such a determining factor to the trip it's hard to compare one to another. We did this trip from Puerto Natales to Puerto Montt just after high season, and true to form the voyage was delayed one day because of weather. However, once on the ship, we had nothing but blue skies, calm winds, no chop and sunny days. Do bare in mind that it is a cargo ship, not a luxury cruise liner. So if you're expecting to have every care and whim seen to you will be disappointed. What you do have are amazing views of a spectacular landscape, the opportunity to see whales and other sea life, and a great place to meet people and make good friends. The food was simple but plentiful, with vegetarian options. I didn't know of anyone to go hungry or lack for food. Navimag's 'no alcohol allowed on the ship' policy seemed more like a don't ask don't tell deal. The Chilean truck drivers, friendly interesting guys, seemed merry most nights. Our guide, Juan Pablo, was fantastic. His English was great, he was knowledgeable, and he was a good lad to chat to and ask questions about where to go from Puerto Montt. Bring plenty of books, games, a deck of cards and 'no alcohol' as well as a positive attitude and this is a perfect place to chill and see a part of the world you can't see via any other means. If you go, I hope the weather treats you well.

review_text: Foto Ruta was one of the best afternoons of my trip so far as the sophisticated workshop - complete with a gorgeous inspirational presentation at the beginning from the fabulously talented Cat Allen, and finishing off with hearty amounts of wine - really opened my eyes to ways of seeing (excuse the pun) and encouraged me to go off piste in Santiago. A must for all true travelers - I can't recommend it enough! Having been in Santiago for four months I know that there are so many wonderful hidden corners in the city - so many more than a guide book could possible tell you about - but, falling into the same trap as many tourists, I seem to have generally stuck to the same well-trodden paths dictated by Lonely Planet! I rarely give myself time to explore and properly reflect on my surroundings let alone get creative with them, which one should really do in a country that has produced so many great artists over the years! We were equipped with a map and sent out to wander the bo-ho side-streets of the Bellavista neighborhood armed with ten or so cyptic 'clues' to interpret through our photography as we wished. Cat talked about the importance of texture, lighting and negative space, to name a few, and encouraged us to learn how to use our cameras (ranging in the group from point-and-shoots to SLRs) to produce photos we could proudly show friends and family after our trip. After an hour or two's photography the group met again to share photos for each 'clue' - I think everyone came away feeling pretty proud of themselves! It was both a time for quiet reflection and personal observation, for learning photography tips from an expert and for meeting new people and having a laugh! An absolute bargain, and the source of many great memories.

review_text: I booked the Volcano and Hot Springs day trip with this company, and enjoyed a fantastic day excursion to a very beautiful and unique place. Liliana and the team at the office were friendly, informative, and was great to chat a while. The guide for the trip (Rodrigo) was friendly, knowledgeable, and you could easily tell had a real passion for eco tourism. The location for this trip, Cajon del Maipo, is breathtaking; during the walk we were able to see the vast Andes mountain peaks, beautiful glaciers, interesting plantlife, animals (horses) and birdlife, including Condors that were circling overhead. The hot pools (Banos Morales) were a great way to follow on from the leisurely volcano valley walk. Due to the four wheel drive access, these were not swarmed by tourists like one might expect, but were nestled away in a tranquil setting surrounded by sublime scenery. It is hard to believe such an authentic South American experience and idyllic location is only a stone's throw away from Santiago city. I would wholeheartedly recommend this day trip to anyone visiting Santiago, and I cannot wait to return again soon and book another trip.

review_text: First of all, the communication with Connie was amazing. She arranged for the van to pick us up at 920 at the door of our building...and at 9:20, Jose showed up for the tour. We jumped into a nicely appointed and air conditioned Mercedes van with a very nice driver and did our introductions. Jose gave us all bottled water. We drove out to Casablanca Valley- about an hour. The reason this company is number one is because they are nice, organized, honest, smart and really love wine---Jose grew up in a vineyard! So if you are worried about anything with this group: Stop. review_text: Seeing the Tatio Geysers and the surrounding scenery was a highlight of my time in the Atacama Desert. Our tour left at 5am and it took two hours to reach the geysers. While they say it's easiest to see the steam in the early morning as the sun rises, I thought it looked most spectacular when the sun was shining. There will be lots of other tour groups there in the morning, but it's still beautiful with people around. Be warned that it is freezing - it was minus 10 degrees celcius - so, dress appropriately. We didn't know it would be that cold and were freezing the entire time. It is also high altitude (4,300m) which means you may experience some of the effects of altitude sickness.

review_text: Friend and I self-drove to these lakes in early April. I loved the drive (2.5 hours) from San Pedro and scenic views, but my friend thought it was a bit far to go for just a view of some lakes that you cannot even get close to to see the wildlife. I brought binoculars and that was the only way we could tell that there were birds and vicunas around/in the lakes. I thought the lakes were absolutely beautiful--volcanoes surround and the colors are just stunning. Just beware that there is not much more than a little bit of hard-to-do 4300 m altitude walking and photography of lakes/mountains here. Your time may be better spent at other sights first. But I think it is worth it if you have some time at the end of your trip, maybe combined with a trip to Socaire or Chaxa and the Lake Tebinquinche sunset on the way back. Easy to get to. The roads are great up until the last few 10 kilometers which is on a dirt road.I think entry was 5000 CHP per person?

review_text: If you like Baroque style, then you'll probably enjoy this cathedral. Personally, I've always thought Baroque was a bit over the top, but I found this one to be a bit more humble while still elegant. However, the crypt beneath the altar seems to have been redone recently, showing off some sleek lines and letting the bishops rest not only in peace, but in style as well. Beyond that, this church doesn't stand out much in my eyes having seen so many before. But it's free and not out of the way, so why not check it out? Although, if you have a chance to go into some of the other old churches in Santiago outside of the center, definitely do it! Nuestra Señora de la Divina Providencia on Providencia between Pedro de Valdivia and Manuel Montt is very nice with much more light!

review_text: Think of a place full of history? Each level of the cerro had something to tell. I was there in the winter and the landscape is breathtaking... but don't be mistaken: the walk is long, and obviously nothing accessible. At first it's a large parallel road, but if you want to get to the main view, you'll need to face narrow paths, with high steps and hardly fit your whole foot. I did not notice if there was bathroom structure, but I saw one or another open kiosk. Inside, on the first level, there is a natural cave where they made a place for a fair where the natives sell handmade items like ocarinas, jewelry, carpets, drawings; and there is also a small cafeteria with items typical of the region. However, it is basically a place to enjoy the view and go to the next, there is not much to do there if not to walk to the view or rest under some shade (or sun if it is too cold).

review_text: If you're in the area this is a "must do". There's a considerable drive from the main road around the lake up to the chairlift base station. Allow time - it twists and winds and is steep in places, but surfaced and well maintained. A return ticket to the top station (2022 prices) for an adult was CLP 20,000 (about £20), and well worth it. I visited twice over the course of a week during the summer. One day was pleasantly warm, the other had a cool breeze. Both days were sunny and clear. The views were to savour. There's a walk at the middle station that's well worth the effort. There are two walks at the summit station - the longer one takes you out to a viewpoint; the other, more poplular walk takes you up to another viewpoint. Both are well worth doing. Be aware of the altitude - strong sun and you might just begin to notice less oxygen in the air. Don't be fooled by conditions lower down - have a warm jacket in case of cold winds - even on a sunny day. A wonderful experience. The chairlift staff are really good.

review_text: This beautiful museum is housed in an incredible building. The natural light plays on the delicate marble statues and infuses them with life. For anyone who has seen Michelangelo's "David" in Florence lit by natural light, you will understand what I mean. There is something magical about the way the sunlight illuminates the nearly translucent Carrara marble that gives the figures life. It also features many paintings in the different galleries. English subtitles would be nice, but we got by with our limited Spanish and enjoyed it greatly. The museum is free, but they issue tickets to maintain a head count, I guess. Even if you are not interested in art, it's worth the time if only to see the wonderful building.

review_text: Chepu is an amazing place to visit and especially to kayak along the rivers. The drowned forest (tsunami, 1960) is pretty wild. We saw lots of different birds and also saw a river otter, which we found out is pretty common in Chepu, but very uncommon anywhere else in Chile. Fernando and Amory were extremely helpful and friendly. They even picked us up from the bus stop on Ruta 5 (bus from Ancud to Castro, KM25 bus stop). They also provided us with the kayaks, waterproof paints, a dry bag and a 2-way radio (in case we had any difficulties on the river). We had no problems at all but it was nice to know we could call them if we had any issues. I've rented many kayaks and never was provided this level of service.

review_text: We highly recommend Venture Experiences! We discovered Venture here on Trip Advisor. Plus, she has a great sense of humor - so we got along super well and shared a lot of laughs. review_text: I have come back to this place, off and on, for more than a decade, and every time I wonder why I do so… The answer is always the same: we live in Brazil, like skiing a lot, have little children and if we want them to ski more than once or twice a year, we need an option for the July school holidays. And options, in the southern hemisphere, are few and far between…This last statement is exactly the principle of semi-monopoly based on which these facilities are managed. To compare Valle Nevado with the alps would be unfair, but this place lags behind its own standards. In more than ten years, no new slopes have been added, no connections has been created and the only new lift added is a short cableway that provides better access to the skiers who come for the day. If you go skiing on the other side of the mountain, forget any comfort facility, not even restrooms (don’t count on hiding behind a tree, for there aren’t any trees…). It is a small resort, in three days you’ll have skied it all many times over. The slopes are ok: not too long, not too challenging, with decent maintenance and usually not too crowded. If you are lucky and catch a perfect day of sun and with lots of new snow, you can have a great day of leisurely ski. Hotels are ski-in ski-out, and other accommodations are not far away. If you have children who still have to learn how to ski, it’s good enough. Hotels, restaurant, ski rental, ski school and shops are ok too: never excellent, but one can live with them. Everything is way overpriced. What really disappoints and irritates in Valle Nevado are the chair and ski lifts. Because of them, I have knocked off one additional star in this review. Every lift was already old ten years ago, and it’s stayed the same (except the new cableway). They are many generations behind those of European or North-American ski resorts, and I suspect that they were bought second-hand from them. Some of the chair lifts are so slow that would have difficulties in keeping up with a funeral.. They also seem to stop much more often than in other places: it is almost impossible to have a ride without at least one stop, often more. And when they stop, they usually take a long time to resume moving; if there is wind chill, as it is often the case, be prepared… You end up wasting a lot of your day on, or in front of, those wrecks. In sum, my recommendations are the following: • If you live in Santiago, it is great to have such a place a two-hour drive away from home • If you live in any other place, you really want to have some ski between June and September and don’t mind having to pay dearly for that, you should definitely consider Valle Nevado • In all other cases, go to Europe or North America: you’ll sky more, have better facilities, and pay much less for that.

review_text: During a recent trip to Santiago, we hired Zerando Chile for a private tour with a group of 18 people. Unfortunately, our experience was far below expectations. The company promotes itself on Instagram with promises of a high quality service, but what we received was completely different. First, the vans provided for the tours were in bad condition, nothing similar to what was presented during the hiring. The guides, who should enrich our experience with information about local history and culture, showed total unpreparedness. Instead of receiving detailed and engaging explanations, we have been running from one place to another, with little or no contextualization. This lack of professionalism made the walks, which should be pleasant, extremely stressful. In addition, we contracted three tours with Zerando Chile, and in all of them we faced problems. On the Tour of Concha y Toro, for example, we asked for a Guide who spoke Portuguese, but when we got there, the Reservation was in Spanish. This only aggravated everyone's frustration. Worse, after we were all in the van, we had to make an unexpected stop at a person's house to pick up the reservations, which further highlighted the agency's disorganization. We also had a serious problem with the return time. We were informed of a timetable, but when we arrived at the venue, they said we needed to come back earlier, alleging a typing error. It became clear that this excuse was not true. In short, our group of 18 people was extremely dissatisfied with the services provided by Zerando Chile. review_text: We were fairly desperate to see penguins and had to extend our stay in la Serena by 1 more night as national parks in Chile are all closed on Mondays. As we hadn't booked a tour because of the price we instead decided to freestyle it. We took the only morning bus to Punta Churros at 9am from la Serena. The journey was fairly scenic but after about an hour of tarmac we then had to persevere another hour of off-road. We arrived in the fishing port and bought a ticket each for the boat tour around the islands at 10.000 pesos each from the little ticket office. We were then introduced to ur captain who claimed to be the best as they put the boat in the water. 8 of us waited around for 30 mins as the captain insisted we needed 10 people to pay otherwise we wouldn't do the trip. Eventually we all chipped in another 2.500 pesos each so that we could leave and return before 3pm to catch the only afternoon bus back to la Serena. The boat ride took just over 2hrs in which we saw sea lions, sea otters, pelicans, dolphins and most importantly penguins. Penguins are awesome! The landscape is also incredible. It is worth noting that the tour is very casual and all in Spanish but you do get looked after and you see all the same stuff that you would see on one of the more pricey tours. Upon returning to the port we still had time to eat some chips for lunch before catching the bus back to La Serena. Overall we paid about 21.000 each for the trip and I believe it was completely worth it!

review_text: My family (comprised of middle-aged me plus two college-aged “children”) contacted Into the Wild in search of an outdoor activity in Patagonia. I corresponded many times with Gonzalo who was professional, informed and flexible from start to finish. He was clearly motivated to help my family to find the best fit excursion while offering suggestions when appropriate. He offers a variety of excursions, including several different treks. We ended up signing up with Gonzalo for a single day long trek to the Base of the Torres. We would be visiting during the so-called “shoulder season” when the weather can be iffy, and Gonzalo had lots of useful advice on what to bring and how to layer clothing appropriately. For the day of the hike, he handled every detail including preparing a delicious lunch that he carried himself during the hike. During the hike, when I realized that I was not going to be able to finish the full hike with any comfort, Gonzalo was happy to discuss options without any pressure or judgement. I decided to stop after about two hours and wait in a very comfortable lodge (with bathrooms and heat and an amazing view) while my adult kids and Gonzalo completed the hike to the Base of the Torres. They picked me up again on the return trip. It was a win-win situation, one that might not have been possible had our guide not been as professional and flexible. We are grateful to have found Gonzalo and Into the Wild. He was an excellent guide and struck the perfect balance in his communications, offering tidbits of insight and information here and there but not so much that the silence and beauty of the wild was disrupted. These day long hikes that include hotel pick-up and drop-off are LONG days and Gonzalo maintained his great attitude the entire time, even with our perhaps too frequent requests for potty and rest stops! Thankfully, Gonzalo was always heads up about the nature around us and even knew the stats on safety with pumas in the neighborhood. Good thing too,as a puma joined us for the final half mile or so of our day’s hike. Quite a thrill! If we are lucky enough to return to Patagonia in the future, we will definitely seek out Gonzalo for excursions and hopefully more than just one!

review_text: Great day out by micro from the rural bus terminal in Ancud. I knew from my guidebook that tours were only half an hour and the guides more enthusiastic than knowledgeable (and only speak Spanish). But it was great fun - our guides Luis and Eduardo were very entertaining - I went out twice it was such fun. As well as the penguins we saw a sea otter, which was a wonderful experience. There are so many birds to see - pelicans, Flightless steamer birds, kelp geese and gulls, red legged cormorants and turkey vultures, to name a few. The bus arrives just before 2pm, and doesn't come back til around 5.30. There are clifftop walks - the views are stunning - a restaurant at the end of the beach that serves cheap, tasty empanadas. If you want to head back it's usually easy to find a lift with another tourist, which is what I did after lunch, a second tour and a walk.

review_text: Me and my boys love skiing. It is difficult for us to not ski from April through December. We found the perfect cure, skiing in Valle Nevado, Chile in August. I have skied in several continents and I have to say, Valle Nevado is certainly at the top of the list. If you have difficulties with altitude, be warned, you are at heights not very common in the US. I think our hotel which is at the base sits at around 11,000 feet. As you take the lifts, you are skiing in the 13,000 to 14,000 feet elevation. Skiing is spectacular. If you don't absolutely love skiing, I would think twice about heading there. To be honest, there really is nothing to do but ski for 8 days. If you absolutely love skiing, head down to Valle Nevado. A quick warning, I found this place as, if not more expensive than Vail and the Alps. There are people who advocate day trip here from Santiago. My thought on this? Don't. The road is crazy, I have never in my life seen anything like it. You have to see it to believe it. Go there and stay a week and ski your butt off!!! Henry, Like many North Americans you've discovered how to get your ski fix in the summer -- Valle Nevado! The road to Farallones (Valle Nevado) is windy however by the year 2016 half the turns will be removed and the entire road widened and repaved (new pavement and wider turns are ready for 2014). Many people come for the day, in fact most Santiaguinos come for the day. Valle Nevado's altitude (hotel complex) is at just under 10,000 feet, and the highest lift goes to 12,000 feet. Like Colorado, many skiers will feel the altitude on day one but by the next day they are usually acclimatized. As for cost, it really depends on the fluctuation of the pesos vs. the dollar. If you're looking to save, there are grocery stores at the base of the hill to stock up before you arrive at the resort. Again, thanks for your post and hope to see you this year! Customer Relations

review_text: The Museum of Memory & Human Rights (Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos) is shocking and confronting but excellent. This is the must do museum in Santiago. Take the green subway line to Quinta Nomal. The museum is on the left, across the road as you exit the station. You will have to check your bag and no photos are allowed. Also be advised that identification is required by at least one person in your party. The exhibits are in Spanish but you can hire an inexpensive interactive guide for around $2 (2000 pesos). Allow yourself 2-3 hours - trust me, you'll need it. Be warned, this museum is the Chilian equivalent of a visit to Auschwitz - something that may not be enjoyable but should definately be done to help prevent this ever happening again.

review_text: I am late with my review but I am sure not much changed since August/September time. I am actually sure that the Sorbac experience got even better! I have had the most amazing holiday while staying in Sorbac. The place is super chilled, everybody is very friendly and I cannot appraise the place high enough. I traveled solo and stayed in Sorbac for about 9 days. I felt there very relaxed, time stopped and I could just enjoy the stunning surroundings, the hospitality of every single person who works there and to feel like a member of a family, really. There was breakfast served each morning, you could have eggs, fruit, bread rolls. Lunch was always part of a tour and dinner could be ordered in the morning. Everything was prepared fresh and made with love. If I could I would stay there much longer, even though I went on every possible tour and also visited San Pedro a few times. I flew in Calama and there are two bus companies which know Sorbac very well so it is very easy and affordable to book a seat and they drop you off just in front of Sorbac. This hostel is located outside San Pedro which is about 35 min walk. I preferred the quiet location and tranquility of the place. I even stayed one or two days in the hostel, just relaxing and absorbing all the amazing experiences I had when visited possibly every tour they organized. The tour guides were always in good spirit, helpful, approachable and super friendly. I traveled from London and visited Easter Island prior to my trip to the Atacama and the whole experience changed me as a person. My travels were part of my healing journey, hence traveling on my own and Sorbac helped a massive amount to make feel happy and grateful for living on this wonderful planet. The nature in the Atacama is just stunning and I wish I could ever visit again. I would never get bored of Sorbac. I highly recommend staying at this hostel.

review_text: I arranged the trek and whale watching and penguin viewing out of Punta Arenas afterwards through Experience Chile. My 18 year old son and I did the 8 day Circuit trek without a guide but using Experience Chile to book all the transfers, refugios, campsites and meals - we camped 3 nights and stayed in refugios 4. This meant we didn't need to carry food or cooking gear which reduced our load and we ate and slept well on the trek. Everything went smoothly on our trip as the vouchers Experience Chile provided were all very clear and allowed us to make all the connections and follow the itinerary without problem. The trip was brilliant. The trek was sublime though the weather didn’t always cooperate. I would recopmmend this way of doing it as a halfway house between an expensive guided tour and the hardman approach of camping in tents and carrying all your food and cooking gear. The Circuit is not for the faint hearted though as on day 4 you climb 600 metres over a 1200m+ Pass which was extremely windy with snow falling and deep snow drifts and then drop over 100 metres. We walked for 10 hours on that day. The track is very muddy in parts but generally easy to follow the orange marker posts. The weather is cold and windy and it rained most days. But the views more than make up for any discomfort. We also did an amazing 1 day 2 night whale watching boat trip in the Magellan Straits at the end with Fitzroy Expeditions, also arranged through Experience Chile. It was a bit pricey but an amazing experience. I would recommend it if you can afford it.

Finally, at the Salar today, Ronaldo wowed us with his photography skills. He led a fun photo and video shoot on the salt flat. I highly recommend this agency and this guide for a tour of the Salar de Uyuni or other tours offered by them in the region.

review_text: We took this tour with Alvaro. The meeting place was much more convenient than the other tours out there, so that was a big plus. Without this tour you would miss the sights - case in point, we were staying at a hotel and little did we know around the corner was the bright, colorful passage way through Cerro Alegre. Lots of information about the city in a 3 hr tour. You make a pit stop half way through at an empanada place. There are 60 varieties to chose from and they are freshly made (so there is a bit of a waiting time). Along the tour you get to ride at least 2 elevators and see many streets. Alvaro talked to us and then gave us time in the different areas for pictures. Do not be afraid if the local street dogs follow you - they know the tour route and will follow the whole way. They do not bother you but you are asked not to feed or pet them to discourage their company.

review_text: I was looking forward to the tour as I had heard great reviews. Whilst enjoyable it didn't live up to my expectations. The tour is run fairly efficiently to a schedule (although we were collected 15-20mins late). Talking, looking through the telescopes then questions over hot chocolate. It's done this way so that 2 (& I was told, 3, but not sure if that's true) groups can be put through sequentially through the night. Also, the telescopes are set up to look at different objects & our guide was continually adjusting every telescope to ensure it was angled correctly, so it would be impractical to combine the talking & looking. The tour is informative & given by an enthusiastic guide. My mind started wandering as I felt there was too much talking initially. It felt impersonal in the same way a museum tour would i.e. I'm getting the standard spiel. This is possibly because of the group size, approx. 30 & time restrictions. We also didn't have much time for questions. That might be because our bus collected us late. Cost is USD 36 or CLP 18,000 (cash) & includes transport & a hot chocolate or tea. Try to book a few days in advance or be there at 12pm when they open. Worth doing if you have the time & money. If not, buy a bottle of wine, grab a torch & blanket, head 5mins outside the town & have your own star gazing tour. The Atacama is a wonderful place to appreciate the night sky.

review_text: can't say it was all that exciting or worthwhile. Made the tour arrangement through our hotel The Plaza San Francisco. We were first transported to a central tour area where we paid and got on the correct bus. It took FOREVER for our tour guide to figure out we had one extra guest who should have been on a different tour bus. Driving to the coast we got some pretty good information, both in English and Spanish. We did a stop at a beautiful winery that was not on my itinerary and thus took a half hour out of our day. Winery was very nice but it's kind of the equivalent of having a forced stop at a jewelry or rug store so I guess we lucked out with wine! Finally got to Vina Del Mar which was rather disappointing.....beach was filthy, flower clock was wacky, winding backwards and never showing the correct time. Spent way too long st both stops while being harassed to purchase from local vendors. Did a little tour of the area before being taken to Fellini's for lunch. We had it done hardly anything and now we were being asked to purchase a full lunch with drinks, dessert, etc that wasn't covered by the trip. We choose to walk around the town which doesn't have any shops it seems worth browsing. The casino is great if you need a bathroom! Be sure to bang your own water as the tour doesn't give you any. Finally onto Valparaiso! We go on a 1/2 h walk though a neighborhood above the town to see colorfully painted homes which was cute but not a lot of information, just a hustle to get to the funicular and ride down about 200 ft to the town square. Those who wanted to go on a boat ride for extra $ went with the guide while the rest were told when to meet up. There appeared to be several historical landmarks, buildings, etc but we weren't given any information nor encouraged to visit them. The area is a little scary and we were warned repeatedly to be aware. I kind of wonder why we were even left there by ourselves if it was so creepy. Back in the bus we go to return to Santiago and no more information from the guide. Can't say this was my most favorite tour ever or that I'd recommend it. review_text: It's hard to understand the good reviews of this place. It seems like an out of the way place where elementary school kids can picnic and run around the fields. This is fine and must be a great experience for students on school trips, but this place doesn't even resemble a botanical garden. It's a run down, difficult to find place just up the hill from an industrial area. There is no signage for local plants and there's no coherent design in the park. The dusty paths running through the park are used by cars and pedestrians and there's nothing interesting to look at along the way. It's also overrun with Eucalyptus trees, which are not native to Chile and are very flammable. A small forest fire broke out while we were there and we couldn't leave the grounds fast enough. It was difficult getting here via the Metro and bus through an industrial and polluted-looking area.

review_text: We were on an expedition cruise with Ponant on the ship Le Soleal from Valparaiso to Ushuaia via Puerto Montt, Castro and Puerto Natales. We sailed through the inland fjords, visited many glaciers with landings and then stopping at Cape Horn. Magnificent trip. We landed via zodiac on the very rocky "beach" and climbed to the top and were greeted by the commander of the lighthouse. The walkways are well done (although needing maintenance in some places) to get to the Albatross memorial and the other parts of the base. Weather was certainly rough and the wind would easy knock you off your feet if not careful. The experience was something to remember for some time. Certificates were awarded for "Rounding the Horn" and champagne opened with ceremony.

review_text: We took a ferry boat which seated 150-180 people and took almost 2 hours each way. There are other options such as the speed boat which takes 50 minutes and seats less. You get about an hour to walk a roped off path around the island. It is grassy, windswept and filled with penguins. It is very cool to see the penguins all over, many in burrows. Many were nesting when we were there in late January. There is a small lighthouse house there which you cannot enter. Do not pet the penguins as they can bite and inflict serious wounds, even if they come close to you. Thousands of penguins are here, I think, 200,000. They give off a bit of an odor. The ones with fur are babies, even though they are almost as big as adults.

review_text: If you don't have a love of awesome views, this might not be the place for you. Otherwise, it is a worthy trip up the funicular at the end of Bellavista up to the top. It was a steep climb for an affordable cost and then there was a little walking to get even higher. For the day, the weather was wonderful and the view was clear. However, sometimes, as Santiago is known for, its smog can obstruct your view. We had our own water, but water, juice, soda and snacks are costly up on Cerro San Cristóbal. There was a recent earthquake this month (March 2012) and so the cable cars were not available (and I was thankful as it looked like a dangling ski lift that could fall off the line with a strong wind). The entrance for both are on different sides of the hill. The funicular is accessible at the end of Pio Nono and you can also drive up. I hear hiking up may not be safe and some may also choose to bike up and down. The view is great and we made it with ample time to spare for a great view of the sunset. It's a nice leisure activity to do in Santiago and there are mountain on all sides. I hope you enjoy your view.

review_text: On the last day of our vacation to Santiago, Chile (August 21, 2018) my wife and I decided to take a market tour and cooking class with Uncorked. Our neighbor in Alexandria, VA recommended that we take a cooking tour during our time in Chile. I was skeptical, but I knew it was something my wife wanted to do. The company we initially booked through had to cancel last min. I searched Trip Advisor for alternatives and found Uncorked. They graciously added us to one of their tours and it may have been the highlight of our trip. The experience was very fun and educational. We learned about the various native meats and fruits found in Chilean cuisine, as well as those food influences coming from neighboring countries like Peru. Later, we learned how to make classic Chilean dishes with delicious and easy to remember recipes in a beautiful, clean, and modern kitchen. review_text: Pablo Neruda is, of course, one of the world's greatest poets (Nobel Prize 1971). He also expressed his art in the three houses he owned in Chile, including the delightful, charming and highly eccentric La Chascona. In 1953, Neruda started to build this house in Santiago, for Matilde Urrutia, his secret love in that time. He called the house “La Chascona” in her honour, that was the nickname he gave her due to her abundant flowing red hair. Matilde remember an afternoon in which they were walking by the neighbourhood, that today is called Bellavista, they found a property for sale, at the bottom of the San Cristobal hill. It seemed covered by blackberries and it had a sharp slope “we were bewitched for a water sound – Matilde wrote in her memories -, it was a real waterfall which came from the channel, at the top of the lot”. Both of them were filled with enthusiasm and decided to buy it. Later, in his poem “La Chascona”, from the book La Barcarola, Neruda evoked the “water that runs writing in its language”, and the blackberries “which guard the place with its bloody branches”. Tours allow you to step into the extraordinary mind of the poet whose eclectic designs earned him the label "organic architect." Winding garden paths, stairs, and bridges lead to the house and its library stuffed with books, a bedroom in a tower, and a secret passageway. Scattered throughout are collections of butterflies, seashells, wineglasses, and other odd objects that inspired Neruda's tumultuous life and romantic poetry. Don't miss this wonderful little gem. You can also visit Neruda's other two houses which are not too far from Santiago on the coast. One is called Isla Negra and the other is called La Sebastiana. Ask your hotel for details of seeing these houses.

When we arrived at the vineyard, the driver took a long time to hand us the entry bracelet and our tour which was 15:40 started at 16:00 and we lost the beginning of the tasting. I asked about the premium jackets and moon boots advertised on their Instagram and the attendant told me that the supplier did not deliver, that is, they advertise something that they do not own and there is not even clothes for everyone as they disclose. I also couldn't rent the glasses, because they told me it was over. The day I went, Laise was there recording beautiful videos to fool customers and I spoke directly to her about the company’s misleading advertising and she said she was gonna fix it, but she left me long waiting until another employee came to talk to me and my husband and told me that the only thing she could do was give me a miserable discount on the rental price, but they didn’t refund me as promised. Because of all these problems, we arrived very late in the park and took a lot of queues to get in and up the cable car. The worst thing is that they marked the turn for 15:15 and the park closed only at 17: 00, that is, we lost two hours. Even arriving at the time set by the guide, our van left there only at 16:00. The tour to Valparaíso and Viña Del Mar was carried out in an old, uncomfortable and noisy van. The guide does not speak Portuguese as advertised and rather a ‘Portunhol’ and did not explain almost anything about the places we visited, it was all quick and superficial, so that we arrived early at the restaurant that they take us to lunch. review_text: Maurizio of Magical Tours provided us with an exceptional experience. We attended 2 tours led by him. A shorter tour to St Laura and Humberston and then Pica before returning to Iquique. The following day we did an extended tour into the alti Plano and left the tour at Colchane on the Chile/Bolivian border and crossed over to Pisiga the next day. Maurizio's knowledge of the economic, political and social history of Chile combined with his archeological and geological knowledge of the region provided us with an enriched experience. Maurizio speaks English as well as Spanish and although we were the only English language speakers on each of these tours and he never neglected us. He was very warm and personable and took special care of us by arranging our Colchane accommodation and even provided us with his contact details a la 'phone a friend' at the time that we left the tour should we encounter any difficulties with our border crossing. A person of integrity and passionate about the landscape and society that his business is showcasing we have no hesitation in recommending his tours.

review_text: An exceptional day hike. My guides, Roma and Mario, picked me up from my hotel in Santiago at 0730 in a 4WD. We got to the park entrance at 0930. The trail consists of a 8km gentle uphill hike (from 1900m to 2600m) to the glacier. The path is well marked, and there are no difficult or dangerous parts. Loose stones and gravel make hiking boots advisable, but I did it easily in trainers. The scenery is spectacular. Roma and Mario were wonderful - they provided nice food, water and endless patience with taking pictures. The hike took 6 hours in total, 3 hours from the start to the glacier, and 2 hours to walk down, and 1 hour for rests, and then 2.5 hours drive to get back to Santiago by 1800. Hislandes Aventuras were very professional throughout, and I felt very comfortable, looked after and free to go at the pace I wished. An excellent day out if you only have 1 day in Santiago. I highly recommend both Hislandes Aventuras and the hike.
