review_text: Rather than take the more famous trail (from Hosteria Las Torres to Campamento Torres), where hundreds of tourists and locals make the pilgrimage to the base of the Torres, we decided to take a side trail that begins just south of the entrance and registration area at Guardería Laguna Amarga (on the northeast side of the park). The hike we took lasted about four to five hours depending on how many side trails you took. Our hike first led us to the painted rocks formations (Pinturas Rupestres), which was a signed side trail which branched off the main trail to Lago Sarmiento. After visiting the rocks, there is a trail which returns you to the Lago Sarmiento trail without backtracking. During our hike we came across four other (guided) hiking groups. While our view of the famous Torres del Paine may not have been quite as spectacular, we had a relatively quiet hike, which we enjoyed very much. It felt like we had the whole park to ourselves, sharing it with the ñandús (ostrich-type birds) and guanacos (llama-type animals) grazing and frolicking on the trails. At the end of the trail near the lake there was a ranger station with bathroom facilities. The other bathroom facilities we used were located at the registration area. Parking our rental car was a little tricky, as there was no designated parking for private cars so we just found some space away from the parked buses. The giant tour buses parked right outside the registration entrance area, but as we arrived early (around 9:45 am) we were able to park where we saw a couple other cars. There was no parking fee, but it felt like we took a chance parking where we did. After our hike we came back to our car and drove through the park taking in the scenery, exiting at the south end of the park (on highway Y-290, which returns you to Ruta 9 near the Monumento Natural Cueva del Milodón). Be prepared to be driving through miles and miles of gravel/dirt roads, more or less from highway Y-156 where it branches off of highway Y-150 until you get to the Monumento. It's doable in a standard car, but something with higher clearance might have made it less stressful. Be sure to bring plenty of water and snacks, as well as your passport and CLP$18,000 per adult in high season (about USD$25) for admission to the park, and prepare for a bit of a paperwork scramble as part of the admission process (bring your own pen if you can). The Servicio Nacional de Turismo office at Av. Pedro Montt 19 in Puerto Natales provided good, helpful advice and maps which really helped us make the most of our day trip to the park. It was a good day visit for us.

review_text: Some friends of mine and I joined group prior to leaving home that had been organised for when the Norwegian Sun would be in Puerta Chacabuco. We met onboard and all left the ship at the same time by tender so as we would be ready to leave as soon as possible. Unfortunately there were two people missing so this took up some time but we were able to go and look at the local handicrafts that were adjacent to our buses. We soon got underway and looked around the local area, visiting a larger town nearby and some waterfalls. Whilst there we saw a man pulling a huge fish from the river - he certainly had difficulty getting it into his van! The scenery en-route was just stunning with mountains in the distance still covered in snow, and plenty of trees in blossom. The main purpose of this shore excursion was to visit a local farm in the Simpson Valley and enjoy their typical BBQ'd lamb lunch and watch traditional dancing. After crossing the river on foot via a small bridge we were welcomed by a man dressed in local costume with a welcoming drink of pisco. The lamb was cooking around the fire and smelled delicious. The farm is family owned and was organised by them - they were the servers and the dancers. After a lovely meal, with plenty of lamb ( or a vegetarian empanada if you were vegetarian) we were entertained by the dancers, showing several different styles of traditional dancing. Suddenly it was time to return to the ship and our visit to Puerta Chacabuco was over, so we took another scenic ride back to the ship. The enPatagonia tour was certainly well worth going on and I would recommend it thoroughly. Book through Anne at enpatagonia@gmail.com - you will tell her if you'd like the lamb or vegetarian option when booking and pay via PayPal or credit card.

review_text: Our visit to this national park on the outskirts of Punta Arenas was our best experience of our visit. You need not book a tour; it is easily accessible by taxi (the rangers will call a taxi for your return; fares were 5800 CLP and 4400 CLP for our trips). We were greeted by friendly rangers who outlined the hiking options, then guided us to the appropriate trailhead. Entrance is 5000 CLP for foreigners, and 2500 CLP for Chilean nationals. We chose a 2 hour loop trail which took us to a spectacular overlook of the city and the Strait. En route, we passed through amazing forests with trees covered in a white moss. The trail was in excellent repair and was very well marked. This was a wonderful excursion, especially for a Sunday when most everything in Punta Arenas was closed.

review_text: My wife and I hired Mauricio Masserano, the Ultimate Wine Lover, and Professor of Wine!!! Because I was on a business trip with little time for recreational activities, my wife and I decided to invest in a private tour, to really see what local foods tasted like and of course to explore some amazing Chilean vineyards. So we went with Mauricio, who picked us up at our hotel and provided private transportation, all day. Such a time saver, especially when traveling in a foreign country. His driver, Claudio, was a first-class driver. Such a super guy. Mauricio not only took us to private vineyards where the general public is not able to enter, but explained everything from why Chile has the best wine to ocean currents that enable Chile to produce the best wines. It was like Wine-making class 101. He also has a PASSION for what he does, which very few people can say. And it's completely obvious. Mauricio, who is also a foodie, took us to some local places to eat authentic Chilean food. From Empanadas right out of the oven, to having hot tea and coffee in his own home. He really made us feel welcomed. That said, we recommend Mauricio as your official private tour guide if you go to Santiago. You will not regret it!! he is the best tour guide we have ever hired. We love this guy. Hope your experience is as enjoyable as ours was. Review of: Unique Wines In Colchagua Valley

review_text: No one tells you that you will be super confused when you arrive. You pull in and there is a small booth where you pay for your tickets ($15.000/adult or $9.000/adult after 2pm on a weekday). Then you drive down a dirt road to a parking lot and you’re like...where is it? There is then a 500 m easy trail that you walk down and descend into a canyon where you will see the thermal springs. Be aware that it’s about 11,000 ft elevation (San Pedro is about 8,000ft) so you will feel it if you are jogging between pools (it’s chilly!) or when you walk back up to the parking lot. There are about 7-8 pools that are each a bit different, but all very warm. You must bring your own towels, locker lock, drinks, snacks, etc. There is no store or anything. It is windy so going between pools is pretty chilly, definitely bring a towel or robe to wrap around yourself while walking! In all, this was totally worth it, and absolutely stunning. The water was clean and clear and warm, rushing through each pool constantly. There are little built in waterfalls as well so it is very picturesque. We spent 3.5 hours there without realizing how fast time was flying by. Bring some lotion for your body afterwards as the minerals do dry out your skin! Enjoy! (No WiFi)

review_text: The W is 5 stars. It’s amazingly beautiful and we were fortunate to have good weather. The Refugio’s food and accommodations are reasonable given their remoteness and the daily turnover. We had Chile Nativo customize a 5-night trip for 4 couples. We hiked west to east to avoid walking into a prevailing headwind. We stayed at Hotel Lago Grey and took their ferry to Refugio Grey. The hotel restaurant is good but the hotel wasn’t worth the additional cost ($450/room). Be aware that their ferry won’t run if the winds are high. We stayed inside at Grey, Paine Grande, and Cuernos. The Refugio’s all have bunk beds and the rooms are for 2-6 people. The 2-4 person cabins at Cuernos were wonderful. Only permanent tents were available this year at Chileno but worth staying there because the location sets you up for the hike to the towers. We left about 7:00 and hardly anyone else there because the dawn hikers were gone and the hikers from Central weren’t there yet. The amount of food provided exceeded our needs and of sufficient quality and sometimes the entrees were good. Chileno, which is supplied by horseback, put the most effort into presentation. We enjoyed the food at Cuernos and Chileno (served) more than Paine Grande and Grey (buffet). We did not like the lunch sandwiches because of the amount of bread to filling ratio and cream cheese (?) condiment. Vegetarian sandwiches (hummus or veggie patty) were slightly better. Next time, we would try to opt out of the lunches and bring snacks and scavenge from breakfast. We didn’t need to carry more than 1 L of water and did not treat any of the water. We had no gastrointestinal issues in our group from the food or water. Shower water ran out Paine Grande at 6:00. We had no issues with showers at the other Refugios. Chile Nativo was willing to customize our tour. However, the execution did not go smoothly. Our emailed itinerary and the app provided by Chile Nativo showed that all of our meals would be provided as we intended. Our first day, they forgot to give us a box lunch but they refunded this cost. We also learned that we hadn’t payed for dinner at Hotel Lago Grey, so we had to buy dinner. Breakfast was included with our hotel room but a boxed lunch was not. There was a problem with our reservation at Paine Grande but my Spanish was inadequate to understand what the problem was. We were provided meals and rooms but we were not placed together in the rooms and 1 couple was put in different rooms. At Chileno, they told us that we had made our meal reservations at Central (2 hr hike away) even though we were staying at Chileno. Fortunately, Chileno was able and willing to provide us meals. Chileno has limited stocks because this Refugio is supplied by horseback whereas the other Refugio’s can be restocked by boat. I do not know if Chile Nativo or the Refugio’s made the errors but each blamed the other. Thank you for your detailed feedback. We're glad you enjoyed the W Trek and that our customized itinerary helped create a great experience. We appreciate your insights on the accommodations and meals. We sincerely regret the reservation and meal issues you faced. We’re reviewing what happened to improve coordination with our partners. Your feedback is invaluable, and we hope to welcome you again for an even smoother adventure. The Chile Nativo Team

It took us about 6 hours to get to the king penguin areas, and we spend just under 2 hours there and then took us about 5-6 hours to return. The tour stopped at some other places which is not quite as interesting but I guessed it was needed for people to stretch their legs. We even got a pisco sour at the last stop. I love penguins and I find this a worth while trip despite the long travel. I didn't want to rent a car so this was a good option for me to see the penguins. The guide we had was good enough, not much English was spoken but he tried his best. We understood each other with sign language / translation app. Note - we saw a tiny penguin chick there, it looks like some of the penguins are still incubating their eggs.

review_text: This could be a very basic, but adventurous experience for people with an open mind. If it was not for the animal cruelty onboard (see last paragraph), this trip would have received a high rating from me, although your comfort expectations should be low. This is what we experienced during our voyage from Puerto Natales to Puerto Montt: Check-in is a day before departure at the main bus station of Puerto Natales, during the day. This is a few kilometers from the city centre. Friendly lady helped us check in our lugage, which we found onboard in our cabin. You have to return to the bus station at 9 pm the evening prior to your departure, to be driven to the harbour and ship. Not very practical, as there is nothing to do at the bus station between check in and pick-up, and the city centre is closer to the harbour then the bus station. When reading the rest of this and other reviews, bear in mind you are joining a FREIGHT ship, that takes some (approx. 100) passengers. Get your expectations right! Having said that, Navimag really sells this trip as a cruise on their website. They should either downgrade their descriptions or upgrade their standard onboard. Boarding: We were driven onboard and personally escorted to our cabins. The Eden ship is from 1987 and is/looks old and rusty, and so do the cabins, which are very basic, with bunk beds, but ok. Rooms have sink and window. Cleanliness is not too good, some bed sheets have stains. Safety briefing: Persy our purser (no joke) is a funny guy who gave us useful information about the ship. This guy has humor and told quite a lot about wildlife and things to see along the way. The safety briefing itself was poor, shown on bad televisions without sound. Interior: As said, an old and rusty ship. Sitting and dining room is in what looks mostly like a cantina, with only a few windows to the side. This ship does not have a bar (no alcohol sold, or to be brought onboard, although smugling is widely accepted), nor a good sitting area with views. On deck five, you can go to an outside area in front of the ship, which has some benches. Great views, if the weather is not too bad. Departure: Well. Rembember you have to check in a day prior to departure. Boarding is at 9pm, departure at 6 am the next morning. The ship has four car decks, which were loaded with dusins of trailers, carefully secured with metal chains. This process takes about 5 hours, executed between 11 pm and 4 am, while you try to sleep in your cabin. TRY! It is a metal and very loud ship. It sounded like the trailers were driving through the cabins, while metals chains where banged against the walls and floors. Seriously, to me it seemed like trying to camp on a highway inside a tunnel. Departure time was delayed (which is apparently very common) from 6 am to 6 pm in the afternoon, due to high winds. It can be risky to leave a pier in high winds. Although Persy the purser is a jolly guy, he was not much seen during this time and information distribution was at a minimum. After 12 hours, we suddenly left the pier in the same fierce winds we have had all day. It seemed like the head quarters had done some financial calculations.... Food: Very basic, but edible, if you have low expectations. Very simple but ok breakfast. Horrible coffee and "juice", as most places I have seen in Argentina and Chile. Warm lunch and dinner, with set menu. Vegetables, potatoes or rice, and meat or fish. The pasta was good. Hand sanity is not good. People are not encouraged to wash their hands prior to dinner and some food, like bread, people can just take with their bare hands. The kitchen personal however used plastic gloves. They were very friendly and efficient. Service & Facilities Friendly staff! Beds were made up every second night (although not cleaned). There is little entertainment onboard. A little cinema room shows very bad, downloaded movies, not suitable for all ages. Prepare for quite some hours of playing cards in the cantine. Besides Chile CNN (in Spanish), there is no TV or internet, which I liked personally. Nice to chat to other travellers and meet new people. Persy gives some lectures on wildlife and things to do after Puerto Montt ("I hate that city, really hate it" as he said, but he came with lots of other good recommendations). Bar sells some soda and chocolate, but no alcohol. A bingo night on the last evening. You can visit the bridge and the officers where very friendly and keen to tell about navigation. Haven't got a clue who the captain is, never seen the guy. The showers are ok with good pressure and hot water, but bring flipflops. The floor and ceilings look old and not too clean. The shared toilets are horrifying. The system can't handle toilet paper. This has to be thrown in garbage bins. People ignore this, so the system got clogged at least four times during our 4 day trip. In the morning, I found the toilets filled to the edge with brown water and floating excrements, while the bathroom floor was flooded with yellow water. On the last evening, people are asked to fill out feedback sheets. I really hope they do something with the feedback they receive. Scenery: A lot of attention goes to poor standards, so remember to focus on the stunning scenery along the way. We saw the beautiful fjords, snow, seals, dolphins, albatrosses and whales. Persy gave some information, but more interpretation could be done. The fact that the PA system was not working, did not help. There should have been, but was not any information board with map and current location and other interesting facts. Again: the stunning scenery and the funny poor standard onboard could have turned this journey into one big adventure for not too much money (700 USD) for me. Animal cruelty: However, the way the ship carries animals changed everything to me and makes me never want to recommend this trip to anyone. The cows and horses are brough onboard in open trailers, with way too many animals in way too little space. This would have been against all regulations in Europe, and might/should also be against any regulations anywhere else. I don't care about my own comfort, but do not treat animals like dirt! Although they get water and grass, they NEVER get to move around and have to stand still, packed together for more than 100 hours (and how long have they been transported before and after the boat trip?). They were trampling, kicking and biting each other and looked miserable. The stench of manure and amoniac penetrated the whole ship. I don't care for myself too much, but the animals must have had a miserable, horrible, traumatic experience. I am surprised no animals died. The crew really did not seem to care.
title: A missed opportunity to become an attraction for the adventurous, due to animal cruelty

review_text: I had heard a lot about this museum before visiting, and it definitely lived up to expectations. It's hard to describe as it is so eclectic, but really covers Chilean and South American history/culture very well. The pieces were all very well-chosen to illustrate each theme. The rooms were all very well set-up and enjoyable to walk around. The lighting and presentation was impressive compared to other museums I've visited. We only had 2.5 hours to visit, but my recommendation would be to visit in the morning to do a quick tour to see what it there, have lunch, and return to go back to the sections you really liked. I think each ticket is good for 24 hours. We went with my in-laws, who don't speak any Spanish, but they agreed with this review and still enjoyed it just as much as we did. Overall, I would visit again and highly recommend this museum.

review_text: I had pretty much decided that this cruise, booked months in advance, was not going to make me happy. First, there was the steep price, then a long walk to the beach in the wind and rain, then an exciting adventure climbing from the galloping floating dock to a pitching zodiac in a bulky life vest, for a splashing ride out to what looked to be a small tugboat out of a children's book only a lot older and worse for wear (there is a new boat coming). Then they crowded 50 people inside – full load – with the windows rain-streaked and fogged over so you can barely see out. And this was for three hours? Fortunately, about halfway out, the captain announced it okay to go topside – up the ladder – and everybody else went out in the wind and rain. Only when we got to the glacier (much further away than it appears; they’re BIG) did I go out on the lower deck (relatively alone) and then on up. Surprisingly, there was enough room for everybody and great views – close to the glacier – with the rain mostly stopped and the glacier's high face blocking some of the wind. The tour then went around to the other two arms of the glacier, not visible from the dock or hotel, and started back. The fantastic shapes carved in the ice by wind and water, plus the incredible blue color, engaged the imagination and the camera. Then it was back inside for the long ride with wet windows, pitching zodiacs, etc. And did I mention the swinging bridge, capacity six persons? If you have seen glaciers up close before, you can probably save the 3-4 hours this trip takes and simply admire the magnificent glaciers elsewhere in the park.

review_text: We booked the volcan Villarrica tour with them (80 000 CHP). The day before we tried the shoes and the pants to check the size. Then we were given a box where we put all the material they gave to us : shoes, gaiters, pants, jackets, gloves, backpack, ice ax, etc. The day of departure we had to be at 6:30am at the office to get prepared. We left our personal bag in a dedicated box. We took a van to go to the base of the chairlift (about 1h drive). We reached the parking and get prepared. Because that day it was too windy, the chairlift was close so everybody has to walk. It is important to consider this possibility as it adds 1h of walk (total 5 hours). We were 12 and had 4 guides. We did short breaks of 1-2 min to drink regularly and longer breaks of 10-15min every hour. The guides reminded us to drink and add suncream. Remember that the ozone has some holes in this area. It was very sunny, a bit windy. The walk is difficult but not impossible. Following the guide rythm with the breaks, we made it to the top without feeling too tired. A person of the group didn't make it as she was too slow during the first part and so one of the guide stayed with her. On the way back, sliding down the volcan was fun. Netherveless, if you have back problems, it can be bumpy so be careful. When we returned to the office, we were offered some juice or beer which was nice. We really enjoyed our day with Summit Chile.

review_text: Took this trip February 6-12 from Punta Arenas to King George Island. The hotel in PA was a mix of tired fixtures and outdated furniture and a very modern vibe to the bar and elevator lobby. On the plus side, the hotel Cabo de Hornos was close to the sea and on the plaza, main town square. It's very windy in P A at that time of year. Our room was very hot and there was only a tip-in window which, when opened, amplified the wind in strength and in noise, and added to the noise from the plaza. The free breakfast buffet and made-to-order egg station in the restaurant made up for the mundane room. We didn't choose this hotel and I don't think that Antarctica21 should in the future. The experience of going to the airport and waiting for many hours to actually fly to King George Island on our appointed day was also stressful. When we finally boarded the plane, it was a very tight fit for everyone, with minimal legroom. It was cute though, painted to resemble a penguin! The flight took about 2 1/2 hrs. On arrival we got off the plane and proceeded to walk on gravel for 1/2 hr in the heavy rubber knee-high boots we needed to get into the rubber Zodiac rafts waiting on the beach, where we could see our floating home for 5 nights, the Hebridean She, waiting in the distance. Once on the ship, there was only time to drop off our outerwear and go to dinner, but the ship appeared to be nicely appointed and our stateroom was quite roomy. Dinner was served in a much smaller dining room than a typical cruise ship. Food was delicious and service exemplary! Everyone of the 70 passengers were excited for our first morning and we had been instructed as to the importance of dressing with multiple layers of warm clothing and waterproof outerwear. After a rocky night as the ship made up lost time crossing open water, we woke surrounded by snow covered shores, glaciers and icebergs. As would become a routine twice a day, we were notified by the PA system to prepare for disembarking and going ashore in 1/2 hr. When we loaded 10 to a Zodiac at the stern, the reality hit--we were in Antarctica! The negatives of the hotel and airplane were forgotten. A short boat ride and we were climbing off the raft and onto a rocky and snow-covered foothill teeming with Gentoo penguins--adults and many youngsters. Our Zodiac driver was also a naturalist and guide as were all of the drivers. Soon the people from the ship spread out, some moving faster and some taking their time to absorb the stunning views. There were no other groups or boats, no buildings-- nothing but nature. Every day after that was in a different cove or a different island, returning to the ship for lunch and dinner. Passengers had an opportunity to meet the others in a relaxing casual atmosphere and share photo questions and tips. One day before lunch, anyone who wanted to could take a quick swim in the 35 degree water--many brave souls did the Polar Plunge. On other days we saw humpback whales from the Zodiac and one morning a pod of orcas swam alongside the ship for a couple of hours. We landed on many islands, some with big boulders, some covered in glacial ice, some with stones and snowpack. Some in our group snowshoed up a to a mountain ridge while others kayaked. Always we observed penguins, Gentoo and chinstrap, fur seals and birds, occasionally some derelict buildings from the past and whales. Eventually we had to reverse the trip and return to that airplane and the hotel and to civilization. But I'll never forget the majestic scenery and the entertaining animals and how peaceful this piece of Earth is. Antarctica21 has now partnered with three hotels in Punta Arenas, Chile and they are considered to be of the best hotels in this city. Details of our airplane are provided on our website and brochure as we do try and prepare our guests for their trips as best as possible. However, it's important to point out that safety is always our number one priority, and taking that into consideration, the AVRO RJ Aircraft, which we use to fly to Antarctica, is a high-wing aircraft particularly suitable for landing on very short runways, like the one on King George Island, Antarctica. review_text: This Vinyard is beyond beautiful!! The staff immediately made us feel welcome!! My husband and I dropped in on a weekday, so it was not busy. Neither of us speak English but we quickly became friends with Alvero whom has spent some time in the states. We asked to do a tour because we really wanted to learn more about the wine making process… especially organic!! The tour started off in the grape fields with Alverero and Nancy. Nancy is one of the wine makers. She is a wealth of knowledge. There they taught us about what is so special about their location and how it affects what kind of grapes they grow. They explained the process of when to pick grapes, what kind of sun and water they need. How they basically grow and care for the grapes. There is much dedication to this tedious process and they do not cut corners! To our surprise the owner Patricio showed up a little into our tour. He took over for Nancy. We were then taken into the barn where they process the grapes. Patricio is very passionate about wine making… especially the organic wines. He spent nearly 3 hours of his time with us. I asked him “why organic wine” his answer might surprise you. It is a touching reason, but It is his story to tell! I encourage you to do the tour with him and ask why! I will only say this man has a heart and passion for wine, people and to make a difference! To make a change! He is definitely taking making organic wine to the next level! Trust me when I tell you…. There is a significant difference in the taste of an organic wine! It tastes much more pure and smooth. We also stayed for lunch in their lovely restaurant area. This vineyard is pure Romance!!! The tour pickup was set at 6.45am from our hotel, 10 minutes before I got a WhatsApp notification that they are running 5 mins behind schedule. On the way Salvador played amazing music from his phone BT and kept telling us the name of the band and significance of the music to area we were in. Salvador then hosted us for a lovely picnic with wine and cheese. We ended our tour in a chocolate factory with really good sweet treats. review_text: Our driver Orlando, and our guide Helmut, provided our group of 12 with a simply AMAZING day long shore excursion tour that encompassed many of the sights that the Arica Chile region has to offer. We were met at the main port gate and then traveled down the coast a bit to walk along the rocky coastline on a paved path to view the Cuevas de Anzota. Then it was back into the city for a view of the surrounding area from the top of Morro de Arica ~ a prominent hill that towers over 450 feet above sea level. From the Morro, we went to a local market, which was simply amazing with all sorts of fruits and vegetables available, as well as many other items. This particular market was one one of the cleanest I have ever seen in Latin America. While at the market, Helmut bought some coca leaves, which were used in an informal ceremony on one of the high overlooks near San Miguel de Azapa and Poconchile. Our extensive tour took in an archeological museum with local mummies on display as well as a relaxing visit to a hummingbird sanctuary in the Azapa Valley. We were also able to view several of the petroglyphs high up on the valley mountain walls. From there, it was off to the village of Poconchile for a lunch of marvelous local Chilean food in a charming local eatery that is definitely NOT a tourist trap. Loved the meal! On our return to Arica, we circled back through the Lluta Valley to view the estuary there and its local birdlife. We returned to the port with plenty of spare time available to those who wanted to purchase souvenirs and local goods at nearby shops. All in all, a FANTASTIC day that really gave good oversight into the geography and history of this unique region. Our guide, Helmut, and driver, Orlando, were superb! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

review_text: Let's start off by saying that Kingston Family Vineyards has breaktaking views! It is absolutely worth seeing. The architecture is also notable and the service is quality. For those of you who only speak English, that is not a problem here. We did a lunch with wine pairings, which I was very excited about. The wines are good...nothing to write home about unfortunately, but that is obviously very subjective. The food, however, was a bit disappointing. I opted for the ceviche, the octopus and the steak. The ceviche was the best thing I tasted all day! The octopus was extremely chewy to the point that I left more than half of it on the plate. And the steak also didn't seem like the best cut of meat either- lots of fat and was marinated in something sweet. I was open to the unique flavor but the texture threw me off. The part that blew my mind at the end was the tab- 94,000 pesos ($122 USD)! I would expect those prices in Napa, but not here! It was substantially more expensive than any of the other vineyards in the region. My suggestion: definitely swing by but order a cheese board or snacks instead of the 4 course lunch and order your wine by the glass (ask for a tasting to make sure you like the wine first).

review_text: We always take a hop on hop off tour when we first arrive in a new city. This one is better than some, and a pretty good value for your money. We opted for the 2 day pass, $60.00 per person, which included the gondola ride up Cerro San Cristobal, and the funicular back down. The first day we just rode the 2 1/2 hour circuit, and decided which stops looked interesting. The stop at Plaza Armas, Cerro San Cristobal and the Mall stop after the Sky Tower are marked, the rest are not. Just be aware of where you get off of the bus as one will return every 30 minutes or so. They make you wear a wristband which really helps you to stand out as a tourist! We did not see anyone buy their ticket on the buses. We bought ours in the Central Mercado downtown. The audio was clear, but at times we either had not arrived at the topic of discussion, or had already passed it. Plan your time well as the busses stop at 6:00 p,m., so if you are not back at where you started, you will have to find alternative transport home. We stopped at the Sky Consentera, and Cerro San Cristobal, and along with a lunch, it was an 8 hour day. There is a great Jumbo grocery store in the Sky Center Mall which carries just about everything. review_text: Good afternoon! We went as a family, a couple and a son, to the astronomical tour in the city of San Pedro de Atacama, purchased through Tripadvisor. The tour itself was satisfactory, with images and teachings about astronomy. It turns out that three photos were taken with the Milky Way in the background, by the person responsible for presenting and transporting tourists, who said that we should send a request for the photos taken within a week, to receive them by email. He told us that the order could be made in Portuguese, English or Spanish. Well, we, my son and I, placed the orders in a timely manner, according to attached copies of email requests, but the photos were not sent, without any satisfaction in this regard. As for the email address to request the photos, the person in charge said to take a photo of a board with that address on it. As can be seen from the emails we sent and the photo of the painting, the address to which the order for the photos was made is strictly correct. The point is that these photos were the most eagerly awaited of the entire Atacama tour, since before the trip! So, the problem involves a terrible feeling of disappointment and moral damage, made worse by not having a single photo of the event because it was at night, which is why the concept we gave to the tour was TERRIBLE. We asked Tripadvisor to send this protest to the person responsible for the tour to resolve the problem, sending the three photos (numbers 1456, 1457, 1463). We would like to thank you in advance for the attention that will certainly be devoted to this matter. Terufumi Katayama Note: The purchase of the tour for three people was made in the name of Cézar Mitsuru Katayama, whose email address can be found in the attached email copy. Review of: Astronomical Tour with Guide and Pick Up San Pedro de Atacama

review_text: This channel (seno in spanish) is a large entry of the sea coming from the Strait of Magellan. Cold water and strong winds bringing sea lions and birds at the summer into the channel. The boat cruising the channel is an exceptional opportunity to get closer to these elements. After many photos and a collection of new perspectives you get comfortable to stay on deck and enjoy the breeze. A moment of peace surrounding us, in a total silence only broken by the noise of the boat engine. Inside the cabin a sample of a Babel tower with many different languages spoken as english, french, portuguese, german, chinese, spanish and others that you just listen as part of the natural elements with their peculiar sounds. Going back from the fjords, the view of Puerto Natales seems different. More familiar, after a full day trip into the boat. Exhaustive? Maybe, but a small price when compared to other silly things we use to make and spend our time living in the city. At the end of the day, body and soul are both claiming for a break, like a child after a full day playing in the garden. We became youth again in this scenario. Like the winds, birds, sea lions and glaciers aging in harmony in this place. Makes sense to call this place as "the last hope". If no other hope lasts, just be there and make the last hopes and wishes in a Patagonian summer day. Useless to spend more words trying to describe this magical place, better be there and see.

See as much as you can whilst in Patagonia, but if you have only one day in Puerto Natales, make sure this place is on your tour.

review_text: I would do this tour again, but it was not my favorite. (My favorites were Salar de Tara and Lagunas Miscanti and Miniques with Piedras Rojas.) The geysers are about an hour out of town, so even though they pick you up at 4:30am, bring a pillow for sleeping so you can get some more zzz's on the bus. Dress WARMLY. Honestly, I read this on every review and thought I was dressed for warmth, but wow it was cold. With no sunlight, you will be COLD. Gloves, scarf, hat, and coat are a MUST. I was still cold even with all of these things. Finally, don't expect any spectacular sunrise. (I thought we'd get beautiful colors.) The sun rises behind the mountains before you see it, so you don't get any of the pretty pinks and oranges of a sunrise. You're really just there super early in the dark so that you can see the steam from the geysers better. If you had to miss this tour, it wouldn't be the end of the world. Additionally, this is the one tour where I didn't necessarily felt like we needed the best tour group. Everyone goes there, and it seemed like everyone was getting the same information.

We decided to walk around the field instead and it was worth it. I recommend this place.

review_text: We just hiked, camped and prepared our own food for 6 nights and 7 days on the classic "W". There's lots written so I'll just give my general comments. Torres has everything from high-end lodges and spas to very basic campgrounds. Most of the advice you need to take with a grain of salt. Erratic Rock said no bugs and there were tons! Other information from them was completely inaccurate. Ask around! Because of them, I took extra shoes for river crossings and didn't need them (check the rain the past 7 days). Do not stay at the Italianos campsite! There are no toilets and the place is becoming one large sewer, with toilet paper as far as the eyes can see in one part of the campground. jDisgusting and tons of flies. There is wireless, but no cellular at most of the locations. Best places to buy supplies are at both ends of the main trek (where you get off the Catamaran and where you trek in to Torres Del Paine peak). Leave early or you could find yourself sleeping on rocks at Las Cuernos!!! The campground at Las Torres was amazing. Don't pass it by. I rank it as average due to the really bad conditions in the free campsites.

review_text: The geyser basin is definitely an experience that you will want to take in, especially if you have not been to Yellowstone or to the geyser area in Iceland. Here in Chile, these are mostly fumaroles. We saw only two relatively small geysers -- and they shot only about 3-5 meters. What's unique about this area is that it is the highest geysir basin the world, at over 14,000' (4320 meters). To see the steam, you need to be there basically at dawn, when it's coldest -- the steam is far less visible as the air warms. But the early-morning steam, with the sun rising over the Andes, does create some great opportunities for good pictures. Dress warmly! When we were there, it was -14C (about 7 degrees Fahrenheit). Thankfully, there was almost no wind, so we didn't have windchill to handle.

review_text: This museum covering the history of the military coup and its aftermath is not an easy visit, but a necessary one. Pictures, testimonies, newsreel, objects all tell the appalling story of the Pinochet regime and its effects on the people of Chile. I didn't feel there was enough about the current impact of the coup - whether there was any reconciliation attempt, how children were educated about that part of their country's history or even about the recent failed attempt to change the Pinochet-era constitution. An important museum, but a few missed opportunities.

review_text: Aboard all the 360 cv power of our Dodge Durango, with my wife, we travelled from Puerto Natales, through Ruta 9 to towards Torres del Paine . review_text: We have been to this park twice now to enjoy some casual 'hiking.' The proximity to the city is perfect as you could easily head out here for a half day if you have other things on your agenda for the rest of the day. There are great trails to follow, taking you along a nice valley. Both times we have crossed the river to walk back along the other side for a different view. The park also has a large number of BBQ pits so it's a nice spot to stay for lunch if you want to plan a lengthier stay and many locals set up all along the river for a nice day cooling off in the river. There is also the option to do horseback riding if you want and there is an abandoned estate house to explore for some fun. There are clean bathrooms at the main area which were great to have at the end of a long hike and potable water for refills.

review_text: How to even begin about our wonderful time with Cristian and Ruta Valparaiso? I sent so many emails to him prior to our arrival, about everything--payment, airports, food, coffee, schedule—and Cristian was always patient and kept it all together. By the time we actually got to Santiago, he knew a lot about us, our goals, and our timeline for this whirlwind visit prior to getting on a cruise. And, wasn’t it wonderful to get out of international arrivals—jetlagged and overwhelmed by taxi offers—to see Cristian standing there waiting to whisk us out of the airport and off to a cool, comfy car and on our way to a coffee spot?! From then on, Cristian and his driver (Italo) took great care of us. We saw so much of Santiago, learned history and politics, saw the changing of the Presidential Guard, walked among the beautiful buildings, took many pictures, and then moved on to our fabulous lunch. Based on our prep, Cristian had booked lunch at a gorgeous spot out in the Casablanca Valley where we could enjoy the breezes and pastoral setting, while eating a tremendous meal. Ever polite, Cristian offered to eat separately if we needed/wanted time alone, but we were learning and sharing so much that we four ate together. And of course the owner came over and we had a little on-the-house appetizer to taste some flavors, and just relaxed and unwound (having been awake for 1.5 days already it was nice to just breathe deeply and see the clear blue sky). After lunch, we went on to a really superb, private winery tour arranged just for us. That was really a difference maker: we had never been the only guests and we got to walk among the vines and ask lots of questions, in addition to looking at the manufacturing side and of course having a tasting. The vineyard Cristian and I picked really worked out well as we were able to buy wine to take immediately on the ship and we sent some home for later. As if this wasn’t a full day, we finished day 1 with Cristian taking us to his beloved hometown of Vina del Mar, where we got some basic directions and dropped off at our hotel for an evening on our own. The next morning, Cristian came right on time to give us day 2. On this glorious sunny morning, we learned more about the history and sights in Vina, the flower clock, the coast northward, the sand dunes, the wildlife, and Valparaiso. In Valpo, we saw so much: we rode funiculars, we walked the alleys and the many stairs between neighborhoods, we saw historical sights, we ate at a tiny restaurant that hung off the side of one of these amazing hill buildings in Valpo; we went to the fishmarket to meet hundreds of sea lions; and continued to learn so much from Cristian—plus we kept running into people he knows! By the time our 2-day tour ended, Cristian had set the tone for the whole of Chile and the whole of our trip. Everywhere we went over the next 16 days, we referred to things Cristian had told us or we remarked how other tours/guides were not as informative and fun as our time with Cristian/Ruta. Considering our tiredness and the amount of things we did, I am still amazed how much I think about this visit. How can I forget? You guys were so much fun and easy going. It was a pleasure spending 2 days in your company. And, wasn’t it wonderful to get out of international arrivals—jetlagged and overwhelmed by taxi offers—to see Cristian standing there waiting to whisk us out of the airport and off to a cool, comfy car and on our way to a coffee spot?! From then on, Cristian and his driver (Italo) took great care of us. We saw so much of Santiago, learned history and politics, saw the changing of the Presidential Guard, walked among the beautiful buildings, took many pictures, and then moved on to our fabulous lunch. Based on our prep, Cristian had booked lunch at a gorgeous spot out in the Casablanca Valley where we could enjoy the breezes and pastoral setting, while eating a tremendous meal. Ever polite, Cristian offered to eat separately if we needed/wanted time alone, but we were learning and sharing so much that we four ate together. And of course the owner came over and we had a little on-the-house appetizer to taste some flavors, and just relaxed and unwound (having been awake for 1.5 days already it was nice to just breathe deeply and see the clear blue sky). After lunch, we went on to a really superb, private winery tour arranged just for us. The vineyard Cristian and I picked really worked out well as we were able to buy wine to take immediately on the ship and we sent some home for later. As if this wasn’t a full day, we finished day 1 with Cristian taking us to his beloved hometown of Vina del Mar, where we got some basic directions and dropped off at our hotel for an evening on our own. review_text: My friend and I booked a private Uyuni Salar tour for 3 days 2 nights and got dropped off in Atacama Desert. We requested Nefe as our driver, English guide and cook based on reviews of him on trip advisor. Nefe was a huge reason why we really enjoyed our trip. We didn’t see other guides throughout our trip do the same for their clients. He also offered to star gaze with us in the desert and brought a laser pointer to point out the constellations. He was constantly telling us we can ask him to stop anytime while we were driving if we wanted to get a photo. There was plenty of food so we were never hungry. I highly recommend him. The agency was flexible and let us book our own hotels. We stayed at Luna Salada our first night and Tayka Desert Hotel the second night. I recommend Luna Salada. It was comfortable and nicely decorated. I do not recommend Tayka Desert. I stayed in one of their older rooms which smelled like paint, heater barely worked and the room was very basic. It cost about ~$175 with the fees they tack on (money order, credit card, etc). It was definitely not worth the money. I hear Huayllara (spelling?) is about the same in comfort at a fraction of the cost ($~40). It’s only about ~30 min from Tayka Desert closer to the Red Lagoon.

review_text: Set on beautifully landscaped grounds, with fantastic view of the vineyards, and ducks swimming in a little pond, Matetic Vineyards is unique for being a biodynamic and organic vineyard (the former being something that is not easily attained, with only 50 or so of them in Chile). The biodynamic pledge (committing to certain plants that are used not only for fertilizer, but also to provide nutrients for the vines; using quartz to help plants retain heat; putting soil in a cow horn and burying it in the earth for 6-8 months for what purpose I can no longer recall) frankly gave me some pause, but I did enjoy the beauty of the vineyards. Sadly, our wine tasting (riesling and a winemaker’s blend) was disappointing, and the bottle prices were higher than average compared to other tastier wines we’d had in Santiago. On the other hand, the onsite restaurant Equilibrio is light-filled, airy and offers a very tempting food and wine menu. It feels as if you were dropped somewhere in Napa or Sonoma. I thoroughly enjoyed my grilled octopus salad, the Corilillo pinot noir and panqueques celestinas (crepes filled with dulce de leche and a side of vanilla ice cream-- need I say more?)

review_text: Odfjell is one of those wineries that although very close to Santaigo feels a bit out of the way. Pretty much hidden (or protected) by a hill, the vineyard features a stable housing about 19 curious Norwegian horses. Be careful not to let them eat your clothes! As to our visit, my wife and I opted to do a basic tasting (CLP 12,000 or USD 18) and skip the tour. It is worth noting that the architect of Odfjell is also did Lapostolle, reason why if you like the gravity concept on the process of winemaking it may be worth to take the tour. The tasting was led by Lorena, a very knowledgable agronomist with a keen interest in marketing, who allowed us to calmly enjoy and discover a number of wines produced by this organic vineyard. The results are certainly interesting, with outstanding results associated to the lack of wood and the favoritism for acidity in their wines (at least in some of them). The tasting was interesting because Lorena allowed us to learn not only from the wine but also from her and her views on the wine business. Certainly the experience was enriching. One of the things I like about this place is that they have dared to bottle unusual grapes for the Chilean market such as Tempranillo, Cabernet Franc, Malbec and Carignan (this last two almost becoming a trend in the market lately along with Pais and Cinsault). Encourage them a buy a bottle before leaving. Give it a try!

review_text: Originally, I had read a lot of great reviews about another bicycle touring company in Santiago and was determined to sign up for a tour with them. However, the day I wanted to go, they didn't have enough people signed up, so they recommended La Bicicleta Verde. There were only 2 of us on the tour (it was a Wednesday morning in November) and the day was perfect! Our tour guide was sweet, enthusiastic and was very informative. My fellow rider and I only spoke English, but our tour guide also spoke very good English, so it was easy to understand her. As an avid cyclist, I'm used to riding in the states, but here it was different-- I didn't feel comfortable renting a bike on my own (as I also knew my head would be site-seeing), but I always felt safe on the ride with them. They provided a bottle of water, and we were even treated to a little treat a the end! There was also a street dog, who knew the path they take, and followed us the entire time-- it was cute. I highly recommend this tour as a way to check out the city!!!

review_text: An easy drive from Valdivia to Niebla brought us to the ferry to Corral. There we found the Castillo de Corral in a strategic position covering the approach to Valdivia. It was one of 18 locations, including forts at Niebla and on the island of Mancera dating back to the 1600s. In 1820 Lord Cochrane led a daring land attack against the forts which were garrisoned by troops loyal to the Spanish crown. Cochrane's victory at Valdivia was an important step in Chile's fight for independence.

review_text: My wife and I are just back from 30 days enjoying Chile. We booked pretty much everything through Cristian Cosignani at Ecotours Chile. We knew we wanted to do some biking in Chile, so started pursuing that with Cristian after friends recommended him. It soon became apparent that Cristian could and would assist with pretty much all of our bookings, including local flights. We spent the first week or so in and around Santiago, including 2 day hikes into nearby parks, and Valparaiso. Then we did Ecotours 4 day bike and wine trip. The biking was casual, the wine tours superb. Next we flew south and enjoyed Ecotours 7 day Lakes and Volcanos bike tour. Longer days in the saddle than biking in the wine district, and more hills, but certainly doable by anyone with decent fitness and a bit of biking experience. Then we flew further south for 7 days of Patagonia trekking based out of the Ecodomes. Great accommodation, great food and great trekking. Arriving at the little lake at the base of the Three Pillars was a real highlight. Next to Chiloe for a few days of sight seeing, then home. Chile is highly recommended as a destination for beautiful and diverse natural scenery, interesting history, and as much top quality hiking and biking as you want. Be sure to check out Exotours Chile website, ecotours.cl. Chile is not an inexpensive place to visit, food and lodging prices are comparable to USA. Our dining and accommodation provided through Ecotours was always great, and what we considered to be fair value and many tours can be personalized to meet your own needs and scheduling. Hi Harley and Heather, thanks for your possitive review, all th staff appreciates it. Looking forward to welcome you again in Chile on the near future. Best regards and keep adding miles on your bikes!! Cristian

review_text: We booked 3 different excursions with Patagonia Shorex and enjoyed all of them. The first was a private guided tour through Buenos Aires which included pick up from our hotel and drop off to the cruise terminal to start our Patagonia cruise. Our guide was excellent and as we are fluent Spanish-speakers he was very comfortable in his mother tongue but also spoke good English. The tour included a comfortable Mercedes with driver which allowed our guide to have us dropped in one spot and picked up in another so we never had to back track. We felt that we saw most of the highlights of the city in just one day, including an excellent lunch in a family style local restaurant with our guide and driver. Our second excursion was in Punta Arenas where we were again picked up from the dock in a private car and taken to the penguin reserve in Ottway. It was a very windy day but we were able to learn alot about the penguins and get close enough for some good photos. Afterwards we returned to Punta Arenas where we had a fantastic seafood lunch on the recommendation of our guide before they took us back to the ship. On our final excursion, Jaime himself was our guide in Puerto Montt. Again we had a comfortable private vehicle and driver for our visit to Osorno volcano and the waterfalls. It was a great day out including another spectacularly good seafood lunch in a restaurant organized by Jaime that was like being in a friends house, albeit a friend who happened to be a great chef! I would not hesitate to recommend Jaime and the entire Patagonia Shorex team. Incidentally all these tours were set-up via email and they were very responsive and accommodating. review_text: My best friend and I were referred to Perro Tour's by the front desk at our hotel. We were looking to take a full day tour to the nearby Casablanca Valley to visit all of the gorgeous vineyards. We reached out to Perro Tour's at 6pm on Tuesday evening with the hopes to book a tour the very next day and to our surprise, we were able to book a full day private tour with Juan Victor and his mother. They were extremely accommodating and allowed us the freedom to choose exactly what time we wanted to be picked up and the duration of our tour length for the next day. During the hour drive from Valparaiso to the Casablanca Valley, Juan Victor provided us with a great background on the history of the area. In addition, he was able to answer all of our questions, ranging from information about the city, to popular Chilean dishes and customs. Upon arriving to wine country, we were given the freedom to enjoy our time at each vineyard. Juan Victor was also a wonderful help in communicating our wishes to each employee at each spot we visited. We enjoyed a wonderful lunch together and got to learn a little more about their lives and personalities - great company for sure! As our day came to an end and we began approaching Valparaiso, Juan Victor asked his mother to stop at a gorgeous look out point just before entering the city. It was a gorgeous view and he was able to provide lots of information about what we were looking at and additional history about the area. Lastly, they stopped at a local cheese shop before we returned to the hotel - they had overheard my friend and I discuss just "how nice it would be if we could find some good cheese to pair with the wine we had just purchased." The day could not have been more enjoyable. We had great weather, awesome views and of course such great company. Juan Victor and his mother really outdid themselves and completely devoted their day to our enjoyment. I would highly recommend that anyone visiting the area should absolutely take the opportunity to meet Juan Victor and enjoy a tour with him - you will not be disappointed! Thanks Juan Victor - it was such a great day!

review_text: I don't usually go on tours, I like to feel free to explore without the restraints of a schedule, and in any case, tours are for old people aren't they? But finding myself in San Pedro de Atacama, a sort-of transit lounge in the desert for international travellers heading every which way, Bolivia, Peru, Argentina, Brazil, El Dorado — trying to find themselves (or maybe loose themselves for a while) — there was little alternative, short of hiring a four-wheel drive and trusting to your map-reading skills. The Atacama desert is an entirely different kettle of cactus needles though, a landscape of dust and rocks, mountains and volcanos, vast salt plains and weird rock formations... 'Err, do we take the dusty unmarked track to to the left, or continue along this dusty unmarked track heading straight towards those rocks?' To be honest I had little idea of what lay outside the town's dusty streets, except more sun-baked dust, rocks and the looming Andes mountains on the horizon. But there had to be a reason why so many people travel here, spending many uncomfortable hours cooped-up on the bus. And of course, the reason is the great outdoors, and by great I mean GREAT, vast, surreal, spectacular, and perhaps even that much misused adjective — awesome! There are many tour operators in San Pedro, and they are all offering variations on a similar theme. Everyone is in on it, even the guys who run the hostel we stayed at — 'Yes, we can arrange any trip for you, at a special price of course...' So it's a case of taking a good look round, talking to other temporary transit lounge residents, and using your instincts to get an idea of what's good to see, and what to give a miss. The prices vary between companies, but not wildly. We paid 10,000 Chilean pesos each (about £12), for the Moon Valley trip, which takes about 5 hours, and also includes Death Valley (similar to Moon Valley, but smaller, more jagged and scary looking), and a scheduled final stop at a nearby vantage point (on the edge of a ravine) to watch the changing colours of the surrounding mountains at sunset. Moon Valley is only a short drive from San Pedro (it's also possible to get there by mountain bike), but it could be a different planet, the Moon perhaps, but with breathable air and a blue sky.

Thank you.

review_text: Traveled with White World Travel to Uyuni from San Pedro. My driver, the EXCELLENT Oscar, spoke English, as did the equally EXCELLENT Nila in the SPA office. This trip exceeded my expectations on all levels and is highly recommended, especially if you like Land Cruisers as, much like Brava grasses, they seem to predominate above 15,000'. The Loco Graveyard in Uyuni is just one of many highlights. See it before they put up a fence and start charging for admission. This outfit is really well organised on the ground and Oscar made every day fun. Accommodation was fine if basic and for where we were, the food was also fine. I am a celiac and and Oscar was able to get Llama steaks and the like cooked in soy oil and other fine gluten free meals. I didn't need any of the gluten free snacks in my backpack. Altitude wasn't an issue but I'd recommend acclimatising for a few days in San Pedro (Salar de Tara is a magnificent drive for example).

Would recommend this company to others performing this climb.

review_text: I recently returned to Parque Nacional Lauca after first visiting in the mid-1990's. Sadly, this mountain wilderness has lost much of its remote, unspoilt quality over the last 20 years. The tar road through the park now seems to be a significant import / export route for land-locked Bolivia. Large numbers of heavy vehicles use the road, queuing for several kilometres within the park on the Chilean side of the border. The road between Arica and Lauca is no longer an enjoyable drive as it is being busy and large scale road upgrades currently in progress lead to long delays. The section of road near Laguna Chungará is in poor condition and there is a lot of rubbish within the park. Comparable or better Andean mountain scenery can be found at Laguna Miscanti, near San Pedro de Atacama or on route 27/52 between San Pedro and Jujuy / Salta (Argentina).

review_text: It has to be one of the best things that I have done. We set off at the crack of dawn and made our way to the base of the Volcano to start the hike up. You start at the base ski station and way above you with the snowy peak way in the distance. The climb is a long way up but it is not that hard, take it easy the whole way up and the higher you get the smaller the steps, you will soon recognise the small steps that you see mountaineers on Everest taking. The last 1,000 ft was tough as the air is getting thin and you get out of breath easily. The top of the volcano stinks as it is still active (thankfully no lava eruptions recently) and it is constantly spewing out sulphur which does not help with the breathing. The views from the top are spectacular and you can see the chain of volcanoes of which Villarica is a part, their snowy peaks getting ever smaller in the distance. Down below you can see the beautiful snowfields that disappear into the brown sides of the volcano and then the forest leading down to the many lakes. One of the best bits is the descent as you getting kitted out in wet weather gear and then slide down chutes through the snow, Amazingly good fun and so much quicker and easier than the descent. The descent down the rest of the mountain is a dusty and dreary, at least there are beers waiting for you at the bottom to allow you to rehydrate. Useful hints: 1. Use all of the equipment that the tour providers give you as yours will get trashed by the volcanic rocks and gravel and dust. 2. Bring all of your things, camera, sun screen, food and drink etc. in a plastic bag as you will using their rucksacks. 3. The top of the volcano stinks as it is still active (thankfully no lava eruptions recently) and it is constantly spewing out sulphur which does not help with the breathing. review_text: My wife and I booked Space Star Tours specifically because of the trip advisor recommendations. Ive always had a love of space and the clear sky of the Atacama Desert seemed like a perfect opportunity to embrace my inner (and outer) geek. It wound up being a fantastic and informative night. Our English Language tour was completely booked and during the early evening there was a chance it might be cancelled because of the weather, but the clouds parted just in time and off we went about 3-5 miles out of town where it is completely dark. Once arriving we were greeted by Less a Canadian astronomer. He was witty, funny and also very friendly. The setup at his residence is nothing short of amazing, consisting of 9 large telescopes all pointed at the night sky. One recommendation: Try to book during the NEW MOON or CRESCENT moon as the brighter the moon gets, the less stars you get to see. During the week of the full moon he does not give tours because of the brightness. The first part of the tour was a explanation of the night sky. Using a laser pointer, Less describes the different stars, planets and constellations we would be looking at. Its also not at all unusual to see one or more shooting stars. Since you are outside I STRONGLY suggest you dress warm. We were there in early summer so it wasnt too bad, but you still needed at least a fleece pull over and warm pants. The second part consists of a description of what each telescope is looking at and an opportunity to look in each one at your leisure. Of the 9 telescopes the one looking at Jupiter and its moons was by far my favorite. The others look at various stars and star clusters, still VERY cool! There is also an opportunity to use your digital camera through one of the telescopes to take a picture of the moon. The last part consists of a question and answer session inside the house with a nice hot cup of hot chocolate (or tea or matte de coca) if prefer. Less is more than happy to answer any questions you may have as your sit in a semi-circle with the open roof above you. If you visit San Pedro, you MUST go on this tour. You really gain an appreciation of the night sky and the universe we live in. You also just might learn something along the way!

review_text: If you are planning a trip to do the seven days Big Paine loop in Chile's Torres del Paine National Park you must have a qualified guide, two if your party is large. We had eight hikers on our trip. Chile Nativo did all our arrangements. This included our hiring out two guide, head guide Mauricio Delgado and assistant guide Fernando Pozo. Mauricio has been guiding for 15 year and has made the 7 days hike many-many times. Inspite of numerous trips he never seemed bored or tired of the routine. He always was enthusiastic and as a regular knew our porters, all the guides on other trips as well as the staff at camp sites. There was no doubt about where we were headed, where we were to camp, what to see, all the details that make a trip run smoothly. Fernando was also extremely knowledgeable, particularly about plants and the incredible geologic features that we were treated to see each day. He had spent a couple of winters working at the Killington Ski Resort, so we Vermonters quickly connected with him. They made a great team. On each of the seven days Mauricio and/or Fernando would stop, maybe a bit too often for my go-go why are we stopping wife, to describe what peaks we were looking up at, call attention to a special flower, plant or fungal-lichen growth. They pointed out edible as well as inedible berries and plants. So if your are booking your trip with Chile Nativo I highly recommend that you specifically request Mauricio Delgado as Fernando Pozo as your guides.

review_text: I don't usually write such detailed reviews but when we arrived in San Pedro there was an abundance of tour agencies offering the 4WD salt flats tour to Uyuni however recommendations/advice from hostels and word of mouth was confusing at best. We visited a variety of agencies all priced between 80 and 130 thousand Chilean pesos - they had almost identical itineraries but I think the major differentiator is the accommodation you stay in. We chose the 3 day 2 night option as we wanted to end the tour in Uyuni and carry on our travels through Bolivia. We went with World White Travel as they gave us a good impression in the office and our minimal research suggested they had positive reviews overall. We paid 110 for a Spanish speaking tour (we presented ourselves as a group of 4 so got a slight discount). We were really happy with our choice, and I would definitely recommend using this agency. We met our Bolivian driver at the border after a Chilean driver drove 2 groups to this point on the morning of day one. Felix was amazing, he was patient with our basic level of Spanish and very professional throughout. He took amazing photos and drove really safely, we were so happy to have spent the 3 days with Felix! The agency told us to bring snacks and water but I personally don't think you need snacks; (unless you really like snacking) we were fed really well! We were pleasantly surprised as we didn't expect much due to what we had heard. The first day has a long wait between breakfast and lunch because the time changes when you cross the border but other than that you really don't need additional food. This is what we had: Breakfast day one; ham & cheese rolls, biscuits, cake, hot drinks Lunch day one; salad, sausages, mash potato (salad includes cucumber, tomatoes, avocado, soft white cheese cubes) Banana each for afterwards 6pm break includes biscuits, coffee, herbal teas Dinner day one; vegetable soup starter with bread, vegetable spaghetti bolognaise for main Tinned peach for dessert Day two breakfast; thick pancakes (cold) and spreads including margarine, dulce de leche and strawberry jam. Remaining tea and coffee Day two lunch; cold rice salad, tuna, sweetcorn and soft white cheese, and another mixed salad plate including tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, avocado, red onion. Apple for afterwards Same 6pm hot drinks with crackers Dinner: vegetable soup with bread for starter and main was a platter of chips, sausages, meat (beef or llama not sure), tomato, fried onions, green peppers Day 3 breakfast: bread, spreads, cake, yoghurt, granola, hot drinks Day 3 lunch: breaded chicken escalopes, vegetables, pasta One thing worth mentioning is no water was served with the meals. It was apple juice and hot water for breakfast, Coca Cola for lunch and nothing with dinner (although we did get a bottle of red wine on the second night). So it's well worth bringing the full 5 litres of water they recommend. As for accommodation, this was fine. We spent the first night in a refugio in a dorm room for 5 people, there were 2 toilets but no showers. Blankets and sleeping bags were included and we weren't cold at all. There were no electricity sockets to charge anything. The second night was in the salt hotel where bedding was again provided and we weren't cold at all. This time we could sleep in matrimonial and twin rooms. There were 2 hot showers but the only temperature was scolding hot. We still were able to shower though. This place had a few sockets in the communal area to charge devices. Something else worth mentioning - you cannot purchase additional food/drinks/goods at the Salt Hotel or the refugio. On day two we stopped at a village shop just before the salt hotel and bought a couple of beers there. There was no similar opportunity on day one. That was our experience of white world travel, I hope this helps others to choose the tour they want. I would highly recommend this company and thought it was very good value for money. Final shout out to our driver Felix, you were great!

review_text: At entry level, I think it is important that the teacher speaks English as it is impossible to explain things properly if not. My teacher spoke very very quickly without making an effort to enunciate her words and speaks clearly so as to give me a chance of understanding what she was saying. She did not seem to understand that I was a beginner and therefore would not understand if she spoke to me in Spanish in the manner she did, and without gesturing etc. My situation was worsened, as the two other people in my group were Brazilian, therefore they understood most of what the teacher said. So after speaking unintelligibly (for me) to them for a while, she would say to me ‘do you understand’ to which I would say ‘no’ which was embarrassing for me and made it slow for the other two, as she would then try and explain to me in limited English what she had just said. Our level of understanding was at completely different levels and we shouldn’t have been in the same group. I asked her multiple times to try and speak more slowly and reiterated that I don’t understand Spanish but nothing changed. She was late one day so I was taught by the teacher in the group above for an hour. She was much clearer and although she spoke minimal English, I still learnt a lot and understood everything she said. I managed fine in this class despite it being the one above. After this, I went to speak to another teacher and the receptionist to inform them of my problems and to ask if I could change groups to the other teacher. They said it wasn’t possible and that they would speak to my current teacher. I said I had already spoken to her and it hadn’t helped. The rest of the week didn’t change and none of the other staff followed up my problem and asked if things had improved. I feel I have big chunks of the lessons missing from my knowledge as the teacher just couldn’t explain them properly and I felt bad for the other pupils by having to make the teacher try and explain in English constantly. On the second to last day, a pupil who could not speak any Spanish whatsoever joined our group for 2 hours. So our instruction was to talk amongst ourselves while she sat and taught him individually. I feel this was completely unfair as we completely missed 2 hours of teaching on top of an already poor week of teaching. It was also very unfair as I hadn’t been allowed to move groups when I could manage in the group above’s lesson. This guy was completely inappropriate for our lesson yet he was allowed to come into a new group later on. This is the feedback I sent to the school seeking some sort of compensation. I had to send them 10 e mail chasing them, for them to just say there’s nothing we can do. Thank you very much for your comments and for let us know about your experience. I ask you to please send an email to customer.care@coined.us, so we can find a way to improve your experience. Many thanks

review_text: A museum that reminds us of the depth and scale of the murderous rampage of the military coup that toppled the democratically elected government of Salvador Allende. Chile needed this museum to come face to face with its past and to remind itself that this should not be allowed to repeat again. The museum documents events preceding and following the coup with extensive documentations in the form of personal interviews, pictures and videos of actual events. The third floor of the museum has photos of many of those citizens who either disappeared or were killed on the wall and an open space in the shape of balcony with candle-shaped lights in the form of tributes to these individuals. Very moving. Almost all of the descriptions were in Spanish. I was at the museum with a Chilean friend who could interpret things for me as needed. However, simultaneous English translations of the descriptions in Spanish would have helped in getting a full perspective of the presentations.

review_text: I live about a 20 minute walk from Cerro San Cristobal and visit it somewhat frequently. However, I find that each time I go I discover something new. Tourists will concentrate on the southern tip where you can climb to the Virgin statue, visit the beautiful chapel, and overlook the city as you sip a mote con huesillo. And that experience should not be missed. However, the "back" part of the hill as it stretches to the northeast is well worth exploring. There is a network of trails and parks extending along the whole length to La Pyramide and beyond. All along, these afford gorgeous views to the east and west. The funicular has been restored and is on the verge of re-opening as of August 2016, and there is an enormous and enormously popular swimming pool that is open in the summer. Cerro San Cristobal is rightly popular with both tourists and Santiaguinos.

The next day it was sunny and many reached the top.

review_text: I took this walking tour again with some friends visiting Chile for a few days. This is a 'must do' I think. The guides are both knowledgeable and charming. They know their history, architecture and political anecdotes. You see so much more on foot than from the window of a bus and you are moving through the city with those who do it every day. Our group was not large, perhaps ten people of different nationalities. At first the thought of four hours walking seems daunting but, unless you have mobility problems, the pace is easy and the time flies. There is a stop for a snack on the walk. Take a hat and water if it is sunny. As others have said, do this first so you can then return another time to visit some of the places you have seen on the walk. If you have only one day in Santiago, do this. The recommended tip is CLP$5000 per person and the tour is worth four times this amount for value given.

review_text: This winery is in a pleasant situation in the Maipo Valley, within easy driving distance of Santiago. Unlike most wineries that we have visited, it is not free to visit. In fact it is surprisingly expensive, especially if you do one of their more involved tours. We did the basic tour, which involved a tour of the vineyard and the winery itself. Our guide, Victor, was very pleasant and informative. This is not a boutique winery and is surprisingly large. They can produce a staggering 250,000 bottles of wine a day, six days a week; wine on an industrial scale. It is a quite historic and some old oak fermenters are on display. The tour finishes with a short video, explaining the history of the area during the war of independence, when 120 rebels were given sanctuary in the hacienda that was on the site of the winery. The wine tasting was very disappointing, in that we were only given three basic wines to taste: a sauvignon blanc: a cabernet sauvignon and a carmenere. We were then ushered to the shop, where there is a wide selection of wines to buy. However the most interesting part of the tour was visiting their superb museum, which housed a collection amassed by an earlier owner of the vineyard. There is a stunning collection of objects from Easter Island and Chile, many of them ancient and some of historical importance. Thank you for giving us your opinion about your visit to Santa Rita, we will work on these points in order to improve the experience. Kindly, Sindy M.

review_text: For my first tour I went trekking in the Cajon del Maipo with some friends. We were only a small group of people which gave the whole trip a very personal flair. Guided by Ignacio we went up the mountain where we had an incredible view! It is definitely a MUST to go there when you're visiting Santiago! After spending the whole day in the mountains, Ignacio took us to the Colina Hot Springs. There is no better way to relax after an exhausing and eventful day! Snacks, Pisco Sour and a typical chilean lunch were also included, so we didn't have to worry about anything. It was a very fun day that inspired me to do two more tours with Ignacio and Fernando: Rafting in the Maipo River and a trip to the vineyards and mountains. It was nice to see how the Chilean wine is produced and to even get to taste some of it. Fun people plus the incredible landscape of the Cajon plus a wild but not too wild Maipo river had the Rafting become an unforgettable experience! Great guides took care of our safety, so that some people falling out of the boat only added some spice to the whole tour. We even got to jump into the river from a 4m high rock! I would really recommend this to anyone who wants to combine getting to know the landscape with some extra activity! I felt very comfortable during all my trips and I am very happy that I was accompanied by such cordial guides. Hi Johannen, We are happy that you like the tours that you have done with us!
