review_text: We were a part of an independent tour during our port of call in Puerto Montt on our cruise Around the Horn. The tour was provided by GV Tours and our group, as I recall, included 32 people, 20 of whom were on a large bus and 10 on a smaller van. The price of the tour was $ 80 pp and included admissions and a nice lunch. Puerto Montt is a real fishing town and the area where the ship docks is a working port. One needs to get out of town to appreciate the beauty in the surroundings. Our first stop was Puerto Varas, a beautiful seaside village known for its roses. We then proceeded to the Vicente Perez Rosales National Park where we saw the beautiful falls and rapids, as well as the volcano, once the clouds parted. For lunch we stopped at a chalet type restaurant called Bon Bon Oriental where we enjoyed a pisco sour, a choice of excellent salmon or beef that was a bit tough, wine, and a kuchen-like dessert. Our last stop was the Bavarian village of Frutillar, situated on the country's largest lake, on which stands an amazing performing arts structure. Upon returning to the port we opted to shop at the Artisan Craft Market adjacent to the pier area. Prices were very reasonable. Also the good, free Wi-fi at the pier was a welcome surprise. Darla was our tour guide on the bus and Gale and Victoria (G and V) were our gracious hosts at the restaurant. The only suggestion would to provide more commentary on the bus about history of the towns, culture, foods, education, etc. All in all, it was a very nice day.

review_text: We did a private 4 day/3 night tour of Bolivia and Uyuni from San Pedro de Atacama and had an amazing experience. The first thing that I really appreciated was communication with the owner, Eric. We traveled with 2 younger children - ages 10 and 12 - and I had a lot of questions about safety, altitude sickness, and other details of the trip. Eric was very patient with me and did a great job at accurately explaining the details of the trip and what to expect. White and Green own the vehicles they use, and employ their drivers directly. There are a lot of sub-par travel agencies in the area that only sell the packages, but have no accountability for the actual trip itself. This was a huge selling point for us since we wanted to make sure we had the best possible experience for our family. Our driver, Vladimir, was excellent. He has 20 years experience doing these treks, and it was so reassuring for our family that we were going to spend our trip with someone who was professional, knowledgeable and who took safety into consideration for the entire trip. We speak Spanish, so we were able to communicate with him throughout the trip, and ask tons of questions. There was a lot of driving, but we had plenty of stops for the first 3 days where we could get out of the car and explore and take plenty of pictures. We were really glad we booked the private tour because it gave us the flexibility to spend more time where we wanted and we never felt rushed. The accommodations were as comfortable as expected. We knew exactly what to expect because Eric was straight forward about everything. The first and 3rd nights were cold, but we had plenty of blankets and sleeping bags that were provided so that we could be as warm as possible. We also really enjoyed the food as well, and our daughters ate everything which was great. Finally, the Uyuni salt flats were definitely the highlight of the trip. We saw one of the most amazing sunrises of our lives, took fun perspective pictures, and had a very memorable experience as a family thanks to our guide, Vladimir. This was a once in a lifetime trip for us, and we are very glad we chose the right company.

Then we asked her to drive us to Vina del Mar so we could see Valparaiso's "sister city" with minimal effort. And she gave us a great tour there, including a visit to a great German restaurant across the street from the beach. As others have noted, it was like being shown around by a friend. review_text: We had a hiking and kayaking tour therough Antares, who were aboslutely fantastic! Our guides were Tadeo(hiking) and Abi (kayak). Both sides of the tour were second to none. We trekked the W trek which was awe inspiring. Tad took us to a few secret spots off the beaten track that only locals know about for magnificent views and photo opportunities that few others would ever get to see. He was very knowledgeable and just a nice person to be around. Note that the trek can be quite strenuous in parts (heading up to the towers and also up the french valley) but they are both well worth it. the food, drinks and company in the refugios are great too. The rooms are just basic dorm rooms which are fine (unless you have a snorer in the room!!!). Seriously though, this has to be up there as one of the most beautiful treks in the world and should be an absolute must for anyone and everyone that is remotely interested in hiking. Massive mountains, glaciers (including glacier gray), wild/birdlife, forests, CLEAN AIR. We were also very lucky that we jagged perfect weather every single day on our trek and kayak tour, which at the end of March is a rarity I have been told! We didnt even have a sniff of wind! The tour ended up with a boat trip up to Glacier Gray with a nice glass of whiskey. The kayaking tour was also well worth it. We camped in the bush (roughing it) but we loved that. Just getting back to nature, without another soul in sight! We saw wild cows, different bird life and once again some phenominal scenery. Safety was of the higest order too so no need to worry about that! On the last day we also got to paddle around the icebergs and glacier at Balmaceda glacier which was something that not too many people would have done.

review_text: What we hoped would be a nice, long day of amazing sights turned into a quasi-nightmare because of a terrible tour guide. The bus was very late picking us up at our hotel, and it was a good thing we were already waiting outside because no one came into the lobby to get us. At that point the guide, Simon, wasn't even on the bus (!) - he had to run to another hotel to collect a guest he had ignored the first time around. Once everyone was finally aboard, information was not only scant but given to those who got off the bus first. The last ones off the bus would miss most or all of the commentary. We had adequate time at the salt flats and the flamingoes were beautiful, but we were never warned that we had a two and a half hour ride to the next stop (the lagoons), with no bathrooms en route and none at the destination. Most of us on the bus were desperate for facilities by the time we reached the lagoons, and were forced to go in the open behind the bus. On the way to our third destination, by this time around 3:00 in the afternoon, someone asked Simon about lunch (we were almost starved at that point), and he came unglued. He became rude, belligerent and insulting to virtually everyone on the bus. We finally got to lunch around 4:30 and it was delicious, but we needed to be told it would be a late lunch and Simon couldn't be bothered to let us know that. Basic information which anyone in a service industry should know to impart was completely ignored. We had other, better experiences with TourisTour, but this experience was abysmal. The tour industry in Chile is totally unregulated, and that needs to change. Professional guides who treat paying customers (and this tour was expensive!) with dignity and respect is not too much to ask. Review of: Altiplanic Lagoons & Piedras Rojas Tour from San Pedro de Atacama

review_text: Just a piece of advice to anyone considering this tour: weather and visibility is everything! We were quite unlucky the day we went and had almost zero visibility, cold rain, and blustery winds. Nobody even wanted to get out of the van and we ended up returning hours earlier than scheduled. So it's hard to give this tour a fair review, with that considered. Obviously they are running a business and thus the show must go on, rain or shine. But I'm just here to say if it's not a clear day, don't waste your time. As for the tour itself, I don't know what other tour operators offer, but it felt like the most basic package. You have to pack your own lunch, pay for your own park entrance online beforehand, and they wouldn't pick us up at our cabin 5 min outside the city (even though it was on the way), so we had to take a taxi to their office. The tour guide was bilingual, and so am I, and to be honest the English versions were definitely a shorter version of the Spanish narration and difficult to follow if English is your second language. The driver was good and the van was comfortable. If we had great weather, for sure it would have been a good day as for the most part this tour is just transportation. review_text: We hired a car from Balmaceda Airport and drove to Rio Tranquilo. The drive is worth it alone, it was absolutely stunning! Snow capped mountains, clean rivers and beautiful forests. There is minimal traffic too. I am not an experienced international driver and I had no worries with it. The roads can get very slippery though (as half of it is unpaved) so a 4WD would be a safer option if you're not too confident driving a 2WD on slippery, muddy roads. We arrived into Rio Tranquilo about 3 hours after leaving Balmaceda. Its a tiny town, not much going on, very laid back. It was late in the arvo and we were tired and hungry so we decided to leave the Marble Caves for the following morning. We got a room from the little hostel / B&B across from where the tourism centre is. It was comfortable, warm, with beautiful views, friendly owner and best of all FANTASTIC home made soup. Well worth staying there if you are staying in Tranquilo for the night. the caves themselves are magnificent. Set on the Azure blue Lago Carrera, they really are a must see if you can afford the time and small amount of money it costs to see them. The boat driver gives you plenty of opportunities to take fantastic photos. They really must be seen to be believed. if there is a bit of wind around ake sure you take your wet weather gear! The caves themselves are protected, but the trip too and from the town can be very bumpy and wet.

We started with a (yawn) very early pick up at our hotel at 6:15 am in a tour van and drove around to pick up the remaining tour-goers others. Our tour driver, Diego, expertly drove and commentated the entire tour. Our first stop was an hour or two into the drive, at a private rest area that had a small cafe to buy coffee and other drinks, empanadas and simple breakfast foods and the every important restrooms. We then stopped a few minutes later to see where two rivers intersected, then the next stop was at the base of the dam to take some photos, then to another photographic point where we could view the beautiful, tranquil, blue turquoise water surrounded by mountains and then to the end of the Embalse de Yeso where we spent a half an hour walking around the rocky “beach” at the edge of the water. On the return trip, we began by stopping at a restaurant where we ate lunch (at our own cost) and admired a fuzzy llama. The next and last stop was back to the initial stop, where Diego set up a picnic with salami, cheese, chips, Chilean wine and other drinks, then we departed for Santiago, arriving back around 3-4 pm. If you need pics, Diego was a great photographer, and the tour was a great deal. Would definitely recommend! Dear squirt3190, Though we want all of our travelers to enjoy memorable experiences with us, we truly appreciate your comments on how your expectations were not fully met. I took my time to address your comment by carefully talking to and reconstructing with Germán and Miguel what happened on March 7, and by thoroughly checking the vehicle's leg room out. First off, regarding our vehicle, we provided you with a comfortable Hyundai H1 (a standard in the tourism industry) with 9 seats for a group of 8 persons —I'm 187 cm tall and I fit perfectly on any of the H1's seats. We opportunely let the group know —before booking— what the type of vehicle we use for such a group size was. In any case, if requested, we might have used a larger vehicle (Mercedes Sprinter or Ford Transit), with at least 15 seats, though leg room would have been the same for each seat (and Hyundai's seats are more comfortable than the other two vehicles'). A large bus with about 40 seats would make no sense for a group of 8 persons without luggage, considering the narrow streets in Valparaíso (in fact, that kind of buses are banned from the most touristic neighborhoods in town) and the much higher price for such a vehicle. As for Germán, though he is Perro Tour's newest guide, by the time you visited Valparaíso in early March, he had already led several tours for over two months; all of them in English. I've personally been in tours with him and, more than three times, have been the guide for travelers who were guided by Germán before and none of them complained about his English language skills or voice volume. Obviously, it's a fact that you couldn't hear or understand him and, considering your own words and Germán's, he didn't explain aloud to all of you the numerous questions one of your companions asked him many times during your tour, which was our guide's fault. Anyway, if you had complained in the beginning of the tour, he might have become aware that not everyone was understanding or following him... Of course, Germán should have paid more attention and ask everyone whether you could hear him or not. I hope we have a second chance to make your time in Valparaíso a wonderful, memorable experience. So next time you visit our city, we offer you a private tour of Valparaíso at our own expense. Kind regards, Juan Víctor

Also if you come in the first half of April you get to see more of the wine making process.

review_text: After me and my girlfriend did the w-trek in Torres del Paine we were not sure how our experiences made there could be overtopped. But we were thaught the opposite: For all animal and nature lovers we highly recommend the Puma Safari with Chile Outdoor! It was a super well organized trip by car through the national park including lunch and local specialities. They picked us up in the morning at our apartment in Puerto Natales. It was just me and my girlfriend and two guides from their team. Even though they had a frame route planned, they tailored the route according to our wishes (e.g. we skipped some lookouts as we already saw them and focused on the wildlife). So we had the great luck to see almost all of the famous animals that live in the park: From skunks to guanaco herds over ñandus to pumas. Our highlight was of course the puma family (mother with 4 offsprings) that we watched almost one hour. We would have not found even one of the animals without the experience and the eageleyes of the guides. They totally focused on what we wanted and how long we wanted to stay to make fotos or watch them. After all we came back at around 6 at hour apartment super happy. All in all for people that want to learn about the wildlife and the park in a private atmosphere on a tailormade trip we highly recommend Chile Outdoor. Thank you Gabriela and Agustín for this amazing day. We learned a lot about the wildlife and the park. review_text: If you are looking for a half day trip, amazing views, easy hikes, and the opportunity of being almost alone in the middle of a beautiful forest, this is your deal. Before going to the park you have to be very informed, since there are different ways to reach it and several trails. But in any case the result is the same, almost not tourists and amazing millenarian Alerces (kind of redwoods that you can only find in Argentina and Chile). In Chile you don't have big animals crossing the paths, but it is plenty of birds that you can listen while walking on the trails. If you are lucky you can even see the Chucao, a very small pretty bird with red chest that is like the soundtrack of Chilean national parks. The park itself is not the only highlight, you have to consider the whole trip. The road to the Park is amazing, great views of the sea and the mountains. depending on the time you'ill see the amazing tide changes. You'll cross typical villages where you can buy some kuchen (kind of pies) and pan amasado (homemade bread). Good to know: There are two roads for reaching Alerce Andino National Park, my husband and I took the southern one that it supposed to be the hardest one (only 4x4). Although it is not a super easy road, you can make it in a regular car. To enter the park you have to pay a fee, but is about US$2.5 each person.

review_text: This jewel of a winery is located about 70 km north of Santiago, in the so-called Aconcagua wine valley. I confess that even though I am a wine enthusiast, I didn't know about this winery. This being my third visit to Chile, I had already been to several wineries before, all larger and better known. This time it was different. Viña Von Siebenthal is small, family-owned, but produces true liquid jewels. We were very well received by Soledad, a Chilean who is the wife of the owner, a Swiss man who fell in love with Chile and decided to make great wines there. And he largely achieved his objective. After a quick tour of the property, we tasted four of the winery's labels, with emphasis on the exceptional Riomístico, a white made with the Viognier grape, aged in oak, and with "only" 15.8% alcohol!!! Detail: Soledad insisted that we taste this wine last, after first tasting three reds. And wasn't Soledad absolutely right? Riomístico is so powerful that it didn't "die" after the reds. In other words, an exceptional wine, which forced me to bring three bottles to Brazil! Therefore, an unmissable visit for those who like high-end wine!!!

review_text: We did the on/off recorded bus tour of Santiago. If you have no other way to see Santiago this tour is better than nothing. As you drive through interesting looking neighborhoods you will hear a most boring history of it with names you've never heard of nor will ever hear of again. But the most annoying thing about the tour is the bus! I've done on/off double decker bus tours in London and Hong Kong so I thought this would be similar with an upper deck for those wanting an unobstructed view and a lower deck for those needing shade or warmth. So mistaken was I. The buses have a canvas roof on the upper deck and a back wall with no windows at all. There are 2 horizontal bars on the windows, apparently to keep the passengers from leaning out to get pictures of the skyline and the other interesting things that the low roof and narrow windows block. Santiago has some magnificent buildings and wonderful views but you will not see them unless you are sitting in one of the 4 seats in the top front row (and then you will only have about 6 inches of leg room). Look for my photo of desperate passengers crowing at the front window while the bus is moving trying to get a picture and blocking what little view the other passengers have behind them. The first thing that came to my mind was that this was a bus designed by lawyers that would keep people from leaning out the side of the bus and keep anyone from getting sunburned. What they have created however, is an incredibly boring dialogue and a bus that destroys any meaningful views. What to do instead? Learn from my mistake. Read Trip Advisor first and take one of their more custom tours with a live tour guide; or hire a cab and have them drive you around the same route. You will do it way faster, the cab driver will know more interesting and current facts than you will hear on the recording. Then, when you are done with the cab tour, take the metro to places that looked interesting. El Golf, the Mall, Bella Vista, City Center, all are easy to get to on the metro. The only way the on/off bus could be a average deal is if you start early and only have to pay 1/2 price. At US$40.00 per person it is a ripoff. A fair price would be US$20.00 per person. A better tour at a higher price will be a better value than this. Actually, watching a good video of the city highlights then taking the Metro to see them would be way better than this on/off bus tour. We appreciate your comment dear traveler, it is very important for us to know about your experience.

review_text: 1) They forgot about me and almost didn't pick me up. I waited until 8:45pm the night before and they had not messaged me with transportation details so I sent them a message. When they didn't respond at 9pm I messaged Viator support to notify them of the situation so I would have more evidence for when they didn't pick me up the following morning. Viator added those details in my booking just in case they didn't and sent an email to Discover Santiago asking why they haven't shared details with me. Wouldn't you know about 10 minutes after Viator yelled at them I get a message on Whatsapp saying "we didn't see your phone number but now it works!" Lies. You forgot about me. But details were shared after. 2) The "tour" is not conducted by Discover Santiago. After the above was fixed I got a message from the driver who was using a completely different WhatsApp business account. The driver was nice but didn't speak a word of English. We used a different tour guide at the equipment rental as a translator. 3) This is advertised as a scenic tour with multiple stops (as you can see in my screenshot of the itinerary of what to expect). That is not true. It is simply transportation for either Farallones family park or Colorado ski resort. We didn't stop at the other spots listed and entrance to Farallones was not included as advertised. I was taken to Colorado resort and basically wondered around the parking lot for 3.5 hours. As I bought a sightseeing tour, I had no interest in skiing. The driver did make an effort for me by picking me up after those 3.5 hours to take me to a town 10 minutes down the road. Nice gesture but there was nothing there. A much smaller ski resort and only hotels I didn't have access to as a non guest. This stop was a lot more boring than the 3.5 hours at Colorado. 4) Now that I've been I understand why no company offers a sightseeing tour. Because it's basically impossible to do. The only things to do are skiing or the other activities at Farallones family park. Doesn't matter what company. Those are literally the only things to do. Because this was falsely advertised I gave it 1 star. It's merely transportation and there are significantly cheaper transportation options. Review of: Full Day Valle Nevado y Farellones

review_text: The Museum is worth visiting just to see the grounds and the architecture of the inside. If, like me, you have almost no knowledge of Spanish or Chilean history, you have two choices: Take the audio guide and spend the full 90 minutes listening to each section in sequence (as otherwise it wont make sense) or just dip into random bits. There are video clips with English subtitles. A lot of it is gripping and chilling drams, as Allende gives his final speech from the Moneda Palace, set against Pinochet and his cronies justifying seizing power. Individual stories are most compelling: Two teenagers set on fire by the army, then a politician explains that it was all their own fault and the army was no where nearby, blatantly lying. I wnated to know if the USA was complicit in supporting the Pinochet regime, and how he came to be tried in Britain, but if this info is there I could not find it.

review_text: I chose this tour over other companies because it was advertised at 4 hrs not 6-7 hrs by two others. This is not a complaint but it was more like 6 hrs anyway. No way could they do the drive and be back in 4 hrs. The tour started at 9 am but we were told we would be picked up at 8.15 am but the transfer bus was 20 mins late. I understand this can happen if people keep the bus waiting and also due to the traffic. The young girl told me I had to pay when we arrived at the bus depot but this was a mistake. I had already paid. We took this tour in December and expected it to be cool so we had wind breakers but my husband wore shorts. We stopped at a concession on the way and walking on snow was mentioned and hiring boots, ski pants and jackets as it was snowing up the top. I believe this costs for the package 24000 pesos which is over $30US We decided due to our age we would not be walking on snow but Jaimie the guide came and suggested my husband hire ski pants as he would be cold walking to the restaurant which was very considerate of him. This was 8000pesos around $11US which used up most of my Chilean currency. These guys supplying the gear have a captive audience and while my husband needed warm pants I thought the charge excessive for a few hours. My advice is take a warm jacket, wear jeans and sneakers with socks. I am 69 and decided to walk to the look out and up the hill in my sneakers wearing my wind jacket. I only had cotton pants and a t-shirt underneath the wind breaker. A fleece jacket and another jumper would have helped but I certainly did not need boots and ski pants and was glad I did not pay the extra for something not needed - not in December anyway as there was lots of places to walk without going near snow. Other tour companies were stopping at this shed to hire gear as well bu do not be sucked in. We stayed up at the resort for over 1hr 45 mins which was probably too long. After walking around the only other thing to do was sit in the restaurant. Jaimie the guide was very nice and Jan Carlos the driver was amazing. 63 hair pin bends and I felt safe the entire trip. If you do walk take it easy as you are at 3000 metres. It is like you are on top of the world. So glad we did it. The restaurant at the top was very nice with a good range of drinks and snacks or meals available. Thank you very much for your comment! We are glad that you had a good experience with our service and we appreciate so much your recommendation. We hope we can travel together again in the future. Best wishes, Turistik Team

review_text: I think this is very different if you're traveling as part of a tour. Traveling alone, I checked the closures list and this was listed as open. But when I stopped in at Hierbas Buenas we were told that the roads were closed due to conditions. Bummed, because it was early evening at that point, and too late to head back to SPdA area to find a place to camp, the rest of my evening before dark was spent trying to find a camping spot in the area. But it was pretty unclear where to go, where to drive, what was safe, etc. So I don't think I actually saw the main part of this. The surrounding area was very pretty, and the treacherous road down into Rio Grande was gloriously fun (not sarcastic! Ended up camping in a pull off on the uphill portion of the road between Hierbas Buenas and the precipice of the hill before you start to descend down into Rio Grande. Not sure if it was kosher - a kindly tour guide said there was no camping in the area, but losing light, I did the best I could. No one bothered me, and I had an amazing view of the canyon from my tent when I woke up the next morning :)

review_text: What a fantastic place! Just on the outskirts of town you will find Nina, who cares for her horses (and dogs and chickens) with love. My guide, Stefanie, was awesome. She is super friendly, knows the horses and the terrain extremely well, and is great to talk to (in English, Spanish or German). I like to ride but hardly ever get a chance to do it. But I was galloping behind Stefanie in no time. Of course, galloping is optional, and you can enjoy a nice leisurely walk if that’s more your speed. The terrain looks tricky in places, but just trust your horse and you’ll be fine. They walk that route all the time and they don’t want to fall either :-) I chose this place because they were the only ones who would book a single rider. So if you are a single rider, look no further. But the reason I will go back, and the reason everyone should choose this place, is because they love their horses, they love people riding their horses, and it shows. There were a few other riders when I started, but they did shorter rides so I had the last 90 minutes as a private tour. Well, not technically private, since several of their adorable dogs accompanied us. I had a great time riding, talking, and taking in the incredible views. When my ride was over, I had a beer with Nina, helped Stefanie wash my horse, and got a ride to the metro stop from Stefanie. It was perfect.

review_text: Very few countries have been able to squarely address in such a clear fashion the difficulties of a social conflict. It is astounding that such an institution has been built in a country in which none of the perpetrators of massive human rights crimes have yet been brought to justice. It is a truth that you might pass an agent of torture on the street in Santiago without knowing it. However it is the aim of this institution to provide a societal memory of these events with the aim that future generations should know and the conditions should be avoided so that it never happens again. This is not an easy place to visit. It does not avoid directly presenting some of the worst activities human beings perpetrate on other human beings. For me the image that brought it home was the map of torture centers across the country run by the military regime. For others it might be the wall of faces of people who disappeared under that regime without a trace and whose whereabouts remain unknown. Highly recommended.

review_text: We were picked up at our hotel at 7.30am, by the time we picked up other passengers and arrived at the trail it took 3 hours. The hike is at 2200m so you do feel the affects of increased heart rate. Our guide Fernando was fantastic at keeping the group together and keeping us informed of our environment and educating us all. The colours of the landscapes are surreal and magical, we never tired of the vistas. The lunch at the small lake was delicious and practical. We loved the hotsprings. Watching the sunset at the end of the day at the end of the valley with speciality wine and food from Chile was an added trip. review_text: It should have been a 28 km round trip from the hotel but our guide pushed us to do the longer route (about 40km) as there was just the two of us and he knew we were quite active, which I am pleased he did. The extension was a lot more of a mountain bike experience (ups and downs with a few squeaky bum moments) than the simple ride up the river bed. We got to it by going past the sign that said “end of route” and then when we hit the main large river we took a right at the fork. We had to walk our bikes up a narrow gully due to the steepness and the sand but once over the hill it was down hill all the way. This route takes you past the church. Throughout the scenery is spectacular - a cross between the gran canyon and the canyon down to Petra! Cycling at altitude wasn’t an issue at all for us - but the heat of the desert was. Every few breaths it was like all liquid in your mouth had evaporated. I Had to talk to myself “breath in through nose - out through mouth” for a substantial chunk of the ride! If I had known I would have taken a scarf to breath through as that would have also dealt with the dust issue! A few other things to note - take water! We are reasonably fit but still drank over a litre each. - the map at the entrance is comical - for some of the distances it literally says “?” - I think the bike breaks are the wrong way round compared to the uk. Me and my husband kept on pulling the wrong one on the steep down hills and that’s the only explanation I can think of! - if your not use to cycling on sand - low low gears!

review_text: If you are looking to get out in the Andes and hike and not just take pictures, this tour is for you! We did a private tour, which was much better than a group! It is more personable and you control what you want to do or how long you want to stay. While the tour picks you up early in the morning from you hotel, it was very convenient and better than having to uber to a meeting point. While we had been out late the night before, the tour guide allowed us to stop at gas station to grab snacks, water, etc. Thank goodness! From the gas station, we then took about a 2 hour drive into the mountains. While the drive was beautiful, the ride was not very smooth. The road winds a lot and the pavement eventually stops half way up the mountain. Then the ride very becomes bumpy. Once you get over the bumpiness, the tour guide (Gonzalo) was very interactive and knowledgeable about the region. He shared with us a lot of facts and showed us every thing along our ride through the mountains. He even let us out to snap shots of things along the way! Including a Casino! This trip would not have been the same without Gonzalo! He was extremely helpful while hiking. He was engaging, personable, funny, and was able to guide us through this trek at +8000 ft. When the rocks were a little tough, he was there with his hand to help us all down. He even gave up his jacket when we were cold! I definitely recommend a good pair of sneakers or hiking boots though! While the trail is not very difficult, it does have some uneven surfaces and the altitude is high. The lunch and wine provided were amazing; the pictures incredible, the experience priceless. If you're in Santiago and want to explore the region with a local, I would definitely recommend the private tour and ask for Gonzalo! I definitely recommend a good pair of sneakers or hiking boots though! While the trail is not very difficult, it does have some uneven surfaces and the altitude is high. review_text: We took on Villarrica with the help of these guys and we can't thank them enough. From the start Willy gave us a full overview of what the day would involve, the difficulty, the dangers and what to expect. We set off on a very clear morning and were making good time up the mountain. Unfortunately for us there was a rock slide and everyone tried to move out of the way. Myself and my boyfriend didn't manage to move out of the way quick enough and got hit by these pretty big rocks! The dangers are real, I guess we couldn't predict that! The guides did everything they could to help us and got us moving again as quickly as possible. We made it to the top and we were unlucky to find there was a lot of smoke and clouds at the top so we didn't get any views of the lava. We saw pictures from the previous day though and you could see right into the crater! That's the luck of the draw! Then came the fun part! We slid down the snow on our bum boards! We were pretty happy with this too as I don't think we would have made it walking all the way down with our injuries. Again the guides were really helpful and made sure we knew how to slow ourselves down and waited for us to get our bearings. It was so much fun sliding in the little paths made for us, descending through the clouds! When we got past the snow our guides took my boyfriend's bag and gave him hiking sticks to help him walk. After about an hour walk sliding down the sandy/rocky areas (I actually enjoyed this a lot!) we got back to the car and they immediately put him in the front seat so he wouldn't have to walk anymore. Back at the office we were greeted by Willy, who was very concerned about our health and offered to take us to hospital if it was needed. We had some beers with the guys in the sun! We had a great day and wouldn't have been able to do it without the help of our guides, a big thank you to them and Willy!

review_text: Ten of THE most memorable miles imaginable. The infamous Rio Futaleufú Class IV-V rapids. Including a pause to tombstone into the abyss, and (deliberately) plop out of the boat between the rapids to bob down on the currents like an otter… From Futaleufú (9am), our group of twelve were driven a few kms out of town with the crew and boat trailers in convoy to the ‘start’. We gathered for introductions by Sharon and a safety briefing by Mauricio – fortunately for me, every one of the Rio Fataleufú Rafting (RFR) team speak good English. Then a quick change into thermals, wetsuits, wetboots, life jackets, and helmets (size details are taken when booking, so everything fits). Our clothing and towels were safely packed into secure sacks to be driven down by the attentive and friendly support crew. Group and individual photos were taken by our host Sharon. She’s a ray of sunshine and a very good photographer, popping up on the river shore several times on our descent with her long-lensed digital SLR camera. We then split into two groups of six – a disparate range of nationalities, ages, shapes and sizes – you’re as young and fit as you feel! Our boat skipper/navigator was the charming Jorge. Shadowing each blue inflatable was a ‘rescue’ canoeist and banana-like catamaran – manned by more RFR experts. They take it in turns to skipper the various craft – RFR often do all this twice a day! I should point out at this point that all the RFR pilots/navigators grew up in Futaleufú and ‘on’ the river – they all know it like the back of their hands. There are family pictures of them as youngsters canoeing on the river in the ‘shop’ in town on Pedro Aguirre Cerda. Of course, there are a number of other W-W-Rafting companies based in Futaleufú, all claiming to offer similar experiences. On that, I cannot comment. Happily, by agreement, each company staggers their start times (an hour+ apart), so you feel like you’re the only people on the water at any one time – a genuinely humbling experience on such a majestic stretch of glacier-fed turquoise water, thundering down between those towering exposed rock faces. Then onto the water – at a very calm point of the river. Whilst slowly drifting downstream, more safety and skipper’s spoken commands were explained by Jorge, including (for practice) each of us plopping into the water and our assigned ‘rescue’-buddy pulling us out – we’re going to get soaked through anyway very soon! For the next few minutes as the boat drifted towards the first of the rapids (which we could feel and hear downstream), there was crew-bonding banter and tension-building anecdotes by Jorge. All the while, Jorge was explaining, demonstrating and instructing us on how and when to paddle or to instantly crouch down into the bottom of the boat to avoid being bounced out like a frog! We did the ‘Puente-A-Puente’, plus two rapids beyond as far as ‘Sorpresa’. I won’t describe in detail here the roar of the water, the speed, the roller-coaster effect, and the adrenalin rush of each set of rapids – I’ll leave that to your imagination! After each rapid, you cannot wait for the next, but are grateful for the few moments in between to catch you breath! As we approached each ‘set’ of rapids, skipper Jorge explained their nomenclature, length, ‘difficulty’, the optimum line in and out, and the distribution and shape of the rocks beneath the waves, etc. Names like Terminator, Pillow and Toro adding to the anticipation! Just be ready to row like Olympians to make sure you hit the Pillow face at the perfect speed and angle! Half way down, we caught up with the other team and stopped for a minute or two to climb ashore and up onto a rocky ledge. One by one several of us tombstoned into the abyss below! I have Sharon’s photo of me mid-flight to prove it! Then onwards to several more sets of rapids and a couple of opportunities to plop off the side into some relatively calmer water to bob down on our backs like otters, before being hauled back into the boats. If conditions permit (height/speed of water on the day) I insist you take that opportunity! The safety boats are ALWAYS nearby. At the end of our adventure, Sharon and the support crew were there to meet us on-shore with our towels and dry clothes, and a picnic table with very welcome cold beers, juices, coffee, cakes and snacks. We were all exhausted – both from rowing and from grinning from ear-to-ear! A real post-exhilaration high and sense of achievement and teamwork – though we all concluded it was Jorge who really did all the hard work and that our paddling was simply to keep us all focussed, balanced, and leaning in the right direction! Even before we headed back to Futaleufú, Sharon had already prepped her photos into individual boat folders, and simply AirDropped 120+ HiRes photos to my iPhone on the spot! Unusually and definitely worth noting, RFR charged nothing for those photographs (download later via email link is also an option). A day or two later, she’d kindly uploaded and shared a link to 3.6GB of 2k footage from Jorge’s POV helmet-mounted GoPro which I was able to download when back in the UK. Priceless audio/video and photographic memories! We were all safely back in town by 2pm. Then a short stroll back to Mirlo’s Hostel (also very very highly recommended). Although RFR often do two trips a day, for the time you are with them, you are ‘today’s’ VIPs! A five-hour, very highly recommended fabulous experience! Thank you. “¡Adelante!”

We personally loved the possibility of coming aboard the ships and touring them from the insides, especially the Nao Victoria itself. It was truly a unique experience.

review_text: For taking in the staggering beauty of the Atacama night sky, you can’t beat Atacama Desert Stargazing. They pick you up and drop you off at your hotel and Jorge provides a fascinating introduction to astronomy and walks you through the night sky initially with the naked eye and then through a half dozen or more telescopes in his backyard. We were a small group of six and everyone had plenty of opportunity to ask questions and view the extraordinary stars through each lens. Fluent in English and Spanish, Jorge was quite entertaining, but he is so passionate about astronomy that the details might be more than some travelers will appreciate. I took the mid-length program that lasted about three hours, including a break in the middle with snacks and warm beverages. Jorge also offers shorter programs which may be more in line with some people’s level of interest. As he spoke, we sat back in our seats taking in the incredible, expansive sea of stars above; following his directions or just gazing in wonder. The Milky Way soared up through the center of our view with the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (satellite galaxies of the Milky Way) floating to the right, the Southern Cross, the False Cross, Venus and Mars, as well as Sirius and other bright stars were clear as could be. At the end of the evening, Jupiter rose above the horizon and we could see the planet in all its glory with four of its moons. Just like Galileo! And we got to see enigmatic Canopus flickering in white, blue, and yellow through the humidity low on the horizon. Jorge also provides brilliantly detailed photos of you and the group standing beneath the expanse of stars as a perfect souvenir. If you find yourself in San Pedro de Atacama and want a fascinating and awe-inspiring evening viewing and learning about the stars, I highly, highly recommend Atacama Desert Stargazing.

review_text: We wanted to visit Museo de Pablo Neruda. It is a truly exceptional place well worth a visit. The grown ups loved it. Our kid also loved it. review_text: We just travelled the Puerto Montt to Puerto Natales in June and it was sensational. The prices were extremely low at this time of year, wildlife is sparse just a few seals and birds to be seen but there were only 3 tourists on the boat and a handful of locals meaning we had the decks to ourselves to take in the views. We paid for a twin room with no bathroom or window and were upgraded to a room with a private bathroom with window. The boat is basic, but it is a cargo ship, if I were paying the summer rates I would probably be disappointed. We were very lucky to have Percy the guide on board with us to tell us what we were seeing along the route. The food was fantastic in our opinion, huge portions and as a vegetarian I had my own special meal every lunch and dinner. The open sea section of the cruise was exceptionally rough and lasted for 19 hours as the wind slowed us down. Be sure to go on the boat armed with sea sick tablets to be sure you enjoy the trip. If you are thinking of booking this in winter do it, it is a wonderful and relaxing way to travel south and to see Patagonia. It is also a cheaper way to travel to southern Argentina as buses in Argentina are exceptionally expensive. You can cross the border from PN to El Calafate and head straight to the glaciers!

review_text: We had a terrible weather here (January): very windy, cloudy and lots of rain. All the attractions lose their charm in such weather. The wind on top of the Mirador Del Mote Ferrier was so strong that it blew my friend of her feet. Luckily, she was far from the edge of the hill. Another example - the famous torres were hidden in the clouds and the mist. I would consider myself unlucky but the staff in our hotel (Lago Grey) actually told us that this kind of weather is pretty common in the park. If so, going there is a gamble: fantastic views & experience in good weather (easily 5*) or a barely enjoyable windy and rainy stay (2*?). Note: At the entrance you should have Chilean Peso (they don't take cards and there is no ATM there). They might also accept US Dollars but the notes have to be pristine (they didn't accept any of the three 20-dollar bills I had because they had minor marks/stains on them - back in the US all three were easily accepted).

We were the only ones on the tour which actually made for a better experience. Our host, Barbara, was energetic, knowledge and her passion for wine making made the tour incredibly enjoyable. We got to see how the wine is made, had a go at at sealing a bottle and then got to taste three amazing bottles of wine. I was convinced I hated Chardonnay until I tasted Aquitania's Chardonnay. All of the Aquitania wines were far nicer than those we tried at other vineyards in Chile. The red wine was so good that on arrival back in the U.K. we tracked down a supplier and bought a case. Being mainly a rose drinker I was gutted that we can't find a supplier of Aquitania rose in the U.K. currently but we'll keep trying!! A special thanks to Barbara who really made this tour. Even in the winter it is well worth a visit.

review_text: If you want to drive your day trip to Lauca National Park consistently and guaranteed 100% to the wall, this provider is warmly recommended! Why? We booked this tour with a guide - and got a tour with a clown called “Freddy” who apparently sees himself as the greatest entertainer/animator of all time. Probably for this reason he continuously demonstrated his (not least thanks to loudspeaker system) unmistakably non-existent vocal skills by permanently repeating the first verse of the same song. This tinnitus suspicious torment was interrupted only by a loud splash of mostly banal words and his regular and non-occasional howling, reminiscent of the howling of a shot coyote. What else is there to report from this memorable day? For example, that he drove past all designated lookouts and instead headed for places that were only partially suitable for good photographic subjects. To compensate, the passengers had to stop there for silly hands-on games. Only proven masochists may appreciate that the car radio was turned up to maximum volume. By the way, Freddy doesn’t even begin to notice that he’s quite alone with this as funny as he thinks he is. For a tour guide, not exactly a predicate of quality... Those who speak/understand only English will not be allowed to expect too much information from their 15-word vocabulary in this language. Catering: maximum frugal. As a result, he turned down the air conditioning permanently to the limit, with the driver and passenger windows open. The result was ice-cold drafts at their finest, as the multiple requests of different passengers helped nothing. Also not quite without problems the fact that he threatened to fall asleep several times on the way back... Tough words, but “Freddy” she really worked out honestly over a day that was too long. We have booked several tours in the last few weeks, all of them excellently guided and therefore have quite comparison possibilities. The question remains as to where the many good reviews come from... By the way: Unlike some guidebooks, the national park is now easy to explore on your own and with rental cars thanks to well-developed roads.

Great day out, thoroughly recommend it.

review_text: Our family went on the tour today with Felipe today. I could not fault the tour. They are easy to find in the main square in front of the cathedral, wearing red (don't confuse with competitors). Our tour commenced at 10. I had done some research on the sites I wanted to see and the we went to all of them and more, without the hassle of looking at maps and reading guide books. The commentary was excellent, and not cheesy. Felipe really brought to life the coup against the Allende government in a very accurate way in front of the presidential palace. He described the views of people in a very balance way, and when he provided an opinion, he made clear it was his view. The spot we briefly stopped for lunch was surprisingly good value and good food- great empanadas ( not that you had to eat). I suppose how good the tour is depends on which guide you get, but it is hard to complain for the cost! The tour took about 3.5 hours and was not a difficult walk.

Note that much of the rest of the museum is only in Spanish, but still well worth a visit. The courtyard café is delightful, with an extensive menu, BUT very popular with locals from 1 -3, so plan your break accordingly.

review_text: We arrived in Santiago in the morning from the U.S. and decided to have something to eat then dive right in with a bicycle tour. Whenever we travel we try to see the cities we visit by bicycle, it is such an intimate way to get to know the area. We were greeted by our guide Fabian with a welcoming smile and he introduced us to the others in the group. We were told exactly what to expect and we set off on our Parks and Politics tour. Fabian was so cheerful and informative, you can tell he truly loves his job and his city!!! At one of our first stops we were told about the stray dogs of Santiago. We hadn't been in the city long enough to see many of them, so we weren't sure of what to expect. As we rode through the city we began noticing these rather healthy, well fed dogs lazing about, in some cases in the street where the buses politely go around them! We rode through beautiful parks and were learning about some of the history and key neighborhoods of Santiago. Fabian mentioned he had a couple of pals that like to join him on his tours. When we arrived at the Presidential Palace we got to meet a couple of these pals! Here enters Rojo and a currently un-named pal I called Rufus! (He just had that look). These dogs were so happy to see Fabian they barked and barked interrupting the other tour that was at the palace. It was such a joy to see these happy dogs and from that point they joined us on the rest of the tour, it felt like they were kind if looking out for us as we rode on the bike paths through the city. We enjoyed the tour so much we came back the next morning to do the Market tour. It was just as awesome and we were lucky enough to get Fabian as our guide again!! The street art in Santiago is amazing and we rode through neighborhoods where is was plentiful! We saw Pablo Neruda's home and visited a local produce and fish market that will blow your mind! And don't forget the dogs! We were joined by Rojo, (Rufus), and another pal Chuleta (pork chop) on our morning tour who very kindly guided us to the markets. We enjoyed sopapillas and coffee in the market, got to see the locals shop and continued to learn more about this lovely culture. Thank you Fabian for introducing us to your amazing city. You made us fall in love with the people, food, art and of course your dogs!!! These are the tours to do in Santiago! What an incredible city!

review_text: Andres was helpful from the very beginning with planning our trip to the Lake District in December. Even though we only started planning a month before visiting, he was able to talk via Skype to discuss what we (my husband and I) were looking for and customized a trip to meet our wants (budget and things to see). He was flexible throughout the process as we went back and forth to make the trip exactly what we wanted. Before we arrived he had booked our flights to and from Santiago/Puerto Montt. He advised us on lodging and offered to book for us, but had no problem when we decided to book on our own. On our first day he arranged our pick up from the airport by Marcelo who was waiting for us as soon as we arrived in Puerto Montt. He offered a brief overview of Puerto Varas via car before dropping us at our hotel. The next morning, Christmas Eve, Andres picked us up in his SUV and we toured Osorno Volcano and Todos Los Santos Lake. It was clear our first day with him that Andres loves Chile and sharing with visitors. Andres arranged for us to visit Peulla with TurisTour on Christmas as he was spending the day with his family. This tour was okay, but we were disappointed as most of the activities were not available once we got to Peulla (we had hoped to horseback ride). I will say the tour arrived at the scheduled time and returned us at the appropriate time (we had read reviews that this was a problem). The following day we were back with Andres guiding. He took us to Chiloe where we visited Ancud and the Penguin Colony. Our last day we were supposed to do trekking in Alerce Andino National Park. It turns out they had changed the path to make it easier, which was great for me, but my husband was a little disappointed it wasn't harder. We enjoyed a small lunch packed for us by Andres (he had snacks for us every day) at a beautiful lagoon before heading back to the airport. Throughout our time with Andres he did his best to accommodate our varying interests. He knew my husband was interested in nature and tried his best to point out interesting flowers/plants on our various hikes. He even stopped by a random farm and asked if we could watch them milk the cows. We did and even bought some queso. We mentioned we liked markets and he took us to one in Ancud and Puerto Montt. We've had our share of private tours and I would definitely recommend traveling with Andres as your guide, just be sure to tell him exactly what you are looking for and he will certainly do his best!

In 1979 one of the hillsides collapsed after heavy rainfall and 10 people lost their lives. All of them were “pelillo” collectors. Pelilo is a kind of red algae used in the food and cosmetics industry. It is collected and dried, after which it is ready for transport.

review_text: We spent two wonderful days with Andes Explora guides, our first trip to Loma Larga Winery and Vineyards in the Casablanca Valley, then a day hike to El Morado in the Andes. Each of these were great trips, and even the scenery on the hour to two hour drives each way were informative and beautiful. Loma Larga is a boutique vineyard with a tour of the facility that is highly informative. Prior to the tour, a horseback ride of about an hour through the vineyards is a delight. The day hike to El Morado is about 10.5 miles, give or take. Somewhat steep at first, it is a very doable hike that is striking in scenery...El Morado itself is breathtaking. Of equal memory, however, were our guides...Javier for the wine valley, and Frenanda and Camilo for the day hike. Each has a wonderful personality, and a real dedication to the outdoors. They are helpful, kind, and energetic young folks who were a pleasure to be around. Their English was excellent. Javier and Frenanda also served as drivers during the respective trips, and gave us safe and enjoyable transport. I can recommend these guides and Andes Explora without hesitation, and would love to go on another excursion with them. Thank you very much for your great review. review_text: We just returned from a one week trip organized with BlueGreen Adventures and these guys are fantastic. We were traveling with a pretty wide range of ages (75, 68, 40, 38, 9, 6 and 2) and abilities. As our wonderful and knowledgeable guide, Chris, explained to us, he had a "Plan A, Plan B, Plan C and even a Plan D," and he really did. Our 2 year old was pretty tired at one point so we cancelled a planned hike but Chris had a Plan B (or maybe it was even a Plan C) so we just did something else (involving Chris teaching our girls how to skip rocks along Grey Lake). We went on a horseback riding excursion and my 6 year old (who has been riding horses for 3 years) wanted to ride on her own (without being tethered to the guide) so Chris stayed right alongside her and helped her through the ride. He and our driver shared their stories about Patagonia and their love for their home was so evident. Not that the area needs any help in showcasing its beauty, but these guys made us fall even more in love with the area. Their knowledge of the area was also tremendous. They spotted wildlife that we never would have seen without them and we constantly felt like we were being let into some secrets of Patagonia, something we could not have felt without being with these guys. These guys also helped organize a camping trip which was another family highlight. Even though we travelled with young kids, Patagonia was the perfect vacation spot with kids. They ran and played and spent HOURS exploring the outdoors. It was honestly, the perfect family vacation. Bluegreen adventures gave us the opportunity to see this part of the world - and we owe a great deal of this trips success to these guys. Can't recommend them enough.

review_text: If you only have time to do one tour when in San Pedro de Atacama, I would really recommend doing the Valle de la Luna and Valle de la Muerte. We booked through our hostel (EcoExplor) so I'm not entirely sure of the tour group's name (sorry) but I think they pretty much all charge the same (it was pretty reasonable) and go to the same places. I thought the scenery was really incredible and learning about how it was formed over millions of years was really thought-provoking. Watching the sun setting over the canyon below and the way the colour changes over the rocks and the volcanoes in the background was unforgettable. San Pedro is an extremely expensive place and this is one of the least inexpensive things to do and one of the most worthwhile. I would pay to do it again. (Possibly if you have been to Arizona or the Grand Canyon you may not find it as amazing as I heard some people comment on how similar it was.)

review_text: Pablo Neruda was quite a character; poet, diplomat, architect, bon vivant and probably Chile's most famous native son. If you intend to go to Chile, particularly Santiago and Valparaiso, read up on the man so that when you visit this house and his others in Santiago and La Isla Negrita, you'll understand what he was all about. Of his three houses, the one at La Isla Negrita is reputed to be the finest (we missed that one), La Chascara in Santiago probably would rank second and La Sebastiana would be third but that said, it still demands a visit! Neruda loved the sea and all things nautical but, unfortunately for him, he was not a sailor... the waves made him sick! To appease his love for the sea, all his houses were built with a nautical motif. From the picture, this house is shaped somewhat like a tugboat and faces the Bay as if it's about to sail off. It is built in four levels, the highest, as seen in the photo, the captain's command post. Naruda was a compulsive collector of knick-knacks found at flea markets and auctions around the world during his travels. He also had many friends who would pick up stuff for him that he might find amusing. Much of it is on display at his houses and the variety and breadth of these collectables is amazing. La Sebastiana is located at Ferrari 692 near the top of the steepest street in Valparaiso. Unless you take this as a personal challenge, do not walk up this hill. A cab will cost a couple of bucks and even they struggle to make it!

review_text: We rented a vehicle in Puerto Natales and drove out to Torres del Paine National Park for the day. It was an easy drive, well marked and very little traffic. Some of the road was gravel as we approached the park. In the park, all of the roads were gravel, but they were in good condition. When you get to the park entrance, you can avoid the long ticket line if you are in a personal vehicle. Just bypass the line and go through a door in the back of the building. The lines are for visitors coming in by tour buses. We saw lots of guanaco as we entered the park and a fox alongside the road. We also saw flamingos on a lake outside the park. We made a stop at Sendero Mirador Cuernos, a beautiful waterfall. It was a short walk from the parking lot to the falls. We drove through the park by numerous lakes and mountains. We drove as far as Grey Lake. It is a beautiful lake with a glacier at the end of the lake and icebergs floating in the lake. Because it was cloudy and a little rainy, we did not get a view of the tops of the mountains. We did not take any of the boat tours or do any hikes due to the weather. However, it is a great drive regardless.

review_text: I visited in early Spring, and had three 1-day tours, returning to base in Puerto Varas each night. I can really recommend these if you only have a day or few spare in the area - I flew in specifically for this, but MotoPatagonia supply the bike and all gear in excellent condition, so I could plan this trip in a few days off work without having my gear with me in South America. Each day’s tour offered something completely different, from Volcan Osorno and Lago Llanquihue, to a taste of the Carretera Austral on day 2, to the coast of Llico Baja on day 3, with a mix of tarmac and gravel/dirt roads well off the beaten track. Having considered a rental I’m glad I went for the tour - as I was a solo rider on my first tour, Daniel was able to tailor each day to my skill level, and was a great guide pointing out points of interest along the routes. Prior to the tour, there was clear contact with very quick responses to any questions I had, with Daniel and Paula making the whole trip absolutely seamless. They were professional at all times, and extremely welcoming, friendly and personable - it’s obvious that they really care about giving you the best possible experience. Overall the trip thoroughly exceeded my expectations, I’m already hoping I can come back to push further south! review_text: In my opinion this is the biggest and most diverse mall in Santiago, having lots and lots of different stores in all directions. In more than one ocassion you WILL get lost, but thankfully there are interactive maps and information counters to help you out. Some stores have a "tourist only discount", so don't miss that. The mall is divided in two: The normal "inside" mall and the "luxury district" on the outside with some pricey stores and lots of different restaurants of all kind. It's an amazing mall that you'll find difficult to visit just one time! ProTip: There's no subway station nearby, but one 4-5 blocks away. If you are staying very far from the mall I reccomend getting there using that station and then walking to the place: There's a big and beautiful park in between, so you'll enjoy a great view while you walk.

review_text: Pickup from the hostel was in time but we arrived at the parking almost an hour before sunrise in minus temperatures. We were the first group. There an outside basic breakfast was served. Followed by long explanations by the guide in two languages to the point it had became light and other groups were already exploring the geyser field. Also once at the geysers the guide continued interesting but long elaboration about the sights. The English speakers could take some pictures while the Spanish talk was done and vice versa. After that he would clap hands loudly in order to collect and count all 27 groupmembers (to be honest I felt like a cow). It was a bit stressful for me and after little free time and only halfway the field we were guided into the bus (so the second half would be simply bypassed by road). Time wasted again to collect all 27. Now we were ready for the highlight: The stretch with the biggest geysers with the volcano in the background. And a natural pool to enjoy a hot bath. Until now the sun had still not climbed above the mountain range and I was now ready to enjoy the fabulous sunrise and the field being illuminated by the sun. Followed by a bath. But no we were only allowed 40 minutes at this site just enough to either explore the bigger geysers or get in the pool. But not both. Dissapointed also because it was still so early. Hand clapping and shouting again. Stress again, and I did not get in the bath yet. Had to skip this highlight. Sad. The reason for rushing so much became clear soon: We were taken to a village where tourists could buy things like souvenirs and snacks. Great (not)! Spending there around 45 minutes. Then we rushed back to town arriving half an hour ahead if schedule. I had been looking forward to this excursion for months but for me this company put the focus on the wrong points and did not deliver. 1. A group of 27 is just not efficient (while the prices are in line with companies who take smaller groups, they make their business mostly through commissions to the popular accommodations in town). 2. Lots of explanations could have been done in the bus allowing much more fun time on site. 3. The breakfast should be skipped or be faster. 4. Why giving the guests equal or more free time in a random tourist oriented village than at the world class natural attraction (after all it is a geyser tour so there should be all the focus). 5. Why cut short the total excursion time with half an hour, why the rush please consider how much you could have pleased your guests by keeping the promise of your flyer. All in all not the great experience that was hoped for.

review_text: I was on the cruise from Puerto Montt to Puerto Natales with my girlfriend in October, 2017. The cabin has an ok size - we had one with two bunk beds, without private bathroom. The beds are nice and clean, and long enough for me (187 cm). The width is however not to be discussed with - only one person - so don't even try. :) The shared bathroom(s)/toilets were quite nasty - particularly the mens'. Quickly it started to smell, pee on the floor and there is no paper or functioning hand-dryer after washing hands (even though this was pointed out). Lastly, I only had cold showers - and not by choice. The food was so-so. What it doesn't have in quality, it has in quantity. But I really didn't expect anything from this, so I was happy. The dessert is always some kind of jelly which you shouldn't expect anything from. However, I was told that the vegetarian food, overall, was quite decent. The staff is, almost, the highlight of the trip. They're all really nice and helpful. The service-level is very high, in general. Long story short: They helped me get treatment for borrelia (which I catched in Ecuador), with great professionalism. There is a nurse, Hugo, on board. Percy is mentioned a lot in here - and for good reason. You can tell he loves his job, and is just as much an entertainer, as a guide/naturalist. The other guide, Christian, is also a really good, dedicated and helpful guide. What did we see? Albatrosses, penguins, sealions, dolphins (Peale's), stormbirds, ducks, gulls, condors, turkey vultures and plenty of other birds. If lucky, you can see whales or even Orcas. The landscape is of course also a great deal of the experience, see the pictures. Here there are mountain-passes, fjords, waterfalls and glaciers. Good to know: - The staff will have pills against seasickness (they will come in handy during the 12 hours cruise in the open pacific) - Don't panic about long (or the total lag of) respond-times during booking and e-mailing with Navimag. This is one og the major flaws of the organization. Things Seem to work out in the end anyway. - Make sure to book in a timely manner during the high-season (jan/feb) - or in general in order to save a bit of money - The ferry sails once per week from Pto. Montt (Friday), so plan accordingly - There are English-speaking guides (also during off-season) - The consumption of alcohol is prohibited (so don't bother bringing any, like we did :)) - There are Daily activities like yoga, classes on flora, fauna and tips on Puerto Varas and hiking in Torres del Paine All in all a very nice experience. You 'll have the opportunity to just sit back and relax, without WiFi, and without thinking a whole lot about what to do the following day. It is a nice break during a longer trip. However, I wouldn't go as far as calling the trip a "must". It is MUCH weather-dependent. Hello, we appreciate your comments, we are glad that it was a positive experience and that you have commented on the aspects that we can improve. Greetings and thanks for traveling with Navimag.

review_text: Tour: Upon arrival we were greeted with some amazing complimentary spiced hot wine. I have never seen anything like this in winery. It starts with a walk around the vine trees explaining the history of Pablo Morandé (owner of Bodegas Re) in Casablanca and how he collaborated to change it from cattle and dairy farms land to one of Chile's best known wine regions. Further, the guide accurately described the grapes used by the winery, what type of barrels they use, the logic behind going back to ancient wine making, and other well known concepts such as dry farming. In particular our guide was able to educate us on how wine making is different between certain regions (or valleys) in Chile and why Bodegas Re decided to work with certain grapes. Moving forward we visited a room were they make liquor from mixing fruit and aguardiente (similar in origin to brandy), followed by looking at how they also make balsamic vinegar. The tour ends with a visit to the barrel room where you are shown clay pots where wine is fermented as in the older days. One thing that caught my attention is that we saw the owner of the vineyard, Mr. Pablo Morandé, actually working on it, and by that I don't mean greeting costumers and putting up a smile (never saw him smiling), but rather he was moving around with a bucket making sure the process of pumping wine from the bottom of the tanks to the top was going OK. For those of you who love food, is like seeing the actual chef/owner of a renowned restaurant in the kitchen, something that indeed makes one feel better about the whole process. Lunch: Our lunch was simple and catered with 4 wines (we got the whole bottles, not just a glass) plus a bit of their liquor as a digestive. Our first course was a duo of soups (lentils and squash) paired with a Pinotel (mix of Pinot Noir and Muscatel grapes) which we though was interesting but not overall accepted. The wine has indeed sweet and had a certain crispiness which made it interesting for an appetizer wine. The second course was a shrimp risotto with salmon paired with a Chardonnoir (60% Chardonnay - 40% Pinot Noir. Same mix as base sparkling wine). We though the wine was indeed very pleasant and refreshing, filled with the buttery notes of the Chardonnay and the expressiveness of a Pinot Noir. Third course was meat slowly cooked in the casserole paired with a Cabernet (Cabernet Sauvignon and Carignan), a lovely strong wine that bring up the together the fruit of the Cabernet Sauvignon and the acidity of the Carignan. Finally, for dessert we had leche asada, a typical Chilean dessert paired with Syranoir, a mix of opposites that made up for an excelent closing. Store: The stores upstairs is filled with options to buy either clothe, wine, liquor, vinegar, etc. The prices are a bit cheaper than retail price (maybe 10%) but not great. The pricing of this vineyard is something problematic to me, as sincerely I like their wines but feel they are a bit overpriced. I understand the amazing marketing and commercial work being done here is something that needs to be reflected in the prices, and indeed they cannot pretend to look as a boutique winery having cheap prices. In the end, along with marketing the price give wine a bit of status and they surely know that. Notwithstanding the above, I suggest to try their Syragnan, a blend of Syrah and Carignan priced at CLP 13,000 and that in my opinion is a lovely jewel still at an affordable price (if compared for instance to a CLP 29,000 Cabergnan and a CLP 19,000 Chardonnoir). Price of the tour and lunch: You need to make a reservation in advance and a deposit equal to 50% of the price. In our case the price was CLP 33,000 per person which included the tour (about 1 hour) plus lunch and wine pairing. Although not required, make sure to tip the guide as she does a terrific job, something that you will realize once you tour other vineyards.

review_text: I always wanted to go to Easter Island and Cristian with Ecotours helped plan three wonderful weeks in Chile for me and my wife. Cristian booked a 5-day tour to Easter Island, a 7-day tour to San Pedro de Atacama and day trips to Valparaiso/Vina del Mar and Casablanca. He also arranged domestic flights from Santiago to Easter Island and San Pedro. It was a pleasure dealing with Cristian. He was extremely responsive and was even able to get us business class on our flight from Santiago to Easter Island for only about $70 USD more than economy. Our 5-day trip to Easter Island was everything that I had hoped for. In 5 days we practically hiked the entire Island. We saw all the main tourist spots in addition to places that were off the beaten path. We were often the only people there! Our tour guide Thais was very good and knowledgable about the island. Our 7-day trip to San Pedro de Atacama was really spectacular. Every hike that we took was different and better than the previous one. Our guide Mariano was extremely knowledgable and we felt well taken care of. We were always hiking through spectacular areas without any other people around. This is a very special place. Both of our day tours were also fantastic. We were very satisfied that all of the tours arranged through Cristian ran without any hitches. On our last full day in Santiago (Christmas Eve), Cristian even met us at our hotel and gave us a bottle of Chilean wine. All in all a fantastic trip to a wonderful country. One thing I did not anticipate was how expensive Chile is. I always thought South America was a relatively inexpensive place to travel. This is not true for Chile, although I would go back in a heartbeat. If you go to Easter Island or San Pedro make sure you have Chilean pesos for park entrance fees. In Easter Island you purchase a park pass right after you exit the plane (and before you get your luggage). If you pay in Chilean pesos you will save quite a bit versus paying in USD. Also, many of the sights in the Atacama desert have entrance fees, some of which are upwards of $25 USD per person. If you are on the fence about going to Chile or using Ecotours, don't hesitate. You will be happy you did.

review_text: I took my daughter (15) to los Queñes for two half day kayak lessons. She had taken some lessons in the US (rolling and basic strokes) but had very little experience on moving water. Our instructor Benjamin was excellent -- knowledgeable and patient. He went out of his was to make sure my daughter was safe and having a good time. The equipment was great -- brand new NRS gear. We spent Saturday practicing strokes and rolls on some currents in front of the "Cabañas Los Queñes", and the pool at the cabañas. Sunday Todd (the owner) joined us and we went up the Claro River a couple of miles and ran it down to the cabins. The river is amazing -- green water, fantastic scenery and just challenging enough for us. We stopped at all features -- and Benjamin and Todd carefully went through the lines and hints. By the end of the run my daughter was enjoying some class 2/3 rapids. It was a fantastic morning on the river! What a great day. We appreciate being apart of your father-daughter outing. And we look forward to many more.

review_text: For our weekend getaway from Santiago, my wife and I booked a whole-day horseback riding tour. My wife had some experience on the horse but I had nada. So I was a bit nervous, but after 10 minutes on the horse, we were on our way. The ride takes us all the way up to the ridge of the steep mountains that surrounds the canyon. It’s crazy scary, because there is a very little room for an error and looking down the canyon was just too scary. But horses are very well trained and easy to ride that for someone with no experience, I started to feel like I was in control after a an hour or two. The view is just spectacular, and by the time we got to the ridge, I felt like I just crossed the Andes. I realised how tough it is to be a horse and huasso in Chile with so much to traverse with so little shade. I now understand why Chupalla has such a wide brim. This was not possible without Pablo, who was our guide horseman. He is seasoned, friendly and English-speaking, which helped me immensely. We trusted him and he did a great job to teach me how to ride a horse from zero. The cost is 60,000NOK per person. It includes a well-trained and cared horse, trust worthy guide, 6-7 hours of breath-taking ride and a grill feast near the mountain top, including beer, chorizo sausages, a big chunk of steak and tasty salad made on the spot. I have to say that as someone who has no experience on the horse, it helped that my wife knew how to ride so I rode between Pablo and my wife. Maybe if my wife was also inexperienced, then it might have been a difficult tour. So if you want to do this, it’s best to have one person in your party who can ride to make sure you are okay! 100% recommended! And ask for Pablo :)
