review_text: The volcano and the whole climbing is a memorizable experience! Totally worth the exhaustions of the tour. Very important: you really need to be in good shape for the whole trip. That means: If you don't do any sports or have never gone on a hiking trip, this might be too much for you! In our group of 12 people, 3 couldn't go to the top, ergo a waste of money... The trip is a bit more exhausting than an ordinary hiking trip: it includes snow hiking with cramp-ons, gravel treks (also a bit exhausting) and a very steep final stage with a lot of large cobbles. One good thing for those who are not sure if they are fit enough: there is a lift for an additional 10000 pesos that saves you 400 meters in altitude. Everyone who has only experience in hill climbing is strongly recommended to use that. One last point: the trip was very fast. That means there are rather few breaks and these few breaks are very very short. Hence, there is not much time for taking photos during the climbing, since you need to use the break to eat and drink... Hence, you should insist on a break whenever you need it (we were a bit too shy...). However, we heard that the tours offered by the other agencies are just as fast, so there seems to be no way around that... Overall, the volcano is so astonishing including the smoke and the lava, that it was totally worth the efforts of climbing to the top!!!

review_text: I closed all tours with Horizon Atacama via WhatsApp a few weeks before the trip. We made the following tours: cejar laguna, puritama thermas, valle de la Luna, geysers del tatio, altiplanic lagoons and red stones, hidden lagoons of baltinache and the Uyuni Salar. The last two tours were made with a partner company from the horizon. Overall, I recommend Horizon, I just found that there was a lack of transparency. But if you want more comfort I recommend closing with another company. A positive point is that every day they created a group on WhatsApp informing the schedule and recommendations for the next day's tour. They always arrived at the right time. Some points that could be improved: 1. The snack was always the same, every day. 2. In no tour provided chairs at the time of the snack in the middle of the desert (some companies provide and seems better the experience of eating enjoying the view). 3. They did not provide roupão on the tour of the Puritama Thermas and it was very missing because there are 7 pools to know and it is cold outside the water (some companies provide such as Araya and Pukarami Travel). 4. They informed that the tour of the hidden lagoons of baltinache and the Salar de Uyuni would be carried out with a partner company, but with the same quality, and that was not what happened. The quality was very inferior and if I knew before I would not have closed these tours. The van from the hidden lagoons arrived late and there was no WhatsApp group to know what was going on. In addition, the van was old, small and crowded. It was very uncomfortable since it was a long journey. The guide, who was also a driver, did not have the same quality as the other guides from Horizonte. 5. Missed to inform with details how is the tour of the Salar do Uyuni. The information they send is very little. I closed the package with room and private bathroom and although I knew that the hostel was simple, I did not imagine it was so simple that there was no heater (we took negative temperature), nor Wi-Fi. It was very cold in the room. The food was also very simple, repetitive and was always cold. It was 4 days and 3 nights and I found it very bad. These are important details that should be described clearly for everyone. The ride car for 6 people also became very uncomfortable since the last seats are very tight and it is not possible to sit normally. The journey is very long and exhausting. The first driver was also very rude and treated us badly when he saw that we were carrying 4 bags. 6. All tours, including the Salar de Uyuni, on the return do not leave at the hotel but in the middle of the square. I found it absurd, at least Salar's should be left at the hotel, since everyone's with bags and backpacks.

review_text: Cerro San Cristobal is a destination that offers an enriching experience for any tourist, especially for families with young children. The experience begins with the climb on the funicular, a transport structure that arouses curiosity about its angle of ascent, a detail that not only attracts attention, but also invites reflection on its engineering and how it integrates with the natural environment. It’s a perfect opportunity to get into a journey that combines respect for nature with innovation. Upon reaching the top, the viewpoint provides an excellent opportunity to interact with the Chilean community, appreciating the panoramic views of Santiago and enjoying the local culture. Here, we taste delicacies such as the mote with bone and the "palm tree," a sweet similar to a millet but round shape, which adds a gastronomic touch to the tour. The visit to the sanctuary of the Virgin, at the top of the hill, is a highlight. The structure, with different levels, allows us to understand how the construction has adapted to the geography of the hill, creating a space of tranquility and spirituality. It is a place that witnessed a Mass officiated by Pope John Paul II, which adds historical and cultural value. The cable car descent offers a new perspective on the hill, revealing the diversity of the park and its multiple levels, with different areas and activities that invite you to explore and enjoy as a family. It is clear that Cerro San Cristobal has been designed to offer a complete and binding experience, where you can appreciate both nature and urban life. A highly recommended destination that combines adventure, culture, and spirituality masterfully.

review_text: After climbing the vulcano in Pucon I decided to take a multi-day beginners white water kayaking course. I never did white water kayaking before. Because of the positive reviews at tripadvisor I decided to check out kajak Chile. And I was not disappointed. It was perfect: Jon, my instructor (english - speaking, he is from the states) was amazing. He did everything to make me enjoying all the days and helped me to progress fast. All his hints and exercises really helped me to improve myself in the lake and the river. In addition there is no fixed training plan. You dont have to commit to a week of kayaking. You can start with one or two days and if you like it you can extend it. Also depending on your progress every day can be adjusted to your needs (class I-III rapids). And what I thing ist very important for a beginner like me: he really takes care for you in the water. I never felt unsafe. The only thing to improve may be the wet - suit and wet-shoes. They were a little worn out. Besides that the kayak and the paddle were in good conditions. I also compared the prices to other places in Chile and it seemed to be slightly cheaper. If you want to start white water kayaking, this is a perfect place. Thanks again Jon for this amazing course and good luck in Pucon. We're glad you were able to experience Pucon to the fullest! Thank you for bringing the shoes to our attention; we should have a shipment coming in for next season. Stop by next time your in Pucon, its always cool to see if our previous customers are continuing their kayaking careers!

review_text: I should start by saying that I am no longer as young and fit as I used to be, that's why I rate a group tour visit to Moon Valley only three stars, since these tours are primarily geared towards adventurous backpackers. I did not expect having to crawl crab-like through a dark cavern (without being advised to bring a torch, because it seems to be taken for granted that everyone carries a mobile) or scrambling up uneven rocks and occasionally knocking your head or hip against one of them. To say nothing about walking up a sand dune. The tour was sold to us as an easy walk, and that it was not. The only easy part was viewing the sunset, and that was truly spectacular, although I have seen better ones elsewhere. But there were other spectacular sights on the way worth stopping for, and these were totally ignored. So if you are in any way incapacitated and/or dislike group tours, and of course have the financial means, I'd recommend visiting the valley with a private guide or hire a car and take your own time to do and see what suits you rather than what the tour operators think you should see and do.

review_text: This was my least favorite of the three tours we took by far. Also, it was more than 4 times the cost of other trips. The first stop is a lagoon that you can swim. Literally they are just 2 holes and nothing else. You can see everything needed to view from the bus. Then you go to a lake in the desert, which is pretty cool though. But is just a lake in the desert. The tour ended with some snacks and a glass of Pisco Sour. The drink was the best part of the trip I am sad to say. If you are thinking between this and another trip, definitely consider another. This trip is just not worth the time and money.

review_text: I did this tour on my first day in Santiago and I am so glad I did - it enabled me to get a feel for the city and the things that I still wanted to see or do again! review_text: We had greatful day with some friends at the vineyard. The place is located at an astonishing mediterranean climate environment near Santiago (about an hour away) and is guarded by a chain of white mountains. The sights of the landscape in a clear day is beautiful. Our tour included a bike-trip arround the huge vine fields that surround the central winery; brand new and good quality bikes makes the tour easy and funny. The guide was very nice and had a deep knowledge of what he was showing us, the growth of every vine depending on its class, and the kind of soil beneath it, the factors that make a harvest be more predominant in some flavours and touches than the other... He was a local person who had worked in those fields since he was 18, and in the meanwhile he studied to specialise and improve in the vineyard management. Those things are the ones that make the difference in tours of this kind. After the ride we had an incredible lunch at the italian-inspired restaurant of the winery; awsome itaslian delicatessen, wonderful wines and excelent attention of the staff. After that we had a tasting of olive oils, olive oil-based mayonaisses and of course several wnderful wines. In summary, it was a great experience to see, smell and taste the flavours of Santiago's periphery.

review_text: Chile's pledge to never again allow a military dictatorship to rule with an iron first for 17 years (as Pinochet did) is epitomized in this wrenching exhibit. The human cost was unimaginable - 80,000 Chileans detained, 40,000 tortured, 3,200 executed & countless others forced to leave their families and live abroad is an abject reminder to the world of the darkest days in Chilean history. The methods of torture, the objects political prisoners made while in detention, and the national and international protests come to life in displays, personal accounts, and audio and video clips. Allow 2 hours (at least) to take in this account of recent history. Don't miss the documentation center on the 3rd floor where (thanks to the Ford Foundation) you can see media clips from the BBC, etc. from the period 1973-1989. The exhibition is free and English audo guide is a must. My only criticism is the museum was very hard to find - across the street from Quinto Normal metro, with an entrance on the lower level. I needed to search for it as there are no signs.

review_text: In-bounds groomed run skiing is most suited to intermediate and advanced intermediate skiers. Unfortunately most of the time we were there the ungroomed areas were not in a ski for fun state - icy refreeze, breakable crust and wind blown snow, very challenging and nobody on it. Later it did snow and the place just opens up - fantastic lift accessible side country and the back country options look amazing with little walking required. Lifts are fairly old, minimally padded and fixed so fairly slow. The lift operators are moderately helpful and will generally let a beginner learn the hard way as witnessed several times, it's not that they don't care they're just quite relaxed - I have skied for 41 years. Tip - go early-ish and go to the top car park. In holiday time the more accessible 'Tata' car park and lift area fills with beginners - we had a one hour wait for a ticket one day and then a 25min wait for the chair!..but nobody at the top of the mountain. In saying that the Tata car park is a better choice if the road is icy as the final stretch to the top car park could be diabolical. This would be one of the only resorts around where you can watch an active volcano venting literally just beyond the end of the chairlift. Ash is in the air, while not noticeable it is better not to use your best pristine white ski jacket - save that for Aspen or Kitzbuhel ha.

review_text: We did both the morning and afternoon tours in Santiago and they were both great! We had Antonia and José, both were so fantastic and enthusiastic. The morning tour takes you through the fish, fruit & veg and meat markets (whilst pointing out the restaurants to come back to!), before jumping on a train and heading to the beautiful Santiago Cemetery. We saw the grave of Salvador Allende among other beautiful mausoleums and we finished the tour in a bar with a free glass of the popular 'terremoto' cocktail, delish! The afternoon tour taken by Antonia was excellent. We learnt about the Chileans love of the stray dogs in the city, saw the beautiful cathedral as well as Parliament House and other great land marks. We walked through 'New York Street' and the London Paris districts before finishing up in Lasterria for a free glass of the delicious (and sweet) borgoño! Thanks Tours 4 Tips for a great day out in Santiago!

review_text: This was the last point of our five-week journey, and it was the best ending we could have had! Traveling through changing landscape: lagoons & volcanoes, various rock formations including canyons, on the third day we reached the Salt Flats. The views along the way were stunning. We couldn't get enough of them. The sunrise on the Salt Flat was the most surreal and amazing thing we’ve seen so far. We had an excellent guide and driver – Filemon. He was friendly, very helpful, creative (thanks to him we have some funny short films and a lot of nice pictures), spoke English and had a lot of experience driving off-road. We spent two nights in Villa Mar and one in Hotel Salt (private room with bathroom). The rooms were basic but fine and clean. Sometimes they turn off the electricity for the night, so if you want to charge your phone or camera do it as soon as you arrive. The food was good and varied. You can ask for a vegetarian diet when booking the trip. One more thing: we almost canceled this trip due to the symptoms of altitude sickness that had appeared during excursions from San Pedro de Atacama (El Tatio Geysers & Altiplano trek). Luckily nothing happened except for a slight headache. But it’s good to keep in mind you’re at high altitude there, so try to prepare your body before you go.

review_text: Enchanted by the company’s marketing (or better, deceptive advertising), I decided to close the Atacama tours with them. My father and I were making a dream trip, something we planned and saved for a long time to live, but unfortunately the agency did not keep what it promised. To begin with, the company outsourced virtually all the tours. Of those we hired, only one was carried out directly by them – we identified this because the van had the agency logo and the guide wore uniform. All others were operated by third-party agencies, without any prior notice at the time of purchase. Even simple details, such as the promised bread on the tours (which is from a particular bakery), were not delivered as announced. The owners of the agency disclose videos on social networks stating that they do not outsource the tours so as not to lose quality. That is, they know that outsourcing compromises the experience, make advertising ensuring that everything is done by them, but in practice, deliver the service to any random agency, deceiving customers. The worst happened on November 18th, 24th, when we had a scheduled tour to the Laguna Cejar (one of the most important of the trip, because I wanted to float in "salt water"), which simply didn't happen. The service has already started badly, with the van delaying more than an hour to pick us up (scheduled for 14h, but only appeared at 15h40). However, the worst part was to discover, upon arriving at the venue, that the agency did not have permission to enter the Laguna Cejar, information confirmed by both the guide and the guard of the park. The question remains: how does a company sell a tour to a place where it has no access permission? And worse: how can they handle this situation without even giving an explanation to the client? Probably not going back to Atacama, and the agency took my chance to live this experience in one of the most amazing places in the world. If I knew that before, I would never have closed up with them. Atacama has several agencies that offer tours at fairest prices and also have guides who speak Portuguese, making the experience easier for Brazilian tourists. A simple walk through the centre of San Pedro de Atacama already allows you to find much better options. After months of contact attempts, the agency just “solved” my problem in March, returning the price of the ride. However, this does not compensate for the damage, as the greatest damage was to trust a company that sells services that it cannot provide. Therefore, if you intend to travel to Atacama, do not entrust your dream to this agency.

review_text: We had a day to kill in Punta Arenas so signed up for Best of Patagonia: Forest Hike + City Tour with Borealis Adventures Patagonia. We had beautiful weather and the hike was a gentle, undulating one through a pretty second-growth forest. It took about three hours due to the guide’s penchant for stopping every 10 or 15 feet to talk at us (very annoying). Be sure to bring your own water as none will be offered. After we got back to the car, we ate a delicious vegetarian sandwich standing beside the road, and then started the “city tour” part of the day. The guide took us to the cemetery and a museum. There was no overview of the town or commentary about places we passed. I asked to return to the hotel after the museum, sacrificing the prospect of tea with our guide. The tour was overpriced at US$153/person. Review of: Best of Patagonia: Forest Hike + City Tour Thank you so much for this feedback. We are sorry that this tour did not live up to your expectations. In order to make this service accessible to adventurers of a wide variety of ages and abilities, we pace our walk at a very leisurely speed, with many stops to allow passengers to catch their breath and to allow our guides to share information about the flora, fauna, geology, and history of Patagonia. We are always working to refine our abilities to gauge our passengers' interest and fitness. You are absolutely correct that we do not offer bottled water. I have updated our tour description to further highlight this and encourage passengers to bring their refillable bottles, so that future passengers will not be unpleasantly surprised. As a sustainable company, we do our best to reduce single-use plastics, and we will continue to strive to improve our communication to this end. I am sorry to hear that you were not able to finish your tour, as we certainly feel that the tea, coffee, and desserts, along with the drive through the Croatian sector and tour of the Croatian style house add value to our tour. However, we completely understand your choice. We appreciate your comment on our pricing, as we are always seeking to deliver great value to our customers and price our tours fairly. We will review this tour's content to see how we can improve to this end. Wishing you all the best!

review_text: The National Monument El Morado day trek was amazing! I did it in early April and had a wonderful time. Awe-inspiring views towards the peak and glacier that just keep getting better and better as they get closer. We had a blue sky day which couldn't have been better. Rodrigo was a great guide and I needn't have been concerned about the level of difficulty. It's certainly a full day (we were on the trek for 6 1/2 hours, including plenty stops and a good picnic) so not suitable for someone who's not accustomed to walking, but the path was good. It's steeper at the beginning but does level out and the valley is beautiful. Rodrigo said the walk is one of his favourites because it's greener than some at slightly higher altitudes. He was also good at pointing out birds and other wildlife. I would love to get back to Chile and would happily do another trek with Andesexplora. review_text: I initially booked four tours with another agency in Atacama, but for one of them, we were transferred to a tour with Atacama Connection. Our guide, Sarah Jones, was exceptional—not only did she possess extensive knowledge about the places we visited, but she was also incredibly kind, ensuring we had ample time to fully enjoy the views and take photos. Because of her, we canceled our remaining tour with the other agency and booked four tours with Atacama Connection. For three of the tours, the agency accommodated our request to have Sarah as our guide! All the tours went smoothly, and we were very pleased with the agency's service. My only complaint was regarding the Rota dos Salares tour. We were not informed that the temperatures could drop significantly lower than on the other tours (it was -7°C on our day), which left us unprepared. Additionally, for this particular tour, we were reassigned to another agency. I prefer when tours are conducted by the agency we originally booked with so we know exactly what to expect. However, from what I’ve observed, it seems common for travel agencies in Atacama to transfer travelers to other tours when they don’t have enough participants for their own.

review_text: Reports of difficulties experienced by travelers in Uyuni are not uncommon, so we looked for an agency that had good value for money and were prepared to stay in simple places, with little infrastructure. Initially, the service at the agency was friendly and attentive, which surprised us positively. The problems started when we left Chile and entered Bolivia. At that moment, while part of our group followed in 4x4 cars from WWW itself, my family and another couple were redirected to a car from the Voy Tours agency, without further explanation. The car was in terrible condition: the driver's side mirror had the glass broken in half, the glass was cracked, the windshield was broken (in times of heavy rain, he had to get out of the car and wipe the window with a flannel to be able to see what was coming in front of him). , dashboard lights all on, hood half open. Furthermore, especially on the first day of the crossing, the driver - who had spent the night driving, as we later found out - was very sleepy, giving him a terrible feeling of insecurity at the wheel. Little by little, we noticed that the WWW guides were attentive to their groups, even giving us instructions throughout the tours, while the one who would be responsible for us didn't even get out of the car. The peak of stress was on the last day of the tour, when we got up at 3:30 in the morning to watch the sunrise over the Salar and the car simply wouldn't start. After a wasted half hour and countless "pacifier" attempts to revive the bodywork, we managed to get out and, finally, follow our schedule. The landscapes along the crossing are, in fact, impressive and, given so many negative reports, we didn't even think the accommodation/food was that precarious. The big problem was the fact that our tour was outsourced to another agency that showed zero care for the integrity of our group.

review_text: Navigating the Patagonian fjords will undoubtedly be a memorable experience as it was for us. The boat rides offered from Puerto Natales will take you on the same path that some 460 years ago the Spaniard explorer, Juan Ladrillero, sailed in search of the occidental entrance to the Magellan Strait, the natural connection between the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans. These navigations were a full-day experience that depart from the docks in Puerto Natales around 7:30am and return at 5:30pm. The journey took us to the Balmaceda and Serrano glaciers, the first of which will be seen from the boat, while the second required an easy 30 min hike to get right up to the front of the ice. During the ride we passed by many sea lions and Cormorant communities, encountered many different marine and land birds, and got to see the untouched flora of Bernando O´higgins National Park.

review_text: The entire itinerary, 3 days 2 nights in Bolivia, was impeccably planned from the moment we arrived, drove around Bolivia and left San Pedro De Atacama. It was worth every penny! Christian would promptly respond to my emails and offer excellent suggestions and advice. We flew into Calama, where a driver was waiting for us. From there we drove to San Pedro de Atacama to stay the night and start the tour to Uyuni the next day. I read a lot of mixed reviews about border crossing. It was extremely easy and safe. Although we drove for long hours over the three days, the views across the Bolivian landscape were spectacular. We had no issues with altitude, even though we were above 4,000 meters for the most part of our three day tour. We stayed the night at the Salt Hotel in Colchani. The stylish rooms were heated and the water was hot too! We also stayed the night at another hotel in San Pedro de Quemez, made entirely with volcanic rocks, Hotel Tayka, run by the community. Once Again, border crossing back into Chile was simple and fast, where we were transferred immediately to the airport in order to catch a late flight back to Santiago. Sol, our tour guide, did an amazing job showing us around Bolivia. She was knowledgable and fun to be around. The same goes for our driver Simeon who organized our lunches really well too and entertained us with good music. We were very happy with the way the trip was planned, away from the crowds. The hotels were clean and managed professionally. I can't think of anything to complain about. All the parties involved involved were well aware of everything, clearly indicating that there were no communication issues between the tour operators, guides and drivers who all worked together to ensure our safety and satisfaction. Thanks Christian for organizing a memorable holiday and making sure we saw everything we wanted to see. The salt flats, lakes,volvanos, rock formations and beautiful flamingos. Not to forget the peaceful Siloli desert. I would definitely choose you again!!

review_text: I was so excited to go here, as they make my favourite Sauvignon Blanc in the world (yes, even compared to NZ!). I didn't even know it when i booked it, but i was getting my very own personal tour! Alejandra was very kind, knowledgeable, and passionate, and taught me a lot. The grounds are beautiful, and the tasting was the best experience i have had. I had a tour in the Maipo valley, and the tasting was done standing up outside - on a windy day! How are you supposed to experience the wine out in the wind?? At LL, we sat in a nice little room with tons of sunlight, as i was given a generous portion of cheese and crackers, and sampled, i think it was 5 different wines, catered to me from what i had told her about what i was interested in. And the wines were fantastic! The Casablanca valley in Chile creates what is known as 'cool climate' wines, every one was unlike any i had had. Lesser sunlight creates a slightly less tannic wine, yet they are very flavourful and complex. I also tried one of their young wines, not as complex, which normally doesn't excite me, but it was really nice, with a simply beautiful acidity. A must if you are visiting vineyards in Chile!

review_text: In short, good option if everything goes well with the car, but really terrible if it doesn’t. Just know that once you take on a ride with Camper Travel, you are on your own, at your own expense. Longer version: One thing I have always heard about Patagonia is that things never go as planned. Well I did not expect to start with the car rental. Poor communication - communication with Sebastián (sales lead) was difficult and uncoeherent. Very low time response and lots of follow ups required from my side. Sometimes it wasn't there at all. The examples below affected my trust, as a customer, right from the first day out of my 6-week trip. Example 1: upon the car pick-up, the car was totally different from what I have ordered online, not a small Suzuki Jimmy but rather a pick-up from a chinese brand that I have never heard before. While I was being talked to into the advantages of this car over the other, I was given no option either than accepting it because there were "no other cars available". I was cornered, either accept or cancel my trip. The car itself was good which I only found out later after accepting it, but the communication with the customer should have been there. Once I approached this the reaction was that I "(...) got a better a car than what paid for (...)" but for me that wasn't the point. Example 2: I wanted to be insured to the maximum to cover any incidents. I was told previously that there was an insurance that would cost 850eur with a deductible of 450eur in damage - some sort of 'premium insurance'. Upon car pick-up suddenly that insurance was not available anymore and I was led to stick to the basic insurance. After a second call with the sales lead (Sebastián) then the insurance suddenly existed again and I went ahead with It. Poor customer relationship mgmt - regardless of what happens on the road whether it is an accident, or some part of the car structure gets loose and breaks; The customer is ALWAYS fully accountable with no room for arguement/defense. Example 3: the kitchen of my van got loose with use - probably I could have been more gentle with It too - but haven't the kitchen gotten a strong reinforced support for the heavy weight it carried this would never happened (tiny and few screws were supporting It). I took the car to the mechanic and he shared the same statement directly with Camper Travel. However, Camper Travel still held me fully accountable for the damage (which was later deducted from my 2000eur guarantee), rejecting the possibility of sharing the cost as I suggested. Example 4: upon car drop off we did a general check to the car and signed the respective papers without any damage to report. From then onwards, the responsibility is on Camper Travel. Nevertheless, 36h later Sebastián reached out to me stating that there was damage in the tent and they would deduct It from the guarantee. Not only this is unfair It is also illegal. Camper Travel Chile held my guarantee of 2000eur for longer than 72h while the contract states 24h. Low maintainance - the add-ons which are built on the car get damaged with use overtime, its normal. It is necessary however to invest on maintainance and supervision before car handover. Example 5: again, the kitchen sliding support was not enough and required further reinforcement. The plastic straps for opening the tent were overused and dry - I could not open it without using a supplementary tool. The pipe for draining the water from the sink broke during the car pick-up. It took 5 minutes for one of the guys from the crew to fix on the spot but broke again later with use - which I ended up fixing myself. The air chamber of the spare wheel was one size smaller than the actual tire - putting constant pressure on the air chamber - so I ended up being stuck at the middle of no where in the carretera austral at 6pm as the spare wheel blew up 10 minutes later after replacing it (ended up staying overnight and hitchiking next day with the wheel). Regardless of my transparent approach throughout the whole trip - by reporting all incidents related to overuse or negligence on pick-up - I was held accountable for all incidents in the end and consequently got them deducted on my guarantee, despite of my repetitve explanations. All in all, accidents/incidents happen and we need to deal with it, its fine. What it is the most unfortunate is that when you bring this up, you are received with non-constructive statements like the following ones, and makes you feel isolated: "you Broke It (...) It is at your own cost.", "(...) The van has been used by other people in the past and they had no problem". "(...) This would have happened in the first rental". We just cannot expect to have a fair customer oriented support when we have a number oriented sales lead dealing with the customers. As a last point, I contacted several times the founder (Rodrigo) to request support and I never got any reaction, reinforcing once again a poor customers experience. Avoid the emotional distress on your vacation and go for an alternative. Wicked or Cóndor campers are betters players out there - though products are a slightly different, they LISTEN to the customers.

review_text: I'm a wheelchair user and when looking for a tour agency in Chile I came across we love and I have nothing but praise for this company. Communication has always been very quick and objective, and the tours that presented some difficulty for those with reduced mobility, the guides helped with everything. The girls who helped me (Sara Gaby and Ellen) are wonderful and extremely quick with everything, from payment to questions that arose. The two guides I liked most were Danielle and Martín. Danny captivated me from the first moment, he made the trip lighter and more fun, not to mention his proactivity the entire time, from taking a photo in a beautiful place to worrying about how I would get down to the beach in one of the tours. I am in a wheelchair and this required special attention from the guides so that I could do all the tours, this happened from the guide Danielle at all times of the trip. I would like to thank we love for having the privilege of being able to travel with a wonderful guide and I recommend her to anyone who goes to Chile and takes tours with them. Martin, despite being more restrained, was also equally careful and proactive with me. At times I preferred to stay in the van (because being in a wheelchair it was more difficult to get in and out of the car) and he always stayed with me talking so that I wouldn't feel alone. (It's a small attitude, but it made all the difference for me). When we arrived at Valle Nevado, he went with me and my companion to the bathrooms and when we arrived at the place where we were going to watch the sunset we came across two flights of stairs, and he promptly volunteered to take me on his back. For me, this was the height of proactivity and commitment to work and to your clients. He was also a guide who made a total difference in my tour. Oh, and both demonstrated TOTAL historical and cultural knowledge of the places we visited. Que depoimento lindo We Lover! ❤️ A gente sabe que cada viajante tem necessidades diferentes, e nosso maior compromisso é tornar cada passeio especial e acessível. Pequenos gestos, como a companhia na van ou a preocupação com os acessos, fazem toda a diferença, e ficamos muito felizes em saber que isso marcou sua viagem. Obrigado por confiar na We Love Chile! review_text: We did a number of hikes in and around the W-Trail. I highly recommend the Los Cuernos trail and the trail to the base of the Torres del Paine. The Los Cuernos can best be viewed from the South side of the lake to the south of them. It is an amazing hike to do early in the morning as you get a great view of them and a great view of Frances Glacier. The hike to the base of the Torres del Paine is well worth doing. It is about 11 miles total, out and back. The final 1 km will take about an hour and a half to complete and isn't for those of average fitness. It is a pretty steep grade and involves a lot of navigation through stationary boulders (there is no scree). It is worth completing though. The park is well worth visiting and is one of the most remote and most beautiful places that I have ever been.

review_text: My wife and I were planning to be in San Pedro de Atacama for a long weekend and were interested in booking some tours. I contacted FIVE tour companies by email and only one of them responded (and that one with insufficient details to complete a booking). Then a friend mentioned that he and his girlfriend had just spend a long weekend there and recommended Turismo Layana. I emailed them and within a couple of hours they emailed me back with a proposed itinerary of four tours (then ones I had requested). They said I just needed to come to the shop once I got to town in order to confirm and pay for the tours (they accept cash or credit card). This was easy to do. For the early morning tours they picked us up at our hotel, and for the afternoon tours (3 PM departure) we left from the shop. This was convenient because was could have lunch at one of the many local restaurants first. We did the Valle de la Luna, the Geysers, the Lagunas Altiplanicas and the Laguna Cejar (for Laguna Cejar we actually went with a different tour company - none of the Layana guides or drivers were working that afternoon because of the Copa America final, but Layana organized this for us). Our favorite was probably the lagunas altiplanicas because we saw vicuñas, a fox, and flamingos on the same tour. Our least favorite was Laguna Cejar because it had an absurdly high admission fee and was by far the least interesting of the tours. The buses and vans were comfortable, the guides were friendly and very knowledgeable, and the scenery was spectacular. I'll definitely use this company again the next time I go to San Pedro.

For the early morning tours they picked us up at our hotel, and for the afternoon tours (3 PM departure) we left from the shop. This was convenient because was could have lunch at one of the many local restaurants first. We did the Valle de la Luna, the Geysers, the Lagunas Altiplanicas and the Laguna Cejar (for Laguna Cejar we actually went with a different tour company - none of the Layana guides or drivers were working that afternoon because of the Copa America final, but Layana organized this for us). Our favorite was probably the lagunas altiplanicas because we saw vicuñas, a fox, and flamingos on the same tour. Our least favorite was Laguna Cejar because it had an absurdly high admission fee and was by far the least interesting of the tours. The buses and vans were comfortable, the guides were friendly and very knowledgeable, and the scenery was spectacular. I'll definitely use this company again the next time I go to San Pedro.

review_text: Having visited most of the providers in Pucon, we decided to opt for Patagonia Experience. Although not the cheapest on the market, Richard convinced us that the insurance cover they had would mean a safe adventure. He also informed us that he would ensure two guides despite a tiny party of 5 - that sounded perfect. What unfolded thereafter was a clear day with little wind and a flawless ascent to the top, with our 'personal guide', Joaquin! The views at the top have been covered in other reviews - it has to be done to be believed - amazing! The service we received however, was particularly epic - kitted out with all the gear the night before to ensure that everything fitted, collected from the hostel on the morning by mini-bus, started the climb at first light, personal guide to the top and back, collected by 4x4 following descent, whisked back to the office for beer and biscuits in front of an open fire to chill. And Joaquin even ensured our safe return in time for the Champions League final - special service and very highly recommended! Thanks guys! I hope that you enjoyed the rest of your travels and that your team won in the football! All the best, Richard and the team.

review_text: One of the quirky houses of probably the most famous Chilean, Pablo Neruda. The house is very unique in both its design and furnishing. There are amazing views of Valparaiso from the living room and bedroom. You'll get an insight into Pablo's lifestyle in Valparaiso as well as some of his life story. The audio tour is available in English (and a few other languages) and is included in the entry price. Photography is not permitted inside the house. But once you're done with looking inside, you can go outside and take photos of the house as well as the amazing view. Lockers are available. You'll need to put in a CP$100 coin, but this is returned to you when you open the locker again to collect your things. The house is quite far up a hill, so I would suggest taking a taxi. Not far down the road is Museo a Cielo Abierto, so I would suggest combining your visit with this. There are some cafes nearby if you need a snack or lunch after your visit.

review_text: Summary: - Great trip but compromised by a (very) poor organisation and communication from the company. - Super friendly staff onboard - Price too high (even in a shared cabin), even more if, like us, you didn't get to see whales, dolphins or half the landscape hidden in the clouds (it's a bit the lottery, knowing the boat won't be looking for the animals, you either see them or you miss them). Honnestly, the price would have been 300-350$ it would be worth every penny, wether you are lucky with the weather/animals or not. --> clearly the priority of the company is the cargo, not the passenger, something we tend to feel in the general organisation (e.g. the numerous change of dates and schedule) To make it short, the positive aspects of the trip we took on February 14th (Puerto Montt-Puerto Natales) was the staff on board which was super friendly, the life on board which is a unique experience and the landscapes which are really beautiful. Sadly, there are some (a lot of) wrong aspects with this trip: - the general organisation is so wobbly and poor. At first, we were suppose to leave Puerto Montt on the 12th. Then, a wee before departure, it was on the 15th. 3 days later, they told us it would be the 14th (and I won't tell you about the hours, which changed so many times I don't recall). Regarding the arriving date at Puerto Natales, they changed of plan while on the boat, making us book a night at Puerto Natales while on the boat, a day before arriving. - the communication from the administrative team is really weak. For instance, they respond to your email four or five days later (if they do), they are hard to get on the phone, they told us about the PCR test we had to make only a few days before the trip (knowing that we left on Monday, doing one during the weekend went on to be really difficult...), etc. - sadly, and even though it's not their fault, we did not see many things during our trip. The promised whales were so far we only saw a few stream at the horizon, the dolphin spot revealed to be empty despite a beautiful weather and half the landscape was covered by clouds. Be aware that your trip and your money clearly depend on your luck, it's a bit the lottery (but let's be honnest if you win, it's worth every penny)

review_text: I am originally from the US living here in Santiago for a few months now, and wanted to take my father who is visiting me, on a tour of Santiago. I opted for the free walking tour and I honestly thought it was one of the best I have been on (I have been on a few in Europe etc.). It lasts 4 hours but you can leave at anytime if you have other engagements but I highly suggest to stay for the whole time as it will be worth your while. It helps show all the major locations and different museums should you wish to come back. You have a break for lunch and we went to a cute chilean restaurant in barrio lastarria by santa lucia hill and had a pisco sour and an empanada. Our tour guide was named Omar and he was so fluent in English and very engaging in all of his explanations and storytelling throughout the different sites. Having lived here and having already been exposed to many historical sites, facts etc., this tour really helped me pull all the pieces together. We were lucky to have Omar has our tour guide on a Monday as he usually does Sunday afternoon tours he said, but I know for a fact I will join a tour again when I have other family and friends visit. You leave a tip at the end according to your experience and I think I tipped more than the average *about $20 for my dad and I, but my justification was that I truly couldn't have gotten this detailed of a tour and fun adventure for this cheap had I paid for a guided tour. I tip on the quality of my experience, so do not think you need to tip as much, it was my option. Thanks Omar!

I thought this was the weakest stop on the trip because of how abbreviated it was. The lunch was great. We opted to skip the wine to avoid getting too tipsy, so I can't speak for the wines at that stop. The last winery was by far the most popular one. It included a tour of the vineyards, a good range of tasting, and you get to keep your tasting glass. Overall, this is an excellent option from Santiago. Santiago does not have many great attractions, so if you are in the city, I recommend taking some of these side tours to make for a more interesting time. This tour is a great option. review_text: We booked two tours with Stamp's Tours through Viator. The first day, we went to visit Santa Rita's Winery. A must! The owner of the tour agency, Emmanuel, picked us up at our hotel (on time), and he drove us to the winery, way outside the city of Santiago. He spoke (and understood) English well. He had a very friendly demeanor and we enjoyed riding with him. At the winery, an excellent guide (Daniel) took us through the entire process of wine making, ending with the tasting of three excellent wines. The local boutique sold these wonderful wines for $5.00 to $10.00...A steal! Emmanuel took us back to our hotel after recommending a good restaurant downtown. The next day, the whole day tour took us to the port city of Valparaiso, the resort of Vina del Mar, and another winery. Our tour guide, named Frank (or Francisco, or Pancho, your pick!) was born in Chile, but he also spent a few years in the U.S. His English was perfect, and he had a great friendly and charming personality! He was also extremely knowledgeable and he answered all of our questions. There were twelve Americans in the mini-bus (air conditioned) and we got to know each other at lunch in an excellent restaurant located above the port. The seafood was delicious and the view very impressive. The famed "Pisco Sours" were flowing and again, it was a fun time! Then Frank took us on a walking tour of Old Town Valparaiso, including the home of famed Chilean poet Pablo Neruda. All in all, an excellent experience with Stamp's Tours. Highly recommended! Additional comments: How could I ever forget to mention our wonderful bus driver, WALDO??? I know, I’m getting old...fast. This is why I have requested to edit the above review. I had the honor of meeting Waldo as he was waiting for us in the bus, at a rest stop. I suspect he understood a bit of English, but I opted to contact him in Spanish. A few moments later, we were discussing and laughing our heads off like two old pals! Under a somewhat reserved demeanor, I found a very nice man and we chatted again at another stop. He also took a very creative photo of my wife and I. During our final stop, Waldo surprised me with a beautiful Chilean cap as a souvenir of our meeting! Waldo was an important part of the tour, getting us safely from point A to point B, and back. As we parted, it was my great pleasure to tip him well, for his kindness and generosity.

review_text: The complete tour, including Laguna Cejar and Tebinquinche Lake took from 4 to 8 pm. Sunset at Tebinquinche Lake was certainly one of the most spectacular sights during our stay at San Pedro de Atacama. Plenty of opportunity to explore the salt flats here and take photos. There is SO MUCH salt! Lots of bird life here; the setting sun seemed to bring them out, and they swooped around the sky. Breathtaking. The lake itself had some flamingos on it. The ruggedness and extreme colours were beautiful, As the sun set, the colour on the mountains was constantly changing. All this was enhanced with snacks provided on the tour and 'pisco sours'. Excellent part of another great tour here. Highly recommended.

review_text: We are a big fan of the hop on hop off bus tours to find your bearings in a new city. We have taken loads of similar tours all over the world. It's normally a very quick way to pick up a ton of information about the city. However this was not the case. The narration is quite sparse with very little take away information. Just ages of buildings and their various heights. Another problem is that the stops are not all marked. The tiny map gives you an approximate position but you only know where the stop is when the bus pulls up. Found ourselves running down a city block to catch the bus sometimes. They are quick to point out that the busses stop running at 6pm, so you need to get on a bus before 5:30pm. Well we got on a bus at 5:10pm thinking it would take us home. Instead it went 1 more stop and parked up for the night, leaving us high and dry. Lucky we like walking and an hour later we got home. Don't waste your money. Buy a city guide book and use the metro's, they are far more reliable. We appreciate your comment dear traveler, it is very important for us to know about your experience.

review_text: We were in the Torres Del Paine National Park in Patagonia with the family recently. Felipe Sunkel who runs Madre Roca Guide Services came highly recommended, and it was one of the best decisions we made. A Geologist by training, Felipe was very knowledgeable. Took us on awesome remote trails less frequented by tourists. Felipe's passion for all things Patagonia and his infective enthusiasm made the hikes and the time we spent with Felipe thoroughly enjoyable. We landed up with a flat tyre on our SUV on our last day while we were at the Lago Grey region. Felipe got the Engineering Department at the Rio Seranno Hotel to get the flat tyre fixed, stayed with us right until the problem was sorted out completely and then took leave. Clearly something Felipe did not need to do !! Easily the very best guide experience we have had anywhere in the world. Keep it up Felipe. All the best to you and Claire at Madre Roca. review_text: The Arco Británico is a monument on Avenida Brasil. It was donated to the city in 1910 by the British community to mark the centenary of the Independence of Chile. The monument, covered in Italian marble, is surmounted by a British Victorian lion and is decorated with the images of four Britons who participated in the Chilean War of Independence: Thomas Cochrane, Bernardo O'Higgins, Robert Simpson and Jorge O'Brien. It also bears the Chilean and United Kingdom coats of arms. Impressive and a nice clean park surrounding.

review_text: We really enjoyed our day trip to Maipo Valley. Me and me girlfriend decided for a tour outside the city and if possible by bike. Huaso Tours and especially Patricio made this experience unforgettable. The Maipo Valley is quite a picturesque Vallry and riding thru it with the bike is even better. Leaving early in the morning allows you to make it to Maipo valley when there is not so many people around. We were practically alone in the whole valley, while when we were heading back it was more people coming up. After some time cycling we made a stop in a privileged spot and they delighted us with a very tasteful picnic of local products (fruits, some sausage, ham, chips) with some juice. We then continued heading down with the bikes. In total we made around 20-25-30 kms most of them either flat or downhill. You need to have some ability riding the bike as heading downhill is not as riding in the city, still you don’t need to be a professional. My girlfriend and me we are used to cycle in the city and I personally do some mountain bike. We could manage without problems and even if you like a bit of action you can get it. Huaso tours provided some of the necessary equipment, helmets, globes and even had some light jackets you could borrow. Still, I would recommend to wear some comfortable clothes as you are going for a mountain bike ride. Concluding, this is a 100% recommended experience to do outside of Santiago Review of: Private Mountain Bike Tour to El Yeso Reservoir and Maipo Valley Hi Juan! Thanks so much for taking the time to review us and describe your experience in such detail. Great meeting you both and spending the day out in the Andes! As you mention, we aim to leave early in the morning so to arrive before all the crowds get in to get some exclusive time in the reservoir. For this tour you need to have a general good experience in riding a bike, to feel comfortable on one, as you describe. We are so happy you would recommend this tour! All the best! Un fuerte abrazo! Huaso Team

review_text: The Village was a welcome relief from the crowded, overwhelming stalls of the Centro Artesenal Santa Lucia. If you want the usual trinkets, go to Santa Lucia. If you want a relatively quiet day in a pretty environment with more creative crafts, come here. The place is organized into small stores on meandering paths. Not everything is great and there is some of the usual stuff but there are also many more interesting pieces. We went on a Sunday and there were lots of families. A man selling CDs played soothing music on a harp. Later some people in native costumes danced, surrounded by enthusiastic kids. There was a little restaurant with decent food. Take the red line to the last stop east at Los Dominicos. When you exit the metro, look behind the stop for the park. The Handicraft Village is towards the right. Check out the parrots in the trees on the way.

review_text: Naming the tour “Walking Through the City as a Chilean Would” is a very apt description of my tour of Santiago with Ignacio and City Trekking Guide. My guide, Ignacio, is an energetic, friendly, courteous, and knowledgeable fellow who knows the streets and history of Santiago like the back of his hand and shares my love for tennis. For this tour make sure to bring your best walking shoes, a smile, and a camera because you will spend approximately six hours walking around the city and seeing numerous sites including Palacio de la Moneda, Plaza de Armas, Mercado Central, Cerro St. Lucia, Baquedano, native dances, and many interesting back streets. Because this tour focuses on small groups (or a private tour in my case), it does allow for some divergence from the tour route to allow for pictures, souvenirs, or whatever else you may need. To make best use of this tour, make sure to book it when you first arrive or when you are planning your activities in Santiago because with the exception of Mercado Central and Cerro St. Lucia you do not linger too long at any one location. Hi Stephen, Thank you for your words! Your also energetic, friendly and really easy going person. I had fun showing you the city and its hidden places. I know that you feel confortable and saw the real Santiago, how the people are, act and what they usually do in a normal day. We have to play tennis when you come back to Santiago. in the meanwhile, practice in Washington DC! and I will be waiting for the day to play. I wish you the best and i thank you again for having chosen us to discover the capital of Chile. Best regards from Chile! Your friend, Ignacio!

review_text: We 5 friends hiked 10 days O Circuit with guide booked thru "Antares Patagonia Adventures", it was amazing experience, went to some remote places, seen many glaciers, gushing glacier water that you can fill your bottle, well maintained park. We stayed 5 days camping & 5 days in Refugio, 6 bunk beds in each room at hostels, clean white bedding, comfortable mattress, 2 people in each tent, thick mattresses & sleeping bags, but we brought our own sleeping bags. Clean bathrooms, hot shower except cold shower at Camp Torres. We hiked Torres the 1st day, then to camp Seron, to Refugio Dickson in remote location, 2 nights at Los Perros Camp, hiked to Puma & Perros glaciers, 21 KM hard hike up to Paso John Garner & down to Refugio Grey, its part of the W trek, very crowded, but we had great 2 days ice hiking/kayaking around glacier, food/drinks just awesome, to Lodge Paine grande another crowded place, cafeteria style food, breathtaking views from every room, to Camp Frances, new modern hot showers/great food/drinks, back to the entrance. We got lucky w/sunny weather everyday, we were told to expect 4 seasons in one day. Total money worth experience. most people booked everything themselves, carrying stove, cooking their own food, there are big rooms with sink & tables at every camp. Unfortunately we didn't see much wild life in 10 days, but saw hundreds of Guanacos, ÑANDÚs, red fox, pink flamingos at the park entrance & on both side of the road while you are driving to the park.

review_text: The Fray Jorge National Park is a nationally important remnant of once more extensive cloud forest. It's approached from route 5 (the Pan-American Highway) by around 25km of dirt road, which is not in too bad a condition - don't be lulled into a false sense of security by the first kilometre which has been surfaced! To a Northern European visitor the land on either side of the approach road, with many cacti in a semi-desert was at least as interesting as the National Park itself. On entering the Park, they can give you a laminated set of rules in English; this states that the last 5km to the actual forest (which is at the top of a very steep track) should only be attempted in a 4WD. The park ranger indicated that this wasn't the case and my ordinary front wheel drive rental car should should be able to get up there. Well it did (and back down again), but it was distinctly hairy as there are patches of loose gravel on a 1 in 2 gradient... Before attempting the trip you should in any event look in the small interpretation centre about 2km into the park; this is only in Spanish (and doesn't say much anyway) but does indicate some of the flora/fauna to look out for. Once at the top, there's a marked trail with about 24 posted markers - but unless you have the Spanish guide, they are not explained. There's also a short boardwalk for those in wheelchairs. The views, both across to the Pacific and inland, are very nice, and the vegetation is unusual, but again to a European visitor it doesn't look so very different from a lot of other Chilean vegetation. Overall, it's interesting, but was it worth the lengthy detour from the main road and the worry about whether my rental company would have insured me had I had an accident? I'm not all that sure.

review_text: I have been there last week, on a cloudy and rainy (a rarity in Santiago!) working day, with my wife. The place can be reached by car in about an hour drive from any place in Santiago. However, there are no visible indication on the Ruta 5 Sur and you need a map (room for improvement?). The place is wonderful. The Museo Andino is fantastic, a splendid example of contemporary architecture: plenty of light, room, quiet and silent. Just perfect. The collection of golds is something worth on its own. If you like arts and crafts and archeology you can spend 3-4 hours there without getting bored, despite the relatively small size. There are samples from 11,000 years b.C. The shop is nice but a bit expensive. The entry is free. Really a wonderful experience worth the trip. Overall, the collection is better than the pre-colombian one in Santiago. The only little remark is that some of the items shown are missing a label, or the items sometime are difficult to associate to the labels (an example is a sort of andean guitar without a label). Now, let's talk about the Restaurant. It's complicated... The buildings of the old fazenda are really fashionable. An italian-style garden and the park surrounding are amazing and the cellar on the floor, that someone from the Company kind agreed me to visit for a second, is astonishing. From an architectural point of view he Restaurant building, the red one, is really one of the best place I have been since I live here in Chile: great interiors, decoration, view, furniture, table. However, the food is in my opinion not what could be. For 25-30.000 CLP per person, from a company of the size of Santa Rita, you would expect something more. It's not a question of servings. The personnel was nice and professional. It's just that there is nothing really remarkable about the food, specially considering the huge potential you have. Looks like a family restaurant dressed as a classy one. That place could become really the BEST restaurant in the Santiago area, while still sporting affordable prices. The coffee in particular was terrible. I know Chile doesn't have a culture of coffee - sorry mates! - but serving that "thing" as a coffee is silly, because this is the last flavour of any lunch and what a customer will remember, and there are now cheap machine that makes a decent espresso. The list of desserts is quite limited. The waiver and the maitre d'hotel, a very professional and committed man, made his best to let us enjoy the experience. However, they struggled to arrange food that was nothing memorable. The menù is ok, but you would expect much more while still remaining inside the edges of the Chilean culinary tradition. I'm not saying I wouldn't get back. But there is a lack of imagination, everything is standard. Nothing really remarkable. And this doesn't fit with the astonishing characteristics of the place. In a nut, go there for the Museum, even if you are on a short visit to Santiago, stroll into the viña and eat at the Restaurant for the ambient, but don't expect any remarkable food there. If I could, I would give 5 stars to the Museo Andino, 4 to the overall hacienda, and 3 to the Restaurant.

review_text: We left our hotel in San Pedro at 6am kitted out with hats, gloves, thermals etc.. It was cold on arrival about 7.30am about 3C but the week before had been -11C. Early start required because as the air warms up during the day the steam becomes less visible. Stopped at the "park" entrance for the loos - no paper.This is obviously a very popular attraction as there were a lot of tourists and vehicles. Most park up and provide a picnic breakfast which appeared to vary from basic to one group frying eggs! Seagulls a bit of a pest so our guide asked us not to feed them.Geysers are interesting but you have to be careful as they can suddenly spurt up very hot water. There are plaques giving good information. They have laid out rings of stones to warn you not to get too close. There is a swimming pool which some people were using but not for us as we were still in anoraks and warm hats! El Tatio means Grandfather -the mountain looks like a grandfather's face lying down. Good bird life on the lakes. Just managed to see Vizcachua [like green rabbits but chinchilla family] on the rocks on the way back.

We did a half day (three hours) ride along (and, at times, in) Laguna Sofía, up the ridge and to some small caves. In spite of the fierce wind and cold temperatures, my two children lived every moment of the experience... That is a huge credit to Pingo Salvaje. On a side note, we left my son's knit cap at the Estancia and later called to see how we could get it back. They hand delivered the cap to our lodging without second thought. A level of customer service that is uncommon in Chile.

review_text: We chose this tour because we've had several guided and independent kayak trips and knew that a guided trip in this region was best for us due to the logistical advantages. Juanfe is a "one man show". He owns his company and is the guide for all his trips. He demonstrated high integrity with how he handled all aspects of this tour from financial components to environmental awareness. He responded promptly to any questions asked of him prior to the trip. He incorporates local families to enhance the tour experience and to give something back to the local economy. The home stays and meals were an added cultural component to the trip. Because of our kayak history, Juanfe did not feel the need to spend additional time undertaking rescue practices, rather he vetted us through discussions and question/answer to know that we had some adequate experiences. His knowledge of the region including history, flora, and fauna were very strong. Due to the portages (carrying fully loaded kayaks) on this trip, Juanfe makes a point of utilizing the tides and predicted winds to the group's advantage. This means he can be fairly dogmatic about when the group needs to wake up, have breakfast, depart, etc. The bottom line is, he knows what he is doing toward this end and his rationale is just...even if it means getting up at 4:00 in the morning and departing at 6:00. Don't go into this trip expecting it to be a relaxing easy paddle into beautiful fjords. It is a mix of relaxed paddling, hard paddling, and sometimes using a sail to take advantage of winds. Due to the environmental conditions, every tour is bound to be somewhat different and thus the trip overview on the Yak Expediciones website should be taken as a guide for the trip if conditions are good. The meals Juanfe was responsible for were basic but absolutely adequate. The meals at the home stays ranged from good to great and more food than any person should eat! Overall we would highly recommend this tour.

review_text: Departing from Modena at 10am (in front of the monument to Salvador Allende) this tour is easy to locate wherever you are based in the city. We were luckily enough to be treated to the changing of the guards. This small group tour made up of nine guests was warmly greeted by the energetic and friendly guide Max. After a brief round of introductionsour group was whisked off to an amazing breakfast spot a couple of blocks down town. Unlike some food tours this is more than just a taster so just have enough breakfast to energise you for the walk. As well as food, Max gave great overviews of interesting & historic parts of town as we passed. Over the next four hours we wound our way through the fish market and finishing up in Santo Christobal park via the funicular. Max made sure the tour went at a great tempo and is an example of how it should be done. Our only recommendation would be to see if the cable car down could be incorporated into the tour (we opted to do this) although we realise this may complicate what is intended to be a circular route. If you are in Santiago and want a fun and energetic food and city walking tour, this is the one for you!

review_text: 9-hour bus tour from Santiago (Chile) to two coastal cities - Viña del Mar and Valparaiso through tunnels and wine valley on excellent highways. Short stop to see the site where the world famous Viña del Mar music festival is held each year. Nice drive along coast from Viña del Mar to Valparaiso where we had an excellent buffet lunch at the casino with 10% discount. Interesting drive up the hillsides to see the city from on high plus option for an interesting walk 40 minutes (downhill) through a local neighborhood and ride on the funicular down the last stretch back to the bus. This tour is a great way to see the countryside between Santiago and these two cities and to learn from the guide interesting bits of Chilean history about the origins of these two coastal cities. review_text: This museum is close to other major sites in the Chilean capital, such as La Moneda. It is subdivided into two major sections, one Chilean pre-columbian artifacts and then the rest of Latin America. I found the Chilean exhibit most interesting. On exhibit were large wood carvings, many ceramics and some fabrics. A spectacular quipu was on display and seemed more like a work of art than a utilitarian record keeping system. The floor with other precombian artifacts was subdivided by region, against mostly pottery, a few stone carvings and even less gold work. The latter it was pointed out for the most part having been smelted by the Spaniards in the 16th century. It leaves one to wonder was magnificent works were unfortunately destroyed in the name of Christian greed.

review_text: We travel all over the world and most cities we visit we start our trip with the "hop on hop off" city tour to orient ourselves with a new city. So we were in Santiago in the Bella Vista neighborhood and "hopped on" the bus to start our tour. However we were informed that they do not sell tickets on the bus. We were told you can only purchase tickets at a Turistik ticket office. So after 2 stops, we were asked to get off the bus and walk to the ticket office which was 10-15 minutes away from the bus stop, pay for our ticket, get a bracelet, and then wait 20 minutes for the next bus. The onboard guides were useless... unable to explain where the ticket office was located. So we exited the bus, were not able to find the ticket office... and therefore, never got back on the bus. Also, we were not able to purchase a ticket online because you need to go to the ticket office to get the bracelet. We were told that several years ago there was too much theft by employees and that was why they no longer accept payment on the bus. So why not accept credit cards only? Why not accept online vouchers and only hand out bracelets onboard? Why is the ticket office so far from a bus stop? Why not have a trusted employee located at the bus stop with a mobile device and able to process payments. That's how they do it in other major international cities. Terrible experience.... useless guides... and extremely inefficient process. We appreciate your comment dear traveler, it is very important for us to know about your experience.

review_text: We have been to many museums around the world, including concentration camps in Germany. But this museum is very unique, as it puts together videos, newspapers, and many, many historical documents to highlight the importance of human rights. It gives very haunting testimonials on torture under Pinochet's iron fist. Some of the reviews on this site criticized a left-wing bias. I would disagree, as the description of the collection stays very clear of the political side (e.g., US CIA involvement, etc.) and just focuses on the many, many missing people, whose remains might be lucky to be found in mass graves years later. Another example is the description of prisoners' lives, as told by the minority who survived. The collection is very thought provoking and inspiring to learn more about Chilean and Latin American history. The museum is about humanity. Let us hope that few totalitarian governments (left, right or centre) in the present or in the future would put their own peoples through such insanities.

review_text: Unfortunately, on the day of our crossing, it rained all day with a low cloud cover. The weather ruined the entire trip. We did not see anything! No volcanos. No mountains. No beautiful emerald lakes. We strongly recommend that you not take this trip when rain is predicted. We booked directly with Cruce Andino. They have a strict cancellation policy and will not issue a full refund if you cancel 16 days or less before the trip. That makes it extremely difficult to cancel an advance reservation. Perhaps you should consider NOT making an advance reservation until you are certain of a good weather forecast for your planned day of travel. I provided feedback to Cruce Andino, admitting that they had no control over the weather, however, at a cost of almost $600 USD for the two of us, I felt like it was a waste of money. Cruce Andino did not respond nor offer any compensation. Otherwise, the logistics of the tour were without incident, apart from the unexpected fees incurred during the crossing for such things as National Park Entrance and border crossing fees. review_text: I have done many tastings in New World wineries (Canada, US, South Africa, Chile, Argentina) and unfortunately this is not one of my memorable experiences. It shouldn't be, as Casas del Bosque has a lot going for it, beautiful setting, nice winery and restaurant and great wines. It just lacks a little passion. I went there for lunch at Taninos and followed with a tour and premium tasting. I was expecting a really great restaurant (1 of the 20 best restaurants in a winery according to a magazine - believe me, it's not). Simple fare, some of it not really well done, such as a seared tuna that was over cooked and calamari rings that were overdone. Overall acceptable meal but nothing spectacular. The service was not the most attentive either. Wines were great however. The tour was the most deceiving part. No history, no explanation of the Casablanca valley, to sum it up it was a view of the vineyard with photo op (no explanation of cultivation methods or location of different varieties until I asked), a quick run down of a few pieces of equipment they use and a visit of the cellar with very little explanation. I think we were done in 20 minutes. The tasting showcased great wines but was pretty rushed as well with very little talk. Maybe I was unlucky with the tour guide we got (in Spanish) but if felt he didn't do service to the fantastic wines that this winery produce. With a little bit of effort on the menu and passionate tours guides this place would be great.

review_text: The end of another really cool and special trip, but this post will not be dedicated to the positive side of everything we experienced in Chile. Anyone who has been will understand more precisely what I want to convey. It's not a cheap trip, so we need a lot of planning time. We create a lot of expectations, we organize ourselves exhaustively so that everything goes smoothly and that includes handpicking a good agency. Going there requires these things due to the fact that it is a “facilitator” for tourists in terms of tours, information, transfers, etc. I chose Zerando o Chile. I started following the owner, Tales Barreto, and the people he invited to go to Chile and, in this way, give greater visibility to all types of services that the agency offers. Zeroing in, you were a HUGE disappointment for me. Very unprepared, lack of information and lack of care for their customers. I felt like I was managing everything on my own. The “being a facilitator” part, at least for me, unfortunately didn’t work out as I imagined. - Snow clothing rental: a real mess. Nobody, I said NOBODY, guides us properly. We rent unnecessary parts, in other words (we throw money away). -A client felt ill due to the altitude and curves on the way to the mountain and had to stay at the hotel where we had breakfast (which is almost arriving at the final destination). Amazingly, she stayed there until late afternoon (no one from the agency was willing to pick her up). -Basic accounts: DON’T DO. How to calculate the number of seats in the van x the number of people who completed that tour. Result: people standing. -They placed us next to the driver on another ride (that's not a problem, as long as it has the minimum comfort.) I was totally squeezed and embarrassed. The driver could barely shift gears. Oh! And speaking of the driver, this one was not bilingual according to the portfolio provided by the agency. - And finally, they wanted to charge me an extra amount, which had already been paid for the first 50% of the value of the tours. I had to explain (again the basic account) that they were wrong and, after much insistence from me, they called the person responsible for after sales and saw that, in fact, there was an error. What was supposed to be VERY peaceful, at times became a torment. If you're going to Chile, I recommend you do your research extremely carefully (see, I thought I had done that). Be careful with agencies that showcase their services through influencers. Your treatment may be a little different. 😉 Olá, Sentimos muito por saber que sua experiência com a Zerando Chile não atendeu às suas expectativas, especialmente considerando o esforço que você fez no planejamento da sua viagem.
