review_text: I found KoKayak during my search of things to do around Puerto Varas. It looked like there were fantastic options, and my family and I were not disappointed. I was concerned that we might not find an outdoor activity to do during our stay on Christmas day. Before we headed down to Chile, I contacted KoKayak for information about activities that might be available. I received an email back from the owner, Richard, that we could bike and do white water rafting that day. He was prompt with his information and gave nice details about our options. It was great that he was flexible about the type and kind of trips we could take with him. We were concerned about the weather and didn’t know whether the bike ride or rafting trip would be a good idea in bad weather. Richard was informative and patient with our questions. Once we arrived in Puerto Varas, Richard followed up and provided us with more details about our options and made suggestions as to how we should plan our day. Even though the weather was supposed to be rainy and in the 50’s (F), we ultimately decided to go biking in the morning with a raft trip in the afternoon. The bike trip was outstanding. My wife, kids (ages 15 and 17) and I enjoyed biking the hills and trails at the foothills of the volcano in the area. The views were spectacular. We biked for about 3-4 hours and enjoyed every bit of it. Richard kept a good pace and kept us all in a great mood, even with the rain. The kids loved it. We didn’t find the ride to be too tough and Richard can tailor the ride to suit the riders in the group. If you want a harder ride, Richard can take you further up the hills in the area. If you need an easier ride, you could tell him and he’d keep in you flatter terrain. Biking -- The Good: We loved all of it. The bikes were in great shape. The trails were nice to ride in. The trails were more like hiking paths than the stone downhill trails you might have for mountain bikes in Colorado. You’re given a water bottle and you’re off on your biking trip. Richard’s information about the ride was great. Richard took pictures of us during the ride and was kind enough to send them to us later that day by email -- a nice touch. The cost of the trip was reasonable considering the quality of the bikes, the time on the bike ride and the experience of our guide. The Bad: We really didn’t have anything negative to say about our bike experience. The food for lunch could have been different. We were given a vegan salad with quinoa, banana and orange juice, plus some chips to munch on. In the cool wet weather, it would have been nice to have a hot drink and a place to dry our clothes. Only one of my son’s would not touch the salad. We also thought that we had a bit too much downtime between the biking and the rafting. We waiting about one hour before we went rafting after finishing our lunch. The wait was due to the time it took to bring a second group in that was also scheduled to go rafting. The rafting was unbelievable. We’ve rafted in North Carolina, and these rapids were more fun and enjoyable. The water level was quite high and we were told that the rapids were between a class 3 and 4. I believe it. But we felt safe and wore wet suits. The water was quite cold and the weather didn’t help any, but the wet suits kept us plenty warm even when the water hit our bodies during the ride. The rafting trip was one of the highlights of the trip to Puerto Varas and Chile. We had a tremendous amount of fun and loved every minute of it. We would truly recommend it. During the raft trip, a photographer was as ahead of us on a kayak. He took some amazing photos. I’d recommend you buy the disk. He sells the disk for about $40-$60. Considering we’ve been to other attractions in the US, where you pay $20-$30 for one photo, it’s well worth the memories. The disk we purchased contained several hundred photos. Rapids -- The Good: The rapids were great. The rafts, paddles and life jackets were in great shape. Some of the wet suits were somewhat worn, but you’re not in the water long enough for the condition of the suit to affect the experience. The cost of the rafting trip is reasonable considering the transportation to and from the hotel and the time on the river. The Bad: We really didn’t have anything bad to say about the rafting trip. We all loved it and enjoy seeing the pictures of the trip. Review of: Rafting rio Petrohue

review_text: They aren't kidding about the 40 switchbacks going up the mountain road -- actually many more because they don't count the less extreme hairpin turns. Somewhat harrowing, especially with trucks coming the other way; I'm not sure I would even attempt driving up there during the winter ... and certainly not without tire chains. Once there, the view is tremendous, and I'm sure everyone is right that the skiing is terrific. Helicopter skiing here is reputed to be the best in all of South America. There are two other ski areas on this mountain -- when you get to the village of Farellones, the road forks -- El Colorado and La Parva are a couple of km further on the left, and Valle Nevada is 13 km further on the right. But once again, it's a treacherous road, even during summer, so you're probably best off hiring a professional to get you there.

review_text: The toughest part is the hike to get to the hike. It is possible to take public transportation, but it only gets you half the way there. You first need to walk along Avenida Independencia towards the reserve and find this 'microbus' along the way. This 'bus' looks like a an old-school VW mini-bus that costs 300 CLP and will drop you off at the intersection of Y-570 and Y-580. You then have another 1.2km to the entrance. I never found out where the micro bus stop is in the city, but if you walk west along Avenida Independcia and you see a tiny VW bus, flag it down. The regular city buses will not take you towards the Reserve. The microbus afternoon schedule is very limited, so you should plan to walk (2hr to Plaza de Armas) or flag down a taxi. See photo. The bus time table (roughly) is: 6:30, 7:30, 9:00, 11:00, 13:15, 16:00, 17:00, 20:00. Once you arrive, there is a CLP 4000 entrance fee, and you fill out some information with the rangers. It is very easy to navigate through the reserve--just follow the red markers throughout the trail. The longest hike loops in a circle and takes 3 to 4 hours to complete. The trail is very, very muddy--I don't think it ever gets dry there, so be careful about slipping in the mud. It is not a popular hike so you will be the only person there, which is a pleasant feeling. The views are similar to what I've seen in Torres del Paine and Tierra del Fuego, but one of the viewpoints definitely made me pause to enjoy it. The view of the city is limited, but you do see many, many trees covering the reserve. In the autumn season, the trees changed to some beautiful colors.

review_text: We couldn’t have asked for a better tour than this. We had a group of 5 and opted for the half day tour, so Cristian took us to an island just outside Maullin to his partners Pepes place and we took a long ride around the island. It felt as if we were transported back in time, the island is sparsely populated and gorgeous viewpoints and scenic beaches were everywhere. It reminded me of the coast of central California before it became so populated. Afterwards Pepes abuela prepared a delicious farm to table meal for us using typical Chilean foods. Cristian was very knowledgeable about the area, the animals, and the people that live there and was excited to share his knowledge with us. He’s been working to bring together different cultures in the surrounding regions and share his passion for riding with everyone. Would give 6 stars if I could!!

review_text: I did 2 'Wally tours' in one day, following a good experience on their Valparaiso counterpart. Carlos was my guide for both. review_text: Wow and wow, this was one of the most beautiful part of our earth I've ever been to. Words or pictures can't begin to describe this area of Patagonia Chile in the southern part of South America. People from all around the world come to visit this gorgeous area. We stayed at a lodge for three days there, drove to Lago Grey went on a boat to the glacier on that lake, it was stunning to get sooooo close to icebergs and the glacier, it's well worth the $100 per person to go see it, and they even make some great strong drinks made with the glacier ice, that was really cool, lol. So plan a whole day to do this activity and dress in layers, this was one of the best days there. You can also stay at the lodge right on the lake called Hotel Lago Grey. Then we drove back to our lodge called Hotel Las Torres, which was nice, very basic rooms but comfortable and a really nice free breakfast every morning. The view was fantasic from our room so request room on mountain side, you do pay more money staying in the Park, but it was well worth it because it would of been a long winding up and down ride in and out of park each day, it takes up too much time to do that, so I'd stay in park for sure, we rented a car from Punta Arenas which I highly recommend because we had our own freedom to do what we wanted and had everything in car we needed. We also ventured to go on the famous hike from the Hotel Las Torres lodge, what a huge mistake that was for me, We weren't prepared at all for how hard it was. I didn't realize how extremely difficult for someone like me, I almost thought I was going to die, but wow did I learn a lot that day, that I will never forget, ever. I'm just an average almost 58 year old woman from Florida, just used to maybe walking an hour or so a day, not a mountain,What was I thinking? I wasn't thinking, I just wanted to see what everyone comes there to see and that is getting very close to the famous Torres Peaks. Well my guy friend is about 44 yrs old and he even said it was a very strenuous 10 hour hike. First of all you must leave as early in morning as you can, we started at 10:30am (wrong). Second always tell someone (staff at the lodge) in case not back at reasonable time. Third, bring enough water and food, you will be very thirsty and need protein for energy. Well we ran out of water and had to drink from the stream up in the mountain which I was so afraid to do, but I was extremely dehydrated and when I got to the main part of the hike well I blackout for a few seconds and just collapsed I had no energy but we had to get down before dark, well we did end up walking by ourselves in the very darkest of all nights (new moon). We were so scared we walked maybe about 1 and a half hours using my friends cell phone for light. So please consider all these things before you begin this very strenuous hike, also you must have the poles everyone else was using, we were very much not wise at all. Another than that it is plenty beautiful to just drive through the park at your leisure, but plan your time right and consider not being on the road in the dark, it is too scary to drive at night in those mountains with drop offs around many corners.

review_text: Connie (U.S.-born) and her husband Francisco (Chilean-born) run a very professional tour business, ColchaguaTours.com. I contacted five wine tour operators in the Colchagua area to book a day of wine tours for my wife and I and they were not only the only operator to respond but they also were fluent in English and very knowledgeable about the wineries in the area. Francisco was our driver, guide, and interpreter. He was not only able to get us into extraordinary wineries for unique tastings, he could have gotten us into others at short notice due to his and Connie's relationships. This is exceptional valuable given the impact COVID-19 has had on wine tours everywhere, especially biodynamic (limited) and organic (unavailable) wineries. Final note: We could have spent at least another day in the area to see the Santa Cruz Museum, which is adjacent to the casino, it comprises four buildings, is considered the best museum in Chile, and is owned by the same owner as the casino; and to visit more wineries. If you visit Colchagua I recommend the La Perla hotel, having a meal in downtown Santa Cruz, as well as having a meal at Montes winery.

review_text: I met the agency because a friend did her tours with them many years ago (before the pandemic) and had already contracted with them tours in 2022 in San Pedro - it is worth noting that they made good price and are open to negotiate, considering that a package with them is closed. This time I booked the tour to the Salar de Uyuni (4d and 3 nights) where I started the negotiation when I was not yet in San Pedro and had all the assistance and information from the Tani staff (Martin and Paula). They were flexible and gave me all the information about the tour, well as offered a price I considered good (approx. 215 usd all inclusive) - I had reviewed prices at other agencies and online as well and they were all more expensive than Tani. Transportation arrived as agreed and the party company in Bolivia (Yuraj Tika) had friendly staff - the guide Daniel was very good! It is worth noting that the route has its difficulty, but it is worth it for all the cute places you will see. Another important tip is that in Bolivia everything is paid - bath between 1-5 bob, wi-fi in hostels 10 bob, and some until the hot shower also pay 10 bob, so it is important to carry your Bolivian reserve - I took 300 bob and they were enough and still returned with tickets to San Pedro.

review_text: Though the area is beautiful, I can’t say I had the best experience with Full Tours on this trip. I had used them the previous week to go to Valparaíso & Viña Del Mar and it was a fantastic experience. Both the guide and driver were fantastic. However, my Cajon experience was not the same. I received my pickup notice the night before around 9:30 pm for a 6:15 am pick-up (the first pick-up for the day). I was ready and waiting. The driver was not. He arrived 10 minutes late. When we got to the next pick-up, he said un momento, left the van unlocked, windows down and I did not see him for 15 minutes. I wasn’t sure if he went home to change from the previous night or what had happen. He finally showed up with 3 more passengers. He proceeded to run several red lights and at one he actually had to swerve to miss a motorcycle. Once we picked all the passengers, a short briefing was giving and thankfully another passenger was able to translate for 5 English passengers since the driver only spoke Spanish. I will admit that I believe it was a booking issue that I was put on an all Spanish van and the company did switch my van at the breakfast stop. Once on the new van and en-route, we were given a very brief introduction to the day and told if we would like to have pictures taken we would need to purchase that service from our guide for 10,000 peso. That’s a new one! Usually your guide is more than happy to snap a pic or two for you. So now the day become a day of photographing those of the tour who purchased the upgrade! The icing on the cake was when the driver on the way home was taking photos while the van was moving in traffic of other tour van licenses plates. He also spent a significant amount of time on his phone. I am sorry but the safety of the 16 people on the van is more important than the instant gratification that was happening. Hello Trixie, first of all thank you for your feedback. The problem of the driver’s delay that you said took 15 minutes was due to the fact that your reservation for the tour was booked as spanish tour, as you are in a language school learning spanish in Chile (who made the reservation with us) informing that every tour with that school should be done in Spanish, not English, for people to practice their lessons. We are sorry for the delay of 10 minutes to pick you up; traffic on a Sunday is a little unpredictable, but we are going to work on our driver´s puntuality. You mentioned that the driver ran red lights, but Santiago´s Downtown has some streets where you may cross with precaution in red light (even those Streets have signs that permit i) that is a little different from traffic in other cities or even in other sectors of the city like Providencia or Las Condes Regarding the subject to the photos for 10.000 pesos, we have a photographer that only sells his photos in some of our tours for those people interested in having profesional photos taken in those amazing places, not being mandatory to buy them. Even though we have a photographer, usually our guide is happy to take pictures if you ask him, not needing a extra tip for that service, as he enjoys having our passengers have a good time in our tours.

review_text: Puritama Thermal Springs was beautiful and refreshing and overall a treat! We arrived in San Pedro by noon - so taking advantage of the 2pm 1/2 price option was perfect for our first day. The water is beautiful clear water cascading down from pool to pool. We found the water to be warmer than body temperature which was perfect. There are clean baños. Wear loads of sunscreen!! Bring your camera, a towel and flip flops (as the boardwalk from pool to pool got very hot to walk on). There is a picnic area where Mauricio, our guide, set up 'catering' for us. Bring your own drinks, snacks etc as there isn't anything available for purchase. When we arrived, we also had a chain closing the road access, but it wasn't more than ten minutes before an employee came by. I must say that our guide was clever enough to ask to drive us down to the base - and thank goodness for that because the walk back up the hill seemed pretty vertical and long on such a hot afternoon in the high altitudes of San Pedro. Puritama and Laguna Cejar (floating in the turquoise salt pool) were highlights of our trip!

review_text: It's one of the cerros that you can hike. It's at 5600 meters of altitude. Some people has difficulty to reach the top because of the altitude that can causes headaches and low pressure. My group have reached the top in 2 hours and half, but to go down it was very easy and took about 30 minutes. You can hike this cerro with a guide or can do it by yourself (I saw some guys doing that). It's important to use properly clothes, to bring water and some snacks. Oh... and the view is amazing! You can see the Licancabur and Juriques volcanoes, also a lake behind them that it's in Bolivia. Totally recommended! One of the best thing to do in Atacama.

review_text: Went here with my husband for a day hike mid January. The coliguacho bugs were out in full force and made the hike itself pretty miserable, but the park was very nice. Helpful Rangers, great facilities, trails are well marked, etc. My only complaint (if it can even be called that, it's more like a preference) is that the park seems to be geared towards those people experiencing the outdoors for the first time, or who want to experience the outdoors but who don't want to forgo modern conveniences (i.e. Lots of premium camping spots, specific rules on which direction you can hike a trail, etc.) I prefer a little less hand-holding in my outdoor excursions, but I think in the Chilean context the park fits the attitudes to the outdoors perfectly. As stated in other reviews, the road leading into the park was crazy bumpy. You don't need a 4x4, just make sure your vehicle isn't low to the ground and that you calculate at least an hour if not more to get from Ruta 5 to the park entrance. Also, be prepared to take hitch hikers from Ruta 5 to the little community at the entrance of the park, or stranded backpackers located in the park. Good karma, and they will be very grateful!

review_text: My husband and I had a day in Santiago before joining a tour group and I contacted Uncorked Wines about a day tour with them to the Maipo Valley. Connie (the owner) responded immediately with a well-thought-out plan, including the small Acquitania Boutique winery, the larger, very modern Haras de Pirque, and the higher elevation El Principal winery. She also included a stop for lunch at Concha y Toro which is also in the vicinity. He husband Jose (owner) was our guide for the day and he did a great job of filling us in on the area surrounding Santiago, and Chile's history, while making our way to the various wineries. The guides at each of our stops were very knowledgeable and interesting. We were particularly interested in red wines and had targeted the Maipo Valley for this reason, as well as for the landscape/views of this part of Chile's wine area. Each of the wineries was different and we thoroughly enjoyed our day - definitely value for money. Connie and Jose were also extremely helpful when we had some issues with accessing a cash machine in Santiago. It was a day to remember and we would heartily recommend Uncorked Wine Tours. Jose also recommended restaurants in Santiago and we had a nice dinner at the very hopping Tiramisu! If we would have had more time we would have taken one of their other tours to the other valleys and tried one of their cooking classes. Book them and enjoy! Review of: Best Wine Tasting in Santiago

review_text: We met Boris at 10:30 at the top of Ascensor Artilleria. A short walk from there we reached his cooking studio where we decided what we would be creating in the kitchen that day. Our intrepid group of 5 students and one Boris then made our way down the ascensor, hopped on a local bus, and arrived about 10 minutes later at the indoor/outdoor food market. Fruits, veggies, fishes, spices, colors and not another turista to be seen. Lots of energy and karma. Leave your Nikon, Rolex, and gold jewelry back at the studio – security is an issue here. Then back to the cocina. Cooking with Boris is a totally hands-on experience. You learn by doing. Meanwhile, Boris talked about the culture, politics, and history of his beautiful country. When all the preparation work was done and the sharp knives were put away, we learned how to make and enjoy the perfect pisco sours. They were followed by several wines and the fruits of our labors. Finally, at about 5 PM we said adios to our new friends. We did not leave hungry. All in all, a great experience.

A few of the jars represented smells that would indicate a bottle of wine was “bad.” We stepped out of the storage facility into a small museum dedicated to pre-Columbian art. I wish we’d had more time there, but we were already at the end of a long tour. Next came a tasting of four different wines which concluded with our being invited to take home our wine glasses. We did, and they made it back intact in our luggage.

review_text: In setting up this tour, they were very responsive to all my questions. We were lucky to spend our day with both Francisca and Sebastian, the founders of I Love Chile; they were fun to be with, knowledgeable and good conversationalists on lots of topics. We were picked up promptly and began our scenic drive Southeast of Santiago through the Canyon de Maipo and climbed into the Andes stopping a number of times at scenic overlooks including once for coffee at an eco-camp. When we were in sight of the glaciers (sadly quite diminished from the multiyear drought; so don't expect to see any snowcaps in summer) and at about 12 Kilometers from the Argentine border, we stopped for a short walk and storytelling. On our way back down through the mountains, we stopped in a beautiful valley for wonderful Chilean wine, cheese and snacks; as well as a fun and challenging 'sport' while watching the little goats from the nearby ranch. Then we had a traditional Chilean lunch at a local restaurant (included) and headed for the Concho Y Toro Winery--the largest wine producer in Latin America and fifth largest in the world--famous for the Castillero del Diablo brand. The winery tour was enjoyable but was 'showy' (e.g., a light show in the cellars) concentrating more on the history of the beautiful vineyard rather than on their grapes, wines and production. There were three included tastings. Would highly recommend I Love Chile for a private tour. What elevated this tour was the guides/founders easygoing and friendly style--more like an outing with friends than a tour. They went the extra mile in providing water, snacks and a parting gift. review_text: If you like traveling in a flock of tourists following a guide with a flag or bull horn, then Spicy Chile is not for you. If, however, you prefer touring Santiago in a small group led by a knowledgeable, bilingual guide who works hard to make your experience memorable, than head over to the Statue of Salvador Allende in front of the Moneda Palace and prepare for a great four hour tour that will cost you nothing but a tip! We took the Good Morning Santiago tour with Jose on July 12. Jose knows his history and was a very competent tour guide. He took us through the center of Santiago into different neighborhoods, stopping to show us points of interest. Our guide let us control the pace of the tour patiently answering questions and showing us photos to supplement what we saw. The tour stops at a nice cafe halfway through for coffee and a comfort break. You will certainly walk a lot on this tour, but it is worth it to get a real sense of the culture and history of Santiago. As another reviewer stated, we did not feel that we were being taken to tourist only sites. Our tour ended at the house of Pablo Neruda in the Bellavista section of town. You will find a nice selection of restaurants and shops in this area. Following the tour, we were able to continue exploring the City on our own. For example,we walked up Santa Lucia Hill (you pass the hill but do not climb it on the tour) to the Castillo Hidalgo - a terrific place to see the city and watch the sun set. We only wish that we had more time in Santiago. Spicy Chile guides have to be good because their compensation is based on tips. We certainly felt that the tip we paid our guide was well deserved.

review_text: Where do I begin? A few friends and I travelled in pursuit of great tours and life changing experiences. When asking for the tours we were offered a package tour for $60000 - cheapest by approx. $10000 from anywhere else. The tours included; Piedras Rojas, Geisers, Valle de la Luna, Valle de arcoris (Rainbow valley). To be fair the first two tours went without a hiccup. We then showed up to the office to get collected for the Valle de la luna tour and the company failed to schedule us in for a tour and to compensate for their mistake they said they could refund us the money. However, this was a short trip and, as you might know, Valle de la luna is a must go. Following an argument in spanglish we were put onto a tour with another company that was satisfactory. Does it end there? Oh God No! On the way back from the tour, we get a whatsapp message with no punctuation and in spanish (even though we clearly identified ourselves as mainly english speakers), that the tour for the next day was cancelled for us unless we agreed to pay an extra $15000 each. we rushed to the office before getting they shut and had another argument with the staff. What we found was that they 'undercharged us for the tours' and that we should pay for her mistake even though our total would have been cheaper if we went with another company! We disagreed and we went back and forth until they agreed to accept responsibility for their mistake - every trip has a few ups and downs, but this does not stop here! The next morning at 8:45 am - the bus driver approaches our hostel and tells us to pay an extra $10,000 each (note the discrepancy from 15000 to 10000) or else he won't let us on to the bus as the tour company failed to pay the minimum required fee for the tour. We were then forced to pay as we wanted to go to the rainbow valley and had no alternative as our flight was that same evening - we thought we would get a receipt and go to the company and have a civilised refund. When coming back from the tour, the bus driver attempts to drop us off without a receipt, we stay on the bus and ensure that before we leave we get a receipt. The person that hands the receipt is from the company and then we explain the situation to him expecting them to already be aware. He tells us that we had the option to cancel the tour the earlier night (not an option when you are given no time and not even the value that you paid back in order to book another tour), and that we must suffer for their stupidity. He then slips and tells us that the package deal is 65000, and that ...plot twist - the bus driver is the owner of the whole company! We by now had paid 70000 each and they were not willing to give us any money back even though we paid 5000 extra. After another 30 minutes of arguing they agree to give us 4000 only, why the discrepancy of 1000? I will never know! We eventually get the 5000 we are owed and were kicked off the bus - in summary we paid an extra 5000 for their mathematical mistakes and god knows how much they would have taken if one of us didn't speak some spanish. Long story short - No. You can get a better tour company for the same price, look around. Lots of Love, Annoyed Traveler

review_text: I went here with a group of wine enthusiasts for a 6 course food and wine matching lunch. We ate: 1) tuna ceviche (amazing); 2) tuna steak (delicious); 3) baby scallops (wonderful); 4) salmon (very good, but I'm getting a little full by now...) 5) slow-cooked beef (excellent, though I struggled to do justice to it) and 6) a thankfully small, very pretty dessert of apple mousse, fashioned to look like the top of a green apple, complete with chocolate "stalk". It was all beautifully presented, and the wines too (of which we were served generous portions) were excellent: I particularly enjoyed their 2018 Pinot Noir rose. Apparently this lunch cost about half as much again as our usual three-course lunches, which makes it an absolute bargain in my book. This meal will linger in my memory for a long time as a highlight of my trip to Chile. Fabulous.

review_text: This company was recommended by our hotel. Our tour went smoothly and was very interesting. Our guide, Edgardo, was friendly, had in-depth knowledge of a wide range of topics and was able to answer questions and give good explanations. Our driver, Jose Luis, was amazing as he saved us from a near head on collision with another van which was unexplainably coming towards us on our side of the road. Thanks to his quick reaction and making the right decision we avoided what would potentially have been a fatal accident. Edgardo was very professional and handled the incident well, continuing with our tour and not letting it spoil the day, despite the gravity of the situation. We were also pleased that Viva Atacama took this safety issue very seriously following up with the tour company of the other van and making a police report so that hopefully some action will be taken against the other driver. I would definitely recommend Viva Atacama. Thank you very much fo your good opinion, this help Us to improve our service, and We gonna tell to Edgardo and Jose Luis about his good Job. Best Regards

review_text: We hired a private driver to drive us from the SCL Airport to the Odjfell Vineyards to have a wine tasting tour as well as a picnic during our 5-hr layout. We were there half an hour early. But Tomas, the winery guide was flexible enough to begin the tour earlier. He was very knowledgeable, friendly and clearly passionate about the wines at Odjfell. Even though we didn't request a private tour, it was just the two of us which made it all the better while comparing to the wine tasting tours of other big producers in the region. After he explained the wine making process, we tasted five wines, and then enjoyed a picnic that was set on the lawn next to the main house overlooking the vineyard. We were given another bottle of wine, cheese, meat, nuts, fruits, bread and water. This whole experience was absolutely wonderful and it was a perfect way to end our trip to Chile, as we were flying back to US that evening. The stars of the tour were of course the wines. They were really good and all organic. We bought three bottles. And we were happy to find out later that those wines were more expensive at the airport duty free and a lot more expensive in US.

review_text: I was in Valparaiso in December and was very eager to see the city and get a better understanding of its history. I was traveling alone and had read a lot about Valparaiso, including that exploring alone as a woman could be a little dangerous. We covered a ton of ground, but the tour never felt rushed. In fact, Cristian made sure to pause and give thoughtful details all along the way. review_text: We had pre booked a group tour of Punta Arenas with GV Tours from home. We arrived by cruise ship & our guide was waiting for us on the dock. We boarded the mini van & travelled to the first stop at Fort Bulnes about an hour away. First we went through the museum then to the well preserved Fort itself. Fort Bulnes was the first Chilean settlement in the far south of the country around 1843. Then we travelled along the coastline stopping at monuments & then for a photo & small market stop at the lookout above the Old Town which had great views including overlooking our ship. Next to our arranged restaurant for a Chilean lunch stop, this was not as previously promised & food quality was below average. Next was a visit to Plaza de Armas including a city tour with some free time, then a guided tour through the Punta Arenas cemetary which was not as good as the Recoleta Cemetary in Buenos Aires but still worth a look. Then off to the ship museum where there is full size replicas of early explorers ships including Magellan's the Victoria & Darwin's ship the Beagle. This concluded our sights for the day which were enjoyed but small things could be improved on. Our guide was overall disappointing, for a lot of the day he gave no commentary at all. We were all quoted an entrance fee price by email to enter the national park in Chilean Pesos so we had brought the correct money from home only to be told the price was now 2000 more. The lunch was supposed to be a 3 course meal which didn't happen. Dealing with this company by email was mostly difficult as they would often take more than 3 days to reply to us. These items spoilt an otherwise interesting day.

review_text: Our guide Mick took us on a tremendously interesting tour, beginning with on-time hotel pickup. We were a small group of five, and Mick was casually engaging as we made our way to Cachagua on the coast. There, we enjoyed a tasting including quite rare Chilean wines, accompanied by Mick’s excellent sommelier narration. He capably answered our many questions. Next, a walk along the scenic coast to the isla to view penguins. Next stop was an alpaca farm where the proprietress, Maria, explained her fully vertical alpaca breeding and textile operation which is truly an awe inspiring accomplishment; plus the alpacas are so darn cute! Next, Flaherty Winery, where we enjoyed a phenomenal lunch prepared by none other than Jen Flaherty, who established the winery with husband Ed. They are very significant people in the Chilean wine scene and gracious hosts. A tour, some tastings, and back to Santiago. Here’s the reason you need to do this tour: somehow everyone involved - Mick, María, Jen, and our tour mates - were very interesting, thoughtful, and fun. The fabulous Chilean scenery was almost a secondary consideration. Do this. Review of: Wine Safari Tour from Santiago

review_text: The first contact with the agency was via whatsapp, it was all right, we received the reservations right. On our first day we went to the agency to close the tours and win the gifts (chocolate and cell phone chip), we were super well served! I made three trips with the company: 1- Farellones: we went with the Guide Antonia, she set up a group on whatsapp, so it was well organized, explained a little about Chile on the way, gave tips to be quick in renting, to make the best use of the park and was super agile with us at the entrance, so we didn't waste time! I forgot the name of the driver (I think it was Vitor) but the van was quite punctual on the go and go. 2- El Colorado: the goal was to ski! The Van passed the agreed time, we went safely to the park, we arrived well, we rented the equipment and we hired class there and it all went well. But this tour was without a Guide, there was only the driver Claudio, and the experience was quite different. I felt that we were more lost about the operation of the park, about where to buy class, ticket, whether it was to rent the ski equipment in the park or in the rental and the driver said nothing. We created a group on account in the van but as we were not very organized, the passage through the rental was much longer. Arriving there we were a bit lost too and ended up asking for help for other Bora Pro Chile guides. Thank God it all went well but we were aware of groups that arrived later and the equipment had exhausted! 3- Viña del mar and Valparaiso: we went with the Guide Constanza, the most friendly Guide on the planet and more Brazilian than many people, deserves a CPF rsrs! The tour was very nice, she spent a lot of information on the tour, took a lot of photos and in the end still sent a lot of tips to enjoy in Santiago. I loved the ride! Unfortunately I do not remember the name of the driver (I think it was Manuel) but the two formed a great pair. In short: we were well served, the vans were punctual, I felt safe on the trails and I had great trips! I recommend!

review_text: This winery is finding an original path, and is making blends I have not seen elsewhere – Pinotel (pinot noir and muscatel), Cabergnan (cabernet sauvignon and carignon), Chardonnoir (chardonnay and pinot noir, as in Champagne, but without the bubbles). Part of the time, the wine is in huge ceramic vats shaped much like the original Georgian wine vessels of thousands of years ago. We found the tour interesting and fun, and liked some of the wines (the dessert Riesling, especially), but many of the wines were not to my taste. Interesting project though, with an individualistic approach, and a fun tour.

review_text: Summit Chile is a fairly new tour operator in Pucon offering Volcano hikes, other climbing, and ski excursions (in season) .. With their level of expertise and professionalism I’m sure they will be quickly develop a reputation as the finest guides in the area. All of their equipment is new and top notch. Suzy went out of her way to track down the perfect sized boot for my husband. Claudio, our guide, shared some of his vast climbing expertise during out trek, explained some of the geology about volcanoes, and helped us understand the Mapuche perspective on volcanoes. Although we weren't new to hiking, we’d never used crampons and ice axes, so his instruction was welcome. Sliding down snow chutes on the way down the volcano (which was so fun!) you can use your ice axe as a lever to brake, and there’s a certain way you should hold it for safety’s sake. We saw other, larger groups on the volcano where there obviously wasn’t much instruction, because we had to stop and explain this to a woman who was struggling. Summit Chile is a class act, all around and I would highly recommend them.

review_text: Excellent trip. We were on a tour run by W-Circuit. Bus driver was speedy but safe and we did two tours with the same company two days apart. We were picked up at 6:30 am and the bus was comfortable. Trekking poles were provided which helped a lot (we had never used before). The first trip we went on 3 roughly 2 hour hikes to the cave paintings, the waterfalls near Las Cuernas, and the Mirador Condor. We hike a lot and enjoyed these. Great start to our stay in Puerta Natales. These hikes were moderate but challenging in terms of vertical gain and strong winds (at one point we were bent over nearly double at the Condor hike!). Our guide Alex was knowledgeable and funny and very good pointing out plants and animals. A herd of guanacos came out right by us and we all got stellar pics. Beautiful intro to the park which truly has stunning scenery at every turn. After that we did the Base Torres Hike but with a different guide named Pablo. Great hike but long (6 hours minimum) and very crowded at times. The hard thing is that people hike at vastly different rates. Our guide had us go ahead and wait in places (great system). We saw tons of birds and even a puma at the end! Again, breathtaking scenery and rewarding. Some people may not be prepared for the steepness of this hike and be unable to finish as were several folks on our tour. Acclimate a bit, have good boots, and be used to hiking—this is 22km (13.7miles) RT! Review of: Classic W Circuit - Torres del Paine

review_text: 🙂: friendly, enthusiastic, convincing, good prices, punctual, passionate tour guides, comfortable and safe transportation. 😐: their "cocktail" was more like a snack. We had a very "rushed" guide who was also a bit annoyed by the number of people she was in charge of, but it's understandable since we were still in pandemic... but, for the same reason, we couldn't enjoy our second tour very much. 🤔: try to change the snack for those who take all the tours with you, try to make sure that if the guide is a foreigner he/she speaks Spanish well since he/she was not very understanding when he/she spoke. And, instead of going to pick us up for the Tours, better to consider the option of dropping us off at each hostel, so that the return trip is not so tedious for those who are further away... Experience: We arrived on Sunday 12/09. We were a group of 4 and it was the first agency we went to for a quote and thanks to Leonardo's "gift of the gab", he convinced us immediately! He gave us good prices for five tours and we appreciate it, plus the ease of payment they offer. Our first tour was to Vallecito with Juvenal (guide) and Luis (driver) very nice both. Juvenal has a very good willingness. So I highly recommend taking a tour with him. 2nd day, tour to the Ojos del Salar... Our guide was Renata, she is Brazilian, she is nice, however, we did not understand her well when she explained and her tone was a little low, besides we felt that she rushed us a lot at the stops. 3rd and 4th tour: Baltinache lagoons with David (guide) and Israel (driver) and Geysers del Tatio, gladly, with David -again- and Rodrigo. In these tours, we had way too much fun, and most of it was due to David, he knows a lot and you can feel his passion for what he does and it is appreciated! He makes the trip fly by because of his dynamic, he tells you the stories, he explains the terms, he goes from physics to altiplano stories easily, he has a great disposition and energy, he is funny, his knowledge is appreciated, so, if you have the opportunity to take a tour with him, do it! Besides, of everything he tells, in the end, he is carrying out a mini-contest and gives away volcanic pebbles or mineraloids? So, pay attention to him! Oh, and how can we forget his contagious laugh hehehehehaha! We were very grateful for the breakfast with scrambled eggs in the middle of the desert 👌🏻👌🏻, without a doubt, our best tours were with them! 5th tour: astrophotography in charge of Lasse. It was good, but I expected more, a panorama like the one we saw when we got off in the early morning before reaching the Geysers... Although it was dynamic, there was good information and willingness, we were a bit dissatisfied with the photos, we were also grateful for the cocktail with wine and typical treats of the area... In short, the experience was super positive and I definitely recommend and would return to this agency! Thankful for making our first trip to San Pedro, an unforgettable one 🙌🏻.

review_text: I decided to use Patagonia Experience for the climb up Villarica after reading all their positive reviews on Tripadvisor. They did not disappoint. I was impressed with their professionalism right from when I first stopped by their office to enquire about making the climb. They kit you out with everything you need from helmets right down to two different types of gloves and the little sit down by the fire with a pisco sour at the end of the day is a nice touch. The first day we tried to go up we got to the base only to find the weather was too bad too make the climb. The next day the weather was perfect. Climbing Villarica is no joke. At times it is quite dangerous. You have to be physically fit and you have to have knowledgeable,responsible guides. Joaquin and 'Pepo' were superb. They pushed us to go a little faster when it was needed and slowed things down when we were struggling and needed to take a little more precaution. I got cramp in my legs about forty minutes from the summit and Pepo was extremely patient with me while he helped me stretch it out as the rest of the group continued on to the summit. We followed at a slower pace. The views from the top of the volcano are amazing but the fun really starts on the way down. We were equipped with simple plastic 'toboggans' that are used to slide down the mountain and Joaquin and Pepo showed us the best routes to take. Definitely an experience I would recommend to anyone in a decent physical condition. Definitely apply lots of sunscreen and take a good amount of drinking water as it does get really hot on certain sections of the climb. I would also recommend using the ski lift at the base as it will cut about an hour off the total climbing time, saving vital energy in the process. Hola Craig N! Thank you for leaving your comments and for choosing us to climb the Volcán Villarrica. It is important to us that each climber has the best chance possible to make it to the top. We will always work to provide that chance whether it means waiting, going slow or taking another route; if we can, we will! At times the climb can feel intimidating and even dangerous as you say, but rest assured that safety is always our primary concern; we never take unecessary risks and always err on the side of caution. The volcano climb is an activity that can be enjoyed by most people, but as you say it is not really suited to those who are particually unfit. Thanks again for your comments and I will be sure to pass them onto Joaquin and Pepo. All the best, Richard

review_text: Hey guys! This is my first rating here on TripAdvisor, and it is going to be a little longer than the usual ones, because I really want to give a shoutout to andoandes and our two guids - Sebastian and Ernesto - it was awesome! I did this tour (Embalse el Yeso) on the 19th of october with a friend and we booked the trip two days in advance. The booking process was very convenient and quick. We received a confirmation mail for further instructions regarding our pickup point and time. We were picked up at our hostel at around 7.30am. The timeframe is 7 till 7.30am, so be prepared to wake up early, but it is totally worth it ;) We were welcomed by Sebastian, our guide, and shortly after that we were on the road to Cajon del Maipo with him, our driver Ernesto (awesome dude), and 6 other guys. The guys were very obliging, we stopped at a gas station for our morning coffee/bathroom stop. After that we continued the ride and drove until we reached the city San Jose de Maipo. There we went to a little coffeeshop for a short break, followed by a city tour (30, 45min) while Sebastian was explaining the history, architecture and special places of the little town. When we were finished, we finally began to climb up the mountains until we reached Embalse el Yeso. Between San Jose de Maipo and Embalse el Yeso was not just the ride. Sebastian told us a lot about the landscape, culture and places, in and around the cajon. We stopped at different places, where we got further information and also were able to take awesome photos of the landscape. Was just perfect - we always stopped at the right spots, not too much nor too little. I dont want to spoiler too much, because I could write a lot more about those spots, it was very beautiful. review_text: We trekked the to the Desolacion Sendar (trail) to a view point, a good climb (3.1 km @ 35 - 40 degree incline) that was an incredible view of the lake and Mt Osorno. The trail starts with an easy 1.5 hr hike on soft sand, Sendero Los Alerzales then to Desolacion. We had lunch at the view point then returned to Petrohue via the lake. That also was wonderful to bathe our feet and just contemplate the beauty of this area. All told, it took us 69 year olds approx 6 hours to complete this well marked loop. One exception to "well marked" - once returning from the beach to Petrohue, they tell us to return by following to the right. We thought it was wrong; it wasn't. Continue downhill to the right, and you'll get back to the starting spot without difficulty. Beauty: amazing. Level of ability - medium unless you try and do in the heat of the day. Then it is much more difficult. Suggest that anyone start the trail before 10 a.m. as much of it is without shade.

review_text: We have recently returned from our amazing holiday in Chile. Thed holiday was everything we hoped for and I would highly recommend both Chile as a destination and Ecotours and Cristian to help make it happen. We had a fairly good idea of where we wanted to go and what we wanted to do when we contacted Cristian but where struggling with the logistics of making it happen within our budget (and with our limited Spanish!). Cristian was a great help - he booked the internal flights at a great price, recommended hotels and tours, gave us ideas on how to cut costs with different transfer options and dealt with all the bookings - hotels, day tours, buses. This allowed us to do everything we wanted to do - including the odd little splurge treat along the way. Our trip covered a huge amount of distance and variety of landscapes - from the high altitude and dry Atacama desert down to the volcanic and lush Lake District then finally to the spectacular glacial Torres del Paines. All areas were amazing and would recommend them all, though our two biggest highlights were climbing Villarrica Volcano (then sledging down all 1500m of our ascent!!) from Pucon (with our guide Guido who was great) and trekking up to the Torres view point - both were hard work but the prize made the effort more than worthwhile. The logistics all went smoothly and the hotels were all great - we expecially liked the Apart del Volcan in Pucon which, with it's kitchen and living area, allowed us to really relax in our own space. The erupting volcano, which did it's best to scupper our flight plans, turned out ok, but Cristian's support to help identify alternatives and impacts was much appreciated. Thanks Cristian for all your help in giving us a great holiday!

review_text: My one regret was not having more time to fully enjoy this beautiful park and its surroundings. The two indigenous figures below represent the Ona and Tehuelche people. (See separate review about the statue and kissing the foot.) There was an attractive red pergola where a few teens were hanging out. I enjoyed chatting with them as they tried speaking in English. The buildings surrounding the park are absolutely architecturally gorgeous. I would have liked more time to walk around the park perimeter to see these buildings. A few vendors with crafts and trinkets sums it up. Lovely section of Punta Arenas.

A Chilean guy later explained that it was super safe, but still... The first bath is the warmest. There was a bus picking up 20 adolescents, and after that there were maybe 10 persons on a Saturday. I had a lovely time. The only thing that I did miss was water to drink. My bottle was empty fast and I had no idea whether the taps in the grass contained drinkable water, and there was no personnel down to ask, this lack of personnel is a bit odd in case something happens as well. All in all, a nice place, denitely worth a visit, nice baths, close to the river. My way home to Pucón and Villarica was easy, no dirt roads. Why there is a time slot of three hours, the lady at the reception could not tell, but I was happy with the water that I got from her.

review_text: Great views of the city and the Andes from the top of Cerro San Cristobal. You can walk/hike up, but we weren't dressed for hiking, and had been drinking wine with lunch, so we took the funicular -- not very expensive. At the very summit is a large statue of the Virgin (unfortunately marred by surrounding radio towers). On the way between the funicular stop and the summit there is also an outdoor theatre/cathedral, a small church, and the stations of the cross, each decorated by a different artist. Although it was relatively crowded, you could always find a peaceful place to relax. And as mentioned, some spectacular views. After descending, stroll back down Pio Nono through the Barrio Bellavista and relax on a patio with a cold drink!

review_text: I have been a couple of times to this small museum, located at the crossroads of what used to be the center of the Inca city in the early 16th century, now Santiago de Chile, in a colonial mansion that once was the customs building. In this symbolic place, the permanent Larrain collection and the somewhat misnamed ¨Chile before Chile" exhibit gives an interesting overview of archeological treasures of indigenous cultural expressions in Chile and Latin America before the european invasion. The purpose of my most recent visit was the temporary exhibit of Paracas funerary mantles. A fascinating and mysterious collection, well displayed. We also stepped into the interactive display for children and looked at the souvenir shop and bookstore. Definitely one of Latin America´s better archaeological museums.

review_text: If Valparaiso was in Italy or North America it would be a stunning representation of a once thriving port city, as is suggested by it's UNESCO world heritage listing. Instead it's in Chile, where a general lack of civic pride is evident in it's urban areas. Crumbling public buildings, poor roads and paving and the ubiquitous, mindless tagging on everything up to 2 metres high including statues of national heroes, seem to be ignored by the locals with a shrug and expression of resignation. Look beyond the graffiti and decay and of course Valparaiso is stunning, but unless the government and citizens set about maintaining and restoring the city,it's charm will be lost forever.

review_text: A submarine of the Chilean Navy is totally open for guided visits. It is a must for those who visit Valdívia! We have a chance to see what life was like underwater, for those whose service was in this vessel. It was used for controlling fisheries, in spite of being fitted out for naval warfare. Visitors can see the cots sailor's shared for sleeping, the bathrooms and showers (used only very sparingly, the motor sectors both diesel and electric, dining rooms, captain's cabin fore and aft sectors and navigation facilities. Questions were stimulated and answered with good humor and in an objective way. It was a nice period of time!

review_text: Andres began our tour with an excellent plan to show us his home town and key sites in the area. We began with a tour of Puerta Montt's main square and waterfront view and a tour of a local farm and fish market where locals shop. This stop was well chosen as we browsed stalls of fresh products and watched locals choose and shop for their Sunday meals. Our tour then took us to the very scenic area of Frutillar, where we witnessed, rather unexpectedly, a military parade celebrating a town event. From this town on the 400-square mile Lake Llanquihue, we were able to see 5 volcanos, some of which are still active, in this region of the Pacific Ring of Fire. Our tour then proceeded to Puerto Varas, a charming lake side town filled with Sunday strollers and sightseers. Lunch at a Puerto Varas restaurant crowned the visit with Chilean seafood featured on the menu. After the drive back to Puerta Montt, we visited an artisan market near the port to shop for locally crafted, quality products. Andres is a professional in every sense of the word. His English is outstanding and his descriptions of places and things, and their importance, made the tour a very enjoyable event. Andres was very sociable, and after a brief period together in the car, was very willing to talk openly about himself, his family, and life in Chile. By the end of the day, I felt I had new friend. Dear Travelers. I appreciate your feedback to our job here in Lake District, Patagonia Chile. We are very glad that you and your friends from USA spent a good time in our shore excursion Frutillar, Puerto Varas and Puerto Montt local markets , especially customized for You. Thank you for visited our beautiful Country, preferring our services and support locals here in North Patagonia, Chile. Warm wishes, Andrés Oyarzun Gonzalez & Team Owner & Director Patagonia SouthernLand Expeditions - Chile

review_text: I have just had the pleasure of doing a “free” walking tour with a company called Ecomapu Travel. The three guides (Felipe, Christian and Esteban) offer several tours on this basis during the week. You pay what you wish -- but be generous, as the tours are excellent! I was on the Sunday 3pm tour which started from Paseo 21 de Mayo. It was a pleasant walk looking at the architecture and learning the history of the area called Playa Ancha which is filled with colorful and architecturally interesting San Francisco-like houses. This tour is offered on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays at 3pm. They also offer other free tours Tuesdays thru Sundays that start at either noon or 4pm from the Plaza Sotomayor. I was so impressed with my guides, Felipe and Christian (both came along) that I am doing a their fee-based Graffiti and Wall Art tour later this week (12,000 pesos) and am trying to find time to do their Culinary Tour (25,000 pesos). This is a good little company that is worth checking out. Dear Esther. With much appreciation, Felipe remembers that he accompanied you on this tour in Valparaiso a couple of years ago. We appreciate your comment which has helped keep us going until today. Greetings from Chile and come back soon!

review_text: Pablo Neruda's houses are always a treat. We visited Isla Negra last year, and we couldn't miss his place at Valparaíso. It's a place so wonderful, full of magic and beauty, you cannot simply imagine. The views are absolutely amazing, and the symbolism in all the objects inside the house is nothing but expected coming from him. Isla Negra is a more personal place perhaps, with more history and more story inside, but La Sebastiana is more magical, if that's even possible. We still have to visit La Chascona in Santiago to complete the trilogy of the poet's houses tour. There's a fee to enter the house, 5000 chilean pesos (about 10 dollars) but it is totally worth it. Unforgivable if you go there and skip the visit inside for the price. This fee entitles you to an audio device in your language of choice (only a handful of languages supported of course) which works as your personal guide to the house-museum, so you visit each of its chambers at your own pace, and even repeat the story around some of them if you need to. And I know I'm repeating myself, but the story and the history of this house is just lovely. Unfortunately, they don't allow to take pictures inside the house, and believe, some views from the house ample windows are worth a million words! The silver lining is that in the entrance there's a small souvenir shop where they sell some greeting cards and small books of pictures, including these views from the inside.

review_text: We experienced beauty on a grand scale during our 4 day kayaking trip. The quality of our 5-star British Canoe Union guide was not to be underestimated. Jeremy’s intimate knowledge of the waters we were on assisted in making this perhaps the single most spectacular trip we’ve ever been on. He was well aware of the currently water and wind conditions and was able to adapt our adventure for what nature provided. The meals that he provided were outstanding, especially considering that Jeremy was cooking in the backcountry. All provided gear was first rate including both the paddling equipment and the camping equipment. We experienced this trip in the middle of March, 2020 and Chile was shutting down while we were actually on the water. Nevertheless, Kayak en Patagonia came up with plans so that we were able to complete the trip. Would we come back? Yes!!! We’ve already booked for 2021.

review_text: I had tried to get in the other Spa rated #1 but you had to book nearly a week in advance, so went here for a facial. The facial itself was nice, but short, just 40 mins - I had thought it would be an hour. It is part of a hairdressers, so even though the lady had nice music in you still heard people chatting and banging around etc. So it's fine if all you need is a quick facial and don't care about atmosphere. My skin was nice after. But if you are looking for a 'spa', this is not the place you should go! I had also booked a massage but they only had a man and I wanted a woman. So the lady who did the facial said she would do it, but by that stage I wanted to get out of there. She was already trying to charge me for the facial (more than I had planned because she had used an extra mask - not that I really understood when she asked me if I wanted it).

review_text: On our route from the Bolivian border to Santiago we stopped in San Pedro, where doing a star gazing tour is simply a must. A lot of agencies (namely those recommended by Lonely Planet) are quite lazy and are canceling the tours if they see clouds during the day. Fortunately for us this one was open, didn't cancel and quickly put us on their waiting list. UNCLE asks an elevated (>average) price but all is really well organized and for almost three hours, provided you're curious enough and astronomy interests you a bit, you will hear amazing descriptions and stories of all visible constellations, tips how to locate yourself in the southern hemisphere, look at Mars, Jupiter and Saturn (and yes, Saturn really does have circles around, we saw it !) and finally have a coffee or hot chocolate with snacks. The team members are extremely open, tours when we were there were in English, Spanish and Brazilian, depending on nationalities. Above all you feel the true interest and passion of every member when they talk about stars, star clusters and other galaxies. A truly mind opening experience. No negative note whatsoever! Dan & Tim, June 2018

review_text: My wife and I did the Eberhard Fjord kayak/hiking trip with Jorge and we absolutely loved it. Jorge picked us up from our hotel in Puerto Natales on time and only took 15 mins or so to get to our launch point in Puerto Prat. One thing to keep in mind is that there's no building or dressing room. You'll be getting into your waterproof gear in the open so whatever you have on is going on under the kayak gear. However there was a secure shed where we were able to lock up items we didn't want to bring along. Jorge was an excellent guide. He was very knowledgeable about local history as well as all the floral and fauna. The kayaking was slightly more challenging than expected as Patagonia is rarely without wind and the way out was somewhat resistant. Coming back in was easier. A little over halfway through our kayaking we pull off for a short hike up to an amazing viewpoint then stopped for a snack and tea which was a nice touch. We saw falcons, condors, ducks, swan and flamingos over the course of the day. Even better is that we had the entire Fjord to ourselves as we did not see a single person the entire time. It was a great way to appreciate the vastness and remoteness of this part of the world. I definitely recommend.

review_text: Venture Patagonia did an absolutely unbelievable job organizing a trip that highlighted the best of Patagonia and Chile. We started off as a group of 26 highschoolers, college kids, and parents on the W trek with Carrie and her team of incredible guides leading the way. They accommodated everyone's individual needs perfectly with a wide range of skill levels in hiking, backpacking, and camping. The meals were amazing and unlike any backpacking meals I've ever eaten (our first dinner was a 3 course meal!). After completing the W trek, a smaller group continued on to the O circuit where our guide Alejandro led us on a 5 day trek on the backside of the Patagonian mountains. The days were long and tough but the views were unlike anything I have ever seen. It was a well planned and well executed backpacking trip that I will never forget (for both the experience and the views). After the O trek, my siblings and I joined up with our parents and we continued on a few more days of adventures throughout Chile and the Torres del Paine National Park. Carrie and her team did a great job giving us a full tour of the park, while letting us plan our own days. We went kayaking, day hiking, experienced the most amazing sunrise over the mountains, and visited penguins on the Magdalena islands. We truly experienced the best parts Patagonia has to offer and it was all stress free, well organized, and unbelievably fun. Being able to interact with Carrie one on one and hear her story of living in Chile completed the whole experience. It didn't feel like we were tourists, but almost like locals getting a secret tour of the cities and mountains. I can honestly say this was the most amazing and unforgettable trip I have ever been on and it will be extremely difficult to top. Venture patagonia was outstanding in all aspects of planning, organizing, and executing the trip and surpassed all expectations. review_text: We completed the full "O" circuit in 7 days/6 nights, camping along the way. We intended to do it in 8 days, but doubled up one day and completed early due to good weather. I highly recommend the full circuit if you have the time and fitness level. It can easily be done in 6 days, the times on the map are wrong. For instance between Seron and Dickson it says 8 hours on the map, in reality it is under 6 hours. In hindsight, we would've skipped Seron and hiked straight to Dickson had we known. Going into the park we weren't sure where to start the circuit. Upon arrival at Laguna Amarga we could see a bit of the Torres, so we decided to start there, this also allowed us to hike day 1 without our heavy packs. By the time we got to the Torres, the weather cleared and it was amazing. Our route was as follows Day 1 - Torres Camping (at the bottom, near hotel) Day 2 - Seron Day 3 - Dickson Day 4 - Los Perros Day 5 - Grey Day 6 - Frances (we went to Italiano, only to be turned away due to lack of reservation, however we left our packs at the ranger station and hiked the french valley, then descended to the new Frances camp) Frances camp has by far the nicest showers/bathroom & view in the park, but all campsites are on platforms which for me is too stiff. A few tips: Garbage bags are your best friend - line your pack with them, keep everything else in ziplocks. Rain covers are great, but the wind can make it pain to keep on. Once you hit the "W" get on the trail early for some peace. Seemed like most people slept in, we would get up at 0530, on the trail by 0700 and wouldn't see another hiker for hours Trekking poles - never used them until this hike, they were indispensable, especially descending the pass to Grey. It can get very muddy and slick, they help steady you and save the knees a bit Remain flexible - when the weather is good, go for it, double up if needed. We camped in the mud and rain at Los Perros since the pass was snowing, we debated just going over in the bad weather. However, the next morning we were rewarded with a perfect day, sun, blue skies and no wind. The pass was our favorite day on the circuit, try to wait for good weather, the views are incredible. Pack light - We took the time to calculate calories needed and package up food for each day to make sure we didn't bring too much. We did all our provisioning in Puerto Natales, starting at the Unimarc and then supplementing with 3 other small stores. We also only brought our hiking clothes, plus our sleeping clothes. Most of our rental gear was light, but the sleeping bags were very heavy. It might be beneficial to rent from multiple outfitters to get the right combination. Enjoy it - take your time, its beautiful!

review_text: I have heard a lot of people talk about Chile's economic progress and relative prosperity and stability compared to some of the other South American countries. This museum is a reminder of the price they paid to get to that point. Irrespective of politics and the rights and wrongs of the policial situation at the time the blatant violation of human rights is a frightening reminder of how a society can implode and become divided. This museum gives some context to a foreigner about what happened and the impact it had on individuals and society. If you don't speak fluent Spanish pick up the audio guide - you won't gain much of an understanding if you don't.

review_text: More than “just a climb to a live Volcano” Been to Torres Del Paine (W Circuit) & San Pedro Atacama (desert in the north), and I found Pucon Volcano to be a contender for my favourite thing to have done in Chile. I didn’t know this (until I booked) but the trip includes body sleighing down the Volcano snow, after you’ve reached and seen the top. Further you can elect to ski or snow board down the volcano. I snowboarded and felt it was the best off piste boarding I’ve done. I would rate the terrain as medium- not for beginners and you don’t have to be an expert. The snow conditions (early Dec 17) was more soft than ice. I stayed at French Andes hostel in Pucon. Loved the hostel. The hostel is affiliated or owned by Aguaventura (tours / sports / hire shop) in Pucon. I booked my tour with Aguaventura. The price was competitive locally and service excellent. They provided all the clothing and equipment (inc gas mask for the volcano top !!) The tour itself was hosted by 4 local Chilean guides (12 tourists in our group). They (guides) were superb. Full of energy, informative, fun and caring. Probably made my day if I’m honest. The French owner of French Andes and Aguaventura I found to be a gentlemen. Very helpful and wanted to ensure we all had a good and safe time. I climbed the volcano on a beautiful sunny and warm day. Of course the weather changes and for this reason I would imagine the overall experience can easily change from day to day from person to person. If your in town I say to you it’s a must trip. And 1 last thing. I saw lava spewing when I reached the top. That’s a bucket list item for me ticked. !!

review_text: My wife, my daughter and my grandchild and I went up on Cerro San Christobal in early January 2017. We went out to the Providencia neighborhood to talk the terriferico, a gondola ride, up to the top of San Christobal. The gondola ride gives an amazing view of Santiago as it gradually gets higher and higher over the city. The gondola ride looks very new, modern and safe. No pets allowed. The gondola ride did not have any significant lines like the funicular does. The top of San Christobal is extensive with snack and souvenir shops, a Christmas creche of beautifully carved life sized wood statutes, and a sanctuary for saying mass. Then terraces with steps going up to the very top are somewhat uneven but with iron railings. The steps go up to the very top of the mountain to the base of the statute of the Virgin Mary. Underneath the statute of the Virgin is a small room with frescoes and a beautiful opened book. To the side and below the Virgin is an area with candles and many things attached to the wall giving thanks for prayers answered. The view from the top of San Christobal is truly magnificent. You can see the city of Santiago in all directions. There was a helicopter flying over the city and it was below us! The river is clearly shown and various buildings can be picked out to help give an orientation to the view. review_text: We recently did the trip from Chacabuco to Puerto Montt. We booked the trip online, very easy. To reach Chacabuco from Coyhaique you just need to take a bus to Puerto Aysén (leaving every hour, 1-hour trip), from where you will find minivans leaving to Chacabuco in front of the supermarket (instead of taking a taxi), which is just like 400 m away from the small bus terminal. The ferry terminal in Chacabuco is basic, toilets, small cafeteria and Wi-Fi available for free. The ferry as many have previously pointed out carries also vehicles and animals. Everything was organized and clean. Cabins were simple (we have a 2 bed cabin, one bunk bed with a window). Showers and toilets worked ok and were quite clean. The meals were very good ans portions were generous. Staff was friendly. Not a lot to do nor see during the 24h ferry ride. No fjords to be seen from Chacabuco to Puerto Montt (you leave Chacabuco during the evening when it is dark). The scenery was monotonous ans we were actually dissapointed. We had time to relax (eat, sleep, read, watch movies). If you happen to be in Cohayque or Puerto Montt and are heading respectively either North or South, then this option is definetely recommended. Much more comfortable and relaxing than bus drives and the price is ok and the meals served are good (breakfast, lunch and 2 dinners). If you plan on doing this trip just because of the landscapes then you will better skip it, you won't see absolutely anything special between Chacabuco and Puerto Montt, just water and some land.

review_text: I thought that this was supposed to be a wine tour plus Vina del Mar and Valparaiso. I also thought that this was an English language tour. They picked us up at our hotel about 8:30 and transported us and many others taking this tour and other ones to their central stop near a mall. Our bus was used for our tour, but I had to still get off and stand in line to pay for our tour. I found out as we were driving out of Santiago that we were not going to any wineries. That was more my hotel's fault and mine as well for not doing more research since I had emailed the concierge that I wanted to visit a winery or two in the direction of Valparaiso plus Valparaiso, but something got lost in the translation. It was a panoramic tour with multiple picture stops plus one long stop for lunch near the casino in Vina del Mar. It turned out also to be a 2 language tour, and 75% of the presentation was done in Spanish! I don't believe it takes 3 times as long to communicate in Spanish so I felt that those of us who only spoke English were short changed and probably lost interest as we did! The tour guide was very friendly, and the driver seemed experienced, but I wasn't impressed. The tour guide spoke English but not well enough to really give English tours plus she really didn't know the area other than the canned tour lines. When I asked her at the lunch stop, she had no idea where we should go for lunch. She mainly pointed people to the casino. We walked the wrong way and found nothing decent so we walked back and went the other direction and found many more choices. In Valparaiso, we did a long walk and then were put back on the bus because the square had too much traffic. I didn't see that much, and it was Saturday afternoon! On the walk, we went down multiple flights of stairs and had to walk through some street and sidewalk construction. There was a couple on our bus who was flying home that night, and the tour guide acted like she was trying to help them, but they still had to take a taxi at the end to get back to their hotel-not sure if they made their flight or not?? I just wasn't impressed with the tour guides very much. It was cheaper than others, and we got what we paid for, I guess. At the end of the tour, our bus was the one taking us back to our hotel so we didn't have to change buses, but we did have a 20 minute wait or so before we left the central point. They dropped others off and then got near our hotel and said we had to get off at the stoplight before and then cross the street and walk the last 100m to our hotel. Their tip amount decreased significantly at this point, and it was already less than I would normally give. Find another tour company and go with them! I wouldn't do anything with Turistik on a future trip to Chile! We appreciate your comment dear traveler, it is very important for us to know about your experience.

review_text: We joined Phillipe's morning tour along with approximately 30 others. What a grat way to start learning about the sights, culture and history of this amazing place. Phillipe was funny, engaging, passionate and very knowledgable about his city. I've noticed on tours in other cities that guides avoid the more contraversial topics or remain infuriatingly 'PC' but Phillipe's insight and honesty was refreshing and fascinating. He offered his own views whilst leaving space to disagree if you chose to. His introduction has made me subsequently find out more about the Pinochet years and has made me fall in love with the Chilean people even more! The tour is free, but of course, the guides need to earn a living and so they welcome tips! The amount they suggest is 5000 -8000 pesos (very approx. £7 - £10). In my view this is inexpensive for a 4 hour tour so packed full of interesting facts, opinions and insights. As an aside, this is a great way to meet other English speaking people in the city. After the tour 5 of us headed off to the Fish Market for lunch and spent the afternoon wandering around the city - which was an unexpected bonus of having been on the tour.

review_text: This is a must for all long term backpackers - the perfect break to chill out, not think about the next few days, not think about cooking / shopping. You get 3 decent cooked meals a day, accommodation, sightseeing, informative talks and great social opportunities. Complete downtime with no internet and without the guilt of feeling like you should be busy seeing something or planning something. Most of the rest is covered in other reviews but a couple other points. It's not a cruise liner, get your expectations right. Its a cargo ferry but its still comfy. Sights and seas... this is very much season and weather dependent which is luck of the draw. We saw blue whales, had calm seas and sunny weather for most of it... you might see more sea life or you might have the roughest seas. You go through some very remote waters. Cost - in the low season it's well worth it if you need to get north and have the time, calculate in the meals and nights of accommodation and you're 50 to 100 out of pocket in comparison to a bus. High season seems too pricey and bus certainly sound more appealing. People onboard are all friendly and helpful especially Percy and the Captain. Its not everyday a captain of a ship lets you into his bridge and tells you about everything. Thank you for sharing your experience!
