review_text: Great hike and definitely worth the distance! My husband and I hiked the circuit in January 2017. Make sure you have reservations for all of your campsites if you plan to do the circuit or they won't let you past the ranger station between Seron and Dickson. While coordinating all of the reservations can be tough, we did not need or use a guide. If you are able to get all of your reservations, the back side is gorgeous. It is much quieter than the W too. Coming over the pass and seeing Glacier Grey for the first time was breathtaking. The W, while crowded, had some amazing views. Unfortunately it was a bit cloudy when we visited Base del las Torres so the view was only ok then. Make sure to spend some time at Mirador Frances. We saw a couple small avalanches while taking a break there. If you stay at Camp Torres, look out for the fox. One lives close to the camp and visits often!

review_text: First from many miles away you see the classic volcano cone topped an icing of snow set against the blue Chilean sky. Then you learn that there is a road that takes you above the tree lineyou even closed to the top of this powerful beauty that last erupted in 1982. If you're a nervous driver, you might want to pay for one of the full day tours of the area (including the beautiful Petroue Falls) or a 'sunset' volcano only one. Or, if like us, you like to self-pace and want to explore more of the Lake District, rental cars are easy enough to obtain. Bring a jacket as it's breezy and cooler where the road ends at the ski lodge, which is open for food, drink, souvenirs and restrooms. Multiple trails leading upward stem from there, too. However you get there, if you do nothing else while you're in this region, don't miss this one!

review_text: This is a must do tour in tandem with lunch at Fuegos de Apalta. Reservations are necessary for both lunch and the tour, especially if requesting a tour in English. We were fortunate to have Nastassia as our wonderful guide and leader of the wine tasting. She is a local, knowledgeable, enthusiastic, and passionate guide. The tour includes a drive through the vineyards where the setting of the valley is a beautiful backdrop to the dynamic and eco sensitive growing process of diverse grapes. Nastassia explains the history of the valley, as well as what makes Montes wines so distinctive and special. We visited after the harvest (in June), but the experience was still outstanding. The truck tour of the vineyards is followed by a walkthrough of the wine production and aging facility. Highly recommend the high range tour as you get to visit the barrel room and taste 4 of Montes’ top wines. Nastassia was a wealth of information with a lovely and welcoming manner - she even helped us unexpectedly find appreciation for Chilean Chardonnay and, especially, Chilean Merlot. And, tasting the Montes Alpha M was worth the price of admission alone! A visit to Colchagua valley without a leisurely stop at Montes and Fuegos de Apalta would be a missed opportunity for a world-class experience. The changing light as the sun came up really showed off the geysers and surrounding area to great affect. The breakfast provided by our tour guide was also very welcome. Well worth a visit, but unless you do it at sunrise you will not see the steam. As the sun warms up, the steam disappears and you are left with just the bubbling.

review_text: Valle de la Luna is breathtaking. Even more so if you do it when no one else is around! Half our group went on an organised tour in the evening, and half hired bikes. On bikes we had the valley almost all to ourselves (the only people in the caves, the only people on the peaks), whilst our friends had to file through the caves with 30 other people. This place is stunning (up their with Foz do Iguacu for wow factor). Unlike Iguazu, you have the opportunity to experience this wild, barren landscape without a million and one other tourists. Hiring bikes should be an option for anyone with a basic level of fitness and competency. The road is only about 6km, wide and empty. There are some gradients in the Valle itself, but these can always be walked without taking up too much time.

Before booking a rafting tour with this agency, I explicitly asked why they charge with 25.000 Pesos much more than the other agencies for rafting bajo (rafting alto was closed due to a lot of water). Most of the time the river was even with a lot of water quite calm, and the trip ia rather something for families than for people looking for adventure. Besides that, I was looking for a tour on volcano Villarrica, and as the only agency Sur Xtremo wanted to sell me this tour for a day on which bad weather was forecasted (it was indeed bad weather on that day with lots of clouds and rain). Thus, I am sorry to write this, but I cannot suggest this agency at all. Book your tours with other more professional and very importantly honest agencies.

review_text: we ate we drank we got merry. And all off the usual beaten track of Chilean enoturismo. We asked Kylie to put together a package that would be interesting and different and she delivered in spades. The tour was a family Christmas treat so started from our flat in Las Condes and took in William Fevre in Pirque (for an early thirst quencher) where we met the enologist who discussed the different terroirs up the Cajon de Maipu and around Pirque, and how they affect the wines. We had a mooch round the wine making facilities and then got to the important bit - a tasting under the trees (yummy) and some retail therapy in the bodega shop. We tried a chardonnay, a rose and the chacai (¿cachai?) a rather excellent asemblaje. Unfortunately we cleaned the shop out of it and would have bought more if we could. Next stop was Chateau Los Boldos - not usually open to Joe Public but that doesn't stop Kylie! Here we met the viticulturist - the guy in charge of actually growing grapes good enough to make the wine. It was here that we learned how much a team effort the whole vitification is (and how the enologists steal all the glory!). We asked loads of questions, almost overstayed our welcome and of course did some tasting. Again excellent wines, no shop a few hints as to where you can buy them in Santiago. next stop was Anakena and lunch. We were late but we still got the tour description of the process tour of the gardens and shown how the leaves of the different vines differ. The to the restaurant which was outstanding. Delicious hors d'oeuvres awaited us while the chef put the finishing touches to lunch. Well he had some more wine with lunch and of course bought yet more (cases) in the shop. After lunch it was time for some photos and then the ride home. Kylie provided a highly personalised service with a great selection of different vineyards and delicious at very reasonable prices. If you hadn't guessed I'd recommend going on one of her trips (unless you don't like wine or food). I'll be going on another soon I am sure. I'm chuffed to receive such a great review. I enjoyed putting this customised tour together and taking us a little further from Santiago for the day, and I had a lot of fun with your group. Thanks for booking the trip with me, and taking the time to recommend me to others. I do hope to see you on another trip soon!

review_text: We did the 1/2 day kayak trip with KoKayak near Puerto Varas. Despite being clear that we were specifically looking for a kayak trip on the main lake they failed to read our messages properly and we ended up at the small laguna nearby which we would not recommend unless you just want to try out kayaking. There is very little to see there. We are travelling on a budget and had been saving up to do a kayak trip somewhere special. We specifically wanted to kayak on Lago Llanquihue so we asked the company before booking if they would be going to the lake on the day we were booking for rather than the small laguna option which we were not interested in. They said they would but on the day we were taken to the laguna and told the lake was not an option. When we complained afterwards the company said it was a misunderstanding and it was our fault for booking a trip with two different options. We politely requested a partial refund since we had not been given the trip we asked for (and which they said they would be running) but they refused. The guide we had on the day was good but we did not enjoy our trip that much due to the location and are really disappointed with the company and their failure to either communicate properly in the first place or to rectify the situation for us afterwards. We regret booking with them, are disappointed to have spent the money on a poor experience in an otherwise beautiful area, and can't recommend this trip. So, we will take all necessary measures to ensure that the customer who comes to us is actually doing the activity they want to do. Having a bad time it really is the last thing we want in Ko'Kayak and it goes totally and absolutely against our policies, which are basically to have a good time with our passengers. On behalf of Ko'Kayak, we apologize and hope that you keep some fond memories of the activity that many others have enjoyed over the years. Sincerely, Maria Noguera & Ko'Kayak team

review_text: My husband and I were the only participants so we got, Lou, our wonderful guide all to ourselves. He spoke great English but also let us practice our spanish. It was great to have a guide lead us through the forest as we climbed up through many different ecosystems on the skirt of the volcano. It was interesting to have Lou tell us about the different plants and the culture of the indigenous people. Then we popped out of the forest and onto the basalt and tundra all around the skirt of the volcano. We were fortunate to have a clear warm day and some beautiful views. The hike down was steep but equally enjoyable. The geometricas were in a beautiful setting and so enjoyable. I would recommend this tour. review_text: This is possible one of the best ways to take in the panoramic views of Santiago. We bought a package deal which allowed us to take a return trip on the funicular followed by the cable car trip. I suggest you go on a weekday as soon as it opens on a clear day to avoid queues. First you take the funicular. As usual try to get the front car for the best views and photo opportunities. Don't jump off at the zoo but go right to the top. Then you can explore the crest, its park, church, and statue of the Virgin Mary. Once you've completed this section jump into the cable car. The views from here are the best in town, so definitely bring your camera. If you ride it all the way to the end its only a 10 minute walk to the tallest building in South America and its observation floor. Its a wonderful way to spend an entire morning. There are plenty of places to get water and a snack en route. Grateful to read your comment and see how detailed each point lived in #ExperienciaTeleferico Jocelyn M. We are happy to be part of your memorable memories during your stay in Santiago de Chile. See you soon!

review_text: This is a full day hike and needs to be undertaken when weather gods look to be in your favour. We had sun all the way up, and rain all the way down! For most people, it will be 3-4 hours each way. The way there is the most challenging on your fitness, the way back is hard if leg or back issues as many steep steps and rocks to negotiate. As others have said, the first section is steep, then some respite as gradual uphill through lovely forest canopy, then the final 45 minute oir more assault on the steep and rocky path to the top. The reward is stunning views, if the weather is still good, and a great spot for lunch and photos. Is well marked for the majority of the way but its popularity means many others are about that can follow. Minimal facilities along the way but welcome centre at carpark, where hike commences, is very acceptable. Highly recommend if moderate or better fitness.

review_text: Skiing in the powdery snow, intense sun, and otherworldly Andean scenery of Valle Nevado in August was a tremendous experience. I would recommend this resort to any skier in the world. Note to travelers: Not wanting to leave anything to chance, I included in my Valle Nevado hotel reservation a shuttle from the airport. It was expensive but I thought it would be the surest option for the rather death-defying two-lane switchback road up the mountain. The vehicle that met me at the airport was unable to get up the road in the snow and had to stop. A second vehicle was damaged in a minor accident immediately upon picking me up. A third vehicle completed the ascent -- total time, four hours. (Happily, the return trip only took an hour and a half.) Alternate arrangements may be advisable.

review_text: We took a day tour to Valle Nevado from Santiago. Including the stops to arrange gear hire it took us more than 2 hours to get there, firstly because the trip organiser was arranging pick ups from lots of hotels and secondly because the road into Valle Nevada is slow and very, very, very windy - something like 35+ hairpin bends on a very steep road. Coming back was even worse and longer because we were slowed by once again having to stop to hand back the equipment hire, split people back onto different buses to drop them back to their hotels and because we arrived into the nightmare that is Santiago's evening peak hour traffic :-( Putting the painful travel to one side, Valle Nevada is a reasonable ski venue. Because it was mid week the slopes were comparatively bare and the runs really un-crowded, so I got a lot of runs in and wasn't having to manage too many competing skiers getting in my way. Snow quality was good and if you took the more demanding and higher trails there's a reasonable amount to challenge your ability at any level - but not a huge variety to be sure. The infrastructure, the number and length of runs compares a little poorly to major US and European resorts where runs are longer and more varied. Added to which food and drink options are limited and very expensive. Given that it is ideally placed to offer skiing when the northern hemisphere is in summer, and at this time of year (southern hemisphere winter) the Australasian slopes can be crazy busy and expensive, it was certainly worthwhile as an alternative ski venue to Australia and New Zealand. For me it was a great tick off the bucket having always wanted to ski in South America. On balance though, it's something I'd do once and for a day trip - the pain of getting there and the relatively limited variety of runs and moderate infrastructure and food/drink options doesn't make it compelling for a longer and more involved stay.

review_text: We were recommended this company by our hotel and called Antü on Sunday night to organise a climb up Villarrica volcano the following morning. Joaquin (the owner) accommodated our last minute request with ease and immediately made us feel very welcome and excited about the trip. The next morning we met the Antü crew who had prepared our packs and shoes and everything we would need for the mountain. Everything was perfectly arranged down to extra thermals and jackets (we didn’t really bring enough warm clothes). The Antü team are fantastic. Very professional and knowledgeable but also good fun and engaging. Unfortunately, we couldn’t climb that morning due to clouds and low visibility. We discussed with Joaquin and our guide Albaro what to do as we had only one more morning in Pucón before we needed to leave for Santiago at around 10am. Joaquin’s solution - Our guide, Albaro, would pick us up at our hotel at 2:30am with everything ready for a very early hike up the mountain so that we could be back down in time for our flight at 9:30am. Sounded tough but very interesting. The next morning at 6:30 am we were standing alone on the top of the volcano with the rising sun to our right and the smoking volcano to our left. We had such an amazing experience from the moment we started the hike. Our guide, Albaro was fantastic, really great company and looked after us all the way. We are so thankful to have met this awesome group of people to make this experience truely unforgettable. I can not recommend them highly enough for your Pucón adventures! First of all thank you very much for having the confidence to carry out the activity with us and we are very pleased that you have accepted the challenge of making an ascent at dawn, that shows that they are capable of a lot of things if they propose it. It was a pleasure to have them as clients and we hope to have them back in Pucon at some point so that they can have the opportunity to dominate the Villarrica volcano of the day, as they did at night. Best regards from the staff of Antü Rios y Montañas.

review_text: We organized a trip to Chile with the specific goal of visiting the top wineries and tasting their top wines. We emphasized to the tour organizer that we had been tasting wines around the world for over 40 years and we specifically did not want a wine tasting 101. We arrived to Viu Manent in the middle of a rainy day, which certainly didn't help. We were shepherded into the gift shop, where after a few minutes we were met by our guide. HE was a somewhat arrogant fellow who never "connected" with the group. Despite our request for a private tour, we were accompanied by another 10-12 people. We had a cursory walk-through the fermentation and maturation areas, then shown the bottling area and then driven back to the wine tasting room. After a "canned talk" about how wonderful Viu Manent wines were, we were rushed through 5 mediocre wines after which, the guide bade us farewell and disappeared. It was one of the most disappointing visits to a winery, especially one that presumes to be a better one.

review_text: I can not recommend Hectour Services and Hector as a guide highly enough. I would even say he is without a doubt the best guide I have ever met in my many years of travels. I came across HecTours after searching the internet for days trying to find any small group or private tours that would drive from Santiago Chile all the way to Cusco in Peru via Bolivia. Most tours would not do the itinerary we wanted to do and most would not allow small tour vans or car hire across most of the borders. After contacting Hector to see if it was possible, he was the first to reply with a 'yes anything is possible' was his words. He always replied straight away to my emails, we even added each other on Whatsapp to keep communication as well, together we created an itinerary and he worked out all the logistics and came up with a price we were happy to agree upon. Our tour was 26 days driving in a 12 seater van with a private driver + Hector as our personal guide, eight of us in total travelling from Chile via Argentina, back to Chile then up through Bolivia to then finish off in Peru. Seeing all the tourist attractions along the way, major highlights like Valparaíso, El Leoncito National Park, Talampaya National Park, Cafayate, Tilcara and the rainbow mountain, San Pedro de Atacama, Uyuni, La Paz, Lake Titicaca, Colca Canyon and Cusco. It was amazing!! Actually incredible!! There was 6 of us (My family) And he took care of us all as if we were apart of his own family, giving extra attention to my parents also, this I loved as it meant us children had someone else to make sure they were always ok. Hector is now apart of our family, he has been adopted as a second son by my parents and we have told him that when he comes to Australia he will always have a place to stay with us. Just for reference, some of the exceptional things he did to go above and beyond was: Help us with all border crossing (this is no joke and very hard to do) He helped us with translating at all hotels, restaurants and with other local tours and guides that we had to book in local areas. He gave expert knowledge on all things he knew in each area we went to, and told us about the history and stories of his country and others that he had been to that we were to visit. When anything went wrong (small hiccups along the way) he came up with solutions straight away so our holiday was not affected and we did not miss out on anything that was on our itinerary. He just made the whole experience seamless and enjoyable the entire way. After spending 26 days with a crazy Australian family he was always professional, polite and put us and all our wants and needs first, I can't thank him enough!! The other members of my family including my father have also put up reviews for him if you would like to read those too. All in all, I can say with certainty that HecTour Services will provide you with exceptional service at a fair and reasonable price for what they provide. You can not go wrong and Hector and his team will always go out of their way to make sure you have a wonderful time and enjoy your holiday. Thanks again Hector for everything, we hope to see you again in the future soon! Mike and I will be in touch when we are able to come back to Chile again. xx

review_text: In a county of beautiful wine estates, Santa Rita stands out as one of the prettiest and most historic. Just 45 minutes from Santiago yet a world away from the city smog and congestion. You can easily spend the day here to experience everything it has to offer (we did)! Vina Santa Rita was founded in 1880 by Domingo Fernandez Concha. Today you can tour the 100-acre park that surrounds what was once his summer home (now the Casa Real Hotel). Then of course there are the vineyards. For Carmenère lovers (that’s me) – make sure you visit the monolith that marks the spot where Carmenère vines, previously thought to be Merlot, were discovered growing in 1994. And don’t miss a visit to the “Bodega de los 120 Patriotas”, a courageous story of Chilean history. Last but not least – let’s not forget the wines! Both the Santa Rita and Carmen labels are known for their premium selections. Everyone we met was so friendly and knowledgeable. My suggestion for the perfect day: Take a tour that includes the park, vineyard and wine cellars. On a sunny spring day, it was beautiful! Follow this with your tasting. By now you’ll have an appetite for lunch at the on-site Dona Paula restaurant. Conclude your Santa Rita experience with a leisurely visit to the free Museo Andino, also located on-site. This is a 5+ star day! Thank you very much for your congratulations! It is very gratifying to know that you enjoyed your experience at Viña Santa Rita and we would love to welcome you again.

review_text: Pablo Neruda, politician and poet, has three homes throughout Chile, but this one is most interesting because it was originally built for his mistress (later wife), Matilde Urrutia. The home was built to resemble a ship and includes multiple buildings and levels. Normally I balk at an audio tour, but this time the audioplayer was glued to my ear. Neruda was an incredible fascinating guy and he acquired some incredible furniture and decor within in home. Photos weren't allowed in the buildings on the tour which was a major bummer, but my favorite piece was absolutely the original Diego Rivera depicting the two sides of Matilde (the private one of her life with Neruda and the public one where she was known as a singer). There is also a silhouette of Neruda's face in hidden in the hair which she was famous for (and that the house, Chascona meaning 'messy hair', was named after). Neruda also had multiple bars within his home, including a "summer bar". Paul and I both agreed that all homes should require a summer bar. I didn't know much about Neruda prior to the visit, but his home was really interesting to see and the audio tour definitely touched on a lot of the political history of Chile. I'd definitely recommend it! It is also walking distance to the Cerro San Cristobal funicular!

review_text: The owners of Mirador de Chepu are dedicated to their cause: preserving the precious and unique natural environment of Chiloé, and by allowing travellers to experience it, I believe their cause is gaining strength. The cost of lodging is minimal and more than fair for the experiences offered. The owners are warm, friendly people who made my group feel right at home. Fernando, the owner, was extremely accomodating, meeting our group at the bus stop to transport us to the isolated and tranquil setting.The Eco-Lodges are situated in a picturesque setting and feature neat, tidy cabins, solar powered showers, and composting. The weather on Chiloé is extremely variable, so plan accordingly. Bring rain gear and warm clothing. The cabins are comfortable and clean, but very small and basic. They are meant to be a step up from sleeping on the ground or in a tent. If you do not have blankets and bedding, they can be provided for you for a small fee. The penguin colony trek is a can´t-miss experience, but be advised that the route is extremely taxing. There is deep mud, slippery hills, off-and-on rain, and rough terrain nearly all the way to the colony. Wear layers and a sturdy pair of hiking boots--in places, the mud can be nearly knee-deep. Please be advised that the lodges are dedicated to making a minimal impact on the environment. No polluting and no loud, disruptive partying--it is a place for people who want to truly experience and appreciate the natural beauty of the island. It is truly an unforgettable and unique experience!

review_text: It is the wold's biggest open pit copper mine, fully state owned. It is impressive by its size: 3x5 km wide and long, and 1 km deep. On the other hand it is sad to see what a big wound we are capable of doing to our Earth. It's a must see if we are in the region and interested in industries, though certainly makes us think. The bilingual visit is informative and well organized by Codelco (name of the sate owned company). You need to request the visit in email from the visitor center, visitas@ codelco.cl indicating the date, and you will receive a confirmation with all the necessary details you need to know. Tours leave at 13.00 from the Office in Calama. After visiting the mine there is a short stop on the former living estate, built 100 years ago and recently fully abandonned. The main square is well maintained, but living districts are locked away, cannot be visited. Belongs to the ghost towns of the Atacama desert. I received fair responses for my questions, but a briefing about the social structures and living conditions, how people used to live here were not part of the tour. I believe it would be as interesting as the explanation of metallurgical details on the mining site. If you are in San Pedro, I recommend you to either use the local buses, or come by the airport shuttle to the airport and then to the Office. They will collect you back to San Pedro too. A return fee is 20000 Peso, plus a few thousand between the airport and the Office. The tour itself is fee but donation for a children fund is accepted.

review_text: Bit of a drive to get here from Copiapo (but the only nearer town is Chanaral, and you certainly wouldn't want to stay there), but once you get beyond Chanaral, the desert/coast scenery gets more interesting, with a couple of very pretty, secluded beaches. The best reason for visiting is a boat trip round Isla Pan de Azucar, home to the northernmost colony of Humboldt Penguins (as well as sealions, pelicans, etc). To reach the island, drive about 30km beyond Chanaral (on the coast road), past the first 'inhabited' beach, and over the headland to the next beach. Then find your willing fisherman! We were a little surprised that even though there were 4 people wanting to go at noon, the fishermen wouldn't set out till three. Still, there was a cafeteria on the beach, so could wait with a nice cold drink and a snack. Makes sense, I suppose, if the penguins are at sea feeding during the middle of the day and don't return till late afternoon... so just don't expect to do it in a hurry! We also had the excitement of the boat's engine dying once we reached the island (you don't actually land, just sail close to it), and taking 40 minutes for them to get it restarted. If the worst had come to the worst, it wasn't that long a swim to the nearest beach...

review_text: We had booked Chile Off Track for their Valparaiso day tour and Santiago half day city tour based on past Trip Advisor reviews. Whilst the tours are quite expensive we were not disappointed. Tessa our lovely guide was prompt in picking us up at our hotel at 8.30am in the company's MPV and on this day we were the only two customers on the tour so the MPV was very comfortable. Before setting off for Valparaiso we were introduced to Pablo a young man who recently joined the company as a new tour guide and who was accompanying us for the day. Both Tessa (a young Dutch national with an interesting career history) and Pablo speak excellent English, and both have engaging personalities. On our walking tour around Valparaiso we were taken on the old funicular railway up to the top of the hill overlooking the city where most of the old heritage listed buildings are situated. We then walked around the streets stepping into interesting art galleries and artisans shops, and seeing amazing street art that adorns many of the walls in the old city. There are plenty of photo opportunities. During the walk we stopped for morning coffee in a quaint old house overlooking Valparaiso port and then later for lunch in a lovely restaurant in the old city again with views of the port and newer city below. After lunch the tour continued by visiting the Pablo Neruda Museum and house for about 1 hour. The museum is dedicated to the memory of this famous poet and writer, who whilst not known well outside of the country, is revered in Chile. The next day Tessa met us and then took us on our Santiago City sights walking tour through some of lesser known areas of Santiago,where you would not venture on your own as a tourist. We then toured the central food markets and the normal tourist spots such as the La Moneda and Cathedral de Santiago. The tour then finished with a 'tapas' lunch at a great wine bar/restaurant in the Barrio Lasstaria. The personalised tours provided by Chile Off Track were a great way of seeing some of the Chilean way of life and locations that you may not encounter if doing a tour in a large group. The tours outlined above are recommended.

review_text: TLDR: Sebastian and our driver did an awesome job handling adversity, keeping us informed, and making sure we had a good time. Not only is the lagoon itself stunning, but the drive up also does not disappoint. My group ended up being a group of mostly Spanish speakers with a few English speakers, and Sebastian did a great job of switching between the two languages. So let me preface my following experience by saying this is NOT how the tour typically goes. So the van picks up the group and all is well as we head up to the Vineyard. We were there for about 20 minutes before the day's plans started changing. Sebastian and our Driver, I wish I could remember his name, did an awesome job of not only being flexible but also keeping us up to date. So anyway, as our time at the vineyard was coming to an end, Sebastian gathered up the group and said that we would actually be doing a wine tasting at the vineyard as there was an accident on the highway up ahead that was blocking the highway. This ended up being a much-appreciated choice as the vineyard was beautiful. We ended up being at the vineyard for about another hour before loading up into the van. We head up the highway and all is going well, under the presumption that the accident had been cleared, little did we know the turn of events that was about to occur. About 30 minutes after leaving the vineyard, traffic comes to a standstill, and it turns out the road is still closed. We then sat for about another 30 minutes before deciding to turn around to find lunch. We ended up finding a restaurant with enough capacity to accommodate our group about 1/3 of the way back to Santiago in Los Andes. Sebastian did well in choosing a restaurant and lunch was delicious. At the beginning of lunch, as a group, we decided to head back to Santiago as the highway to the lagoon was still closed. Disappointed, we eat lunch and get ready to pay. Here comes the good news, we find out the highway has reopened, and asks if we want to head up (it was 4 pm at this time). As a group, we decide that that's what we want to do so we pay and head up the mountain. Due to construction on the two-lane highway, and the remaining backlog of traffic, it ended up taking about 2.5-3 hours to make the trek up the mountain. It was so worth it in the end and heading up was definitely the right decision. We spent about an hour exploring the lagoon and then headed back to Santiago arriving back in the city around 11 pm. Again huge shoutout to Sebastian and our driver for making the best of the situation and giving the group a good story to tell at the end of the day. Review of: Andes Range Tour at Inca Lagoon & InSitu Winery Snack Included

review_text: Pablo Neruda is Chile's most famous son: Nobel-prize winning poet, diplomat, leftist politician with a powerful and influential voice against the exploitation of the Chilean people, he was hated by Pinochet who probably had a hand in his death. La Sebastiana is one of the 3 lodgings he owned, however, I must admit that I did not gain much from visiting it: it’s more about the trivial bon vivant than the great poet he was. And, frankly, I find the artist and the politician more interesting than the compulsive collector of knick-knacks. (However, if you like knick-knacks, the audio guide does a good job of presenting the house and its furnishings). I just wish there would have been a better presentation of what Neruda brought to the world: How his poetry illuminates the Spanish language. How, unlike most poets, Neruda was a man of action who put his life at the service of his convictions. (In his poem “Let me explain a few things”, Neruda explained his own change from romantic author of love poems to committed political writer: “ You will ask why this poetry does not speak of dreams and leaves” he wrote. “Come and see the blood in the streets, come and see the blood in the streets!”). As a diplomat, during the Spanish civil war, he helped save some 2,000 Spaniards from fascists, by evacuating them to Chile. La Sebastiana is located high on a hill, in a lovely neighborhood, with beautiful views, and there is a lovely gift shop adjoining with various Neruda books and quality souvenirs.

review_text: Sewell is a mining town full of history. This town is located at the Andes mountains, in the 6th region of Chile and is more than a hundred years old. It was built to make the life easier to the families who had a member working in the mines of El Teniente. I recommend a guided tour for visiting this place or doing a deep research to get to know everything about this important old town. You only can visit the town on a touristic and authorized bus, but dont worry: there are plenty. The town is conformed by a hospital, a church, a bowling, a pool and a lot of residential buildings. This place used to have all the novelties of the period, being an advanced city when we refer to modernity. The town is abandoned and there are no basic services in the town itself, like restrooms, food services, not even cafes, so if you are planning to go you need to be prepared. If you are planning to go, it is a 2,5 hour trip from Santiago de Chile. You need to be prepared for the col during winter, but if you visit during summer, it will be very hot and you will need to wear sunscreen.

review_text: On one of my previous trips to Chile (in 2010) I had the opportunity to climb the Villarrica Volcano. It was a good hike, but somehow I got the feeling that I wasn’t doing something special. Don’t get me wrong: the Villarrica is a beautiful mountain with stunning views, but I was part of one of four 30-50 person groups climbing the Volcano that day. Furthermore, I got the feeling that the climb did not challenge me at all. Don’t get me wrong I am not the fittest bloke in the world nor am I an extreme outdoorsman (the Villarica was my first snow-capped mountain climb), but I do enjoy physical and mental challenges. Nevertheless, that climb up the slopes of the Villarrica in 2010 opened my appetite for the Chilean mountains. So, for my next trip, I decided to look for something different. Trawling the net I came across the Osorno Volcano climbs organized by Huella Andina Expeditions (HAE). By reading other reviews on trip advisor I quickly realized that this adventure better suited my expectations, i.e. very small groups as wells as more physically and mentally challenging climb. I got in touch with HAE by email. The communication with the company was clear and prompt. All the information was provided via google docs and I was able to arrange all the necessary payments on-line via webpay.cl (a Chilean version of Paypal). I found the price to be more than adequate for what the activity entailed, i.e. accommodation, meals, good quality gear and a very experienced guide. The night before the climb I met my guide Jose Miguel at the “Refugio Teski” lodge located on the lower slopes of the Osorno volcano. At the lodge we first did a thorough equipment check and then discussed the details of the climb over dinner (included). The climb is a 12 km long round trip with an altitude gain of approximately 1500 m. Jose explained to me that only about 300 people attempt to climb the Osorno every year (about 120-200 people climb the Villarrica every day in summer) and I was delighted to find out that Jose and I were going to be the only people on the Volcano the next day. Jose also took me to the Park Ranger hut where we signed in for our adventure (Jose was in constant VHF radio communication with the Ranger during our trip). The next day we wake up early and started walking at 0445. The first section of the walk (done in the dark) took Jose and I up a rather loose and steep sandy track to the lower edges of the Osorno volcano glacier. It took us a little more than two hours to get there at a good pace. Once at the glacier we put on all the necessary climbing gear: i.e. crampons, harness, helmet and piolet. Jose gave me a very good introduction to the basic techniques for walking safely on an icy slope. The second section was an increasingly steeper path up the glacier to a little icy ledge called “la roca”. Jose’s knowledge of the Glacier allowed us to safely navigate the crevasses and to gain altitude quickly (We reached “la roca” at 0845). At this point the steepness of the icy slope (45 degrees) and the view of the crevasses below started to test my nerves. Nevertheless, Jose’s calmed and collected attitude allowed me to progress further. The third section was for me the hardest part of the whole climb, as it involved ascending 20 m high and 60 degrees sloped wall. First Jose fixed several anchoring points to the icy surface of the “la roca” ledge. This anchoring point allowed to temporarily secure ourself and the base of the climbing rope to the mountain. Then Jose proceeded to explain to me the climbing plan: First he would climb up to secure the rope at the summit edge. Next, with the rope secured to the top, I would have to connect my harness to the rope and then commence my ascent supported by the piolet on my left hand, a climbing device called ascender on my right hand and the frontal spikes of the crampons on my feet. I am aware that climbing attached to a safety rope may not sound difficult to someone with climbing experience but I can assure you that it was definitely challenging to me. First I had to overcome the mental challenge created by the views of the glacier hundreds of meters below my feet and then was the physical challenge of hauling my body up the icy slope. Nevertheless, with the help and support of Jose (and a large dose of adrenalin) I was able to get to the top at about 0940. The views from the mountain top were breathtaking. There was not a single cloud in the sky and you could see all the mountains, lakes and rivers that surround the volcano… Magic! To top it off, Jose showed me a glacial cave at the top of the mountain: really something special. We did not spend too much time at the top as it was rather windy. The decent process involved a combination of rappelling and belaying. Again, the quality of Jose’s mountaineering skills allowed me to descend with confidence. Once our feet were back on the shallower slopes of the glacier we only had to retrace our steps back to the lodge. The whole trip took about seven hours. At the end I got what I paid for and MUCH more: I got the physical challenge as well as the mental challenge; I got the real wilderness experience; I got a one-on-one mountaineering tutoring session. In summary, the whole trip was a blast. I can’t wait to arrange another climbing expedition with HAE!!!

Then Jose proceeded to explain to me the climbing plan: First he would climb up to secure the rope at the summit edge. Next, with the rope secured to the top, I would have to connect my harness to the rope and then commence my ascent supported by the piolet on my left hand, a climbing device called ascender on my right hand and the frontal spikes of the crampons on my feet. I am aware that climbing attached to a safety rope may not sound difficult to someone with climbing experience but I can assure you that it was definitely challenging to me. First I had to overcome the mental challenge created by the views of the glacier hundreds of meters below my feet and then was the physical challenge of hauling my body up the icy slope. Nevertheless, with the help and support of Jose (and a large dose of adrenalin) I was able to get to the top at about 0940. The views from the mountain top were breathtaking. There was not a single cloud in the sky and you could see all the mountains, lakes and rivers that surround the volcano… Magic! To top it off, Jose showed me a glacial cave at the top of the mountain: really something special. We did not spend too much time at the top as it was rather windy. The decent process involved a combination of rappelling and belaying. Again, the quality of Jose’s mountaineering skills allowed me to descend with confidence. Once our feet were back on the shallower slopes of the glacier we only had to retrace our steps back to the lodge. The whole trip took about seven hours. At the end I got what I paid for and MUCH more: I got the physical challenge as well as the mental challenge; I got the real wilderness experience; I got a one-on-one mountaineering tutoring session. In summary, the whole trip was a blast. I can’t wait to arrange another climbing expedition with HAE!!!

review_text: Freddy 3/19/2023 Pride Tour - Santiago If you’re looking for an English-speaking guide who knows everything you need to know about Santiago and the surrounding area, Freddy Crump is the best. I was part of a very diverse group of six (2 men, 4 women) traveling together in South America. We had booked three days in Santiago to relax and sightsee after a cruise, but, as a group, we also had a whole laundry list of different things the individual group members wanted to do. Freddy was a pro – answering our endless emails in the months before we traveled and coordinating every member’s disparate request into a seamless tour. Freddy is really reliable, friendly and fun to be around, but he is also a great guide with a capacity to arrange car / van service, investigate all the best places to eat with locals, and the best places to be at the best time of the day for photography. Pickup at San Antonio Pier – Freddy met our group as soon as we were off the cruise ship at the San Antonio pier and drove us in a new Mercedes van into Santiago to our hotel. He offered options for tours along the route and also described some of the scenery. Gave advice for currency exchange, etc. He set the tone for a very cordial and interactive tour guide – asking about preferences, likes / dislikes, and setting our priorities firmly for the upcoming tours. He took us on a variety of tours that were all spectacularly planned and executed. The standouts were: Cajon del Maipo, a beautiful, secluded natural hot springs in the Andes mountains, complete with picnic. This spa was probably about 1.5 hours outside Santiago. Freddy told us everything we needed to bring for the day. We were picked up at the hotel and driven to the spa, which was very rustic and fed by mountain streams. After the spa we met at the van where Freddy had set up a first-class picnic with meats, cheeses, snacks, finger foods, drinks, wine, and many types of desserts. He took group photos and allowed us to enjoy the views before we headed back to Santiago. Enroute back to Santiago, he stopped the van at a wonderful ice cream shop (La Casas Chocolate), and then again on the outskirts of Santiago to buy us a sample of local Chilean bread. Best of Gay Bars which included transportation, dining at a local restaurant, and drop in at a couple of area bars, plus transportation back to our hotel. Whether he was guiding us through an afternoon of casual sightseeing or making sure that everyone on our impromptu bar-crawl made it home safely, Freddy was always the type of guide you knew you could rely on. If you’re visiting Santiago, all six members of our group highly endorse Freddy for intelligent, client-focused and friendly leadership of your tours. He doesn’t waste your valuable time and he is also very easy to work with before your trip to make sure your itinerary is filled with the destinations your group really want to visit.

review_text: My partner and I are long term clients of Kayak Pucón. We visit at least twice a year to paddle with Rodrigo and Ema's operation. We always go out on the duckys, the inflatable Kayaks that offer great stability and require little technique. It's always a fantastic time. We get the rush of being out on the rapids, and we always feel exceptionally safe with Rodrigo as our guide. This time around we went out for two consecutive days. One day we paddled the more intense Trancura river, and the next day the Liucura. Both rivers are exceptionally beautiful, with crystalline waters, and amazing vistas of the forests, birds, volcanos, and mountains. We're addicted to the experience, and we'll certainly be back soon, and in the coming years. Kayak Pucón may cost slightly more than other operations, but it's well worth the cost. The level of professionalism, the attention to detail and to safety, and the cleanliness of the wetsuits and river clothing, make it a no-brained choice for us. Highly recommended for all experience levels!

review_text: Even with only some 25% of the site still around, the site deserves its World Heritage Site designation. This was a classic company town situated on the side of hills in a very rugged part of the world in the early 1900's. As an active mining site, we could not go underground but there was enough history passed on with our guide to get a very good sense of the dynamics of the time. North Americans had their entertainment areas while the locals did too. Class dynamics were involved. The greatest loss of mining life [355 souls in a 1945 fire] took place here as did a murder leading to very unusual empanadas. In the middle of the proverbial nowhere, the town was complete with a bank, a cinema and a church. Almost all of the bowling alley is original. The tour ex Santiago is a long day of some 11 hours. We were lucky enough to see condors in the Andes. While the time at Sewell is about 3H, you do pass by mining operations to get a flavour of this giant mine which has worked 24/7 for over a century.

review_text: I thought there was one more thing to see in Punta Arenas, but I wasn't sure whether it should be the replica of the Nao Victoria – Magellan's ship – or the replica HMS Beagle – Darwin's ship – or the James Caird – Shackleton's famous lifeboat – or the Ancud – the ship which brought the first colonists to the Punta Arenas area back in the late 1800s. We had seen advertisements for all of them, and I wasn't sure there would be time to see even one of them. We got back from Puerto Natales about 4:30 in the afternoon, too late for sightseeing, and had to be out of our hotel by 10:30 AM with a 1 PM flight the next day. There would not be time to go and return before check out, and if we waited until after hotel check out we didn't know what to do with the bags, or we might miss our flight home. Fortunately the nice ladies at the hotel Ilaia (see my review) arranged a cab to take us and our bags out to the Nao Victoria (halfway to the airport, it turns out), wait for us, and then drive us to the airport from there, all for about $24, thus solving the timing problem. When we got there, we discovered all 4 boats in the same place, neatly solving the problem of which one to see; we saw them all! You can read all about the history of these boats online, but I'm sure it is more interesting to do it there. It really brings home the ruggedness of these early sailors, pioneers, explorers and heroes, especially in the constant cold, biting wind. Particularly interesting was a map of the area with the Straits of Magellan clearly marked. It is NOT the Beagle Channel as we thought, and where we recently cruised in luxury, comfort and safety aboard our modern (and much bigger) 90-passenger ship the Stella Australis.

review_text: As a student who studies Latin American politics and history, this museum strikes me as one of the most important things for you to visit on your trip to Chile. The museum documents the coup that led to the military regime, life under the dictatorship and the human rights violations that occurred, resistance under the dictatorship, and the eventual return to democracy. The experiences of those who were tortured and of those who had family members who were killed or disappeared are heartbreaking, but what is documented by the museum are an important part of Chilean history. For English speakers, many of the exhibits are in Spanish, but there are available audio tours for 2.000 pesos (about $4 USD) that speak English, and many of the video clips of speeches, etc. have English subtitles. Overall, a very important place to visit if you are interested in understanding a little better the history of Chile and even the human rights abuses that have occurred worldwide.

review_text: GREAT Professionals that understand how to deliver a holiday full of adventure and fun for the entire family. Our family loved this company, their excursions, and especially their guides. We are a family of 4 that was seeking a variety of activities. We let SouthernEx Chile plan propose an agenda and they delivered a family adventure that included; sunset/dinner on Volcan Villarrica with great wine, A visit to a tour/visit to a Mapuche village, Geothermal hotspring baths (we loved this), kayaking on la Poza Lagoon, lunch and tour of Volcano Osomo, full day tour of Desolación trail. SouthernEx Chile also took care of all our accommodations and transfers. The hotels and lodges that they booked were incredible. All were very kid friendly and nearly all had spectacular views. They also prepared/catered a few of the venues and we were never disappointed with the food, or beverages! The planning, venues, activities were fantastic but the the SouhernEx Chile team of guides, drivers, and hosts was what really ensured a wonderful, stress-free, vacation. We never had any communication issues, the drivers were always were on-time, and the knowledge of the guides was very impressive. We have 2 boys (age 4 and 10) and on multiple occasions the SouthernEx Chile team was entertaining our children while me and my wife were relaxing or having a nice glass of wine. One of the things that is important when it comes to having a travel guide partner is “issue resolution”. I don’t like being on vacation and dealing with issues. SouthernEx Chile excelled at this. Our travels in the Chile (Villarrica, Puerto Varas, and Santiago areas) were during the Coronavirus outbreak. There were multiple restrictions that were introduced during our visit and could have had a huge impact on our holiday. SouthernEx proactively dealt with all this by rearranging our agenda (activities, hotels, and a flight). All of these changes executed by SouthernEx with no stress on me or our family. They were great about informing us about these regulation issues, but they always had a proposal that effectively dealt with the issue and keeping our vacation wonderful. I recommend this company to all seeking a wonderful adventure with no planning stress!

review_text: We arrived and were escorted to the far end of the beach - it was strange to drive past all the other services but it turned out that the company with the next departure has a staff person at the entrance to maximise the number of people in each departure. There are 6 companies offering tours and the number of boats and the schedule is controlled by the parks and municipal services. The tour operators are diligent about sticking to the rules which is best for the penguins no doubt! We put on the big ponchos provided and were wheeled out to the boat on an elevated platform so we didn't get wet feet! Our guide was excellent, explaining in Spanish the nesting and feeding patterns of the 2 different penguins in the reserve (Humbolt and Magellanic) and also about the 4 species of cormorants, the sea lions, Magellanic flightless duck and numerous fish species. We saw most of these animals on our tour and then returned to the beach to play in the sand and waves - the water is cold so swimming even on a hot sunny day is a challenge but the location is nothing short of spectacular. We were also exceptionally lucky to see a miniature Chilote deer (Pudu) making it's way up the hill behind the beach. Rating 10/10!

review_text: Coming over from Argentina (Cruce Andino), we visited the beautiful grounds of Hotel Peulla and walked over to the bar by the lakeside port to grab a burger and beer instead of the more formal buffet line at the hotel. After lunch we ventured down through the “village” to the lake and were being “attacked” by pesky deer/horse flies. We found a little relief by the more windy shore and the waiting area but were quite relived to board our boat and get out of the heat and attack. Leaving Port Peulla, there were several quaint small fishing boats nestled in the small harbor with Indian Paint Brush plants in the foreground the Andes in the background.On the emerald waters, Jenny the guide explained that this lake was called Lagos Todo los Santos for the Europeans discovered it on All Saints Day (November 1st) by Jesuit Missionaries. The lake was about 1,000 feet deep which was the magical depth for the sunlight to turn the silt-churned eater into a soft emerald hue. Half way across the lake we started to get a closer view of both Volcan Puntiagudo and Osorno (Chile’s version of Mt. Fuji). After about two hours of a very relaxing lake crossing, we arrived in the port of Petrohue.

review_text: We had planned our wine tasting trip ourselves and of course started with the big names. Then, after having seen the biggies we longed for a smaller scale winery. The Kingston's lay on our way, and we turned into their driveway almost unplanned. And what a good decision that turned out to be! Due to the raging bushfires in the area the number of tourists was down all over the Casablanca Valley, and at Kingston's we found us all by ourselves. Incredible and so pleasant. We got our own tasting out in the open, in the shade of a pergola, with a view over grapes and meadows all the way to the horizon. Conny, our hostess, spoke perfect (American) English and was knowledgeable about the family owned winery, the history of winemaking in The Casablanca Valley, and was happy to answer our more or less informed questions. The tasting lasted well over an hour! Lovely stuff she presented us with, too! I was amazed by Kingston's red varieties. Considered pioneers for growing red wine grapes in a valley known for whites, they certainly know what they are doing and are passionate about it, and Conny was good at conveying that passion. It was a most pleasant experience. ¡Gracias Conny! Kurt, thank you for visiting us here at Kingston Family Vineyards. We are delighted to hear that you enjoyed your time with us. Coni was really happy to read this and she told me she really enjoyed meeting you, as well. Thanks again!

review_text: Absolutely gorgeous property with very calm horses and friendly guides. We did the three hour tour and I highly recommend it. We went through Pingo Salvaje for transport which felt a little overpriced for a random dude in a t-shirt in car but he was on-time and friendly. There was one other couple in our group who arrived by transport almost at the same time, so extra points for good logistics. Had a quick and efficient briefing before getting our gear and horses. Horses all appeared well cared for and they all behaved during our ride. Right out of the gate there's a short down and up through a stream bed so you quickly understand these horses are more than capable and you just need to sit back (or forward) and enjoy the ride. And what a ride it was! The views are stunning over the entire duration of the ride. Our guide stopped at several amazing spots and took pictures for us. Condors were out all day, though mostly from afar. While we rode at other estancias closer to Torres del Paine but this was by far our favorite. I also noticed other reviewers commenting on the time of the ride. I looked at the time stamps on pictures I took and we were riding for 2.5 hours. As best I can tell, the path taken is accurately pictured on the website. So if it's a fixed route the duration is going to vary based on your speed and time spent at stops. Our small group didn't linger very long at the viewpoints, and kept moving so I wasn't surprised it came a little short of 3 hours. Thank you very much for your kind words. We are honored that you enjoyed our ride and it motivates us to continue providing exceptional experiences.

review_text: We visited House, Emiliana, Bodegas RE, Vina Mar, Veramonte and Quintay. We love white wines and were amazed at how complex and lovely the wines of the Casablanca Valley were--much better than expected. Our tour guide, Kylie, of Chile Wine Trails - Tours, was able to navigate the appointments, transportation and entry into all of these wineries for us. I can't imagine trying to do it all for ourself, especially since we don't speak Spanish! All of the vineyards were different experiences and had different features we loved. The tour of the organic Emiliana was fun and the tasting room was cozy. Vina Mar was huge and less personal, but the sparkling wine was good. House had a great selection of wines from the area and Veramonte had our favorite Chardonnay and the food pairings were a nice touch. Bodegas RE is unique in that it specializes in mixing grape varieties to create new flavors of wine and Quintay's vineyard and tasting room is beautiful. Each one was so different and the wine pours at all of them were generous! One note is that there were not a lot of souvenirs to purchase at the tasting rooms, so if you see something at one place that you like, buy it. You probably won't see it again.

review_text: We visited this winery in January, 2013, as part of a private tour organized by Uncorked Chile. I would love to be able to blame our negative experience completely on the tour company, but the fault was not all theirs. Let's start with some positive...I am always suspect of a completely negative review. We had a lunch reservation at the lovely restaurant at Casa del Bosque. Although the place was completely slammed, we were seated promptly. The food was fresh and delicious. The grounds and physical plant are beautiful...which made us even more disappointed at the way our visit turned out. At first we were told to hurry and finish our lunch, as they were ready for our wine tasting (which we had booked and paid for months in advance). Then they told us to take our time. A group had just started, and it would be "awhile." After about 45 minutes we went to our guide and asked him to run interference for us. Several of the staff spoke English, but not all. Bottom line...the Tasting Room could not accommodate us, and we were turned away after having pre-paid, pre-booked arrangements. The place was absolutely overrun by cruise ship passengers....relatively speaking our private two person booking was unimportant. My opinion....there are plenty of places to get an expensive lunch in Casablanca Valley. If you want good service (make that ANY service) skip this winery. Too bad. Casas de Bosque coulda been a contender...

Thankfully I found Espiritu and signed up for a last-minute kayak trip in Lago Grey. The trip was very well organised and just what I needed, transfer, gear, basically everything arranged. I did not have sea kayak experience nor am fit, so was a little worried but didn't need to be. After we got there, I was informed safety instructions, then we changed into dry suits which can be a bit uncomfortable at first but you will soon forget about it as soon as you started heading out. Angelo and Natasha were such great, fun guides!! As I was travelling solo I was in the same kayak with Angelo which gave me a huge peace of mind, all I needed to do was to follow his instructions. He's very experienced, we only have a short time window to go up close to the glaciers before the wind picked up, I was glad and grateful that Angelo hurried us, otherwise we would have missed the chance. After the adrenaline rush, we headed down a river which was relaxing. Finished off with a picnic before heading back to town. I enjoyed seeing the glaciers this way a lot. Did boat tour and mini ice trek in El Calafate afterwards but they are not nowhere as thrilling nor exclusive (this is not a large group tour kind of experience / did not see anyone else during the entire time), definitely the highlight of my Patagonia trip! I brought my GoPro, Angelo also took some great shots and they were emailed to me afterwards so I could download them. The tour was expensive, I think the minimum is 2 persons, I was travelling solo as mentioned so I believed I paid for 2. But it is a private tour with everything arranged, I think it was still utterly worthwhile for such a great experience. What an amazing day we had in the wind and all the ice sculptures. We hope your travels around the world continued to be delightful!

It's not a huge museum, but has a carefully curated number of true masterpieces and unique artifacts. There is a lot more signage in English here than in other parts of Chile. The museum doesn't include any displays or information on contemporary Indigenous peoples of Chile (of which there are several prominent and vibrant communities), which is imho a strong shortcoming. However at 16:00 suddenly it filled up hugely with tours so if you are able to self drive - worth planning around that!

review_text: Initially I went on this trip because of the beautiful landscapes, but now at the end of the trip what I liked most was the experience created by the agency. I rarely overcome my laziness in evaluating, despite several trips made, this is the second or third time I evaluate, and in this case it was due to the treatment of the agency's professionals that went beyond what I had ever seen. Well, we closed a package of tours and transfers, on the first day I was already impressed by the explanation given by the guide Oscar, it was impressive how he studied what he was talking about (I even asked if he was a geologist). I felt like I was living in a National Geographic documentary. Then the way they handle each situation, coming out of freezing water and waiting for us in a robe, serving dishes from renowned restaurants in a volcano caldera, taking incredible photos and every detail thought out that I just won't say so as not to ruin the surprise. I love traveling by car because I have more freedom but this time I admit that I can't imagine having a better experience. Atacama is a place that needs some care, it is high and coming without knowing and choosing tours without a planned schedule can cause you inconvenience. I saw people on their own and people who chose their tours get sick. Now in our class only small symptoms, very different from what I saw here from the unsuspecting independents, as the walks were designed to gradually get us used to the altitude. For me the highlight was the geyser and I didn't even get into the water. Cati and Oscar are a very well-aligned pair of professionals who shaped my trip into an unforgettable experience. I will post some photos they took (they are very good photographers) of me that I loved.

review_text: We read good things about Cruz Andina on Tripadvisor so we chose to do the tour with them. We booked via e-Mail, made a deposit and got to their office in San Pedro de Atacama as soon as we arrived to get details and pay the rest. The schedule was as described and we were blown away by all the beautiful landscapes and animals we saw. The food was good (also for vegetarians, just tell them beforehand). Accommodations were basic, as also described in their brochure (no heating, no wifi, no glitz & glam) but it was clean, we felt safe, there was hot water and loads of blankets and Cruz Andina even provided warm sleeping bags. It was very cold and windy outside and we'd advise you to pack alot of warm clothing, so you can layer up, gloves, scarf, hat, maybe even wear leggins underneath your jeans (may depend on the season you're going, but the trip goes up to 4900m so it's gonna be cold all year long). and sunscreen. and sunglasses. basically everything Cruz Andina tells you to bring along, you really do need to bring along. Now the best thing about our tour was our guide Saúl. He was so nice, always made sure we were fine, checked on us, explained where we were going next, how long it will take us, when the next meal's gonna be and also he gave us alot information about the different landscapes and the history of the places we visited. Now we were lucky that 3 out of 6 people that came along understand and speak spanish and could translate, I guess you're better off if you know at least a little spanish (like it's the case in south america generally). We highly recommend you to chose Cruz Andina and ask for Saúl, it was an excellent experience! Thank you, Saúl! Amy & Noah

review_text: I had a great birding trip over all Chile, in more than a month, organized by "Birds Chile" and personally by Raffaele di Biase Cuomo. Started from Atacama desert (Arica, Putre), then I visited San Pedro de Atacama and the National Park "Los Flamencos". Then I moved to Santiago and to different national parks of the central Chile. Then, more to south, I visited NPs Altos de Lircay, Huerquehue, then arrived to Puerto Varas and took a look at this region. After this, I drove all the Carretera Austral till Villa O'Higgins! Then - Torres del Paine and Tierra del Fuego. Raffaele helped me to find good birding guides for each area I was traveling through, to adjust my itinerary, to reserve lodges and ferries along the Carretera Austral. He always stayed in contact with me by e-mail or by phone, ready to ask all my questions. I got a lot of photos of birds and mammals, including rare ones and ones difficult to photograph, for example: Puna Rhea, Puna Tinamou, Horned coot, Magellanic Snipe, South Andean Deer. Highly recommended for birders and nature photographers!

review_text: I was a little apprehensive to use this company after reading some reviews, but decided to go ahead upon arriving in Santiago yesterday as we were far too exhausted to figure out the public buses when we don’t speak Spanish. The booth to book the tickets is after baggage collection along with another company and some pre paid taxi companies. The gentleman who served us spoke good English so we were able to book a shared minibus for 7,000 CLP each and could pay on card. We got given our receipt and the gentleman said that the minibuses are lined up on the road outside, and there will be drivers with Transvip jackets on. We walked through the final passageway for passengers and had a lot of people approach us for taxis or minibus bookings. One man did have a Transvip lanyard on but not the jacket so we walked past him to the road side. (We had read there are scams where people pretend to work for Transvip wearing lanyards). He didn’t re-appear. We got to the roadside and there were several minivans lined up with Transvip written on them. Se Tesla drivers stood together and one took our receipt, asked for our hotel address and wrote it down an returned the receipt to us. We got in his van which was almost full. 10 minutes later we left, and soon dropped off at our hostel door no problems whatsoever. The main concern we had was the lack of seatbelts and the speed of the driver. It’s worth mentioning also that we didn’t see any drivers wearing a lanyard but some had blue and orange jackets on and shirt/ties so they’re the guys you should look out for. I wouldn’t expect that Transvip would have people working in the foyer to take you to the minibuses as it’s about a 30 second walk, so watch out for that.

We got given our receipt and the gentleman said that the minibuses are lined up on the road outside, and there will be drivers with Transvip jackets on. We walked through the final passageway for passengers and had a lot of people approach us for taxis or minibus bookings. One man did have a Transvip lanyard on but not the jacket so we walked past him to the road side. (We had read there are scams where people pretend to work for Transvip wearing lanyards). He didn’t re-appear. We got to the roadside and there were several minivans lined up with Transvip written on them. Se Tesla drivers stood together and one took our receipt, asked for our hotel address and wrote it down an returned the receipt to us. We got in his van which was almost full. 10 minutes later we left, and soon dropped off at our hostel door no problems whatsoever. The main concern we had was the lack of seatbelts and the speed of the driver. It’s worth mentioning also that we didn’t see any drivers wearing a lanyard but some had blue and orange jackets on and shirt/ties so they’re the guys you should look out for. I wouldn’t expect that Transvip would have people working in the foyer to take you to the minibuses as it’s about a 30 second walk, so watch out for that.

review_text: The W trek is amazing. I did this solo but stayed in the Refugio and buying breakfast/dinner. Lunch was usually given to me by others because the portions were so large. Plan for random Patagonian weather. Dress in layers. I had more rainy days than sunny, and even when it was dry, it would randomly start raining for several minutes and then stop again. It would be hot and then the sun would be clouded and the winds pick up, and then you're chilly and ready to throw on some extra layers. For being Chile's première trek, portions of the trail appear to be in poor condition (those portions not caused by disrespectful hikers hiking off trial and adding to the severe erosion). I'm referring to the wooden walkways that are destroyed, or feeling like they will break the moment you step on it. Be careful stepping on them, or you twist your ankle or worse if they finally give way. Enjoy the moment with fellow trekkers during meal time, and don't forget to say "hola" to others as they hike past.

review_text: If visiting Chile this has to be on your list of things to do, we had never been riding before , however our son persuaded us to try. For the trip we were collected by Frank from our apartment and driving out to a small ranch in the Maipo valley where we met our guide and his horses. This guy is amazing! after introducing us to the horses we would be riding and allowing us some time with them for them to also know us, we were them offered some refreshments ( his home made bread, ginger )did some Yoga and stretching excercises and generally got to know each other The fine part was getting on the horses however we felt very well looked after The scenery is wonderful and the area is so peaceful, you are taken through the vineyards, cross rivers and some rickety but safe bridges and even get to sample a few of the grapes gradually get to relax into the whole experience. There is a break half way with some meditation, and again this just completes the whole experience to make you more relaxed but aware of everything around you. On return to the ranch we had wine from the local vineyards - delicious Throughout the day Frank films the event and sends on after The whole day - 3 hours riding ,plus time at the ranch and travel so about 7 hours altogether This is a must do event , perfect because it is very personalised to your ability, you feel totally safe with the support and care and would love to do this again Thank you for a lovely review

review_text: We went on 10 hour tour today. Pros: excellent service, great tour guide, speaks perfect English and Spanish, very nice and kind people, just like all the people in this country. Cons: The way the tour was put all together didn’t make sense. The bus stop where tour starts is located 5 mins away from our hotel. the Agency scheduled to pick us up from the hotel 1 hour before the actual tour starts and took us around town while picking others up. We were supposed to be the last ones for pick up and not the first ones. I got up at 6am to be driven around town for an hour when I could have walked directly to the tour bus within 5 mins. Then they took us to the winery and gave us 30 mins only!!!!!!!!!!!!! What?!?!!?! The next stop was a horrible restaurant in a secluded area where we were forced to have our lunch and we had to be there for !!!!!!!!! 1.5 hour!!!!!!!!!!!!!! We could have eaten in that beautiful winery but no, no, they brought us to a dirty place where there was no other choices around. The city tour was fun and interesting but my mood was completely killed by running through the winery like a crazy person and then brought to terrible restaurant for 1.5h. I don’t recommend booking this tour agency. Dear Kristina We think your comment has no relationship of what we offer, but still we understood your disappointment and even we invited you to a wine tour, to give you the experience that you wanted. Our tour is called Viña del Mar and Valparaiso, we don't offer a tour to Casablanca Wineries. The brochure has all the information: The price, itinerary, what is included. We only mention that we have a tasting of 1 wine, but we never mentioned Casablanca or any other place related to a wine tour. Regarding to the shuttle, yes, we do offer a free shuttle to the Starting Point. In the case of your hotel, we had to organize the pick-up following the traffic program of the city, considering the rush hour. Yes, there was lack of information in terms that you could walk from your hotel to the starting point. But we still prefer to provide the shuttle to our tourist cause is safer and more comfortable. Regarding to Lunch: We do have to stop in a restaurant. This is a full day tour ( 10 hours as you mentioned) , so our driver and guide need to have lunch and a little rest to keep providing a safe and excellent service for the rest of the day. We stop in a restaurant that give us a parking site, and they book a space for the group which is very useful in a busy day. The restaurant is located in an area where there are more restaurants, just in front of the Pacific Ocean, near to a rock full of sea lions and birds, so you can choose to stay there or not, we don’t force people to stay in that restaurant. Finally, we are very pleased that you enjoyed the service provided by our driver and guide and the tour in one of the most fascinating cities in South America. Many Thanks, TurisTour Team !

review_text: The wine estate bicycle tour can be marred by rainy weather. That does not happen often but as you are taken out of Santiago by car these are available. The bicycle route takes you down rural roads, along some wine estates and even through some of the vineyards. Lunch is served in a small but traditional restaurant in a village. The food is not tourist fare but rather dishes that the locals would have, nothing fancy but interesting to experience. 2 wine farms are visited. The first, a smallish organic wine estate where the owner himself proudly takes you on a tour of his estate and ends it off by sampling (straight from the huge wine-making vats) wines still on it's way to the final product as well as completed wines - a very novel experience. The second estate is a large, old and well established wine estate. Tours are conducted in a slick and professional way. What it lacks in personal contact is made up for in spectacle and glitz. Here the fine wines are poured in pre-determined amounts for the tasting even before the next group enters the the tasting room and then in measured time herded through into the the second tasting area. The extensive, beautifully set up, wine shop where the tour ends attested to a well run, affluent estate. The two estates visited shows wildly different aspects of the Chilean wine-making art. English is not spoken or understood in Chile except in a few touristy places. So, experience Santiago and surrounds in the company of a knowledgeable, English speaking guide and it will make all the difference.
